title: Update deposit contract
body:
This patch updates the deposit contract with the version in the 0.9.0 spec.

--

The primary change here is that the deposit contract at `contracts/deposit-contract/depositContract.v.py` has been updated to the one in the 0.9.0 spec.  This contract has two main changes from the prior one:

   - renamed `get_hash_tree_root()` to `get_deposit_root()`
   - `deposit()` now requires the deposit root as one of its parameters

The first change is simple to fix in the code, the second not so much.  Various places in the code sent junk data to the `deposit()` function, and these need to be replaced with valid data.  In addition, some places that tried to send valid data had bugs that were not picked up until the new contract tests it.

The deposit contract has a minor (albeit critical) difference to the one in the specification: on contract creation it takes a parameter of an address, and adds a function `drain()` that sends all Ether held by the contract to this address.  This change has been retained.  Note that the prior version of this contract in Prysm had another change where it could override the minimum amount of Ether deposited for a contract; given the desire to remain as close to the spec contract as possible, along with the fact that whatever Ether is sent to the contract can be drained, this change has not been retained.

The tool to deploy the deposit contract has been tested (result at https://goerli.etherscan.io/address/0x50b8fe1857812c18ff00b621e28a460e3f9ec269), as has the tool to send a deposit (result at https://goerli.etherscan.io/tx/0xe3a350fed89c12f48693ddf6374a3519fbbdbf8a0c447b8a9068d236d2c791ee).

title: Add generic state feed
body:
At current there are a number of individual event feeds in the beacon chain (state initialised, head updated, chain started, etc.) and scope for more.  Rather than have lots of single-purpose feeds this PR provides a generic "state feed" that can be used for all of these notifications.

This is achieved by making the event pushed in state feeds a little larger, containing a type and type-specific data.  The state feed itself is initialised at the top level of the beacon chain service and passed down to whichever services require it.

This will help with untangling some of the beacon chain code and separating non-critical-path items.  For example, at current the block processing function also updates metrics for Prometheus and carries out additional logging; with the state feed it will be easier to have a separate metrics service in its own package that responds to each event accordingly in its own goroutine.

This PR implements the state feed and moves over one existing feed, the HeadUpdated feed, to show how it will be implemented.  After this PR has been merged further PRs will move over the remaining existing feeds individually.

### [`v0.9.0`](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/releases/0.9.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/compare/0.8.0...0.9.0)

**Incompatible Changes**

-   Make sets.bzl point to new_sets.bzl instead of old_sets.bzl new_sets.bzl and
    old_sets.bzl should be removed in a following skylib release.

**New Features**

-   common_settings.bzl: Standard data types for user defined build
    configuration. Common scalar build settings for rules to use so they don't
    recreate them locally. This fulfills part of the SBC design doc:
    <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vc8v-kXjvgZOdQdnxPTaV0rrLxtP2XwnD2tAZlYJOqw/edit#bookmark=id.iiumwic0jphr>
-   selects.bzl: Add config_setting_group for config_setting AND/OR-chaining
    Implements
    <https://github.com/bazelbuild/proposals/blob/master/designs/2018-11-09-config-setting-chaining.md>.

-   run_binary: runs an executable as an action

    -   This rule is an alternative for genrule(): it canrun a binary with the
        desired arguments, environment, inputs, and outputs, as a single build
        action, without shelling out to Bash.
    -   Fixes [#​149](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/issues/149)

-   New `native_binary()` and `native_test()` rules let you wrap a pre-built
    binary in a binary and test rule respectively.

    -   native_binary() wraps a pre-built binary or script in a \*\_binary rule
        interface. Rules like genrule can tool-depend on it, and it can be
        executed with "bazel run". This rule can also augment the binary with
        runfiles.
    -   native_test() is similar, but creates a testable rule instead of a
        binary rule.
    -   Fixes [#​148](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/issues/148)

-   diff_test: test rule compares two files and passes if the files match.

    -   On Linux/macOS/non-Windows, the test compares files using 'diff'.
    -   On Windows, the test compares files using 'fc.exe'.
    -   See [bazelbuild/bazel#​5508](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/5508), [bazelbuild/bazel#​4319](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/4319)

-   maprule: move functionality to maprule_util.bzl.
    maprule_util.bzl will benefit planned new rules (namely a genrule alternative).

**This release is tested with Bazel 0.28**

### [`v1.8.0`](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/releases/v1.8.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/compare/v1.7.0...v1.8.0)

In addition to adding a go.mod file, this release also updates the implementation of the `%+s` and `%+v` formats to provide semantically equivalent behavior when compiled in either a GOPATH or module based project. All existing tests still pass in both modes. Several cases of using this package in a module aware main program and with stacks that include modules >= v2.0.0 have been manually tested to ensure the results are useful in those cases.

There is one subtle difference in the behavior when using modules. That is, stack frames originating in vendored packages built with the `-mod=vendor` flag will report their import path as seen in the source code rather than a path in the vendor folder of the main project. Some may consider this an improvement—having paths that match the import path used in the source seems more natural—but opinions may differ here. Also note that the `%#s` and `%#v` formats still produce unmodified full paths to the compile time source locations as always.

### [`v1.7.0`](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/releases/v1.7.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/compare/v1.6.0...v1.7.0)

This release updates the implementation to use [`runtime.CallersFrames`](https://golang.org/pkg/runtime/#CallersFrames) to examine stack frame data. CallersFrames was added in Go 1.7, so this package no longer supports versions of Go prior to 1.7. If you need to use Go 1.6 or earlier, you should pin this package to v1.6.0.

Go 1.9 [changed the way stack data is returned from `runtime.Callers`](https://golang.org/doc/go1.9#callersframes). The good news is that we can now see stack information for inlined functions. The bad news is that inspecting stack data is generally [slower and requires more memory](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/pull/19#issue-257935796) than before.

### [`v1.6.0`](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/releases/v1.6.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/compare/v1.5.4...v1.6.0)

This release adds the `%k` formatting verb to output the package name for the function or method of `stack.Call`. The unadorned verb outputs only the last segment of the package import path, while the `%+k` variety produces the full import path of the package.

Note that `%k` was chosen in part because one of this package's forks (<https://github.com/getlantern/stack>) had chosen it for the same purpose. `%p` was considered, but the `fmt` package already uses that for formatting pointer values, and we wanted to avoid potential confusion with that use case.

### [`v1.5.4`](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/releases/v1.5.4)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/compare/v1.5.3...v1.5.4)

This release should fix several recent reports that some environments don't handle the intentional `nil` pointer dereference used by this package to cache the address of `runtime.sigpanic`. Caching the address of `runtime.sigpanic` was a performance optimization, so `stack.Trace` is slower in this release as shown by the benchmarks posted here: [#​12 (comment)](https://togithub.com/go-stack/stack/pull/12#issuecomment-307648686).

But correctness takes priority over speed, so this release addresses correctness in the simplest way possible. A future release may be able to regain some of the lost performance.

#### Notable Changes

⚠️ **This release fixes a potential denial-of-service (DoS) vector in gorilla/websocket, and we recommend that all users upgrade to this version (v1.4.1) or later**

The vulnerability could allow an attacker to consume excessive amounts of memory on the server by bypassing read limits, and potentially cause the server to go out-of-memory (OOM).

See the published [security advisory](https://togithub.com/gorilla/websocket/security/advisories/GHSA-jf24-p9p9-4rjh) for more details.

Credit to Max Justicz (<https://justi.cz/>) for discovering and reporting this, as well as providing a robust PoC and review.

title: Return Empty Results Instead of Pagination Error in RPC + Prevent Future Epoch Requests
body:
Resolves #4019 and resolves #4018

---

# Description

**Write why you are making the changes in this pull request**

As highlighted in #4019, if an RPC result contains 0 items, attempting to paginate them would lead to an error. Also, we should return an error if a request is for a future epoch.

**Write a summary of the changes you are making**

This PR modifies our RPC server endpoints to return empty results if no results are found instead of attempting to paginate a list of size 0. This PR also throws errors if requests for data are for future epochs.

- [x] Tested at runtime

title: Resolve Panic in ListValidatorBalances RPC
body:
This resolves #4020 

---

# Description

**Write why you are making the changes in this pull request**

This PR resolves a bug in in `ListValidatorBalances` that would lead to a panic at runtime when using archival functionality:

```
returns rpc error: code = Unknown desc = runtime error: index out of range [345] with length 345
```

Specifically, this would happen under the following conditions:
1. Current epoch is 100
2. Request balances for epoch 50
3. More validators exist in the state at epoch 100 than at epoch 50
4. See the code below:

```go
    // return everything.
    for i := 0; i < len(headState.Balances); i++ {
        res = append(res, &ethpb.ValidatorBalances_Balance{
            PublicKey: headState.Validators[i].PublicKey,
            Index:     uint64(i),
            Balance:   archivedBalances[i],
        })
    }
```
5. We would loop over `headState.Balances`, which might have len > archivedBalances at epoch 50
6. We would index into `archivedBalances[i]`, which would cause a panic

**Write a summary of the changes you are making**

The loop should be over the archived balances, not over `headState.Balances`. A regression test was added to ensure the proper default responses for both archival and regular functionality so this will never happen again.

body:
Part of #3865 

This PR implements aggregator selection for RPC server and hardness the aggregator connection between beacon node and validator client. There's no breaking logic changes. Validator client simply queries beacon node on per slot basis to check if it's an aggregator. You should see these 2 logs if the validator is also an aggregator

INFO rpc/aggregator: Broadcasting aggregated attestation and proof committeeIndex=0 slot=3 validatorIndex=30

INFO validator: Assigned and submitted aggregation and proof request committeeIndex=0 pubKey=0x82cd058276c7 slot=3

* Added `AttestationsBySlotCommittee`, it returns to-be-aggregated attestations based on slot and committee

* Started `/client/validator_aggregate.go`, it implements `SubmitAggregateAndProof`, the validator computes slot signature to send it to beacon node's aggregator server
* Added PB definitions for service `AggregatorService` and call `SubmitAggregateAndProof`

title: Properly Return Finalized Epoch in GetValidatorParticipation Archival Endpoint
body:
No tracking issue

---

# Description

**Write why you are making the changes in this pull request**

We currently face a problem that the `GetValidatorParticipation` archival endpoint _always_ returns true for the value of `Finalized bool` in the response. It turns out that was hardcoded.

**Write a summary of the changes you are making**

Instead, we set the value of `finalized` in the response as:

```go
Finalized:     requestedEpoch <= headState.FinalizedCheckpoint.Epoch,
```

An invariant of finality is that any epoch <= a finalized epoch is also finalized by definition. Thanks @terencechain for the suggestion.
author: rauljordan

title: Fix hang on initial sync
body:
This fixes two issues introduced with the new state feed.

The first is a simple missed `Unsubscribe` to a feed when we're finished with it.  Because we don't unsubscribe to the feed it has events pushed to it and blocks due to the channel being full.

The second is a little more interesting.  When receiving a `StateInitializedEvent` but the start is in the future it waits until the start time before continuing.  This would block if further events come in to the channel whilst we are sleeping so we actively unsubscribe prior to sleeping to avoid this potential situation.

body:
This implements the `ListPeers` API call.

Couple of notes on the implementation:

  - the peers returned are only the active peers i.e. ones that have completed a handshake.  libp2p is aware of various other peers (unconnected, DHT, _etc._) but these are not relevant to the call and not returned
  - this required a new subpackage in p2p called `peers` containing the struct returned by `Peers()` as `p2p/testing` has a mock implementation of `p2p` and this needs to return the relevant data structure (so a separate package was needed to avoid a dependency loop) . title: Update lastUpdated on peerstatus.Set()
body:
`peerstatus.Set()` is meant to update its internal `lastUpdated` information for peers on set, but only does so for the initial `Set()`; subsequent sets retain the original `lastUpdated`.  This results in data being considered stale when it is not, and more requests to peers than are necessary.

This patch ensures `lastUpdated` is set correctly whenever `peerstatus.Set()` is called for a given peer.

title: Initial work on voluntary exit
body:
Voluntary exits require work in various places so planning to push it in multiple patches to ensure each piece fits expectations.

This patch creates an RPC endpoint for validator exits that takes a `VoluntaryExit` struct  The endpoint validates the data presented and if it passes the struct is pushed out to subscribers on the state feed with the new `VoluntaryExitReceived` event (for which there are currently no subscribers; that will be the next PR).

This also adds a skeleton for the other RPC endpoints in etheruemapis for the validator that have yet to be written (these fall outside of the remit of this PR).

Note the choice to validate the `VoluntaryExit` at the point it is received rather than later down the line means that there will be some duplication of validation code in the P2P and RPC receive methods.  There will be an attempt to share as much of the validation code once the P2P receive method is implemented, however we don't want to accept the struct blindly in the RPC call and validate it later (_i.e._ in the state feed subscriber) because then we lose the ability to return errors to the caller.

title: Advanced peer tracking
body:
This PR comes from a discussion with @nisdas regarding the fact that we can't track peer statuses accurately, combined with various talks about moving `peerstatus` to `p2p` and the fact that the `ListPeers` RPC call, although useful, could be a lot more useful with additional info.  It combines the previous `peerstatus` and `p2p.peers` information sources and provides both more and better-detailed information.

Some notes on the changes here:

  - `peerstatus` is gone.  It has been merged with `p2p.peers` in a struct that can hold more information in future (would be lovely to add peer software version).  It was also an evil singleton, which irked me (and made ugly code; see `peerstatus.Clear()`)
  - `p2p.peers` has a better view of what is going on with each peer at the protocol level.  Additional states such as "connecting" mean that we can more accurately manage our peer count even though everything is asynchronous
  - the disconnection handler has been changed in `handshake.go` to no longer assume that peers we are disconnecting from are bad peers.  This is because we can disconnect from good peers when _e.g._ we have enough peers.  Instead, bad peers are marked explicitly by incrementing `badResponses` and this value is referred to in conjunction with the exclusion list to decide if we want to talk to the peer or not
  - logging in general in the handshake is more targeted as a result of the additional information available to it.  It won't bother logging connection requests it is going to reject because it considers the peer bad, and it won't log each disconnection for bad peers

This is both a tidy-up and a base to provide more advanced features later on.

title: Give peers a chance
body:
At current once a peer hits `maxBadResponses` in peer status it is ignored forever.  For very long-lived nodes this could result in legitimate peers being ignored because of a few transient network issues, or for upgraded peers to continue to be ignored due to past indiscretions.

This adds a decay feature to peer status: every hour the `badResponses` for all peers is reduced by 1.  If the peer is still bad it will quickly be re-marked as bad, but if it is reformed it will be able to rejoin the network and eventually its `badResponses`will decay to 0.

title: Add ticker shared helper
body:
There are a number of places in the code that create a goroutine that runs some code and waits, in a loop.  This is carried out in different ways (`time.Sleep`, `time.NewTicker`) and with varying degrees of completeness (_e.g._ checking for `ctx.Done`).

This patch provides a standard function, `runutil.RunEvery()`, that reduces code elsewhere and standardises the way that these functions are run.

The patch also retrofits some of the existing loops to provide examples of how `RunEvery()` works (and fix the occasional bug).  Additional loops can be moved over to this method, but it was considered that doing too many of them at once would make this patch touch too many files.

title: Fix cloning target state for check point state cache
body: As part of `process_attestation`, we retrieve `target_state` (ie. state by `target_root`), if such state is behind `target_epoch`, we advance the the state up to `target_epoch` via `process_slots`. To avoid running this this for every attestation, a `check_point` to state cache was advocated in the spec. To avoid mutation of the base target state, state gets cloned before the `process_slot`. This caught my eye because clone it took a big chunk of flame graph: Upon further investigation, I found a bug where the return of `process_slots` is assigned back to the `baseState`: `baseState, err = state.ProcessSlots(ctx, stateCopy, helpers.StartSlot(c.Epoch))` Should be: `stateCopy, err = state.ProcessSlots(ctx, stateCopy, helpers.StartSlot(c.Epoch))` Fixed the issue and verified the flame graph again, clone is much smaller and barely noticible: Edit: After chatting with @prestonvanloon the above description is missing a few more info. To clarify reassigning `baseState` is not any impact performance change. However only saving the checkpoint sometimes is a performance diff. It could be incorrectly updating the cache

### [`v0.9.0`](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/releases/0.9.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/compare/0.8.0...0.9.0)

**Incompatible Changes**

-   Make sets.bzl point to new_sets.bzl instead of old_sets.bzl new_sets.bzl and
    old_sets.bzl should be removed in a following skylib release.

**New Features**

-   common_settings.bzl: Standard data types for user defined build
    configuration. Common scalar build settings for rules to use so they don't
    recreate them locally. This fulfills part of the SBC design doc:
    <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vc8v-kXjvgZOdQdnxPTaV0rrLxtP2XwnD2tAZlYJOqw/edit#bookmark=id.iiumwic0jphr>
-   selects.bzl: Add config_setting_group for config_setting AND/OR-chaining
    Implements
    <https://github.com/bazelbuild/proposals/blob/master/designs/2018-11-09-config-setting-chaining.md>.

-   run_binary: runs an executable as an action

    -   This rule is an alternative for genrule(): it canrun a binary with the
        desired arguments, environment, inputs, and outputs, as a single build
        action, without shelling out to Bash.
    -   Fixes [#​149](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/issues/149)

-   New `native_binary()` and `native_test()` rules let you wrap a pre-built
    binary in a binary and test rule respectively.

    -   native_binary() wraps a pre-built binary or script in a \*\_binary rule
        interface. Rules like genrule can tool-depend on it, and it can be
        executed with "bazel run". This rule can also augment the binary with
        runfiles.
    -   native_test() is similar, but creates a testable rule instead of a
        binary rule.
    -   Fixes [#​148](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/issues/148)

-   diff_test: test rule compares two files and passes if the files match.

    -   On Linux/macOS/non-Windows, the test compares files using 'diff'.
    -   On Windows, the test compares files using 'fc.exe'.
    -   See [bazelbuild/bazel#​5508](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/5508), [bazelbuild/bazel#​4319](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/4319)

-   maprule: move functionality to maprule_util.bzl.
    maprule_util.bzl will benefit planned new rules (namely a genrule alternative).

**This release is tested with Bazel 0.28**

    templated_args = ["--node_options=--require=$(rlocation $(location :bootstrap.js))"],

such as `templated_args = ["--node_options=--require=$(rlocation $(location :bootstrap.js))"]`.

title: Improvements to Committee Assignments for multiple key requests
body:
Still needs a bit of work, but results are very promising. 

```
bazel test //beacon-chain/rpc/validator:go_default_test --test_arg=-test.v --test_output=streamed --test_arg=-test.bench=BenchmarkCommitteeAssignment --test_filter=Benchmark --test_arg=-test.benchmem  --test_arg=-test.cpuprofile=/tmp/cpu.profile --define=ssz=mainnet
```

At 16k validators:
```
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
BenchmarkCommitteeAssignment-8                 8         182708160 ns/op        85009310 B/op     952701 allocs/op
PASS
```
Previously was over 4 minutes for 8k validators. 

Test benchmark set up takes almost 3 minutes for the benchmark, maybe @0xKiwi has a way to load a mainnet state from disk. 

I also removed the span for validator index. This method almost always is a cache hit and can generate a lot of spans at scale. It serves little benefit and was a red flame on the flame graph.
author: prestonvanloon

title: Optimize aggregator process slots
body:
For aggregator, head state is used to calculate committee indices of the requested slot. Which only needs to be calculated at epoch boundary slot.

We naively advance slots up to requested slots which was unnecessary.

Ex:
head slot is 100, req slot is 150, epoch start of 150 is 128. Advance 100 to 128.
head slot is 100, req slot is 127,  epoch start of 127 is 64. Do nothing

title: Optimize Insertion in Deposit Trie
body:
Resolves #[PR]

---

# Background

Our current workflow for computing the Merkle trie of eth1 deposits is as follows:

- Keep track of all deposits we have seen
- As soon as a new deposit comes in, **recompute** the entire Merkle trie of deposits from its leaves

This means every new deposit takes up O(n) in runtime, which makes it difficult to process a large number of deposit logs. This PR brings insertion down to O(log n), as instead we can just recompute the changed branch when a new deposit is seen. This will be a huge improvement to the initial deposit verification flow upon launching the beacon node.

## Benchmark Results

```
goos: darwin
goarch: amd64
BenchmarkInsertTrie_Optimized-4            61989             16087 ns/op
BenchmarkInsertTrie_Slow-4                   111          10635884 ns/op
PASS
```

title: Process slots exit early if same slot
body: With the recent addition of skip slot cache, we `HashTreeRoot` the `state` every time `ProcessSlots` is called. Even under the condition where input `slot` is equal to `state.slot` https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/master/beacon-chain/core/state/transition.go#L277 It was an unnecessary operation and was discovered while running a 16384 validators node. The proper fix here is to return the input `state` early if the `slot` is equal With this, we see a 3x reduction when profiling RPC request attestations

title: Optimize committee helpers
body:
A lot of places in our code `chainService.HeadState` was taken for granted. The call gets more expensive as state size grows and more validators entered testnet. This deficiency was optimized by providing `chainServce.HeadValidator` and `chainServiceSeed`. Then a few refactor of current committee helpers API to allow indices and seed instead of state object. 

Change list:
* Update `BeaconCommittee` API 
from `(beaconState, att1.Data.Slot, att1.Data.CommitteeIndex)`
to `(activeValidatorIndices, seed, att1.Data.Slot, att1.Data.CommitteeIndex)`
* Update `CommitteeCountAtSlot` API 
from `(state *pb.BeaconState, slot uint64)` 
to `(validatorCount uint64)`
* Update `IsAggregator` API 
from `(state *pb.BeaconState, slot uint64, index uint64, slotSig []byte)` 
to `(committeeCount uint64, slot uint64, index uint64, slotSig []byte)`
* Add `HeadValidator` to chains service info interface
* Add `HeadSeed` to chain service info interface

400x improvements running a beacon node with mainnet config 

![Screen Shot 2019-12-18 at 5 50 54 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/71197884-70e06d00-2247-11ea-8c7b-fcf5024547db.png)

![Screen Shot 2019-12-18 at 6 12 40 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/71197887-72aa3080-2247-11ea-822c-60107b6f47a0.png)

Will open subsequent PRs to clean up rest of code with this change

### [`v0.4.0`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.3.1...v0.4.0)

Added features:

-   ([#​85](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/85)) The comparison logic now has cycle detection and can now handle graphs.
-   ([#​176](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/176)) The [`cmp.Exporter`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Exporter) option provides finer-grained control over exactly what types to permit unexported field access on.
-   ([#​158](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/158)) [`cmpopts.EquateApproxTime`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#EquateApproxTime) provides the ability to compare timestamps with looser precision.
-   ([#​178](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/178)) [`cmpopts.EquateErrors`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#EquateErrors) provides the ability to compare error values using the new [`errors.Is` semantics from Go 1.13](https://golang.org/doc/go1.13#error_wrapping).

Bug fixes:

-   ([#​169](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/169)) Use of `unsafe.Pointer` has been fixed to comply with [stricter pointer rules for Go 1.14](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.14#compiler).

### [`v0.3.1`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.3.1)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1)

Minor reporter fixes:

-   ([#​142](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/142)) Fixed reporter to invoke the `String` method when formatting map keys.
-   ([#​148](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/148)) Fixed reporter to properly elide a struct field on the right side if it is a zero value.
-   ([#​147](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/147)) Fixed reporter to avoid diffing by lines if any line exceeds a certain maximum length.
-   ([#​152](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/152)) Fixed reporter to properly treat -0.0 as _not_ being the zero value.

### [`v0.3.0`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0)

Added features:

-   ([#​108](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/108)) The `_` field is always ignored when comparing a struct.
-   ([#​109](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/109)) The naming rules for [`cmp.Transformer`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Transformer) is relaxed and clearly specified.
-   ([#​82](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/82)) [`cmpopts.AcyclicTransformer`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#AcyclicTransformer) makes it easier to write a transformer that avoids infinite recursion when the output type contains the input type.
-   ([#​126](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/126)) [`cmpopts.IgnoreSliceElements`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#IgnoreSliceElements) and [`cmpopts.IgnoreMapEntries`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#IgnoreMapEntries) provide the ability to ignore specific slice elements or map entries.
-   ([#​123](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/123)) [`cmp.Reporter`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Reporter) provides users the ability to add custom difference reporters.
-   ([#​119](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/119)) [`cmp.PathStep.Values`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#PathStep.Values) provide the current `reflect.Value` for the `x` and `y` arguments at that given path step. 

Bug fixes:

-   ([#​87](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/87)) Fixed proper comparing of slices where one is a sub-slice of the other.

Reporter changes:

-   ([#​124](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/124)) The [`cmp.Diff`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Diff) output has been completely re-written to provide a unified diff of the two Go objects as a literal in pseudo-Go syntax ([example](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#example-Diff--Testing)).
-   ([#​131](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/131)) The default reporter has built-in heuristics to detect whether a string or a byte-slice looks like binary data or human readable text, and can provide more humanly readable differences in certain use-cases. For example, a string may be detecting as containing multiple lines of text, for which it will print the difference based on the lines.

### [`v0.2.0`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0)

Added Features:

-   Add implicit filter to transformers where a `Transformer` can only apply if that specific transformer does not already exist within the tail of the current `Path` since the last non-transform step. This filter makes it easier to create same-type transformations (e.g., `func(T) T`) without needing to manually add your own filter. ([#​29](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/29))

-   Add `Path.Index` method, which provides an easier way to index a `Path` without needing to manually perform bounds checking. ([#​56](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/56))

-   Add `Transform.Option` method, which returns the original `Transformer` option. This enables the creation of non-reentrant transformers. ([#​59](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/59))

-   Add handling for `purego` build tag, which prevents use of `unsafe`, which is necessary to implement`AllowUnexported`. However, `unsafe` is not available in some build environments such as GopherJS and Google AppEngine Standard. A future release will remove special casing for these two environments. ([#​68](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/68))

Reporting changes:

-   `Diff` only batches multiple differences together for slices of primitives. ([#​45](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/45))
-   `Diff` prints uses a `s` prefix to indicate that the `String` method was used. ([#​46](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/46))
-   `Diff` prints strings using the raw literal syntax when helpful. ([#​46](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/46))
-   `Diff` reports the type of a primitive when helpful. ([#​65](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/65))
-   `Path.GoString` elides printing type assertions on anonymous types. ([#​21](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/21))

Bug fixes:

-   Unexported map values no longer panics when printing. ([#​38](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/38))
-   Explicitly convert assignable nil interface values. This works around a reflect bug present in Go1.9 and below. ([#​49](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/49))

### [`v0.5.1`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/releases/v0.5.1)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/compare/v0.5.0...v0.5.1)

This is a small, mostly bugfix release:

-   Demote stream deadline logs from errors to debug to reduce logspam ([#​768](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/issues/768)).
-   When a NAT reports an unroutable address (via the NAT port mapping protocol), advertise both the reported address and the observed public address. Previously, we just reported the observed public address assuming that the NAT was buggy. However, this broke communication between NATs within NATs ([#​771](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/issues/771)).
-   Add an option to configure a static set of relays. Unfortunately, libp2p has no way to (currently) determine if a relay is "good" so we spend quite a bit of time picking random relays and getting disconnected, again and again. This new option allows one to specify a set of known-good relays.

### [`v0.4.0`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/releases/v0.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/compare/v0.3.1...v0.4.0)

This release is mostly a bugfix release but it gets a major version bump as it introduces two new features.

Features:

-   Add a `UserAgent` option to libp2p for specifying the libp2p user-agent. Previously, this was specified using a global `ClientVersion` global variable.
    -   Set the default user-agent to `$repo@$version` (where `$repo` is the _downstream_ project importing go-libp2p).
-   Add a `Filters` option to the constructor for specifying an address filter. This can be used to restrict which peers libp2p will connect to by IP/port/transport.

Bug Fixes:

-   Update multiple deps
    -   websocket (bug fixes)
    -   sha256-simd (arm build fix)
    -   mdns (race conditions)
-   Update for go-multiaddr protocol definition refactor. Multiaddr protocols have been moved out of libp2p transports into go-multiaddr itself.
-   Fix some issues with non-constant time operations involving libp2p secret keys.

### [`v0.3.0`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/releases/v0.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/compare/v0.2.1...v0.3.0)

A security-focused release that propagates up the following changes:

-   The minimum allowed strength of RSA keys is now **2048 bits**. Any tests that have been written using RSA keys with fewer than 2048 bits will now generate errors upon key generation. go-libp2p-testing has been updated to prefer [`Ed25519`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/commit/Ed25519) keys by default, and it's recommended you use that library for libp2p testing needs.
-   Key comparisons are now constant-time.
-   Passing unknown curve types to the elliptic curve key generation functions now returns an error, rather than panicking.
-   The new `insecure` transport has been released. **This should only ever be used in tests. The new `insecure` transport is not backwards compatible with the old `insecure` transport.**

### [`v0.0.26`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/releases/v0.0.26)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/compare/v0.0.25...v0.0.26)

Changelog:

-   Both stream multiplexers now coalesce small writes to reduce secio/tls overhead and reduce the number of packets sent. This introduces a 100us delay when writing a small amount of data to an otherwise idle connection but this shouldn't be noticeable on a real network.
-   Yamux now correctly implements deadlines so SetDeadline on a yamux stream will now affect an active read/write.
-   The connection manager now trims connections in a background worker instead of trimming every time we receive a new connection. This should make it more reliable. See [libp2p/go-libp2p-connmgr#​42](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-connmgr/issues/42).
-   The connection manager now uses segmented locking to reduce lock contention when using the `UpsertTag` function to atomically update tags.
-   Update go-smux-{multistream,multiplex,yamux} to import them into go mod. If you get errors about missing dependencies/tags, please update _everything_.

### [`v0.0.23`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/releases/v0.0.23)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/compare/v0.0.22...v0.0.23)

Breaking Changes:

-   `github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/p2p/protocol/ping.Ping` now returns a channel of results (`PingResult{Error, RTT}`) instead of a stream of RTTs and a single error. That way, we can return errors we encounter _after_ we start pinging instead of simply closing the channel.

Features:

-   Libp2p now (optionally) supports using OpenSSL for all RSA operations for a significant performance boost. To enable, build with `-tags=openssl`.

Bug Fixes:

-   The identify service is now correctly canceled when the host shuts down.

Dependency Updates:

-   Goprocess updated to reduce the number of goroutines it uses.
-   Update go-libp2p-circuit updated to improve performance under heavy load.

### [`v0.3.0`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/releases/v0.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/compare/v0.2.5...v0.3.0)

#### PeerIDs encoded as CIDs

In order to bring multibase support to peer IDs, we're slowly switching to encoding peer IDs as libp2p-key CIDs when formatted in text. They're currently formatted as raw base58 encoded multihashes.

This release:

-   Adds support for encoding peer IDs as libp2p key CIDs (not used by default).
-   Adds support for decoding libp2p key CIDs as peer IDs (enabled by default).

#### Go 1.13

This release depends on go 1.13 as it uses go's built-in [`ed25519`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/commit/ed25519) library. If you are unable to upgrade, please work with the go team to address your issues with 1.13 and/or hold off on upgrading this package.

#### P2P Multiaddrs

We've switched the default libp2p multiaddr format from `/ipfs/Qm...` to `/p2p/Qm...` (in text only). All libp2p implementations have supported parsing these addresses for quite a while now so we don't expect any issues.

See <https://discuss.libp2p.io/t/multiaddr-format-change-ipfs-p2p/330>.

#### Bug Fixes

As this is a release of the core package, there aren't all that many bug fixes. However:

-   We've fixed an issue in our metrics library that would cause it to report nonsensical bandwidth spikes in some cases ([#​65](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/issues/65))
-   We've regenerated our protobufs to fix some potential parsing issues.
-   We've fixed some potential multiaddr parsing issues.

title: Update TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee  from 2 to 3
body:
After further investigating on missing participation of certain epoch, It turns out `TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee` set as 2 was not safe enough for 4 validators committee. There's 6% chance of missing an aggregator per committee. This PR updates `TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee` from 2 to 3 to cut down the chance of missing aggregator to 0.3%

| TargetAggregatorsPerCommittee|  len(committee) | Chance one validator gets selected   | Change of no aggregator  |
|---|---|---|---|
|  2 | 4  | 0.5 | 0.062   |
|  3 | 4  |  0.76 | 0.0033  |

title: Remove verify unaggregated attestation when aggregating
body:
When running 16384 validators on a beacon node. One of the biggest bottleneck is attestation aggregation. With 16384 validators, there's going to be roughly 64 aggregators per slot (16 per committee, 4 committees). Per aggregator, it verifies all the unaggregated attestations, and doing it 64 times is intensive. Although it's unlikely one will run that amount of validators on a single beacon node in production

This PR removed unaggregated attestation verification as part of aggregating loop. To compensate this removal, we added signature verification when attester service receives unaggregated attestation so attestation with bad signature won't get accepted into the pool nor broadcasted 

Before and after:

title: Aggregate attestations periodically
body:
In the current naive design, the node aggregate attestations based on live request. If 4 aggregators request to broadcast aggregated attestation for slot 100, committee 1. The node will aggregate the same attestations 4 times. This is inefficient, and viewed as the main bottleneck in single node + 16384 validator set up.
To improve above, the node will periodically aggregate unaggregated attestations and have them already ready in the pool. When aggregator requests them, there is no computation. See below for improvement numbers

Below flames were captured during the first epoch transition

**Before** (SubmitAggregateAndProof 7%, 121 seconds)

title: Add protos for validator proposal slashing protection
body:
This PR adds the proto required for validator proposal slashing protection. 

`ValidatorProposalHistory` consists of a bitfield that maintains a bit for each epoch, to indicate whether it has been proposed for or not, and a `LatestEpochWritten` to help keep track of what epochs the bitlist represent and to help with pruning.

body: As we have seen in attester logging, it gets unbearable when multiple validator keys registered within a single client. So many duplicated `Submitted new attestation` logs when the difference is just the public key This PR updates attester logging experience to be more sane. As it waits till every attester has submitted unaggregated attestation or until end of context. Then it logs `Submitted new unaggregated attestation` with new key field `ValidatorIndices` Another pro from this is gives us more space to log a few more key fields such as committee index, source and target check points. This greatly enhances debugability

- [x] on FRU eviction save to db
- [x] on load re-detect all attestations in db to update span-maps
- [x] lazy load all db to cache
- [x] save all cached items to db on close

title: Efficient computation of epoch participation
body:
Currently archiver service has a bottleneck, it's described as the following. The service recomputes validator participation whenever a new block gets processed. `ComputeValidatorParticipation` is an very expensive procedure. It goes through all the attestations in the state and calculates the total attested balances versus total eligible balances. You can think of it like epoch processing and we are doing it every slot. While this has not been an issue with 1000 validators, it'll soon become an issue with 16384 validators mainnet config.

Another problem is the RPC service calls `ComputeValidatorParticipation` whenever users wants to query participation status. This opens the door to DOS attack

This PR alleviates from described bottleneck by storing a `epoch -> participation` map in chain service. This map gets updated as part of process epoch routine so no extra work would be involved. Another benefit of this change is it allows us to delete tons of old code such as `MatchedAttestations` and everything in `participations.go`

title: Change database *Index() to use slice
body:
This patch change the signature of the validator-related methods in `beacon-chain/db/iface/interface.go` from taking arrays to taking slices as their argument for the public key.

There are a few reasons for doing this.  First, every instance of the code that called these functions outside of tests held slices, so wrapped all of the keys in `bytesutil.ToBytes48()` to pass the argument which were then all accessed with `[:]` as the downstream functions also use slices.  So this change reduces unnecessary allocations.

Second, wrapping the keys hid potential issues with keys of incorrect lengths, as `ToBytes48()` will always provide a 48-byte array regardless of the length of the slice.  Storing and retrieving keys will now error if they are of an incorrect size.

Third, arrays are hard-coded to 48 bytes when we store this value in our configuration parameters and would prefer to use that.  The code now checks length against `params.BeaconConfig().BLSPubkeyLength`

The patch also fixes up a number of tests where invalid public keys (e.g. `[]byte{'A'}`) were used.

1550 1 [11000111 11100010 01111000 10110011 01101111 00111011 10000011 11101101 11101110 11101111 11101011 11100110 11011111 01110011 11110000 11111111 00000011]

title: Forkchoice att seen cache consider bitfield overlaps
body:
This PR optimizes the process attestation work flow for fork choice. As we see here, there's too many attestations getting passed to fork choice:
```
[2020-01-10 09:11:47]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=62 deposits=0 slot=5158
NUMBER OF FORKCHOICE ATTESTATIONS:  52
[2020-01-10 09:11:53]  INFO forkchoice: Executing state transition on block root=0xde60a4f2... slot=5159
[2020-01-10 09:11:54]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=33 deposits=0 slot=5159
NUMBER OF FORKCHOICE ATTESTATIONS:  47
[2020-01-10 09:12:05]  INFO forkchoice: Executing state transition on block root=0x49ee842f... slot=5160
[2020-01-10 09:12:06]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=74 deposits=0 slot=5160
NUMBER OF FORKCHOICE ATTESTATIONS:  46
```

The reason is the seen cache only tracks individual attestation for uniquness, it doesn't consider bitfield overlaps. So 2 of the same attestations with bitfields [7] and [6] will both consider unique, but [7] is what's needed. This PR updates the `seen` cache to be aware of bitfield overlaps. The result looks much better:
```
[2020-01-10 10:47:41]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=51 deposits=0 slot=5638
NUMBER OF FORKCHOICE ATTESTATIONS:  15
[2020-01-10 10:47:52]  INFO forkchoice: Executing state transition on block root=0xc5ad8126... slot=5639
[2020-01-10 10:47:52]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=61 deposits=0 slot=5639
NUMBER OF FORKCHOICE ATTESTATIONS:  29
[2020-01-10 10:48:05]  INFO forkchoice: Executing state transition on block root=0xd4fc9bea... slot=5640
[2020-01-10 10:48:06]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=17 deposits=0 slot=5640
NUMBER OF FORKCHOICE ATTESTATIONS:  14
[2020-01-10 10:48:15]  INFO forkchoice: Executing state transition on block root=0x38b8ee38... slot=5641
[2020-01-10 10:48:16]  INFO blockchain: Finished applying state transition attestations=15 deposits=0 slot=5641

```

title: Better resync checking and running
body:
The check in the `sync` service to decide if to call `Resync()` had two problems.  First, it was being called once per epoch as part of a separate periodic check, and second it didn't take in to account if the entire network was behind or just the node itself.  The former caused issues with falling behind for a while before noticing, and the latter mean that often attempts to resync resulted in a fast failure and loop until other peers moved ahead of us.

This patch makes two changes.  First it breaks out the resync check in to its own periodic function that runs at a faster tick (16 times per epoch).  Second the periodic function itself does not loop, so if it fails to sync it will give up until the next tick.

There are also a couple of minor related tweaks.  First, the resync check also now checks its knowledge of its peers to see if they are ahead of it before attempting a resync; if we're behind but so is everyone else there is no point in attempting a resync.  Second, the peer status update now runs twice per epoch rather than the previous hard-coded value.  This should allow us to have a more up-to-date view of other peers' views of the chain regardless of the configuration under which the chain is running.

title: Benchmark and Optimize ListValidatorBalances
body:
Resolves #4531

---

# Description

**Write why you are making the changes in this pull request**

Currently, fetching validator balances via the `ListValidatorBalances` call takes more than 1 minute to complete! After looking into it, it turns out that while we do have pagination, it does the work to compute all 30k validator balances in the state and _then_ filters/paginates that list. Instead, we should be only performing as much work as the `PageSize` in the request, up to `MaxPageSize`.

Additionally, we were using `ssz.Marshal` for marshaling validator balances into the archive, which ended up being super slow. Instead, we can have a simple, custom marshaling method for that type and get almost a 10x improvement.

**Link anything that would be helpful or relevant to the reviewers**

BenchmarkListValidatorBalances-4                   18540             62207 ns/op           96474 B/op       1012 allocs/op
BenchmarkListValidatorBalances_FromArchive-4       62989             28187 ns/op           17936 B/op        170 allocs/op
```

New implementation only doing as much computational work as the MAX_PAGE_SIZE possible on each request:
```
BenchmarkListValidatorBalances-4                   96092             10719 ns/op           10136 B/op        109 allocs/op
BenchmarkListValidatorBalances_FromArchive-4      133644              8016 ns/op            6168 B/op         70 allocs/op
```
This PR also clears caching in a broken RPC test that was not manifesting due to test sharding, thereby resolving #4531

title: Fix step 2 of initial sync
body:
This patch fixes an issue in step 2 of the initial sync routine.

The term 'finalized epoch' was used to mean both the finalized epoch as our node sees it, and the finalized epoch as the majority of the network sees it.  This attempts to clear this up by using 'target epoch' as the term for the latter (because it is the target epoch for the sync algorithm).

Step 2 was attempting to sync to an epoch based on our view of state, rather than the highest epoch known by our peers.  This resulted in the code hanging as it waited for a peer with data for this epoch even though none existed.

There are now log entries in all wait loops so users are informed what the node is waiting for rather than sitting silently.

This patch also contains a precautionary alteration to `BestFinalized`.  Previously `BestFinalized` returned a list of peers that were at or above the majority finalized epoch, however in the current network this appears to result in it returning peers that are giving us bad blocks.  The change results in `BestFinalized` only returning those peers that strictly report the majority target root and epoch.  This is likely too restrictive for the long-term, and needs to be revisited, but for now it helps avoid the occasional issue of the initial sync getting a bad block and exiting early.  The original code remains in place but commented out (along with relevant tests), and further testing can take place once the network is stable.

title: Sync to highest possible head given the peers available
body:
Step 2 of the initial sync process looks for a peer with a finalized epoch of the local node's latest head slot.  This is okay if at least one peer is fully up-to-date, but if not it causes a problem because no peer is able to serve the node any blocks and the code stays in the loop.

This PR changes step 2 to fetch blocks from the peer with the latest finalized epoch regardless of where it is in absolute terms.  This ensures that step 2 of the initial sync process will definitely be able to proceed.

(Note that there is a general issue with both old and new code that if none of the peers to which this node is connected is up-to-date the node will, unsurprisingly, fail to sync to head.  This will resolve itself eventually if the peers are themselves connected to up-to-date nodes, but the node could take more active measures to find up-to-date peers.  This is something to explore later.)

title: Move to keymanager/keymanageropts command line parameters
body:
Now that the `keymanager` interface is in place we need a way for the validator users to choose which key manager to use and provide them with parameters.

At current the key manager is inferred through logic of seeing if particular parameters are present or not.  This becomes increasingly complex as more key managers are added, not to mention it can cause user confusion if they forget a parameter as the validator will run but not validating with their keys.

This patch adds two new command line parameters to the validator client: `keymanager` and `keymanageropts`.  The former is the name of a key manager (currently one of "interop", "unencrypted" and "keystore").  The latter are the options to pass to the key manager, either as a direct JSON string or a path to a JSON file.  The fields in the key manager options file are handled by the individual key managers.

This patch deprecates the following parameters:
  - `keystore-path`
  - `password`
  - `unencrypted-keys`
  - `interop-num-validators`
  - `interop-start-index`

All previously valid command lines should continue to work, but will generate a deprecation warning with details of the appropriate parameters to use in their stead.

At a later date we can remove the parameters listed above and make `keymanager` mandatory.

title: Create New Beacon State Data Structure
body:
This PR resolves #2011 

---

# Description

**Write why you are making the changes in this pull request**

We need a way to avoid cloning the beacon state 56 times per slot as we get closer to a mainnet release. This PR adds a new beacon state data structure that recomputes its hashtreeroot on writes to fields and provides getters which copy fields on reads to maintain immutability. This PR will be backwards compatible with our current beacon state, and will help runtime a lot.

**Write a summary of the changes you are making**

Adds a new beacon state struct which looks like this:
```go
type BeaconState struct {
    merkleTrieLayers [][][]byte
    state *pbp2p.BeaconState
}

func (b *BeaconState) Balances() []uint64 {
    res := make([]uint64, len(b.state.Balances))
    copy(res, b.state.Balances)
    return res
}

func (b *BeaconState) SetBalances(vals []uint64) error {
    // Recompute the branch up the Merkle trie for the
    // state.Balances field and update the cached value of state.Balances...
    ...
}
```

**Link anything that would be helpful or relevant to the reviewers**

We should expect resource consumption and bottlenecks to reduce significantly. This PR only implements the new data structure with tests but does not yet integrate it into our runtime.

## Next Steps

Next, we need to begin integrating this new type throughout the repo. We would first need to amend the db.SaveState and db.HeadState functions to take in and return this type. Then, we would to modify the head fetcher (from the chain service) to use this type instead. Afterwards, we can just go package by package, checking for any instances of `.HeadState()` and replacing with appropriate getters instead. The `HeadState()` function should no longer clone, but instead just return the new beacon state type because all its fields are protected behind getters that copy.

title: Use New State Type in Prysm's Runtime
body:
Resolves #2011 and is a follow-up to #4602

---

# Description

**Write why you are making the changes in this pull request**

This PR utilizes the new state type defined in #4602 and integrates it into the Prysm runtime. This is a major PR that modifies much of our core code and needs to be executed carefully before merge.

**Link anything that would be helpful or relevant to the reviewers**

Here is what has been done so far:
- [x] Rewriting the DB interface to use the new `*state.BeaconState` type instead of the protobuf definition for all state related functions
- [x] Ensure all DB tests pass and that saving the new state to the DB is backwards compatible with old DB's
- [x] Utilize the new beacon state as the cached `HeadState` in the `blockchain` service and modify the head fetcher interface to return this type

In terms of modifying our `core/` package, here's what has been done:
- [x] Modify most code to use the new state type in terms of inputs and outputs
- [x] Create helpful functions in `beacon-chain/state/getters.go` and `setters.go` such as `state.AppendValidators` or `state.NumValidators()` to prevent giant cloning of `state.Validators()` in a bunch of core functions
- [x] Create other useful setters such as  `state.UpdateCurrentEpochAttestationsAtIndex` setters which modify a single element of a field in the new beacon state type
- [x] Prevent multiple calls to `state.Validators()` in the core state transition function and instead try to pass in the same value downstream to the helper functions within the state transition func
- [x] Modify the output of many helper/core functions to return `error` instead of returning state since we are no longer doing the pattern of `state = ProcessAttestations(state, block)` with this new type, but instead `if err := ProcessAttestations(state, block); err != nil` as an alternative
- [x] Fix the state transition function to fully utilize this new type
- [x] `core/state/` package has yet to be touched and has yet to use this new type

In terms of whats left in the repo:
- [ ] Fix tests (oh boy)
- [x] Integrate in other services such as RPC/Sync
- [x] Integrate into blockchain/forkchoice
- [ ] Fix up spec tests

Runtime
- [ ] Improve Calculation of Balance and Registry Roots. Currently it is a large bottleneck when updating the balance of each validator

title: Better caching of attestation pre state
body:
This PR fixed up `OnAttestation` to better use the check point cache. As we previously implement from the spec, which required duplicated DB and cache read, it was bad as we saw it occupied most of the flames. The better algorithms are specified below:


**Before**
1. Always attestation pre state from DB and perform a few checks with it
2. Then check if the attestation pre state is in cache, if yes, clone the attestation and use it instead of the one in DB
3. Check if the attestation pre state is processed to latest epoch slot
4. if 2 or 3 are *no*, we use the state from step 1, and process state to the latest epoch slot
5. Save the processed state to cache

**After (optimized)**
1. Get the attestation pre state from cache
2. If it's not in cache, we get the attestation pre state from DB, clone the pre state
3. If attestation pre state is not processed to latest epoch slot, process the state to latest epoch slot
4. Save the processed state to cache
5. Perform rest of the checks

As you can see, the optimized version requires far lesser DB reads code and cloning. This has bene tested run time

**Before**
![Screen Shot 2020-01-29 at 9 41 56 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/73385146-79ce5080-4281-11ea-968a-1c9f79a1dcda.png)
**After (10x improvements)**
![Screen Shot 2020-01-29 at 9 08 53 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/73385145-79ce5080-4281-11ea-9599-dce749c5d1ff.png)

title: Don't insert head to proto array DAG as index 0
body:
Looking at the Vizgraph, I was confused on why initial sync and regular sync don’t belong in the same branch. As we didn’t think it was that big of the deal, the following warning log was temporary as it eventually goes away:
`[2020-02-04 15:31:07]  WARN blockchain: Skip head update for slot 187055: head at slot 187008 with weight 4831 is not eligible, finalizedEpoch 5842 != 5843, justifiedEpoch 5843 != 5844`

After looking at this more, we realized to resume syncing, node gets the 1.) head block then start start sync from 2.) last finalized check point. So fork choice insert head block into the array as index 0. The issue is illustrated as the following:
```
Index 0, block_at_slot: 888 (head block)
Index 1, block_at_slot: 800 (last finalized block)
Index 2, block_at_slot: 801 (last finalized block)
Index 3, block_at_slot: 802 (last finalized block)
…
…
Index 889, block_at_slot: 889 (head_block_slot + 1)
```

What's wrong with above is the node at index 889 got built on top of index 0 instead of index 888 and became its separate branch. So everything from index 1 to index 888 basically didn’t count which is why it takes some time to get a new head when node first starts. Bottom branch is 1 to 888. And top is 889 built on top of index 0. The graph proved it:

![Screen Shot 2020-02-04 at 3 32 30 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/73802266-fd041080-4771-11ea-8add-ba873ef2c572.png)

To fix this, a node simply should not insert head to index 0, there's just no reason to do it.

title: Strict verify attestations in pubsub
body:
Due to a misunderstanding of the networking specification, we were only verifying that the attestation signature was any valid BLS signature. The intended behavior is that the attestation signature is verified against public keys of the attesters. This change stops validation of attestations with invalid signatures from propagating throughout the network.

The caveat here is that we don't have dynamic and optional subnet subscriptions for attestations. In other words, every beacon node subscribes to every subnet topic and will now validate signatures for all of those attestations. This may increase client side load temporarily until the dynamic and optional subnet subscriptions are implemented. 

If this feature causes undue stress, please use the temporary feature flag `--disable-strict-attestation-pubsub-verification`

### [`v0.20.0`](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-gazelle/releases/v0.20.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-gazelle/compare/v0.19.1...v0.20.0)

#### General changes

-   When `update-repos` is invoked with `-to_macro`, Gazelle will add a call to the macro and a `# gazelle:repository_macro` directive to WORKSPACE if neither is present.

#### Go changes

-   Gazelle will avoid generating duplicate `go_repository` rules when two module paths differ only in case. Thanks to [@​linzhp](https://togithub.com/linzhp).
-   When deriving a repository name from an import path, all non-word characters will be replaced with underscores, not just dots and slashes. Consecutive non-word characters will be collapsed to a single underscore. Thanks to [@​carnott-snap](https://togithub.com/carnott-snap).
-   Imported repository rules are now sorted.

#### Proto changes

-   Gazelle will add `load` statements for `proto_library` to comply with `--incompatible_load_proto_rules_from_bzl`. Thanks to [@​Yannic](https://togithub.com/Yannic).
-   Fixed a bug recognizing services in .proto files. Thanks to [@​asv](https://togithub.com/asv).

Added features:

-   ([#​85](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/85)) The comparison logic now has cycle detection and can now handle graphs.
-   ([#​176](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/176)) The [`cmp.Exporter`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Exporter) option provides finer-grained control over exactly what types to permit unexported field access on.
-   ([#​158](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/158)) [`cmpopts.EquateApproxTime`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#EquateApproxTime) provides the ability to compare timestamps with looser precision.
-   ([#​178](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/178)) [`cmpopts.EquateErrors`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#EquateErrors) provides the ability to compare error values using the new [`errors.Is` semantics from Go 1.13](https://golang.org/doc/go1.13#error_wrapping).

Bug fixes:

-   ([#​169](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/169)) Use of `unsafe.Pointer` has been fixed to comply with [stricter pointer rules for Go 1.14](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.14#compiler).

### [`v0.3.1`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.3.1)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1)

Minor reporter fixes:

-   ([#​142](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/142)) Fixed reporter to invoke the `String` method when formatting map keys.
-   ([#​148](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/148)) Fixed reporter to properly elide a struct field on the right side if it is a zero value.
-   ([#​147](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/147)) Fixed reporter to avoid diffing by lines if any line exceeds a certain maximum length.
-   ([#​152](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/152)) Fixed reporter to properly treat -0.0 as _not_ being the zero value.

### [`v0.3.0`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0)

Added features:

-   ([#​108](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/108)) The `_` field is always ignored when comparing a struct.
-   ([#​109](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/109)) The naming rules for [`cmp.Transformer`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Transformer) is relaxed and clearly specified.
-   ([#​82](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/82)) [`cmpopts.AcyclicTransformer`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#AcyclicTransformer) makes it easier to write a transformer that avoids infinite recursion when the output type contains the input type.
-   ([#​126](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/126)) [`cmpopts.IgnoreSliceElements`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#IgnoreSliceElements) and [`cmpopts.IgnoreMapEntries`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts#IgnoreMapEntries) provide the ability to ignore specific slice elements or map entries.
-   ([#​123](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/123)) [`cmp.Reporter`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Reporter) provides users the ability to add custom difference reporters.
-   ([#​119](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/119)) [`cmp.PathStep.Values`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#PathStep.Values) provide the current `reflect.Value` for the `x` and `y` arguments at that given path step. 

Bug fixes:

-   ([#​87](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/87)) Fixed proper comparing of slices where one is a sub-slice of the other.

Reporter changes:

-   ([#​124](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/124)) The [`cmp.Diff`](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#Diff) output has been completely re-written to provide a unified diff of the two Go objects as a literal in pseudo-Go syntax ([example](https://godoc.org/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp#example-Diff--Testing)).
-   ([#​131](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/131)) The default reporter has built-in heuristics to detect whether a string or a byte-slice looks like binary data or human readable text, and can provide more humanly readable differences in certain use-cases. For example, a string may be detecting as containing multiple lines of text, for which it will print the difference based on the lines.

### [`v0.2.0`](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/releases/v0.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0)

Added Features:

-   Add implicit filter to transformers where a `Transformer` can only apply if that specific transformer does not already exist within the tail of the current `Path` since the last non-transform step. This filter makes it easier to create same-type transformations (e.g., `func(T) T`) without needing to manually add your own filter. ([#​29](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/29))

-   Add `Path.Index` method, which provides an easier way to index a `Path` without needing to manually perform bounds checking. ([#​56](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/56))

-   Add `Transform.Option` method, which returns the original `Transformer` option. This enables the creation of non-reentrant transformers. ([#​59](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/59))

-   Add handling for `purego` build tag, which prevents use of `unsafe`, which is necessary to implement`AllowUnexported`. However, `unsafe` is not available in some build environments such as GopherJS and Google AppEngine Standard. A future release will remove special casing for these two environments. ([#​68](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/68))

Reporting changes:

-   `Diff` only batches multiple differences together for slices of primitives. ([#​45](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/45))
-   `Diff` prints uses a `s` prefix to indicate that the `String` method was used. ([#​46](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/46))
-   `Diff` prints strings using the raw literal syntax when helpful. ([#​46](https://togithub.com/google/go-cmp/issues/46))

<summary>ipfs/go-datastore</summary>

### [`v0.4.0`](https://togithub.com/ipfs/go-datastore/releases/v0.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/ipfs/go-datastore/compare/v0.3.1...v0.4.0)

This is a major release only because it includes some breaking changes to previously unspecified behavior in the query logic to align it with expectations.

**Prefixes**

Prefixes in queries will now be cleaned (you may need to update your datastores for this).

Additionally, querying with a prefix `/foo` will now:

-   Match anything under `/foo` (including `/foo/bar`, etc.).
-   Not match `/foo`.
-   Not match `/foobar`.

This is what users want 90% of the time. Previously, one had to use the prefix `/foo/` to mean "anything _strictly_ under /foo`. However, due to how key cleaning works, turning`/foo/`into a datastore key would result in`/foo`(which included`/foo`and`/foobar\`).

**Mounts**

Put: Given mounts at `/foo` and `/` in a mounted datastore, puts to `/foo` will now go in the `/` datastore, not `/foo`. Previously, puts to `/foo` would been written to `/` in the child datastore which isn't a valid key in many datastores.

Query: Previously, querying for the prefix `/foo/` on a datastore with mounts `/foo` and `/` would search _both_ datastores. However, keys starting with `/foo` living in `/` shouldn't be visible when another datastore is mounted at `/foo`.

**Documentation**

The behavior and edge cases of datastores is now better documented (and tested).

A security-focused release that propagates up the following changes:

-   The minimum allowed strength of RSA keys is now **2048 bits**. Any tests that have been written using RSA keys with fewer than 2048 bits will now generate errors upon key generation. go-libp2p-testing has been updated to prefer [`Ed25519`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/commit/Ed25519) keys by default, and it's recommended you use that library for libp2p testing needs.
-   Key comparisons are now constant-time.

Changelog:

-   Both stream multiplexers now coalesce small writes to reduce secio/tls overhead and reduce the number of packets sent. This introduces a 100us delay when writing a small amount of data to an otherwise idle connection but this shouldn't be noticeable on a real network.
-   Yamux now correctly implements deadlines so SetDeadline on a yamux stream will now affect an active read/write.

### [`v0.0.23`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/releases/v0.0.23)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/compare/v0.0.22...v0.0.23)

Breaking Changes:

-   `github.com/libp2p/go-libp2p/p2p/protocol/ping.Ping` now returns a channel of results (`PingResult{Error, RTT}`) instead of a stream of RTTs and a single error. That way, we can return errors we encounter _after_ we start pinging instead of simply closing the channel.

Features:

-   Libp2p now (optionally) supports using OpenSSL for all RSA operations for a significant performance boost. To enable, build with `-tags=openssl`.

Bug Fixes:

-   The identify service is now correctly canceled when the host shuts down.

Dependency Updates:

-   Goprocess updated to reduce the number of goroutines it uses.
-   Update go-libp2p-circuit updated to improve performance under heavy load.

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/compare/v0.2.5...v0.3.0)

#### PeerIDs encoded as CIDs

In order to bring multibase support to peer IDs, we're slowly switching to encoding peer IDs as libp2p-key CIDs when formatted in text. They're currently formatted as raw base58 encoded multihashes.

This release:

-   Adds support for encoding peer IDs as libp2p key CIDs (not used by default).
-   Adds support for decoding libp2p key CIDs as peer IDs (enabled by default).

#### Go 1.13

This release depends on go 1.13 as it uses go's built-in [`ed25519`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/commit/ed25519) library. If you are unable to upgrade, please work with the go team to address your issues with 1.13 and/or hold off on upgrading this package.

#### P2P Multiaddrs

We've switched the default libp2p multiaddr format from `/ipfs/Qm...` to `/p2p/Qm...` (in text only). All libp2p implementations have supported parsing these addresses for quite a while now so we don't expect any issues.

See <https://discuss.libp2p.io/t/multiaddr-format-change-ipfs-p2p/330>.

#### Bug Fixes

As this is a release of the core package, there aren't all that many bug fixes. However:

-   We've fixed an issue in our metrics library that would cause it to report nonsensical bandwidth spikes in some cases ([#​65](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/issues/65))
-   We've regenerated our protobufs to fix some potential parsing issues.
-   We've fixed some potential multiaddr parsing issues.

### [`v0.2.5`](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/releases/v0.2.5)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/compare/v0.2.4...v0.2.5)

This release [fixes a bug](https://togithub.com/libp2p/go-libp2p-core/pull/74) in the insecure plaintext security protocol. The implementation now conforms to the spec by using varints to delimit messages instead of fixed-length integers.

-   Forbids <2048 bit RSA keys when compiling with OpenSSL. Previously, these were only forbidden with go's built in RSA implementation.

### [`v0.9.0`](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/releases/0.9.0)

[Compare Source](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/compare/0.8.0...0.9.0)

**Incompatible Changes**

-   Make sets.bzl point to new_sets.bzl instead of old_sets.bzl new_sets.bzl and
    old_sets.bzl should be removed in a following skylib release.

**New Features**

-   common_settings.bzl: Standard data types for user defined build
    configuration. Common scalar build settings for rules to use so they don't
    recreate them locally. This fulfills part of the SBC design doc:
    <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vc8v-kXjvgZOdQdnxPTaV0rrLxtP2XwnD2tAZlYJOqw/edit#bookmark=id.iiumwic0jphr>
-   selects.bzl: Add config_setting_group for config_setting AND/OR-chaining
    Implements
    <https://github.com/bazelbuild/proposals/blob/master/designs/2018-11-09-config-setting-chaining.md>.

-   run_binary: runs an executable as an action

    -   This rule is an alternative for genrule(): it canrun a binary with the
        desired arguments, environment, inputs, and outputs, as a single build
        action, without shelling out to Bash.
    -   Fixes [#​149](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/issues/149)

-   New `native_binary()` and `native_test()` rules let you wrap a pre-built
    binary in a binary and test rule respectively.

    -   native_binary() wraps a pre-built binary or script in a \*\_binary rule
        interface. Rules like genrule can tool-depend on it, and it can be
        executed with "bazel run". This rule can also augment the binary with
        runfiles.
    -   native_test() is similar, but creates a testable rule instead of a
        binary rule.
    -   Fixes [#​148](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel-skylib/issues/148)

-   diff_test: test rule compares two files and passes if the files match.

    -   On Linux/macOS/non-Windows, the test compares files using 'diff'.
    -   On Windows, the test compares files using 'fc.exe'.
    -   See [bazelbuild/bazel#​5508](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/5508), [bazelbuild/bazel#​4319](https://togithub.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/4319)

-   maprule: move functionality to maprule_util.bzl.
    maprule_util.bzl will benefit planned new rules (namely a genrule alternative).

**This release is tested with Bazel 0.28**
