title: Implement Standard Slashing Protection JSON With Importing Logic
body:
Part of #7813 

**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

We have written up a design document for this feature [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12SZgszMbfhUqwGukJWKQCOmoCa8nY8D3GtYEElgjEKk/edit#).

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR implements the standard slashing interchange format defined by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3076. It allows for unmarshaling an input JSON file and converting it into our internal representation of attester and proposal slashing protection. Then, we can import this representation into our database atomically.

Among the features included are:
- [x] Reading a JSON file and ensuring its necessary fields are not junk data
- [x] Checking against the version field of the parsed JSON
- [x] Allowing for duplicate public keys in the slashing protection data with possibly different signed blocks and attestations
- [x] Comprehensive tests for ensuring we handle duplicate data, bad data, and good data
- [x] Tests for different helper functions, especially string parsers
- [ ] Validate genesis root #7813 
- [ ] Validate whether the data we are importing is slashable with respect to our database #7813
- [ ] Validate whether the data we are importing is slashable with respect to other entries in the JSON file #7813

**Other notes for review**

The underlying representation of proposal protection assumes that everything imported from the JSON will have a signing root, however, signing roots are optional in the EIP. The tracking issue mentions this as an open action item to tackle in a future PR.

title: Continue In ProcessPreGenesisDeposits
body:
Part of #7410, this PR returns an error in `ProcessPreGenesisDeposits` if a pubkey for a deposit is not found in the beacon state. This is a good best practice as outlined by trail of bits. However, the conditional will never trigger because of how the function works:

1. Process all new deposits into the beacon state
2. Then, for each deposit that was processed, fetch the validator corresponding to the public key in the deposit

Since step (1) added new validators into the state before (2) runs, there will _always_ be a corresponding validator for a public key for each processed deposits. As such, it is impossible to write a test for this. However, we should still handle the error for consistency.

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR prevents usage of ioutil.WriteFile and os.MkdirAll in our repository, as those are unsafe when it comes to checking permissions. For example, an attacker could create a directory `p` with 777 permissions, and `os.MkdirAll(p)` will fail silently, without overriding the permissions of the attacker. Instead, we enforce Prysm to use our own `shared/fileutil` package that properly checks for permissions errors compared to the Go standard library. We enforce this using a static analyzer that prevents `os.MkdirAll` and `ioutil.WriteFile`.

title: Use a short cut in migration step
body:
This updates migration method to apply a short cut. Currently:
```
1. Retrieve `missingState` using `missingRoot`
2. Check if `missingRoot` is in DB
3. If not, save `missingState` in DB
```

We simplify this to:
```
1. Check if `missingRoot` is in DB
2. If not, retrieve `missingState` using `missingRoot`
3. Save `missingState` in DB
```

So we don't have to `retrieve` if the `missingRoot` was already in the DB

title: Init-sync fetcher: backtracking
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- This PR introduces backtracking routine only. It doesn't amend any existing semantics (but has some refactoring - particularly, "extract method" type of refactoring) and is not wired into init-sync queue. So, in that sense it is safe to merge this PR (it still needs a proper review, of course).

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Algorithm:**
- When FSMs blocks do not move head, FSM is considered as stuck and is reset from the current head (we have 8 FSMs, and the last one is used to to "look forward" resolving potentially long chain of skipped blocks).
- When stuck on a block, counter is increased, and FSM is reset and blocks are re-requested (to account for situations when it was just some unfavourable peer selected during previous run, and mesh actually has required blocks).
- After counter grows beyond certain threshold value, queue knows it is legitimately stuck, so it requests exploration of alternative works from fetcher:
  - Fetcher checks if we are far from finalization point, as if we are not, resetting to that finalized point is enough to progress.
  - Otherwise, fetcher queries all known peers, that have higher head that ours, it does so until:
    - some peer produces block for which we do not have parent i.e. potential fork
    - using blocks by root requests, blocks parent is requested and on that parent blocks the same procedure is repeated, up until we find common ancestor (that's we found point at which that forked block enters our known chain) or exhaust some configurable threshold (I am experimenting with 128 and 64 hops).
    - if common ancestor is found, queue forwards all the blocks we have discovered (and they are processable as they lead from the common ancestor till that block w/o a parent we started from)
    - this gives us all the intermediary blocks and on the next FSM reset, we will be able to process further blocks from that fork

If a given fork is still unfavourable process continues, potentially exploring all the forks.

title: Batch verify aggregated attestation signatures
body:
This PR batches verify all 3 signatures within aggregated attestation, the 3 signatures in aggregated attestation: selection signature, aggregator signature, and attestation signature. 

It combines the following 3 verifications into 1:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/98453485-71f3e480-210e-11eb-9a8a-2b9620348cae.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/98453512-c4cd9c00-210e-11eb-9f41-046d84363107.png)


With the following benchmark: https://gist.github.com/terencechain/412ef767ff37562a2735237c7ffc8b71
We gathered the following results:
```
Before:
BenchmarkValidateAggregateAndProof
BenchmarkValidateAggregateAndProof-12             295       3931547 ns/op
PASS

After:
BenchmarkValidateAggregateAndProof
BenchmarkValidateAggregateAndProof-12             414       2812799 ns/op
```

The result showed 40% improvements, roughly 1200000ns of saving on per attestation. There's currently 260 aggregated attestation per slot in medalla. That’s about 300ms we could save on per slot.

title: Correct how AllValidatorsAreExited creates status request
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This bug fixes #7707 -- If you look at this in validator/client/validator.go

```
	var publicKeys [][]byte
	for _, key := range validatingKeys {
		publicKeys = append(publicKeys, key[:])
	}
	request := &ethpb.MultipleValidatorStatusRequest{
		PublicKeys: publicKeys,
	}
```

What I saw during debugging is that after the range-for loop, publicKeys ends up with a set of identical keys that match the last key appended.  This is likely because the iterating variable (key)'s memory address is appended and since this address will last hold the last key iterated over in validatorKeys, publicKey ends up with multiple copies of the same key.  If the validator associated with the last key is exited, then this function will true that all validators are exited and this leads to the described bug.  To fix this I just create a copy and append that instead.  There is a regression test created as well which creates a couple of sample keys and sees if the request is as expected.  This test fails on current master and passes with this PR.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #7707

title: Remove redundant calls to os.exit() in TestMain
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other / Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- As of go 1.15, we do not need to call `os.Exit(m.Run())` explicitly, as value returned by `m.Run()` is stored into unexported field of `m` and `go test` executable is smart enough to automatically call `os.Exit(retValue)` when `TestMain()` returns (with that stored value passed as `retValue`).
- This simplifies `TestMain()` (we do not need to call `os.Exit()` explicitly), moreover, it allows us to register teardown functions as deferred (since we are not calling `os.Exit()` explicitly, which prevents any defers, `TestMain()` returns normally, all deferred functions called).

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**
- For implementation details (how this is implemented in Go), see [testing: TestMain should not require os.Exit](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/34129) in the official Golang GH repo.

title: Disable an account without having to restart the node
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
Currently, disabling and enabling an account requires users to restart their validator nodes.
This could be particularly dangerous (mostly for disabling accounts) as users could think that a signing key is disabled and re-use the same key with a different client or different server resulting in a potential slashing condition. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
Fixes #7787 

**Other notes for review**
With the current approach of detecting a change for keymanageropts.json, I am able to hot-reload after disabling an account but I am NOT able to hot-reload after re-enabling an account.
This can be explain by the fact that keymanageropts.json contains a list of `disabled_public_keys`, removing a key from that list can be picked up by the watcher, but we won't know which one has been removed.

title: Refactor HD Wallets for Enhanced Security
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.
2. Please file an associated tracking issue if this pull request is non-trivial and requires context for our team to understand. All features and most bug fixes should have
   an associated issue with a design discussed and decided upon. Small bug
   fixes and documentation improvements don't need issues.
3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to
   be updated. If you're unsure what to update, send the PR, and we'll discuss
   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Refactor

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Our current HD wallet is extremely insecure, and other teams do not follow our convention. Currently:
- We create a mnemonic for a user and tell them to write it down
- We encrypt the seed derived from the mnemonic with their wallet password
- We store the encrypted seed on disk
- We load the seed to RAM upon startup of the validator
- We generate N keys as needed at runtime by deriving them from the seed

If someone takes this seed, or dumps a validator's memory, they are screwed. Moreover, storing a seed on disk is still not an adequate substitute.

This PR advocates for a different approach to our HD wallet altogether. Instead, we make it a **simple wrapper** around our imported keymanager. During wallet creation, we now show the user a mnemonic and ask them to write it offline, then we ask the user to generate N accounts where N > 0. Then, we import those as keystore files into our imported keymanager. The seed nor mnemonic are never stored after this.

This PR also removes the `accounts create` command the RPC endpoint given there is no longer any way to create a new account in Prysm. This must be done by another tool such as ethdo or the deposit cli.

```
FAIL: //beacon-chain/sync:go_default_test (shard 3 of 4, run 1 of 10) (see /home/j/.cache/bazel/_bazel_j/1ba834ca9d49f27aeb8f0bbb6f28fdf3/execroot/prysm/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/testlogs/beacon-chain/sync/go_default_test/shard_3_of_4_run_1_of_10/test.log)
```

**What type of PR is this?**

> Other / Refactoring

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Extracted from #7480, adds the following changes:
  - [x] Removes weight from bad responses scorer (score is penalty, so no weight is necessary)
  - [x] Removes contexts from scorers. We have this anti-pattern everywhere, when we are passing `ctx` to control life-time of the service: fortunately, `ctx` in scorers are not used at all, so easy to refactor/remove.
  - [x] Adds `Scorer` interface, makes sure that both scorers and scorer service comply to it. This means that we can use individual scorers, and when necessary can query service object, which will traverse all registered scorers. For ex, `IsBadPeer(pid)` when called on service object will traverse all the individual scorers and mark peer as bad if *any* of the scorers mark it as such.
  - [x] Adds weights to individual scorers, allowing us to control how much each individual scorer contributes to the overall score (also allows having scorers with 0 weight - such scorers are useful individually, but not contributing to overall score).

title: Extract common types from sync
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other/Refactoring

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Extracted from #7480
- Peer scorers need access to common sync errors and possible goodbye messages (codes). Particularly, status peer scorer (implemented in #7480, that scorer decides whether peer is good/bad based on validation error). 
- When it comes to goodbye codes - then they are used as an extra elaboration on why peer is considered bad:
```golang
// Disconnect from peers that are considered bad by any of the registered scorers.
if s.p2p.Peers().Scorers().IsBadPeer(id) {
	goodbyeCode := p2ptypes.ErrToGoodbyeCode(s.p2p.Peers().Scorers().ValidationError(id))
	if err := s.sendGoodByeAndDisconnect(s.ctx, goodbyeCode, id); err != nil {
		log.Debugf("Error when disconnecting with bad peer: %v", err)
	}
	return
}

```
- This PR moves error messages and goodbye codes into `p2p/types` sub-package (we cannot move to `p2p` as it will create circular dependency `p2p/peers/scorers -> p2p -> p2p/peers/scorers`).

**What type of PR is this?**

> Refactor

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Part of #7813, this PR performs a very important refactor of slashing protection. Currently, our slashing protection is tightly coupled with the validator service, making it hard to write extensive tests for it. It also does not use the proper abstractions, making the code mixed with remote slashing protection confusing. Many functions use unclear names, have many responsibilities that should be at different layers, and overall this reduces confidence we have in the feature. This PR is meant to be a refactor and a simplification, while keeping the underlying core logic of how attesting and proposal histories work as we are so close to mainnet launch.

**Other notes for review**

Among the changes included are:
- [x] Move all slashing protection logic into its own service called `slashing-protection`
- [x] Define a `Protector` interface that can be used as a simple black box whenever slashing protection is desired, such as in the validator client service
- [x] Remove the duplication of slashing protection checks. We were performing the _same checks_ twice to see if a block or attestation is slashable. This is unnecessary and inefficient.
- [x] Improve error handling across the feature
- [x] Simplify the slashing protection functions, which were mixed in with a lot of logging, feature flags, metrics updates, and overall complexity that obfuscates how simple some of the methods should be
- [x] Fixes all tests
- [x] Tried at e2e

```
When processing deposits (before genesis state):
*prometheus.Service: OK
*p2p.Service: OK
*attestations.Service: OK
*initialsync.Service: OK
*sync.Service: OK
*gateway.Gateway: OK
*powchain.Service: OK
*blockchain.Service: ERROR genesis state has not been created
*rpc.Service: OK

After processing deposits (during sync):
*powchain.Service: OK
*blockchain.Service: OK
*p2p.Service: OK
*initialsync.Service: ERROR syncing
*sync.Service: ERROR out of sync
*rpc.Service: OK
*gateway.Gateway: OK
*prometheus.Service: OK
*attestations.Service: OK
```

Fixes #6682

title: Fix Alpine Docker Image
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR switched the alpine base image for running the compiled binaries. The binaries expect dynamic linking to `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` which doesn't exist by default in alpine image. [libc6-compat](https://pkgs.alpinelinux.org/package/edge/main/x86/libc6-compat) provides a fix for that. Hence, a custom docker image is built for that: https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/pinglamb/alpine-glibc.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #5768 

**Other notes for review**

The `Dockerfile` for reference:

```
FROM alpine:3.12
RUN apk update && apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
```

End Goal:

title: Improve Slashing Protection for V1, More Tests and Observability
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Slashing protection, in current `master`, lives with some really serious problems. Although most of these issues are patched in #7848, that PR needs time to be tested in pre-production environments before making into the master branch due to how radical it is and how much it changes. Unfortunately, we still have some bugs today in detecting surround votes, which we have observed today in our internal infrastructure. The issues are with respect to false positives, meaning that local slashing protection detects certain attestations as slashable which are not. Moreover, **we do not have enough logs available to help us understand the problem**. This PR adds the following changes:

- [x] Add a Debug log containing all attestation details in case local slashing protection detects a surround vote or double vote, same for beacon blocks
- [x] Add more informative logic about why the offense detected is a surround vote or double vote
- [x] Refactor our logic which checks whether something is a surround vote or not, ensuring we have full unit tests for _all possible permutations of surround votes_
- [x] Ensure we do not have dangerous variable shadowing the underlying method which marks all epochs up to a certain target epoch as attested
- [x] Add comprehensive tests to ensure we are within the weak subjectivity period when checking slashable attestations
- [x] Add better error handling

title: Attestation aggregation: optimizations and benchmarks
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix
> Feature
> Other/Refactoring

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In this PR:
- `optMaxCoverAttestationAggregation()` method is added. See https://hackmd.io/@farazdagi/in-place-attagg for details on design of that optimized aggregation procedure. Once this feature is tested, `optMaxCoverAttestationAggregation()` will replace existing `Bitlist` based implementation.
- New flag value (`opt_max_cover`) for `attestation-aggregation-strategy` flag has been added (flag is tracked via #8365). So, new aggregation is used when one of the following is set:
  - `attestation-aggregation-strategy=opt_max_cover`
  - `--dev`
- E2E tests are also configured to rely on a new optimized max-cover.
- ❗ It should be safe to merge this PR, in a sense that it affects only `--dev` mode of beacon node.

PRs extracted from this PR:
- [x] Performance benchmarks #8043
- [x] Fix issue with proper sets #8063
- [x] Baseline benchmark (max-cover vs naive) #8308
- [x] Clock-time benchmarks #8352
- [x] More optimized validation of incoming attestations #8213
- [x] Max-cover on attestation selection by proposer (will be tackled separately in #8353)


**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #7871 

**Other notes for review**
- It is very hard to benchmark the `Aggregation()` function, because it updates attestations in place, so for each bench mark run you need to create another copy of attestations lists (and when using `b.StopTimer()/b.StartTimer()` inside the `for i := 0; i < b.N; i++` loop -- so that each case gets its own copy -- benchmarks seem to hang.  
- So, attestation copying was put inside as a part of benched function, but that copying is more heavy than aggregation itself, so results on number of operations completed are only relatively useful.
- Still, benchmarks allow to see the difference in allocations (which was the purpose of this optimization -- get rid of unnecessary allocations), so benchmarks are still useful:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/106329489-90dbc000-6292-11eb-9742-ac1033c90c2b.png)

title: Add ValidatorDB Methods for Highest and Lowest Signed Proposals
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR adds database methods to save and retrieve the highest and lowest signed proposals for a validator key. This logic is important as part of enforcing the slashing protection logic from the EIP-3076 standard. The approach is as follows:

Upon saving an incoming proposal into our validatorDB:
1. Check the bucket for the proposer public key
2. Check if we have a value under the lowest signed proposals key
3. If we do, then we check if the incoming proposal slot is lower and override it
4. If we do not, then we save the incoming slot as the lowest signed proposal slot

We do the same logic above for highest proposal slot signed.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #7813

**NOTES**
This PR also changes a few DB method signatures to use [48]byte instead of a slice for consistency purposes

title: Update blst to v0.3.1 and incorporate subgroup changes
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Update blst version

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Update blst to v0.3.1
Update blst wrappers for the new subgroup check API changes

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

The overall subgroup check methodology is public keys should be check for validity using KeyValidate() at time of first seeing them. This will check for infinity and in group. Those keys can then be cached for future usage. All calls into blst set the pkValidate boolean to false to indicate there is no need for on the fly checking of public keys in the library. Additionally the public keys are expected to be validated for proof of possession outside of blst.

For signatures the subgroup check can be done at time of deserialization, prior to being used in aggregation or verification, or in the blst aggregation or verification functions themselves. In the interface wrapper the call to SigValidate has been left in place (it used to be inside of Uncompress), though it could be moved to the verify calls instead. 

All checks on signature are done for subgroup only. There are no checks for infinity. The rationale is an aggregate signature could technically equal infinity. If any individual signature was infinity (invalid) then it would fail at time of verification. A loss of compute resources, although safety would be preserved.

title: Init-sync: enable peer scorer by default
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other / Feature Release

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Peer scorer in init-sync was enabled in `--dev` for months, so relatively it is much more stable than peer scoring in p2p and/or gossip (which are protected by the very same `--enable-peer-scorer` flag).
- The purpose of peer scorer in init-sync was to probabilistically select peers that provide better data: if data provided by peer moves head forward well (on average), peer's score gets increased, and peer gets better chances to get selected.
- The problem with ineffective peers was amplified on `altona` when some clients returned 1 block (or few blocks), and sync was becoming really slow. With peer scorer such ineffective peers can *still* be selected, but with lesser chances (weighted random selection).
- After discussing with @nisdas we decided to release this part of peer scorer separately, w/o waiting for other types or scoring (to make sure that init sync process is more effective). Since scorers are quite cohesive, and can be used independently, we do not have to couple init-sync scorer's release cycle and that of other types of scoring. It is ready, and has been tested running for long time in `--dev` mode.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

title: Update go-libp2p to 0.12.0
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

go-libp2p 0.12.0 made some significant changes to the stream interfaces around stream closing:

* Close now closes in both directions and frees the stream. However, unlike FullClose did, it doesn't _wait_ for the remote peer to respond with an EOF.
* To close for writing, call CloseWrite (like one would on a TCP connection, etc.).

This patch:

* Replaces calls to FullClose with Close where appropriate.
* Replaces calls to Close with CloseWrite where appropriate.
* Removes redundant Close calls.
* Calls Reset to where appropriate to indicate that the request/response was aborted. Unlike Close, this will not flush and will not cause the remote peer to read an EOF. Instead, the remote peer will read an ErrReset error.
* Ensures we always either close or reset streams. Send wasn't closing the stream on some error paths.
* Now that stream closing is async, we explicitly wait for a response when "hanging up" on a peer (so we don't hang up before they receive our response/goodbye message).

**Design Question 1**

Given that all requests/responses are length delimited, the use of `Reset` is optional. The upsides of using reset are:

* It's often faster than calling close (and flushing).
* It lets the other side know that you didn't finish sending your response.

The downside is that the choice between reset/close isn't always obvious and resetting a stream after writing will cause the write to be lost (by design).

If you'd rather just stick with close and avoid reset entirely, I'm happy to rework the patch to do that.

**Design Question 2**

This patch makes stream closing async to more closely mimic a TCP connection. However, this can cause issues when a close is immediately followed by a disconnect. I'm currently working around this issue by mimicing the old `FullClose` (now `closeStreamAndWait`) where necessary.

If desired, I can go back to synchronously closing everywhere, at the cost of losing out on some potential (maybe) latency improvements.

**What type of PR is this?**

> Removing old/expensive feature


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`BlockTimeByHeight` is not a cheap call when running external hosted web3 provider (e.g. infura). The call gets significantly more expensive with more unknown validating keys. 

The actual usefulness of `Deposit for validator received but not processed into the beacon state` log is questionable. Validators use beacon block explorer with their eth1 address to check deposit status. Removing this log to save eth1 bandwidth is a fine trade off imo.

Most importantly, excessive calls to `BlockTimeByHeight` + using hosted web3 provider can cause context deadline and cause validators to miss attestation, that's ultimately what we want to avoid

Note: I didn't remove protobuf field since this has higher pirority. Removing the actual protobuf field will come later

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.

3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to

4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.

**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Before this commit, it was not possible to pass in base64-encoded
content as a header value if it contained an equals sign. This commit
changes the behavior slightly. Rather than ignore key/value pairs where
the value happens to have an equals sign, we assume the first equals
sign delimits the key from the value and pass in the rest of the value
as-is.

Also, instead of printing the header name along with its value, we only
print the name, so there is less risk of leaking information into logs
that shouldn't be there.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

This has not been tested in the context of the full validator client.
Instead, a small example was made to demonstrate the feasibility. The
example is shown here:

```go
package main

import (
	"log"
	"os"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davecgh/go-spew/spew"
	"github.com/urfave/cli/v2"
)

type Config struct {
	GrpcHeadersFlag string
}

func main() {
	app := &cli.App{
		Action: func(c *cli.Context) error {
			for _, hdr := range strings.Split(c.String("grpc-headers"), ",") {
				if hdr != "" {
					ss := strings.Split(hdr, "=")
					spew.Dump(ss[0])
					spew.Dump(strings.Join(ss[1:], "="))
				}
			}
			return nil
		},
		Flags: []cli.Flag{
			&cli.StringFlag{
				Name: "grpc-headers",
				Usage: "A comma-separated list of key value pairs to pass as gRPC headers for all gRPC " +
					"calls. Example: --grpc-headers=key=value",
			},
		},
	}

	err := app.Run(os.Args)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

Example invocation:

```command
❯ go run main.go --grpc-headers=key=value,Authorization="Basic $(echo -n hello:world | base64)"
(string) (len=3) "key"
(string) (len=5) "value"
(string) (len=13) "Authorization"
(string) (len=22) "Basic aGVsbG86d29ybGQ="
```

title: Attestation aggregation: remove proper set duplicates
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Deduplicate aggregated attestations that contain some attestations which are nothing more but proper sets of other attestations (thus do not have any new info).
- Such proper set attestations can be removed, **but only in situations where we do not plan to do any more aggregation**, since if we do -- some profitable (ones that produce profitable aggregation) intermediary attestations, even if they are proper sets, might be removed. So, this deduplication must take place as late in the process as possible, hence it is implemented in proposer.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #7871

**Other notes for review**
- Extracted from #7938
- In `attestations/kv/aggregated.go` we make sure that we do not add redundant bits (see `attestations/kv/seen_bits.go`). However, while our method is good enough to make sure that non-overlapping attestations all have some unseen bits present, **after** the aggregation situation can change (so, we still need to make sure we deduplicate before proposing). 

Here is a sample case:
- Suppose we have the following two atts in database:
```
1001.0001
1100.0000
```

So, seen bits are: `1101.0001`. 

Now, another aggregate comes in: `0100.0010`. It will not be marked as seen as it introduces new info at 0000.00**X**0 position. So, pool will be updated to:
```
1001.0001
1100.0000
0100.0010
```

On aggregation, it will become:
```
1101.0011 (1001.0001 + 0100.0010)
1100.0000
```

And, clearly, `1100.0000` is redundant as it is a proper subset of the first aggregate, thus needs to be deduplicated.

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Validators running a lot of keys are running into deadlines due to lock contention when we update validator slashing protections. title: Check for Signing Root Mismatch When Submitting Proposals and Importing Proposals in Slashing Interchange
body:
Part of #7813, this PR makes sure we check the following when importing proposals via slashing interchange:

Given signing roots are optional in the EIP standard, we behave as follows:

  For a given block:
    If we have a previous block with the same slot in our history:
      If signing root is empty, we consider that proposer public key as slashable
      If signing root is not empty , then we compare signing roots. If they are different,
      then we consider that proposer public key as slashable.

title: Simpler and Safer Attester Slashing Protection
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Our current slashing protection for attesters suffers from significant lock contention and is not thread-safe as cache invalidation happens at the same time as some data might be accessed from the map itself. We have written up a design doc on what the problem is here: https://hackmd.io/1A2Pb4ZaTuGq2jiNyX3HIw as well as a proposed solution. We decided the best path forward given the time constraint is to have better separation of concerns for saving and retrieving attester history data. We believe this logic should live at the database layer. With this approach, attester protection will work as follows:

### Separation of Concerns: Move the Caching Logic to the DB

In the validator/client package
1. A new slot arrives based on the ticker
2. Fetch duties at that slot (no-op if start of epoch or duties exist)
3. Launch N goroutines for the N assigned duties that you have at that slot
	- 100 attesters, 1 proposer, 30 aggregators
4. During each call to SubmitAttestation(pubKey [48]byte)
	- lock by public key using mputil.NewMultilock()
	- get attestation data from the beacon node
	- fetch the attester history from the DB for that public key
	- check if att is slashable, return err if so
	- we update the history in the DB
	- sign the attestation
	- submit to the beacon node

In the validator/db/kv package
1. In DB NewKVStore() fill a cache of attesting histories by all our public keys we have in our database
3. AttestingHistoryForPubkey()
	- Look into the cache if we have a history then return it
	- If we have a miss, then we look up from the DB and save to cache
4. SaveAttestingHistoryForPubkey()
	- Saves to the cache and the DB

#### Caveats

We will now be using 2Gb of memory for 1000 validating keys in the validator client. Only a few people will be affected by this on mainnet and in Pyrmont. It is a fair tradeoff to make while we work on optimizing slasher.

## Notes

The db cache for attesting history can be disabled with the validator feature flag:

```
--disable-attesting-history-db-cache
```

which we can use to observe just how bad the behavior is without the cache at runtime in the Pyrmont testnet.

title: Properly Handle Duplicate Public Key Entries in Slashing Interchange Imports
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The EIP standard for EIP-3076 slashing interchange requires us to properly handle entries in the JSON with duplicate public keys, such as:

```
"0x2932232930: {
  SignedBlocks: [Slot: 5, Slot: 6, Slot: 7],
},
"0x2932232930: {
  SignedBlocks: [Slot: 5, Slot: 10, Slot: 11],
},
```
Even if the data in them is the same, we should still process all those entries and not deduplicate. The current approach deduplicates, potentially missing slashable data.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #7813

title: Fix issue with roaming data dir on Wins
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Updated default paths to use local paths, not paths that can be shared (both for performance and security reasons)
- Updated executables:
  - [x] beacon-chain (`AppData\Roaming\Eth2 -> AppData\Local\Eth2` by default, if previously installed, files are copied)
  - [x] validator (`AppData\Roaming\Eth2Validators -> AppData\Local\Eth2Validators`, if previously installed, files are copied)
  - [x] slasher (relies on the very same data directory function, so uses updated default path).


**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #5660

**Other notes for review**
- All use cases have been tested on Wins10 machine (I've also stress-tested the thing to work with large, up to 1GB, files).

- Works as the following:
  1. Checks if shared data dir is found (e.g. `C:\Users\username\AppData\Roaming\Eth2`)
  1. If it is, checks if new default data dir is empty
  1. If both conditions are true, all files from the previous directory are copied to the new directory. User sees the following message
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/102257740-2d821280-3f1e-11eb-9e39-1cc70474e159.png)

  1. Once copied, directories' checksum hash is calculated, and if equal, users are asked whether they are ok with removal of the outdated directory. If checksums don't match, nothing is deleted, user is warned (this shouldn't happen -- as I check for errors in copy function quite aggressively, so if that function completes successfully, there's little room for error left).
- ~~**Nothing is deleted automatically**, we copy over the files into a better location (or into a custom location provided by user), and then present user with nagging screen on each next invocation:~~ After discussing with the team (concerns raised by Nishant), we've decided that we will indeed remove original/outdated data directory (making sure that checksums of outdated and copied directories match each other i.e. we're confident that copy of files was integral). However, in case that there exists an outdated directory, but the new directory is not empty (say user used default dir before, but specifies directory via `--datadir` now), then the message below will be displayed (asking user either remove the current directory, so we can automatically move outdated directory, or remove the outdated directory manually):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/102257841-4e4a6800-3f1e-11eb-9163-aa015eb67b57.png)

title: Implement Migration for Unattested Epochs in Attesting History Database
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

When we mark epochs as attested for in the validator's attesting history, and we have a gap in epochs, for example:

1. Attest to epoch 1 with signing root 0x01
2. Attest to epoch 5 with signing root 0x05

Then, every single epoch in between is just empty, 0 padded data. This makes it hard to differentiate whether a validator actually attested source epoch 0 and signing root 0x0 or if it is simply unattested for.

To resolve this, we verified there were no attestations with source 0 and signing root 0x0 in mainnet, then we implement a migration logic that marks all those unattested epochs as FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH in this PR.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #7813

title: Add mutex to params/config
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- When testing #8158 the following error was reported:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/102713657-dfcd2780-42da-11eb-9dd8-467a8428595e.png)


That's there's a race of updating and accessing main beacon config. This PR adds a lock to protect access to the config object.

**Implementation details**
- Build tag is used to conditionally build lock support. In order to enable lock protection, one needs to build with `-tags develop`.
- If no extra tags are provided, `shared/params` tests will fail with the following fatal:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/103513150-12e6ed80-4e7b-11eb-9edb-45b697c6ad22.png)
- The `test` build tag is required by `bazel test //shared/params` tests too:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/103513282-593c4c80-4e7b-11eb-9d65-1fd68e57ecbe.png)
- Currently, only `shared/params` require that build tag, this is enforced by `shared/params/checktags_test.go` (copy that file into any package that required that extra flag):
```golang
// +build !develop

package params

import (
	log "github.com/sirupsen/logrus"
)

func init() {
	log.Fatal("Tests in this package require extra build tag: re-run with `-tags develop`")
}
```
- Original beacon config functions have been copied into two files: `config_utils_prod.go` and `config_utils_develop.go`. The former has `+ build !develop` set and the latter `+ build develop` i.e. the `config_utils_prod.go` is used by default when no tags are specified -- it is the original implementation, w/o locks; and when `-tags develop` is passed then lock-enabled `config_utils_develop.go` is used.

**Other notes for review**
- Regression test added, to run `go test ./shared/params -v -race -run TestConfig_DataRace -tags develop`
- This PR only introduces the build tag based beacon chain config functionality + tests to confirm it is working. In order to enable it in other packages (we hardly need to enable everywhere, just when it fails), we need the following:
  - add `checktags_test.go` file to ensure tags are enabled
  - add `race = "on"` (or include into race-enabled tests) and `gotags = ["develop"]` into `go_test()` part of `BUILD.bazel` file

**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This fixes a bug where a validator always waits for 4 seconds before submitting any attestation, regardless of whether the validator receive the block before this mark. As outlined in the spec:

>A validator should create and broadcast the attestation to the associated attestation subnet when either (a) the validator has received a valid block from the expected block proposer for the assigned slot or (b) one-third of the slot has transpired (SECONDS_PER_SLOT / 3 seconds after the start of slot) -- whichever comes first.

Currently prysm validator does (b) and doesn't do (a). Not allowing (a) could cause attester to miss attestation inclusion in block and lose profitability. 

This PR fixes it by moving wait for 1/3 or wait for current slot block to beacon node.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #8185

This change touches critical code path, we will require more eyes on this and more soak time on pyrmont. I tested with my own validators on Pyrmont and Potuz also tested with his.

title: Optimal Local Slashing Protection DB Schema
body:
Fixes #8066

**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

First of two PRs. The second PR will run a database migration to actually utilize this new schema in validator client code.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Local slashing protection has been a really big problem for performance on Pyrmont, and as mainnet approaches Pyrmont levels, we need to have a much better schema for validator local slashing protection. At the time of writing, we use an extremely suboptimal approach. For every public key, we store in the database a slice of 54,000 (signing root, source epoch, target epoch) triples every single slot for every single attestation we produce. We also read this data from disk to check for slashing protection. All of this can be resolved by instead having a smarter schema that we can check against and save smaller blobs of data every slot to support large numbers of validators.

Upon creating a new attestation, we need to check if it is slashable before submitting it to a beacon node. That is, for an attestation `A` we want to check that no other attestation `B` exists with:

`B.source_epoch < A.source_epoch and B.target_epoch > A.target_epoch`

and

`B.source_epoch > A.source_epoch and B.target_epoch < A.target_epoch`

The boltDB docs [mention](https://github.com/boltdb/bolt#iterating-over-keys) the following

> Iterating over keys

> Bolt stores its keys in byte-sorted order within a bucket. This makes sequential iteration over these keys extremely fast. To iterate over keys we'll use a Cursor:

```go
db.View(func(tx *bolt.Tx) error {
	// Assume bucket exists and has keys
	b := tx.Bucket([]byte("MyBucket"))

	c := b.Cursor()

	for k, v := c.First(); k != nil; k, v = c.Next() {
		fmt.Printf("key=%s, value=%s\n", k, v)
	}

	return nil
})
```

The key phrase here is “Bolt stores its keys in byte-sorted order”, meaning we can leverage quick scans over buckets. A simple approach is to have a bucket of public keys and each public key has a sub-bucket where the (key, value) pairs are source_epoch, target_epoch. Then, for an incoming attestation with source epoch X, we can scan through this subbucket where keys are all source epochs and check for surround and surrounding votes. The complexity of this would be O(k*n) where k is the number of validating public keys in the validator client and n is the number of source epochs each key has attested for. This all depends on the speed of iterating through this subbucket of source epochs in boltDB. If this is extremely fast, with a max number of keys of WEAK_SUBJECTIVITY_PERIOD (54,000), then it could be a decent approach for us. Moreover, if each validating key is attesting in its own goroutine, the `k` factor in this time complexity is not relevant. 

To prove the effectiveness of the approach, here is a timed approach towards checking surround votes:

**Embedded KV Store: BoltDB**

Using a ForEach leveraging bolt DB's byte ordered keys, we get

```
=== RUN   TestKVStore_CheckSurroundVote
Checking surround vote with (source 27000, target 54000), took 1.891648ms
Checking surround vote with (source 0, target 54000), took 7.321µs
Checking surround vote with (source 53997, target 54000), took 2.222819ms
Checking safe vote with (source 54000, target 54001), took 1.229145ms
```

**SQLite Relational DB**

Using the following query
```
select source_epoch, target_epoch
from attestations
where source_epoch < ? and target_epoch > ?
order by target_epoch DESC
```
We get
```
=== RUN   TestSQLite_CheckSurroundVote
Checking surround vote with (source 27000, target 54000), took 4.933052ms
Checking surround vote with (source 0, target 54000), took 7.618146ms
Checking surround vote with (source 53997, target 54000), took 2.007821ms
Checking safe vote with (source 54000, target 54001), took 2.000708ms
```

Our approach ends up being better than SQLite even in the **worst case scenario**.

title: Start from last valid root in loadStateBySlot
body:
This PR simplifies and optimizes `loadStateBySlot`. This function is called by the API call `eth/v1alpha1/validators/balances` for example that it's being used by explorers. 

The current behavior is
1. Grab the latest saved state
2. Grab the last valid block up until the requested slot. 
3. Replay all blocks from the latest saved state.
 
The problem is that in order to replay the blocks, what is actually done is first get the parent root of the first block to replay and call `loadStateByRoot` to get a starting state. This is needed since the list of blocks that we may be getting may start from a block that is not a direct child of the last save state. 

Since a call to `loadStateByRoot` is made anyway and this call itself will replay blocks from a saved state to get the state. What this PR does is call directly `loadStateByRoot` from the last valid block before the requested slot. Since we are guaranteed to not have any blocks between the last valid block and the requested slot, we can just process the slots to get the requested state.

title: Batch Attestation Records and Flush All at Once in Validator DB
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Part of #8242, the new attester protection methods have a serious flaw when running many validating keys, as all of them will attempt to acquire the boltDB write lock and lead to significant contention. Instead of every single attestation being its own boltDB transaction, we do the following:

When a validator attempts to save an attestation record to the DB:
1. We send the attestation over a channel and also subscribe to a feed that will notify us when the saving is complete. Block until we are notified.
2. We run a routine in the background which batches these channel receives into a slice
3. If a certain amount of time passes or if the max capacity of the slice is reached, **whichever comes first**, we save the batched attestations in a single bolt transaction
4. Once flushing completes, we notify all listeners to unblock them

This approach preserves **atomicity**, as saving will be required before the validator proceeds with submitting the attestation to the beacon node. It is simply a layer of abstraction that improves efficiency.

### Parameter discussion

There are two important parameters in this PR we should discuss that affect the effectiveness of these changes.

```go
const (
	ATTESTATION_BATCH_WRITE_INTERVAL = time.Millisecond * 100
	ATTESTATION_BATCH_CAPACITY       = 2048
)
```
The first parameter, `ATTESTATION_BATCH_WRITE_INTERVAL` corresponds to how often we will force flush attestation records to the validator DB. This means that every 100 milliseconds, we will always try to save batched attestations `if len(atts) > 0`. 

The second parameter, `ATTESTATION_BATCH_CAPACITY` describes how many attestations are held in a slice in memory before they are force flushed to the DB. If we hit this capacity, we will always attempt to force flush. 2048 is selected as a default because that's as high a number of keys we can imagine a single validator client will run on mainnet.

Given an attestation record is represented as:

```go
type attestationRecord struct {
  target uint64
  source uint64
  signingRoot [32]byte
  pubKey [48]byte
}
```
storing max 2048 x 96 bytes in memory before flushing totals to around 196kb, which is negligible.

`ATTESTATION_BATCH_CAPACITY` roughly corresponds to the max number of validating keys we expect a validator client to be running at the same time. If we are running more than this capacity, any leftover attestations will have to enter the next batch and be saved at the next `ATTESTATION_BATCH_WRITE_INTERVAL`. The `ATTESTATION_BATCH_WRITE_INTERVAL` corresponds to an acceptable interval at which we can process batches. 100ms is short enough that the flushing will feel like a simple, synchronous update instead.

The aim of this PR is to unify the way we use loggers in beaconchain/validator/slasher. Every package-level logger will be declared in a `log.go` file dedicated for each package and each log will always include a package-level `prefix` field.

title: Introduce base structure for services
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

At the moment all services contain a context `ctx` and a cancellation function `cancel`, as well as some "standard" code to instantiate these values and cancel the context in the `Stop` function. The reason why I wrote "standard" in parenthesis is because different services use different approaches, leading to inconsistent code for the exact same functionality.

Examples:

```
if s.cancel != nil {
    s.cancel()
}
```
```
defer s.cancel()
```
```
if s.cancel != nil {
    defer s.cancel()
}
```

Moreover, it's easy for an `s.cancel()` piece of code to go unnoticed during a code review, and calling `s.cancel()` manually is always a mistake. `Stop()` should be invoked instead because it may contain necessary cleanup code.

This PR introduces a `ServiceBase` struct which should be nested inside each service. It handles the boilerplate work of context cancelling, so that service implementers only need to invoke `s.base.Stop()` at the beginning of the service's `Stop()` function to make sure they handle cancelling correctly. It also does not allow to cancel the context directly from external code, making it necessary to invoke `Stop()` instead. Another benefit of this approach is that it will be easy to extend services in the future if we want to ensure consistent and common behavior - just place the relevant code in `ServiceBase`.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

title: Implement Migration Up/Down Logic for Validator DB
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

When performing minor semver version bumps (v1.0.5 to v1.1.0), we typically have important database migrations and need to ensure users have data integrity when upgrading or downgrading their Prysm version. It is important if they have a problem with v1.1.0 to be able to migrate safely back down to v1.0.5. This PR adds the following commands to the validator client:

```
validator db migrate up --datadir=/path/to/validatordb
validator db migrate down --datadir=/path/to/validatordb
```
When downgrading, users should run the down migrations before running the previous Prysm versions. Specifically, this PR adds down migrations for attester slashing protection.

```
Took 16.326195918s to run down migration for 10,200 epochs and 2048 validator keys
```

title: Require Web UI Password Only for POST Requests or Sensitive Information
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Passwords for our web UI today lead to a poor user experience, as they are always needed when reloading the page. Instead, we should require a password when the user is performing a sensitive action such as importing keystores or creating a wallet, and then not require them for read-only data. All the data in the web UI is accessible in block explorers and is not sensitive.

The auth flow remains similar, except that token expirations are reduced to a minute. When users are performing a sensitive action, they will login via a pop-up in the web UI to receive a JWT token, then their post request will include the bearer token in its http headers. The token will then be thrown away by the web UI.

Part of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm-web-ui/issues/137

4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Minor improvement

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Use strings builder to construct lock key for attesting. It is more performant than casting. It's about 70% faster and 10% less bytes per allocation. 

```go
BenchmarkTwoInputs-12    	 2901903	       397 ns/op	     432 B/op	       7 allocs/op
BenchmarkOneInputWithConcat-12    	 3710899	       316 ns/op	     448 B/op	       7 allocs/op
BenchmarkOneInputWithStringBuilder-12    	 4719397	       245 ns/op	     408 B/op	       7 allocs/op


func BenchmarkTwoInputs(b *testing.B) {
	pubKey := [48]byte{'a'}
	b.ReportAllocs()
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		mputil.NewMultilock(fmt.Sprint(roleAttester), string(pubKey[:]))
	}
}

func BenchmarkOneInputWithConcat(b *testing.B) {
	pubKey := [48]byte{'a'}
	b.ReportAllocs()
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		mputil.NewMultilock(fmt.Sprint(roleAttester) + string(pubKey[:]))
	}
}

func BenchmarkOneInputWithStringBuilder(b *testing.B) {
	pubKey := [48]byte{'a'}
	b.ReportAllocs()
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		var b strings.Builder
		b.WriteByte(byte(roleAttester))
		b.Write(pubKey[:])
		mputil.NewMultilock(b.String())
	}
}
```

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

Leaving proposing side untouched because it's less relevant

title: Configurable testutil's BeaconState
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Testing

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Using `NewBeaconState` from `shared/testutil` is very unwelcoming when one wants to work with a state with non-default values. This is because each call to `NewBeaconState` initializes a new state from package-level "seed" data. Changing the seed data inside one test breaks other tests. This is bad as tests are not isolated from each other. 

This PR decouples tests by creating new seed data every time `NewBeaconState` is called. The function allows passing one or more options which modify the desired state.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #7510. This PR is a prerequisite for some API unit tests.

**Other notes for review**

Main file to look at: `shared/testutil/state.go`. The `...options` argument idea comes from https://dave.cheney.net/2014/10/17/functional-options-for-friendly-apis. The main benefit is not having to declare a big config object and pass `nil` values everywhere where the default is sufficient (meaning everywhere at this point).

Example usage:

```
st, err := NewBeaconState(func(state *pb.BeaconState) {
    state.Slot = 1234
})
```

title: Detection Algorithm for Optimized Slasher
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Now that we have all the required parts of slashing detection using the optimized approach from #8331, we need to glue it together into a cohesive algorithm to detect surrounding and surround votes. This PR begins the detection process, with an algorithm that looks like this when given a batch of attestations

1. Group the attestations by chunk index.
2. Update the min and max spans for those grouped attestations, check if any slashings are found in the process
3. Update the latest written epoch for all validators involved to the current epoch.

The algorithm for updating min and max spans is as follows:

1. Determine the chunks we need to use for updating for the validator indices in a validator chunk index, then retrieve those chunks from the database.
2. Using the chunks from step (1):

```
     for every attestation by chunk index:
        for each validator in the attestation's attesting indices:
          check if the attestation is slashable, if so return a slashing object.
```

3. Save the updated chunks to disk.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331

**What type of PR is this?**

> Clean up

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Update proposer cache took two arguments:
```go
UpdateProposerIndicesInCache(state *stateTrie.BeaconState, epoch types.Epoch)
```

One argument would have been better to avoid fragmentation: 
```go
UpdateProposerIndicesInCache(state *stateTrie.BeaconState)
```

With this change:
* The `epoch` (i.e. `helpers.CurrentEpoch(state)`)  should have been derived from the state instead of allowing caller to dictate.  
* `postState` should also be advancing one slot to `UpdateProposerIndicesInCache` since it is one slot behind

title: Ensure Default Wallet Password Permissions Are Consistent
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Summarizing the issue found by a contributor:

> If Prysm is started with --web and --write-wallet-password-on-web-onboarding it will store the wallet password in ~/.eth2validators/prysm-wallet-v2/walletpassword.txt after onboarding is completed, and this is later used to unlock the wallet when starting Prysm with the --web flag. File permissions are set correctly at file creation (0600), but Prysm will continue to start in the event that permissions are later adjusted to be readable by any user on the server.
Starting Prysm with --wallet-password-file and pointing to a wallet password file with incorrect file permissions also allows Prysm to start.
Given that this file contains sensitive data (cleartext version of the wallet password) it is advised to not allow Prysm to start if the file permissions are incorrectly set, similar to how SSH deals with private keys.

title: Detect Slashable Surround Votes in Optimized Slasher
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Part of #8331, this PR implements the full surround vote detection algorithm and min/max span chunk updates according to our design document [here](https://hackmd.io/rGRGUicASqiei73xopAwsQ). The algorithm lives in a key function named `applyAttestationForValidator`. It works as follows:

1. Given an attestation and a validator index, retrieve the chunk the attestation's source epoch corresponds to
2. Check if the attestation is slashable based on the chunk from (1). If so, then return a slashing, otherwise, continue
3.  Get the start epoch of the chunk we need to update
4. Update the chunk, determine if we need to continue updating another chunk (in case the epochs we need to keep updating live in a different chunk)
    - If we need to continue, then fetch the start epoch of the next chunk, restart (4)
    - If we are done updating, return

**This PR allows us to write real integration tests that pass in a series of attestations into a black box slasher and expect that it is able to detect surround offenses by itself!** These tests are included in the PR.

title: Stop Early in Validator Surround Vote Local Protection
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Refactor

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

After much discussion trying to understand why validators underperform on Pyrmont on startup when having 2000+ keys per validator client, we spent a long time looking at bolt DB internals, especially around db write lock times and the rate of seconds per write and read. Overall, we noticed a huge inefficiency in performing reads when checking if an attestation is slashable. Namely, the algorithm would loop over every single source epoch, target epoch pair a validator has attested to in the past and cross check it with an incoming attestation. With some of these buckets in our database having over 7000 key, value pairs, this check becomes untenable, and pushes bolt to perform very inefficient operations to accommodate it, also leading to significant db lock contention.

Thanks to @prestonvanloon, he came up with the idea of keeping two buckets with the following schema:
`source_epoch => [target_epoch]`
and 
`target_epoch => [source_epoch]`

Given these buckets are guaranteed to have ordered values, we can instead check for surrounded votes by iterating from the back of the bucket since we are looking for target_epoch > att.target_epoch, and stopping early if an existing target epoch <= the incoming attestation's target epoch. We can do a similar "stop early" approach for checking surrounding votes. This guarantees we can stop expensive computation early and in most cases, we will if the network is performing under normal conditions.

This PR adds a migration with up and down logic to add a new bucket called `attestationTargetEpochsBucket` and adds unit tests.

title: Add Slasher Simulator for Profiling, Benchmarking, and Testing
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Our new, optimized slasher implementation is cool but we need to have confidence in its performance at scale. Namely, we want to measure CPU/RAM, disk I/O, blocking, lock contention, and all other cool things that tools such as Go's pprof give us. We also want to identify any low-hanging fruit in terms of bottlenecks and see if slasher can still successfully detect offenses at scale. We also want to measure database growth. Having a simulator that is configurable enough to allow for different scenarios would be a useful tool in our arsenal before the new slasher ever makes it into production. Eventually, this can become part of e2e, but for simplicity, we are writing it as its own tool for now.

**Notes**

A few parts of the logic of slasher were needed to make this happen. Namely:
- Detection happens per slot, as intended (previously doing per epoch was a mistake)
- We hash tree root block headers and attestation data when receiving them to use their signing roots

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331

title: Better Handling of Subscriber Errors in Logs Streams
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.

3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to
   be updated. If you're unsure what to update, send the PR, and we'll discuss
   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Thanks to @nisdas, after doing some investigation of why the beacon node gets into a deadlock when running the web ui, he was able to identify the following offender:

```
#    0x14d760f    reflect.rselect+0x38f                                        GOROOT/src/runtime/select.go:566
#    0x151773b    reflect.Select+0x19b                                        GOROOT/src/reflect/value.go:2260
#    0x1f2ca44    github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/shared/event.(*Feed).Send+0x5a4                    shared/event/feed.go:170
#    0x24caab2    github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/shared/logutil.(*StreamServer).Write+0x72            shared/logutil/stream.go:69
#    0x152ad66    io.(*multiWriter).Write+0x86
```

Essentially, the subscriber to the event feed where beacon node logs are being sent to is blocked and does not get unblocked at all.

```go
func (ns *Server) StreamBeaconLogs(_ *ptypes.Empty, stream pb.Health_StreamBeaconLogsServer) error {
    ch := make(chan []byte, ns.StreamLogsBufferSize)
    defer close(ch)
    sub := ns.LogsStreamer.LogsFeed().Subscribe(ch)
    defer sub.Unsubscribe()
```

We believe the buffer size is too small, and also, we should not be defer closing a buffered channel this way in a grpc call. Additionally, we were **not handling** a select case for subscriber errors. If there was ever an error in the subscription, we would never exit the function and likely that's where the beacon node logs were getting stuck without our awareness.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #8430

title: Add In ValidateKeystores Validator Endpoint
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently, the validator web UI onboarding takes users through a series of steps in which they upload keystore files, set a wallet password, and a web UI password, and at the end creates a wallet. If some step along the way fails, the user does not receive appropriate feedback in the form of errors, and even worse, a wallet ends up being created. Instead, we separate the concept of keystore password validation and wallet creation.

In this PR, we introduce an api endpoint called ValidateKeystores which takes in a series of JSON keystores and a password and returns no error if all of them decrypt correctly. This will allow the web onboarding to give early feedback to a user in case their keystore passwords are incorrect and they need to amend it before creating a wallet. Additionally, this will ensure that when a wallet is indeed created during the onboarding, that there will be no errors decrypting keystores and the operation should be as atomic as possible.

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.

3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to
   be updated. If you're unsure what to update, send the PR, and we'll discuss
   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently, slasher chunks for min/max spans in the optimized slasher implementation track only 16 epochs at a time. Our code works fine until we get an attestation that spans multple chunks, in which we get an issue of "chunk not found", and then slasher failing to work as expected for its entire duration.

The issue can be reproduced by creating an attestation with source 15 and target 16. This attestation lives in 2 different chunk indices, and our current approach could not handle this. As a solution, we fallback to the DB to retrieve a chunk if we get an attestation across chunk boundaries for ease of access.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331 

**Other notes for review**

It seems that some slasher tests were also flakey, because we should be using mutexes in the lock as the tests directly deal with concurrency. This allowed the tests to always pass. Specifically, some tests had `processAttestations()` running in the background, but modifying the queue without acquiring the lock in another goroutine.

title: Fix validator activation monitoring with inactive keys
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

When starting a Prysm validator, the client would monitor the beacon chain for activations of its public keys. If none of the keys are active, it will continue to monitor until one of the keys has been activated. One of the features of the validator is that the key manager is monitoring for new key additions. **What type of PR is this?**

> Refactor

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently
```go
ProcessAttestationNoVerifySignature {
// Verify attestation slot, epoch... etc
// Modify beacon state with attestation
// Verify attestation valid indices
}
```

In Prysm, we use `ProcessAttestationNoVerifySignature` as a pure verification function without the advertised side effect as modifying beacon state.  This PR changes:

```go
VerifyAttestationNoVerifySignature {
// Verify attestation slot, epoch... etc
// Verify attestation valid indices
}

ProcessAttestationNoVerifySignature {
VerifyAttestationNoVerifySignature
// Modify beacon state with attestation
}
```

Note that `Verify attestation valid indices` now comes before `Modify beacon state with attestation`. That is ok and arguably better

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Helps #8563

title: Fix issues with dynamic key reload for imported/derived keymanager
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**High-level overview:**

I added a new case in the runner, where I listen to account changes via a channel. After such changes occur, I handle key reload by logging out statuses and returning if any keys are active. If there are no active keys after the reload, I call `WaitForActivation` passing the channel as a way of reacting to reload inside the function. Note that the call to `WaitForActivation`, which happens before the main loop, does not need an external channel, so it manages its own when `nil` is passed in.

I defined a `validatorStatus` struct abstraction to be able to log out statuses from both `WaitForValidation` and `HandleKeyReload`.

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR adds the ability to defer processing of attestations that will be valid in the future in our optimized slasher implementation. The way it works is:

1. Every epoch, get a set of attestations to process from the queue
2. Filter out the attestations which are valid, invalid, and valid in the future
3. Put the ones valid in the future back into the queue
4. Throw away the invalid ones
5. Process the valid ones

title: Integrate Optimized Slasher Into Beacon Node Runtime, Part 1
body:
Part of #8331, this PR integrates the new slasher code into the beacon node at runtime, able to run it using a --slasher flag. This involves starting a slasher process in the beacon node if the flag is enabled and sending over relevant feeds that slasher will receive data from during block and attestation validation pipelines.

This is the first of three PRs, and this one includes the following changes:

- [x] Forward all attestations in a block to the slasher in the blockchain service's process block routine
- [x] Forward attestations right after nil integrity checking in the sync, p2p validation pipeline to slasher
- [x] Forward block headers right after nil integrity checking in the sync, p2p validation pipeline
- [x] Register and start slasher as a service in the beacon node's node.go file
- [x] Initialize slasher by waiting for a chainstart notification to retrieve the genesis time
- [x] Define a `--slasher` feature flag used by the beacon node
- [x] Fix tests

In the next PR, we will modify our slashings pool to receive any slashings detected by the optimized slasher. In the final PR, we will verify the signatures of detected slashing events in slasher before sending any detected slashings over a feed.

4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.

-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Refactor/clean up

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Move field roots compute functions from `stateutil` pkg to live next to its implementation `state` pkg. As I look closer to revamping state for hard fork 1, one flaw that I saw was field roots compute is implementation dependent with the beacon state itself. (ie. genesis state and hf1 state will have different field root implementation). Given that, we should move all the field roots compute functions to be next to the implementation, rather than having them in a shared pkg (i.e. `stateutil`). 

I thought about using different pkgs within `stateutil` to distinguish but I think that is uglier:
```
state
 -stateV0
 -stateV1
 -stateutil
   - v0
      - field_roots.go
   - v1
      - field_roots.go  
```

I prefer the following:
```
state
 -stateV0
   -field_roots.go
 -stateV1
   -field_roots.go
 -stateutil
```

I also broke it down into granular files for ease of reading:
```
field_roots.go
field_root_attestation.go
field_root_block_header.go
field_root_eth1.go
field_root_validator.go
field_root_vector.go
```

title: Return status.Errorf instead of plain errors from gRPC functions
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

It is not straightforward to reason about types of errors returned by gRPC functions when some code paths return `status.Errorf` and some return plain errors. The latter is correct when helper functions return `status.Errorf`, which is currently the case. It's also easier to make a mistake and use the wrong error type because there is no clear separation of responsibilities.

This PR simplifies things by always returning `status.Errorf` from top-level gRPC functions and plain errors from helper functions.

title: Change early exit error message
body:
Currently when exiting a validator before the required threshold of `SHARD_COMMITTEE_PERIOD` epochs, the message is a bit misleading, eg:

``` 
    WARN accounts: Could not perform voluntary exit for account 0x974dc2826f2d: failed to propose voluntary exit: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = validator has not been active long enough to exit: 187 epochs vs required 384 epochs
```

which can be read as "the validator has been active for 187 epochs and 384 are required. While in fact 187 is the current epoch and 384 is the epoch at which the validator becomes eligible for exit in the above example. In this example the validator was active for only 64 epochs. 

This PR changes the message for 

```
    validator has not been active long enough to exit: 64 of 256 epochs. Validator will be eligible for exit at epoch 384.
```

title: E2E refactoring: ValidatorNode and ValidatorNodes
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other / Refactoring

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Follow up to #8659 (see it for implementation details)
- Adds `ValidatorNode` and `ValidatorNodes` components:
  - When initializing validator nodes we do so either for a single validator of or for validator set. In both cases, we want to make sure we know when the entity is fully started (in case of a single validator, entity will be the validator process itself, and in case of validators set it will be **all** validators). Therefore, `components/validator.go` contains both `ValidatorNode` (which abstracts a single validator process) and `ValidatorNodes` (which is a set of validators, which all should be ready before the component signals its readiness to downstream).
  - Roughtly, `ValidatorNode.Start()` and `ValidatorNodes.Start()` will replace functionality of `StartValidatorClients()` and `StartValidatorClient()` respectively. ❗The only code that is introduced in `ValidatorNode(s).Start()` methods is that dealing with waiting for node start, and using `exec.CommandContext()` instead of `exec.Command()` -- the rest is extracted from `StartValidatorClient()` function.❗ 
  - The `errgroup` package is used in `ValidatorNodes`, to wait up until all contained nodes are started.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
