**What type of PR is this?**
 Feature  [#8664](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/8664)

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
Web UI is being updated to be an alternative to recover wallet CLI.  In doing so, the backend has to handle the recover Wallet request. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of [#8664 ](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/8664) The portion about using the supported bip39 Mnemonic language in recovering their wallet from a mnemonic. 

**Other notes for review**
While that portion of the issue started as adding the Menomic language support the following modifications were done 

1. Recovering from wallet involves using an optional 25th word.  So the request has to accommodate for whether the user wants that or not  ( a flag to skip or not and the paraphrase itself).  The accounts.RecoverWalletConfig  struct used in recovering, either specifies the paraphrase if not to be skipped or keeps it nil. 
2. The rpc CreateWallet was divided into the three types of Wallets  (Imported , Derived or Remote).  The imported stayed part of the rpc.CreateWallet, while the derived is the rpc.RecoverWallet with the added checks and balances(see below) to handle the passed parameters.   
In short, Either you import keystores, or you recover a wallet. (remote are not supported through the web) 
3. Test cases cover :   passing a supported language from the web,  passing a 25th mnemonic(if not to be skipped) , validating the passed password ( the check between a password and its confirm is part of the web frontend), validating the numAccounts(atleast 1) . Once that passes, the RecoverWalletConfig  struct is passed to the legacy accounts.RecoverWallet

title: Space Efficiency in Slasher DB Schema, Add More Metrics
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Slasher currently runs out of disk space very quickly with some low defaults on the Prater testnet, meaning it will have massive disk usage on eth2 mainnet. Slasher stores a ton of data on disk, especially related to attestations. This PR incorporates a few improvements suggested by the Sigma Prime team for their slasher here https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/issues/2286. 

We incorporate the following improvements

* Use 5 bytes to encode the validator index (max validator registry size is 2**40)
* Use 2 bytes to encode the target epoch (store it modulo history_length/4096)
* We perform snappy compression on all attestation related data in the slasher db schema

Additionally, this PR changes the following

* Add metrics for pruning to better understand how slasher prunes information
* Ignore the attestation records database in bolt db metrics as metrics scraping takes way too long for a large DB
* Add a package-level comment to `beacon-chain/slasher`
* Change the slasher parameter historyLength to exported HistoryLength as it can be used across packages

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331

title: Altair: Sync committee helpers
body:
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Add sync committee helpers for Altair:

```python
def get_sync_committee(state: BeaconState, epoch: Epoch) -> SyncCommittee:
    """
    Return the sync committee for a given state and epoch.
    """
    indices = get_sync_committee_indices(state, epoch)
    pubkeys = [state.validators[index].pubkey for index in indices]
    partition = [pubkeys[i:i + SYNC_PUBKEYS_PER_AGGREGATE] for i in range(0, len(pubkeys), SYNC_PUBKEYS_PER_AGGREGATE)]
    pubkey_aggregates = [bls.AggregatePKs(preaggregate) for preaggregate in partition]
    return SyncCommittee(pubkeys=pubkeys, pubkey_aggregates=pubkey_aggregates)

def get_sync_committee_indices(state: BeaconState, epoch: Epoch) -> Sequence[ValidatorIndex]:
    """
    Return the sequence of sync committee indices (which may include duplicate indices) for a given state and epoch.
    """
    MAX_RANDOM_BYTE = 2**8 - 1
    base_epoch = Epoch((max(epoch // EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD, 1) - 1) * EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD)
    active_validator_indices = get_active_validator_indices(state, base_epoch)
    active_validator_count = uint64(len(active_validator_indices))
    seed = get_seed(state, base_epoch, DOMAIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE)
    i = 0
    sync_committee_indices: List[ValidatorIndex] = []
    while len(sync_committee_indices) < SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE:
        shuffled_index = compute_shuffled_index(uint64(i % active_validator_count), active_validator_count, seed)
        candidate_index = active_validator_indices[shuffled_index]
        random_byte = hash(seed + uint_to_bytes(uint64(i // 32)))[i % 32]
        effective_balance = state.validators[candidate_index].effective_balance
        if effective_balance * MAX_RANDOM_BYTE >= MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE * random_byte:  # Sample with replacement
            sync_committee_indices.append(candidate_index)
        i += 1
    return sync_committee_indices
```

https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/beacon-chain.md#get_sync_committee_indices

4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Optimization

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently, our optimized slasher has a not-well-optimized db schema, particularly for attestation records. We have a single bucket called `attestationRecordsBucket` which stores all attestations as follows:

```py
(target_epoch ++ validator_index) => (signing_root ++ compressed_ssz_encode(attestation))
```
The way we save to this bucket is as follows. Say we receive an attestation that looks like this:

```py
{
  AttestingIndices: [0, 1, 2, ..., 500],
  Data: 0xab
}
```

We perform the following routine for a given epoch:

```py
attesting_indices = attestation.attesting_indices
for validator in attesting_indices:
  put(validator++epoch, attestation)
```

This means if an attestation is 300 bytes, for example, we would be storing the same data duplicated 500 times! 150k bytes for this example sans-compression.

Instead, we propose the alternative schema:

**attestation_data_roots_bucket**
```py
(target_epoch ++ validator_index) => (signing_root ++ fastsum64(attestation.attesting_indices))
```

**attestation_records_bucket**
```py
(signing_root ++ fastsum64(attestation.attesting_indices) => compressed_ssz_encoded(attestation)
```
Then, our saving routine becomes:
```py
attesting_indices = attestation.attesting_indices
signing_root = signing_root(attestation)
attestation_records_bucket.put(signing_root++fastsum64(attesting_indices), encode(attestation))
for validator in attesting_indices:
  signing_roots_bucket.put(
    validator++epoch, signing_root++fastsum64(attesting_indices),
  )
```

If an attestation is 300 bytes, this is an 7.5x improvement to the current behavior in terms of disk use.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331

title: Altair: Process sync committee
body:
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Add process sync committee for beacon block for Altair:

```python
def process_sync_committee(state: BeaconState, aggregate: SyncAggregate) -> None:
    # Verify sync committee aggregate signature signing over the previous slot block root
    committee_pubkeys = state.current_sync_committee.pubkeys
    participant_pubkeys = [pubkey for pubkey, bit in zip(committee_pubkeys, aggregate.sync_committee_bits) if bit]
    previous_slot = max(state.slot, Slot(1)) - Slot(1)
    domain = get_domain(state, DOMAIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE, compute_epoch_at_slot(previous_slot))
    signing_root = compute_signing_root(get_block_root_at_slot(state, previous_slot), domain)
    assert eth2_fast_aggregate_verify(participant_pubkeys, signing_root, aggregate.sync_committee_signature)

    # Compute participant and proposer rewards
    total_active_increments = get_total_active_balance(state) // EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT
    total_base_rewards = Gwei(get_base_reward_per_increment(state) * total_active_increments)
    max_participant_rewards = Gwei(total_base_rewards * SYNC_REWARD_WEIGHT // WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR // SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)
    participant_reward = Gwei(max_participant_rewards // SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE)
    proposer_reward = Gwei(participant_reward * PROPOSER_WEIGHT // (WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR - PROPOSER_WEIGHT))

    # Apply participant and proposer rewards
    committee_indices = get_sync_committee_indices(state, get_current_epoch(state))
    participant_indices = [index for index, bit in zip(committee_indices, aggregate.sync_committee_bits) if bit]
    for participant_index in participant_indices:
        increase_balance(state, participant_index, participant_reward)
        increase_balance(state, get_beacon_proposer_index(state), proposer_reward)
```

title: Spec checker tool
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- This tool allows to download specs documentation, parse Python code blocks from it, and then use parsed blocks to compare with documentation pseudo code we are using when implementing specs functions. Otherwise, it is a simple CLI utility relying on AST parsing.
- The delta of this PR is big, due to inclusion of parsed reference specs (see the rationale for this below).
- This PR implements the separate CLI tool (and not the static analyzer), because `go_tool_library` doesn't support `embededsrcs` attribute (which `go_library` does support), and our tool relies on `go:embed`. Once `rules_go` are updated, we can turn this tool into static analyzer, easily.
- Multiple definitions with the same function names are possible (for example you can have `def func_name():` defined for both phase1 and phase0). As long as one of the definitions matches our comments, we consider comments to be up to date.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #5717

**How to update referenced specs?**
```bash
bazel run //tools/specs-checker download -- --dir=$PWD/tools/specs-checker/data
```
This will pull the files defined in `specDirs` (see `main.go`), parse them (extract Python code snippets, discarding any other text), and save them to the folder from which `bazel run //tools/specs-checker check` will be able to embed (using `go:embed`):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/114362104-a36e5180-9b7f-11eb-939c-790a17ccc3bc.png)

Note: see included README for more details.

**How to run tests?**
```bash
bazel run //tools/specs-checker check -- --dir $PWD/beacon-chain
bazel run //tools/specs-checker check -- --dir $PWD/validator
bazel run //tools/specs-checker check -- --dir $PWD/shared
```
Or, to check the whole project:
```bash
bazel run //tools/specs-checker check -- --dir $PWD
```

**How do results of the check look like?**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/188194/114014204-05be0e00-9871-11eb-87a2-77a13d4e37d2.png)

**Why save parsed reference definitions, why not discard them after the check?**
There are several reasons for doing that:
- I found it particularly useful when downloading *updates*, since reference definitions are versioned, on `git diff` I immediately see what files have changed, to better understand the scope of updates I need to do on our comments.
- When used as static analyzer, re-downloading from GitHub on every build attempt is not the best idea, so having those results cached comes handy. I could have implemented more sophisticated caching scheme, where tool will check the update time of the spec files and re-download only if older than a given period, but I consider it as a bit of an overkill for the tool that simple. So, it is up to us to decide how often do we want to pull updated specs from the upstream.
- Finally, it is way easier to debug, as you have all the reference definitions saved within our project. As a side-kick: when updating the comments (if it is out of date), you can just grep the saved reference docs, and do not have to fish through specs repo site in order to find the up to date version of a snippet.

title: Altair: process attestation for block
body:
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Add process attestation for beacon block in Altair:

```python
def process_attestation(state: BeaconState, attestation: Attestation) -> None:
    data = attestation.data
    assert data.target.epoch in (get_previous_epoch(state), get_current_epoch(state))
    assert data.target.epoch == compute_epoch_at_slot(data.slot)
    assert data.slot + MIN_ATTESTATION_INCLUSION_DELAY <= state.slot <= data.slot + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH
    assert data.index < get_committee_count_per_slot(state, data.target.epoch)

    committee = get_beacon_committee(state, data.slot, data.index)
    assert len(attestation.aggregation_bits) == len(committee)

    if data.target.epoch == get_current_epoch(state):
        epoch_participation = state.current_epoch_participation
        justified_checkpoint = state.current_justified_checkpoint
    else:
        epoch_participation = state.previous_epoch_participation
        justified_checkpoint = state.previous_justified_checkpoint

    # Matching roots
    is_matching_head = data.beacon_block_root == get_block_root_at_slot(state, data.slot)
    is_matching_source = data.source == justified_checkpoint
    is_matching_target = data.target.root == get_block_root(state, data.target.epoch)
    assert is_matching_source

    # Verify signature
    assert is_valid_indexed_attestation(state, get_indexed_attestation(state, attestation))

    # Participation flag indices
    participation_flag_indices = []
    if is_matching_head and is_matching_target and state.slot == data.slot + MIN_ATTESTATION_INCLUSION_DELAY:
        participation_flag_indices.append(TIMELY_HEAD_FLAG_INDEX)
    if is_matching_source and state.slot <= data.slot + integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH):
        participation_flag_indices.append(TIMELY_SOURCE_FLAG_INDEX)
    if is_matching_target and state.slot <= data.slot + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH:
        participation_flag_indices.append(TIMELY_TARGET_FLAG_INDEX)

    # Update epoch participation flags
    proposer_reward_numerator = 0
    for index in get_attesting_indices(state, data, attestation.aggregation_bits):
        for flag_index, weight in get_flag_indices_and_weights():
            if flag_index in participation_flag_indices and not has_flag(epoch_participation[index], flag_index):
                epoch_participation[index] = add_flag(epoch_participation[index], flag_index)
                proposer_reward_numerator += get_base_reward(state, index) * weight

    # Reward proposer
    proposer_reward_denominator = (WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR - PROPOSER_WEIGHT) * WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR // PROPOSER_WEIGHT
    proposer_reward = Gwei(proposer_reward_numerator // proposer_reward_denominator)
    increase_balance(state, get_beacon_proposer_index(state), proposer_reward)
```

title: Altair: Slashing for block and epoch
body:
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Add process slashing for block and epoch for Altair:

```python
def process_slashings(state: BeaconState) -> None:
    epoch = get_current_epoch(state)
    total_balance = get_total_active_balance(state)
    adjusted_total_slashing_balance = min(sum(state.slashings) * PROPORTIONAL_SLASHING_MULTIPLIER_ALTAIR, total_balance)
    for index, validator in enumerate(state.validators):
        if validator.slashed and epoch + EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR // 2 == validator.withdrawable_epoch:
            increment = EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT  # Factored out from penalty numerator to avoid uint64 overflow
            penalty_numerator = validator.effective_balance // increment * adjusted_total_slashing_balance
            penalty = penalty_numerator // total_balance * increment
            decrease_balance(state, ValidatorIndex(index), penalty)

def slash_validator(state: BeaconState,
                    slashed_index: ValidatorIndex,
                    whistleblower_index: ValidatorIndex=None) -> None:
    """
    Slash the validator with index ``slashed_index``.
    """
    epoch = get_current_epoch(state)
    initiate_validator_exit(state, slashed_index)
    validator = state.validators[slashed_index]
    validator.slashed = True
    validator.withdrawable_epoch = max(validator.withdrawable_epoch, Epoch(epoch + EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR))
    state.slashings[epoch % EPOCHS_PER_SLASHINGS_VECTOR] += validator.effective_balance
    decrease_balance(state, slashed_index, validator.effective_balance // MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_ALTAIR)

    # Apply proposer and whistleblower rewards
    proposer_index = get_beacon_proposer_index(state)
    if whistleblower_index is None:
        whistleblower_index = proposer_index
    whistleblower_reward = Gwei(validator.effective_balance // WHISTLEBLOWER_REWARD_QUOTIENT)
    proposer_reward = Gwei(whistleblower_reward * PROPOSER_WEIGHT // WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR)
    increase_balance(state, proposer_index, proposer_reward)
    increase_balance(state, whistleblower_index, Gwei(whistleblower_reward - proposer_reward))
```
https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/beacon-chain.md#beacon-state-mutators

title: Batch Pruning for Optimized Slasher
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Our new slasher keeps around 4096 epochs worth of data, and prunes every piece of data that is older than what we need in our current history window. A naive approach was to simply prune all at once as soon as the history limit was reached, which led to our slasher blow up in a cloud environment, as bolt DB had to delete over *37 million records* at once, and bolt DB hates long-running transactions. 

Instead, we opt for an approach where we prune in increments of N epochs, making the procedure easier on the database. To do this, we need a cursor-based approach to pruning to ensure we clear out all required data. The following is the algorithm contained in this PR: 

1. We retrieve the lowest stored slot in the proposals bucket
2. We initialize `epochAtCursor := lowestStoredEpoch`
3. Determine the end pruning epoch as `endPruningEpoch := currentEpoch - historyLength` where historyLength is 4096
4. While `endEpoch-epochAtCursor > 0`, we prune as many epochs as we can in the pruning increments of N, and advance the epoch cursor
5. Each pruning process is a bolt transaction

With `pruningIncrementEpochs` of 100 and `historyLength` of 4096, we have a reasonable improvement over doing it all at once.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331 

**NOTES**

The logic for prune attestations and prune proposals is pretty much the same save for some type differences, which we cannot deduplicate unless we have some heavier abstraction or generics in Go :(

title: Amend DepositNumberAndRootAtHeight Function to Fix Off-By-One
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In summary, there was a serious incident affecting eth2 mainnet this past evening CST, which affected block proposals from Prysm validators throughout an eth1 voting period. This bug was causing Prysm nodes to vote in an incorrect eth1 data due to an off-by-one error through an edge case in the Go standard library.

In summary, we have the following problem:
```go
items := []int{1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5}
```
and we use binary search from the Go standard library `sort` package, `sort.Search`, to find the index of an element `x` such that `items[i] > x`. However, the [official Go docs](https://golang.org/pkg/sort/#Search) for `sort.Search` state the following:

```
func Search(n int, f func(int) bool) int
Search uses binary search to find and return the smallest index i in [0, n) at which f(i) is true, 
assuming that on the range [0, n), f(i) == true implies f(i+1) == true. That is, Search requires that f is
false for some (possibly empty) prefix of the input range [0, n) and then true for the (possibly empty) remainder; 
Search returns the first true index. If there is no such index, Search returns n. 
(Note that the "not found" return value is not -1 as in, for instance, strings.Index.)
Search calls f(i) only for i in the range [0, n).
```

That is, the function returns the index in `[0, n)`, which means the upper limit is *not-inclusive*. If we wanted to return 5 (because total number of deposits start counting at 1) for searching for 5, we would *not* receive the expected value using the stdlib.

This led to an issue in determining the number of deposits at a given block height if said edge-case condition was met.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #8298

While #8809 could be an improvement, especially if this list is long and the found elements are typically at the very end of the list, we do not have the supporting benchmarks or data to support the changes at this time. 

Given the sensitivity of the incident, I am proposing we revert the changes introduced in #8809 for now.

body:
# Build Debian packages 📦

**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This pull request is to add new Bazel build targets for creating Debian .deb packages for the beacon-chain and validator binaries.
Along with the executable, these packages also include a basic YAML config file, and a hardened systemd unit file.

Adding these build targets to the CI pipeline will allow Prysm to offer pre-built packages for download from the website for users who would prefer to use a more traditional package-based approach, rather than the bespoke `prysm.sh` script.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

This PR does not completely address #8092, but it is a first step towards maintaining a PPA. 
Managing the PPA (including for package upload from CI) will require a Prysm community account, as well as keys for signing the packages.

**Other notes for review**

1. Systemd unit files for the validator and beacon-chain have been hardened with various security options. Some of these options may interfere with certain configurations, and while testing has been performed, it has not been exhaustive.
These settings should be reviewed from a security standpoint, but also from a usability one.
1. Default configuration options to be deployed with the packaged YAML files are also open to suggestion.
1. Documentation of these packages has not been considered yet.

title: HTTP proxy server for Eth2 APIs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

gRPC and HTTP are not best friends. [Eth2 APIs spec](https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/) includes several particularities that cannot be currently achieved with gRPC, even with the help of grpc-gateway. These are:
- sending hex values to gRPC functions expecting byte arrays
- returning errors with fields other than `message` and `code`
- returning lowercase enum values
- returning timestamps as UNIX time
- sending hex values to URL parameters
- sending an array as the top-level JSON value (an array is a valid JSON) when submitting attestations
- sending less than 32 bytes to the graffiti field, which is tagged `ssz:"size=32"`

This PR implements a gorilla-mux HTTP server that acts as middleware between the client and the grpc-gateway server. It handles all the above issues by intercepting the client request, processing it as required to make gRPC happy and forwarding it to grpc-gateway. It does the same on the way back: intercept the response from grpc-gateway, process it to comply to Eth2 API spec and forward it to the client. The proxy server achieves all of this by making extensive use of structs defined in `middleware_structs.go`, which are mostly representations of proto structs, annotated specifically for the proxy server and its field processing functions.  

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of overall API work

Tests will come in another PR. This PR is big enough as it is. What's more, we should review this asap.

title: Use Pruning Sliding Window for Slasher
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Our new slasher in #8340 has serious performance issues when performing database pruning. For the purposes of slashing, we only care about data from the last N epochs where N is a safe weak subjectivity period, such as 4096 epochs. We should be pruning old data every slot to avoid accumulation of unnecessary info. Our current pruning algorithm has a serious bug in that it does as follows:

1. Run for 4096 epochs
2. Upon hitting epoch 4097, prune _everything_ before it

This is very dangerous and incorrect as a solution. Instead, we should be using a _sliding window_ between [current_epoch-HISTORY_LENGTH, current_epoch]. For example:

With `HISTORY_LENGTH = 4`, if we have epochs `0, 1, 2, 3` and we then reach epoch `4`, we should update the sliding window to `1, 2, 3, 4` and delete everything in epoch 0. This will drastically reduce the impact of pruning and retain correct logic.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331

title: Duplicate val detection
body:
New Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
The PR follows this [design](https://hackmd.io/KXlyLQxiRzK9sIBwLu1UNA)  The summary of which is as follows

1. A new flag -- enable-duplicate-validator-detection is introduced. If present the validator will run duplicate(doppelganger) detection check.
2. A new (N=2) DuplicateValidatorEpochsCheck variable is introduced in config in mainnet, minimal and test_e2e configs. Currently set to 2 in prod and 1 in test. 
3. The duplication logic is called if the above flag is set and is part of the validator runner class.  The logic gets called after all the following: wallet initialization, slasher protection setup , waiting for beacon chain connection and synch and getting the canonical head. 
4. A new file duplicate_detection.go is added with the utility functions to retrieve the validator's keys and iterate through the signed blocks looking for a duplicate. 
5. The logic loops through N epochs worth of slots examining each previous slot along the way. Once a duplicate is found with the same Keys which either proposed or attested in a signed block the func signals an event into a channel which is received at a goroutine process part of the node class. 
6. If no duplicate is found, the goroutine shuts down, if a duplicate is found then the node is shutdown similar to an os.signal interrupt message. 

The core logic loops through each signed block to see if the proposer's key matches the current validator's. It then goes through the attestations within that block , retrieving the attesting indices from the attestations bits and committee, to find a matching key to current validator. 

**Testing** 
The unit testing is done cosmetically and has to be revisited. One needs to: 

- [ ] create a mock beacon chain with signed blocks for at least N epochs. 
- [ ] create testing conditions for  a duplicate attestation to be caught. So far using interop all duplicates caught were a proposer doppelganger. 
- [ ] considering the brute force search approach one has to benchmark the detection process  for different number of validator keys (e.g 100, 2000, 4000) to ensure enterprise-level performance. 

The following testing was done using interop

1. bazel run //tools/genesis-state-gen -- --num-validators=4000 --output-ssz=/tmp/genesis.ssz --mainnet-config
2. bazel run //beacon-chain -- --datadir /tmp/chaindata --force-clear-db --interop-genesis-state /tmp/genesis.ssz --interop-eth1data-votes --min-sync-peers=0 --http-web3provider=https://eth-goerli.alchemyapi.io/v2/tXXYYYY --deposit-contract 0x8A04d14125D0FDCDc742F4A05C051De07232EDa4 --pyrmont --bootstrap-node=

Then in two separate terminals you will have one validator running a key in the default folder .eth2validators and another validator whose wallet in a copied folder. 

3. bazel run //validator -- --beacon-rpc-provider localhost:4000 --interop-num-validators=4000 --interop-start-index=0 --force-clear-db  --enable-duplicate-validator-detection
This validator will loop for 6.4 seconds ( N=2 epochs ) before it continues normal execution. 
4. bazel run //validator -- --beacon-rpc-provider localhost:4000 --interop-num-validators=4000 --interop-start-index=0 --force-clear-db  --verbosity trace  --wallet-dir "/home/ahaddad/.dupeth2val/prysm-wallet-v2" --enable-duplicate-validator-detection
  This second validator will exit with a proposer error. 

> [2021-05-25 09:13:27]  INFO validator: Doppelganger service - found a proposer duplicate
[2021-05-25 09:13:27]  INFO validator: Doppelganger detected! Validator key 0xaab9137830a261e07261ebd46c8d8c53ffa532cb3f2de7eacc87966b82f1281c54400835fc09897730fa40e1ce6d90cc seems to be running elsewhere.This process will exit, avoiding a proposer or attester slashing event.Please ensure you are not running your validator in two places simultaneously.
[2021-05-25 09:13:27]  INFO node: Duplicate Detected...Shutting down; Key 0xaab9137830a261e07261ebd46c8d8c53ffa532cb3f2de7eacc87966b82f1281c54400835fc09897730fa40e1ce6d90cc at slot 32
panic: Panic closing the validator client due to duplicate usage
goroutine 90 [running]:
github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/validator/node.(*ValidatorClient).Start.func2(0xc0004fed90)
        validator/node/node.go:179 +0x29a
created by github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/validator/node.(*ValidatorClient).Start
        validator/node/node.go:164 +0x21c

If the `--enable-duplicate-validator-detection` is not used both validators will with out the N epoch check.

title: Add Tool for Git Repository Mirroring via Webhook
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Prysmatic Labs leverages a monorepo architecture for Prysm, however, we have a few external projects that we maintain as separate git repositories. Unfortunately, working with those projects has become really painful given frequent need to update them as dependencies in Prysm, and we estimate many man hours have been spent on dealing with this technical debt. Users of such external repos such as [github.com/prysmaticlabs/ethereumapis](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/ethereumapis) have mentioned they like the separation of repos due to those repos having more permissive licensing than Prysm. Instead, we decided to keep those external repos as _mirrors_ of changes that happen within Prysm, and move those repositories to the Prysm monorepo for all future development.

This PR adds a tool under /tools/gitmirror which creates a small Golang web server listening to Github webhook release events for a set of specified repositories, and is able to mirror directories from Prysm into specified mirror Github repositories. The tool can be configured with a yaml file as follows:

```yaml
cloneBasePath: tmp
repositories:
  - remoteUrl: git@github.com:prysmaticlabs/prysm.git
    remoteName: prysm
    mirrorUrl: git@github.com:prysmaticlabs/ethereumapis.git
    mirrorName: ethereumapis
    mirrorDirectories:
      - proto/eth
```

**NOTES**
Diff is large due to some testdata files that are checked into the repo

title: Process future Blocks and Attestations
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 - Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
- Currently prysm has a very low tolerance for future Blocks and Attestations (500ms). 
- This PR increases this tolerance level to two slots. 
- If a Block arrives for a future slot, it is queued and processed at the right time.
- A similar mechanism is done for Attestations too.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
- Fixes #8606 

**Other notes for review**
For Blocks:
- Allow blocks until two slots in future
- Enqueue the block if the block slot is greater than current slot
- Queue Processing:
   * process blocks that belong to only the current slot
 
For Attestations:
- Allow Attestations to be received to slots in future .
- we need not do anything for processing queued Attestation, because they are processed only if their respective blocks are processed.

title: Enhance attestation signature set checks
body:
Caught this issue while reviewing altair code, if beacon state's fork epoch is > 1 and beacon block's attestations are empty on either side (ie. pre fork/post fork), run time panics. 

Reason:
if you pass in empty list of attestation in `createAttestationSignatureSet`, it returns nil signature set, and when you aggregate a nil signature set, run time panics. 

Preventions implemented in two steps:
- don't aggregate signature set if it is nil
- don't pass empty list of attestation in `createAttestationSignatureSet`

title: Capture ChainReorg, FinalizedCheckpoint, and NewHead Events in Beacon Node
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

As part of #9001, we need to capture a few important events in eth2 that are required for the eth/v1/events standard API endpoint. These include chain reorgs, finalized checkpoint, and new chain head.

**IMPORTANT**

The eth2.0-apis chain reorg event does not capture enough information about whether the reorg was across epoch boundaries. Currently, we have a `StreamDuties` endpoint that is **UNUSED** in Prysm which only resends duties if there is a reorg across epoch boundaries. Unfortunately, we can no longer tell this information and therefore we simply send the duties if there is a reorg at all. This should not be be very harmful as reorgs should be very rare and the endpoint is unused in v1alpha1.

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently the code in `shared/gateway` has knowledge about the beacon node and validator. There are separate `NewBeacon`/`NewValidator` functions and the `Start` function runs specific code conditioning on the type of service. What's more, there is no way to mock out protobuf handlers when testing because their registration is buried deep down inside the gateway.

The aim of this PR is to reverse dependencies so that each service registers itself in the gateway. This will resolve the mentioned extensibility and testability issues.

title: Prevent Exporting False Positive Slashing Event Due to Old Prysm DB Schema Bug
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

A user came across an interesting, corrupted slashing protection history from their Prysm validator database that looked something like this:

```js
"signed_attestations": [
  { source: 0, target: 102122 },
  { source: 1, target: 2},
  ...
]
```
Leading to all attestations in that list appearing as slashable after the first entry. This was identified as a result of an old slashing protection database schema Prysm used and has since deprecated. We estimate this old schema affects users that were attesting with Prysm since December 2020. I personally confirmed the bug happened to me as well as I have been validating since then and received a similar slashing protection export.

As a layer of protection, we add special edge-case handling for that corrupted scenario as we cannot safely account for this bug in a general way without introducing further bug risk or more false positives to Prysm slashing protection. This PR adds a regression test to ensure the bug does not manifest itself again.
  
**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #8893

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.

3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to

   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.

**What type of PR is this?**
 Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
`SyncCommittee.Pubkeys` contains byte arrays that are 48 bytes long (sha256). There is a bug in fastssz (https://github.com/ferranbt/fastssz/issues/43) where the generated code fails to right-pad the value to a chunk-aligned boundary before adding to a byte array for HTR computation. This PR updates prysm generated code using the fix for computing hash tree root, as well as temporarily pointing at a branch in my fork of fastssz so that bazel codegen runs also use the correct codegen version. The spec test for `SyncCommittee` has been updated to use the fixed generated type and I have confirmed that the spec tests all pass now via running `bazel test //spectest/mainnet/altair/ssz_static:go_default_test  --test_output=streamed --test_arg=-test.v --test_arg=-test.failfast --cache_test_results=no --test_filter= --test_tag_filters=spectest`.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

We don't have a prysm issue for this problem, just https://github.com/ferranbt/fastssz/issues/43

title: Reorder WORKSPACE go dependency registration
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This reorders the go dependency registration.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

The way that our bazel upstream dependencies work and prysm go dependency registration works is that each dependency is wrapped in a "maybe()" helper which essentially says "if this dependency doesn't already exist, then provide it to bazel". So the problem is that prysm dependencies also conform to this standard of "maybe()", so if  there are upstream dependencies defined before prysm dependencies then prysm dependencies will not override the upstream dependencies.

title: Bazel: minimal test build transitions
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Adds build transitions to support `bazel build //...` with mix build configs.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

**Other notes for review**

Replaces the `--define=ssz=minimal` with a more standard practice for config settings. Going forward, bazel users should use `--//proto:network=<value>` to specify the configuration setting for build time templating in protobuf definitions. One of the benefits of this change is that we can now hardcode configurations within starlark rules. Our custom `go_test` definition is an extension of the upstream `go_test` with an incoming edge transition that sets the config and gotags to the appropriate network value. In other words, if a go_test has `eth_network = "minimal"`, bazel will insure that all incoming dependencies will be compiled with the "minimal" go tag and "minimal" ssz config protobufs.

Examples: 
- `//endtoend:go_default_test` no longer requires `--define=ssz=minimal` or the new flag `--proto:network=minimal`, instead, the incoming edge transition handles this automatically and users simply need to run `bazel test //endtoend:go_default_test`. 
- `bazel test //spectest/...` now runs all mainnet and minimal spec tests in a single command.

title: Use sync committee start period root as cache key
body:
Currently to use sync committee cache, the key is `current_sync_committee_root`. This was not good UX and this PR made radical improvement on that. Instead of using `current_sync_commmittee_root`, it opts to use `current_sync_period_start_root`. Benefits:

When using `current_sync_commmittee_root`:
1.) Get head state
2.) Get sync committee from head state
3.) Hash tree root sync committee
4.) Use result root to look up cache

When using `current_sync_period_start_root`:
1.) Get head state
2.) Get block root at period start using state
3.) Use result root to look up cache

`current_sync_period_start_root` saves one copy and one hash tree root and easier to reason on. Change list:
- Added metrics for instrumentation `SyncCommitteeCacheMiss` and `SyncCommitteeCacheHit`
- Moved `SyncCommitteePeriod` to `helper` pkg to avoid import cycle
- Added `SyncCommitteePeriodStartEpoch` helper and test
- Added `syncPeriodBoundaryRoot` helper
- Updated cache to use `current_sync_commmittee_root` as key

title: End-to-End Test Suite For Synced Slasher Node
body:
## Background

We believe there is a gap in slasher where if

(a) There are beacon nodes and validators running
(b) Some validator, `v`, produces an attestation before some epoch, `N`
(c) A beacon node with --slasher joins the network after epoch `N` and syncs the chain
(d) Validator `v` produces a slashable offense after epoch `N`

The slasher from part (c) did not join until after epoch `N`, therefore slasher did not have a record of validator `v` producing a slashable offense. This would mean slasher would **not** catch the offense from part (d). We believe this can be resolved by performing a backfilling routine from the epoch slasher syncs to minus `WEAK_SUBJECTIVITY_PERIOD` epochs to populate its history.

To prove this, we can start with an end-to-end test which demonstrates the scenario above.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR adds an end-to-end test suite for running a beacon node + validators and _then_ syncing a beacon node and evaluating policies on the synced node. Currently, we have a primitive way of doing this that does not allow much customization on testing the synced node.

Using the addition mentioned above, this PR also sets up an example end-to-end test which

(a) Runs beacon nodes and validators
(b) At some epoch `N`, we sync a new beacon node with --slasher from peers
(c) Some validator produces a slashable offense after epoch `N`
(d) We expect slasher **will not catch** the slashable offense in its current form

A red test is a successful result of this PR. The plan is to then turn that test **green** in another PR.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331 

**NOTE**: Marked as draft until this test becomes green after adding the slasher backfilling logic

This is an optimization PR over `runtime.assign`.   Whenever a node processes a block, it processes the `SyncAggregate` object. This PR optimizes `TotalActiveBalance` by moving `SlotToEpoch(state.Slot()))` out side of the `ReadFromEveryValidator` loop. Every time `state.Slot()` is involved, it must obtain a beacon state read lock and that's obviously not efficient obtaining one instance of read lock for every validator (190k as of today)

title: Sync committee pool can retrieve without pop
body:
Sync committee object pool saves and retrieves objects using the priority queue. For retrieve, it uses the method `PopByKey`.  Using pop has an unintended consequence. By definition pop removes object on return and this does not fit our use case. In spec, there's multiple aggregators across multiple subcommittees. It means after aggregator at subcommittee 0 retrieve objects at slot N, it will empty the queue for slot N and leave aggregators at subcommittee 1,2,3 with nothing to aggregate.

To solve this we implement a new method `RetrieveByKey` for the priority queue. The method returns the object without removing the object from the queue.

Note: pool is still correctly getting pruned based on save. It gets trimmed after `syncCommitteeMaxQueueSize` is reached.

title: Add active balance to committee cache
body:
This is needed for `altair` as the retrieval of active balance becomes more frequent during block processing. Comparing to phase 0 where active balance is only used during epoch processing or validator slashing and epoch processing has its own optimization to flatten all the performance variables. 

To cache active balance, we add a new field `ActiveBalance` to committee cache struct. We remove functions `ShuffledIndices` and add new function `activeIndicesAndBalance` where it computes for active indices and active balance. To get the shuffled indices, we feed in the results of `activeIndicesAndBalance` into `UnshuffleList`. Keep in mind that everything is the same as before, we simply refactor `ShuffledIndices` into smaller pieces where active balance could use.

The helper function `TotalActiveBalance` is updated to use cache and fill in cache when there's a miss. I tested this with Altair run time to ensure integrity intacts

title: Implement Slasher Data Backfilling After Initial Sync
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR is based on the design document found [here](https://hackmd.io/RMkGw1iMSimKa7B9ZM3-mg) explaining the problem and need for slasher to perform data backfilling after initial sync. The way it works is:

1. Wait for slasher to finish initial sync
2. Get the head epoch of the chain **minus** the weak subjectivity period
3. Fetch all blocks from the value in step (2) up to the head epoch inclusive
4. For each block, process each header and all attestations in slasher
5. If at the end of the process the time between the last processed epoch and the current time-based epoch is different, go back to step (2)

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8331 

**NOTE**

This will likely incur a significant resource drain on a node if done naively. For example, fetch all blocks and attestations from epoch N - 4096 to epoch N and processing all at once may be overkill. I want to get this algorithm correct **first** and in a follow-up PR investigate it's real life performance.

title: Fix next epoch sync duty calculation
body:
Fixed a bug when validator requests beacon node for duties at slot epoch boundary -1 (ie. every `N * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH-1`), beacon node incorrectly responds sync committee duties based on next period, instead of current period. The only time beacon node should respond based on next period is epochs per sync committee period multiply epoch boundary - 1 (ie. every `N * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD-1`)

While fixing the bug, I also fixed much of the bad usage of terminology where `epoch` and `period` are mixed up

title: Move v1alpha1 into Prysm API namespace
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Based on the doc https://hackmd.io/i-5rPWDhQO6GSHO5PzuncA, we have decided on a direction for Prysm's APIs moving forward for stability and simplicity. This PR is the first which moves v1alpha1 into the Prysm API namespace for better organization

- Using a simple versioning schema of v1, v2, v3, etc. aligning to major version upgrades of Prysm
- Always supporting a trailing version. For example, if Prysm is in v2, we will support v1, but aim to drop support for v1 upon the next new version
- All endpoints and types will be carried over to new versions as needed, so there is no need for consumers to deal with mixed versions. For example, someone could implement a tool using only the Prysm v2 API
- Concretely, we would copy over all endpoints from v1alpha1 into v2 and implement new endpoints we need for Altair. For example, we can have a ListBlocksAltair endpoint.

title: Implement Batch Verifier For Pubsub Objects
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In gossip, the beacon node receives multiple objects over the wire and has to verify them separately. This brings about a 
significant load to the beacon node as the validator set in mainnet grows. Beacon nodes running on single/dual cores will eventually be insufficient due to to increased number of pairings that need to be performed. By using batch verification with randomized factors, we can reduce the number of miller loops performed with the result of reducing the CPU time required to verify `n` signatures. In the event batch verification fails due to an errant signature somewhere this method will fallback to verifying all signatures one by one. 

- [x] Implement verifier routine to regularly perform batch verifications of incoming signature sets.
- [x] Modify relevant gossip validators to allow them to provider signature sets for batch verification.
- [x] Add feature flag to gate this feature.
- [x] Add in relevant tests for this feature.

body:

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Prysm currently exposes its API via gRPC and also via an HTTP JSON gateway known as [grpc-gateway](https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway). Currently, we require these to be at parity, however, we do not have conformance tests to ensure the gateway and gRPC requests and responses match. If there is a problem that breaks our gateway for v1alpha1, we will not know until users report it. As such, it is critical to add end-to-end test evaluators to this feature.

**Other notes for review**

This is not a comprehensive set of evaluations for all v1alpha1 endpoints, as that would take too much time. Instead, we test a few items such as GET/POST requests and also one-of query parameter requests. Perhaps we need a systematic way of doing most endpoints? How much confidence do we need?

title: Improve `v2` protos
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Prepares protos for https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs.

Some `v2` messages contain references to `v1` messages. The API spec requires an option to return the SSZ-serialized version of the signed beacon block. To achieve this I added the `ssz_gen_marshal` rule to the Bazel build file and I had to include `"//proto/prysm/v1:go_default_library"` because of the `v1` references. Unfortunately this resulted in an error. It turns out that our current SSZ library does not allow two structs with the same name, even in different packages, which means I had to rename all `v2` messages that had a name conflicting with `v1`. I added the `V2` suffix to all such messages.

title: Update Altair proposer reward quotient
body:
`PROPOSER_REWARD_QUOTIENT` was still on phase0 value for altair.

In phase0, we have: 
` proposer_reward = Gwei(whistleblower_reward // PROPOSER_REWARD_QUOTIENT)`
source:  https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/beacon-chain.md#slash_validator

in altair, we should have:
`proposer_reward = Gwei(whistleblower_reward * PROPOSER_WEIGHT // WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR)`
source: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/beacon-chain.md#modified-slash_validator

Please cross check on my math whether the ordering matters

title: Update synccommittee spectest
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
SyncCommittee.Pubkeys contains byte arrays that are 48 bytes long (sha256). There is a bug in fastssz (ferranbt/fastssz#43) where the generated code fails to right-pad the value to a chunk-aligned boundary before adding to a byte array for HTR computation. This PR updates prysm generated code using the fix for computing hash tree root, as well as temporarily pointing at a branch in my fork of fastssz so that bazel codegen runs also use the correct codegen version. The spec test for SyncCommittee has been updated to use the fixed generated type and I have confirmed that the spec tests all pass now via running `bazel test //spectest/mainnet/altair/ssz_static:go_default_test --test_output=streamed --test_arg=-test.v --test_arg=-test.failfast --cache_test_results=no --test_filter= --test_tag_filters=spectest`

title: `ValidatorIndexByPubkey` length check
body:
# Description

Triggered in Pyrmont after hard forking to Altair. 
```
{"error":"could not process block in batch: could not process block: could not process block operation: could not process deposit from 0x98203936167e: index of 128335 does not exist","message":"Batch is not processed","prefix":"initial-sync","severity":"WARNING"}
```
The bug could be summarized as:
 - while processing deposit
 - node thinks validator exists in the state at index N but the validator length is at N
 - updating the balance at index N returns index does not exist error

Upon further debug, I noticed v1 state getter implemented the following condition in #8860 while v2 state getter does not have it:
![Screen Shot 2021-08-19 at 8 49 50 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/21316537/130100698-7eede6de-c7b6-4574-9d6b-191c79e0b1a3.png)

I'm not exactly sure the rationale why `valMapHandler` returns the length when `idx` does not exist, but v2 getter implementation should be following v1

title: Remove Nested BoltDB View Within Update Transaction in SaveHeadBlockRoot
body: **What type of PR is this?** > Other **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** End-to-end tests flake _a lot_. In particular, we noticed it has been draining developer productivity and affecting how fast we can iterate on features. To diagnose this, we decided to gather opentracing spans during endtoend, which can be replayed to a jaeger collector and visualized in the jaeger UI. To accomplish this, we wrote a tool for collecting spans in endtoend tests, and another tool to replay them to jaeger collector in #9341. The first time we took a peek at the spans, they showed some slowdown in certain disk operations, which we attributed to not running on an SSD. However, Preston from our team confirmed the nodes that run CI are using SSD, so we ignored the issue as there was not much to do. Today, we decided to pick this up again and inspect the failure happening in CI once more by looking at jaeger spans. We noticed that most of the issues are in ReceiveBlock in functions related to checking state summaries. Specifically, `SaveHeadBlockRoot`. Upon further inspection, we see the function opens a write-transaction in bolt, and within that transactions opens another read-transaction. This seems potentially dangerous. There is no way a single db.Put operation is taking almost 4 seconds. Next, Kasey from our team brought up some information regarding this from the bolt documentation: > Read-only transactions and read-write transactions should not depend on one another and generally shouldn't be opened simultaneously in the same goroutine. This can cause a deadlock as the read-write transaction needs to periodically re-map the data file but it cannot do so while a read-only transaction is open. As such, this PR tries to remove that by simplifying the logic with a small refactor. We hope this will be the root cause of end to end failing this much.

title: Increase seen attestation cache sizes
body:
# Description

Given today's validator count (220k), the seen attestation size is ~70% around max size at 10000. This PR increases seen attestation cache size with the budget of 600k which should last us until early 2023 given activation queue's rate limit.

unaggregated: 600k / 32(`slots_per_epoch`) = ~20k
aggregated: 64(`max_committees_per_slot`) * 16 (`target_aggregators_per_slot`) = 1024

At 600k validators, the unaggregated cache size will be 60MB, we can further optimize this down to ~32MB in the next PR

title: Sync Committee Message P2P Validations
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR implements p2p gossipsub validation pipelines for sync committee messages according to the altair consensus specification:

> Sync committee subnets are used to propagate unaggregated sync committee messages to subsections of the network.

> sync_committee_{subnet_id}
> The sync_committee_{subnet_id} topics are used to propagate unaggregated sync committee messages to the subnet > subnet_id to be aggregated before being gossiped to the global sync_committee_contribution_and_proof topic.

The following validations MUST pass before forwarding the sync_committee_message on the network:

- [IGNORE] The message's slot is for the current slot (with a MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY allowance), i.e. sync_committee_message.slot == current_slot.
- [REJECT] The subnet_id is valid for the given validator, i.e. subnet_id in compute_subnets_for_sync_committee(state, sync_committee_message.validator_index). Note this validation implies the validator is part of the broader current sync committee along with the correct subcommittee.
- [IGNORE] There has been no other valid sync committee message for the declared slot for the validator referenced by sync_committee_message.validator_index (this requires maintaining a cache of size SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE // SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT for each subnet that can be flushed after each slot). Note this validation is per topic so that for a given slot, multiple messages could be forwarded with the same validator_index as long as the subnet_ids are distinct.
- [REJECT] The signature is valid for the message beacon_block_root for the validator referenced by validator_index.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #8638

title: Update to spec test beta3
body:
# Description
This PR updates spec test to beta3 which included a new spec test format/folder `random`. While integrating the new spec test `random`, a bug was discovered where `ProcessEpochParticipation` processes flag indices for incorrectly marks **inactive** validators as true. In other words, for `get_unslashed_participating_indice`:

```python
# Spec:
active_validator_indices = get_active_validator_indices(state, epoch)
participating_indices = [i for i in active_validator_indices if has_flag(epoch_participation[i], flag_index)]
# Our implementation:
participating_indices = [i for i in state.validators if has_flag(epoch_participation[i], flag_index)]
```

Side note: `RunBlockProcessingTest` was refactored to use `folder_path` to it could be reused for `random` spec tests

Credit: Thanks @ralexstokes and team for the spec tests and helped with the debug

title: Stategen: fix state by slot off by 1
body:
# Description

This fixes a long existing bug for retrieving state using slot. The retrieval method is only used in a few RPC end points, so there's no consensus relevance to this. The summary of the bug is:

- When process state up to slot N
- The node **should not** process the block at N 
- The node should process the block up to N-1 then process slot to N

Today we process slot to N but also process the block at N. One negative consequence of doing this is latest block header will no longer be useful

title: Save orphaned attestation in its own pool
body:
# Description

Motivated by #9523, this may or may not fix the issue but it's certainly an improvement.

Before when the node saves an orphaned attestation, the attestation goes back to the regular attestation pool. What it means is the orphaned attestation will be treated as a fresh attestation. While this is good for block proposer, the downside is fork choice will have to re-process the orphaned attestation again. This PR fixes such deficiency by separating orphaned attestation into its own pool. Note that I chose to neglect orphaned unaggregated attestation, this can be follow up later or completely dropped.

title: using upstream fastssz with altair fixes
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
`SyncCommittee.Pubkeys` contains byte arrays that are 48 bytes long (sha256). There was a bug in fastssz (ferranbt/fastssz#43) where the generated code fails to right-pad the value to a chunk-aligned boundary before adding to a byte array for HTR computation. This PR updates prysm generated code using the fix for computing hash tree root. The spectest for SyncCommittee has been updated to use the fixed generated type (previously hardcoded to skip the failing test). I have confirmed that the spec tests pass via running `bazel test //spectest/mainnet/altair/ssz_static:go_default_test --test_output=streamed --test_arg=-test.v --test_arg=-test.failfast --cache_test_results=no --test_filter= --test_tag_filters=spectest`

Note that this replaces https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/9408 which I am going to close.

title: Correctly filter sync committee message at period boundary
body:
## Background
In spec, the sync committee duty is defined as:
```
Being assigned to a sync committee for a given slot means that the validator produces and broadcasts signatures for slot - 1 for inclusion in slot. 
This means that when assigned to an epoch sync committee signatures must be produced and broadcast for slots on range 
[compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) - 1, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1) 
rather than for the range 
[compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch), compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)
```
That also means at `EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD`'s slot - 1, the validator should sample next sync committee duty instead of current sync committee duty. 

## Issue
- RPC package that is to serve validator `rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator/sync_committee.go ` successfully does it. It implements `[compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) - 1, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH - 1) `
- Sync package that is to validate incoming sync committee message `beacon-chain/sync/validate_sync_committee_message.go` **does not**. It implements `[compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch), compute_start_slot_at_epoch(epoch) + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)`
which means at `EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD`'s slot - 1, `validate_sync_committee_message` would filter out correctly intended sync committee message and it implies block at `EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD` will contain less sync committee bits. 

## Resolution

Refactor `HeadSyncCommitteeIndices` to be shared between `RPC` and `sync` package so there's more asymmetric 

## Credit:
This issue was discovered by @prestonvanloon working on long running end to end test at epoch 16. Regular end to end test did not catch this because `EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD` is too long.

title: clear pending atts after syncing block
body:
Call `processPendingAtts` right after receiving and processing a block. this calls only once per block received instead of twice per slot. There is no point in calling this routine at a fixed time now since we won't be able to process any attestations if we hadn't synced the block. 

This PR separates the two functions of the pending attestation queue, namely requesting pending blocks, and processing attestations, to be made in parallel and on demand when validating the newly arrived attestation and right after syncing a block respectively. It follows the design in https://hackmd.io/@potuz/B1yC3gFNY

Credit goes to @nisdas that traced the problem to `attest-timely` used in conjunction with the pending attestation queue design of prysm. 

Fixes #9662

title: Allow sending Altair blocks to `/eth/v1/beacon/blocks`
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

A bit of explanation on what happened in `custom_hooks.go`.

`setInitialPublishBlockPostRequest` is triggered before we deserialize the request JSON into a struct. We don't know which version of the block got posted, but we can determine it from the slot. We know that both Phase 0 and Altair blocks have a `Message` field with a `Slot` field, so we deserialize the request into a struct `s`, which has the right fields, to obtain the slot. Once we know the slot, we can determine what the `PostRequest` field of the endpoint should be, and we set it appropriately.

In `preparePublishedBlock` we transform the `PostRequest`. gRPC expects either a `phase0_block` or a `altair_block` field in the JSON object, but we have a `message` field at this point. We do a simple conversion depending on the type of `endpoint.PostRequest` (which was filled out previously in `setInitialPublishBlockPostRequest`)


**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #9669

**Other**

This PR also makes sure that `AltairE2EForkEpoch` constant is not publicly visible any more. Its misuse caused a bug in the initial implementation.

title: Refactor Web Authentication to Use Auth Token
body:
As part of our web UI revamp for better authentication and user experience, we are moving to a token-based auth system as specified in our design document [here](https://prysmaticlabs.notion.site/Web-UI-Revamp-Plan-a93169eda58743bca327af04ee1c63bc). This PR removes all logic regarding web ui password settings to instead log an auth token to the logs and to a file on disk (0600 permissions), and forces all web ui endpoints to be authenticated.

The way it works is as follows:

**On validator client initialization**
Check the wallet directory to see if an `auth-token` file exists. We then read it, which contains

1. The jwt secret
2. The jwt token
3. The jwt expiration

If the file does not exist, we generate new random jwt secret and _save it to the file_ along with the token and expiration.

**If user forgot token URL for auth**
The user can also run the command `prysm.sh validator web auth-token`, which will generate the 3 jwt items above and persist them to a file in the `--wallet-dir` path specified by the user. This command is also useful for third-party services such as dappnode to plug-in this auth token experience into their applications.

title: Deregister Remote Slashing Protection Until Further Notice
body:
Slashing protection is one of the riskiest features to include in an Ethereum beacon chain implementation. Prysm today supports three methods
1. Local slashing protection database. This is enabled for every validator client, **cannot** be disabled, and is, in general, a quite safe way of protecting against double signing of data
2. Doppelganger detection. This is an optional feature that looks at some beacon chain information to determine if a validator key is performing its duties on chain. This can halt the process right away and is helpful for preventing getting slashed in case a user is running the same validator key but on a different machine. It is not perfect and redundant key setups should be avoided at all costs.
3. Remote slashing protection using a **slasher**. Slasher is a process that acts as the "police" of the network. It is a highly resource intensive process, and is not bug-free. The team is still working on improving slasher. However, trusting software that is still being drastically improved with something as risky as "slashing protection" is dangerous. 

It has been brought to our attention that slasher currently returns incorrect data for its `HighestAttestations` endpoint, which is used by some stakers for slashing protection. We believe this is a serious risk and are now _disabling_ the ability for validator clients to use remote slashing protection until we feel 100% confident in its safety for further notice.

title: Switch to lazy state balance cache
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

(enhancement / code health, eventually part of WSS)

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR adds a modified state balance cache implementation. Instead of any code that modifies the copy of the justified root recorded by `blockchain.Service` needing to update the balance state cache, the cache is updated on read based on the requested block root.

This reduces the need for code to explicitly update the cache when updating the  copy of the justified state. This simplifies several areas of the code, consolidates responsibility for the cache into the cache type, and decouples the cache from the service somewhat, enabling further refactoring of service initialization in support of weak subjectivity sync.


**Other notes for review**

Previously the update cache method also triggered a sync of the init sync blocks: `s.cfg.BeaconDB.SaveBlocks(ctx, s.getInitSyncBlocks())`. This has been removed based on the assumption that justified states are always saved to the database because they lie on epoch boundaries (which is our minimum state persistence interval). To strengthen this invariant we also changed the order of operations in `updateJustifiedInitSync`, ensuring that `SaveJustifiedCheckpoint` completes successfully before changing `Service.justifiedCheckpoint`. `SaveJustifiedCheckpoint` will fail if the corresponding state hasn't been saved to the db, so doing the swap after the save ensures a more atomic update of both db and runtime variable.

~~Marking this as WIP for now because I may want to add some additional test coverage to this type. Currently it is only tested transitively through service tests. On the topic of tests,~~ edit: added some test coverage directly on the cache. this PR also contains updates to every test that calls `NewService`, because NewService has been modified to initialize the cache. Previously many tests set the `.cfg` field on the Service after calling NewService, but since the cache is initialized inside NewService, it needs stategen to be set first. This was accomplished by updating all these call sites to use the new functional opts (`[]Options` param to NewService). Some helpers were added to cover common test initialization patterns and some care was taken to not add test db initialization where not necessary.

title: Slasher Significant Optimizations
body: # Background This PR contains significant optimizations to Prysm's slasher implementation, recently released in [v2.0.2](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/releases/tag/v2.0.2) as a result of a deep comparison between the Lighthouse team's implementation of slasher both in benchmarks using real data and also in the Prater testnet. It is clear that Prysm's slasher is performing poorly from users running it, sometimes leading to incredibly high memory usage. Additionally, Prysm's slasher sometimes takes ages to run on a group of valid attestations, making us suspect the runtime is getting clogged up due to the slow processing, and making it hard to recover and produce reliable results. ## Current Testnet Performance Prysm currently performs slashable attestations checks in around 7-14 seconds, sometimes taking **7 minutes** to process a group of valid attestations. The variance is astounding. Lighthouse consistently processes 1000 attestations per slot in **1.5 seconds** on average. Prysm's memory footprint is huge, with some users reporting maxing out RAM. ## Local Benchmark with Real Fixtures The following tests were performed on a M1Pro Chip ARM Darwin MacbookPro 2021 using Go 1.17 and the stable release of Rust as of Oct 28, 2021. ### In Prysm To really understand why we have this huge discrepancy and poor performance in Prysm, I extracted all attestations from two blocks in [mainnet](https://beaconcha.in) testnet, along with all beacon committees for its epoch to convert the attestations to indexed form. The attestations were then written as SSZ encoded bytes into a local output directory. For ease of reproduction, a zip file of the indexed attestations folder is attached here below from slots 2385621 and 2385622: [attestations.zip](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/files/7436955/attestations.zip) and [attestations2.zip](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/files/7437137/attestations2.zip) The data was extracted using a bespoke Go tool called `fetch-attestations` and can be seen in the diff below: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/compare/develop...slasher-benching Additionally, I began writing a local test that reads these attestations and passes them through our slasher while logging out processing times. What was found was not ideal. **Current Prysm Slasher** ``` Got a snapshot of valid attestations 128 Took 14 minutes, 980 batches by validator chunk index ``` **14 minutes** to process a simple block of attestations. Something must be wrong... ### Using Lighthouse In a fork of the lighthouse repo, I wrote rust tests to perform the same local benchmark with the same fixtures through their slasher implementation: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/compare/stable...rauljordan:stable On rust stable, `cd slasher && cargo test -- --nocapture` **Current Lighthouse Slasher** ``` Reading attestations from slot N+1 Processing queue Got a snapshot of valid attestations 128 Storing valid attestations in slasher DB Grouping attestations by validator chunk index Processing 980 batches test process_attestations_from_file has been running for over 60 seconds Took 4.03 minutes, avg 247ms per batch Reading attestations from slot N+1 Processing queue Got a snapshot of valid attestations 128 Storing valid attestations in slasher DB Grouping attestations by validator chunk index Processing 980 batches Took 10.7 minutes, avg 655ms per batch ``` Clearly we are much slower than lighthouse, and it seem to perform far better at different steps of the process. ## Optimizations Upon further investigation, here are the problems found and how they were solved: **_We group attestations into batches by validator chunk indices, but we perform double vote detection on each batch_** Double vote detection is a fairly expensive part of the slasher routine, but we were overdoing it for every single attestation batch. Instead, we could do it only **once** for the entire list of valid attestations whilst processing. **_We were updating the entire validator registry's latest written epoch in a single BoltDB transaction_** We had a bolt transaction that was storing _250,000 entries_ all at once, during each iteration of slashing detection over attestations. This is extremely excessive and too much for boltDB to handle. We believe this is a root cause of the excessive memory use, as bolt hates extremely large and long-running transactions. Instead, we only update the validators we care about and avoid doing so in a giga-sized DB transaction. **_We were neither pre-fetching nor updating validator min/max span chunks for the change in current epoch_** Loading chunks from disk is an expensive procedure. However, all chunks need to be updated for validator indices in attestations if there is a change in epoch. We can use the start of slashing detection to load and update the relevant chunks for the change in epoch, and this allows us to **cache** loaded chunks for later use and fewer DB reads **_We were updating validator chunk data for validators that are irrelevant to the attestation in question_** We had some code that had a map of latest epochs written by validator index. For nil entries, we would set the latest epoch written to `0`. Our code that would perform the update would consider this as an epoch to update from, leading to incredibly inefficient and unnecessary updates to validator chunks _from genesis_ when they could have been skipped altogether. Instead, we add an `if ok := someMap[validatorIndex]` check to the map before doing further processing, avoiding an extremely slow operation. ## Final Results Prysm now **matches** Lighthouse's performance on mainnet: ``` level=info msg="Done checking slashable attestations" avgBatchProcessingTime=1.669984ms elapsed=1.670214893s numAttestations=900 numBatchesByValidatorChunkIndex=1000 prefix=slasher ```

title: Make Validator Accounts List Use Functional Options
body: As part of a greater refactor to rethink the concept of a `Keymanager` in Prysm discussed [here](https://www.notion.so/900393aa4cb243f5aead5578c8e801d7), we want to introduce better separation of concerns in the validator client, especially when it comes to dealing with account management. The main functions that let users perform operations on accounts via the CLI are super convoluted pieces of code that parse CLI arguments and have a ton of duplicated logic around initializing a wallet. Instead, we should be abstracting that away to the actual CLI entry point and using functional options to configure these functions. This PR starts by changing `AccountsListCLI` to not take in a cli context, but instead use functional options and a cleaner approach. This will be applied to every exported function in `validator/accounts`

title: Validator monitor
body:
WIP 

This PR implements a validator monitor within the beacon node. It adds a feature flag `--validator-monitor-indices` to the `beacon-chain` command taking a list of validator indices (not necessarily connected to the validator). The beacon then logs messages and emits metrics in the following events 

- A beacon block is proposed by a tracked validator
- A beacon block includes an attestation by a tracked validator
- A beacon block includes a slashing of a tracked validator
- A beacon block includes a voluntary exit of a tracked validator
- A beacon block includes a sync-committee contribution by a tracked validator
- An unaggregated attestation by a tracked validator was processed by the beacon node
- An aggregated attestation by a tracked validator was processed by the beacon node
- An aggregate attestation where the aggregator was a tracked validator, was processed by the beacon node
- A voluntary exit by a tracked validator was processed by the beacon node

It also keeps a structure for aggregated performance since launch, but currently it does not log them

The current PR is a WIP. Collaboration with @terencechain 

- [x]  Logic for logs and emit mettrics in place
- [ ] Automatic detection of validators connected to the RPC node
- [x] Log aggregated performances periodically
- [x]  Write extensive tests
- [x]  Test in runtime

title: Monitor attestations
body:
This PR is the third in the implementation of the validator monitor, it should be reviewed after #9899 

This PR implements logging of performance for attestations viewed by our tracked validators. For attestations included in blocks it logs 

- Timely Head, Source, Target
- Inclusion Slot
- Balance and Balance Change

In addition to the basic information
- Validator Index
- Attested Slot
- Source, Target and Head block roots. 

For unagregated and aggregated attestations processed by the node (after P2P validation but not necessarily included in a block), we log only the basic information above. 

In addition, for P2P aggregated attestations, we log the event that one of our tracked validators was the aggregator. 

The P2P logging (namely not included in blocks) is only performed if the appropriate Beacon  State is currently cached to avoid expensive lookups. This requires addition of the appropriate function in the stategen package. 

## info for reviewers

- This PR includes the most expensive performance hit of the validator monitor: the state copies to log unaggregated and aggregated attestations coming over the wire. I have tested this on Prater and the beacon stays in sync, but this would require testing on testnet to verify if it is a resource intensive operation or not. In principle we are only requesting states from the cache. 
- This PR has a larger diff than the previous two, but as a consolation reward, the next PR will only include the addition of metrics and will be minimal.
