title: Warn Users if Slashing Protection History is Empty
body:
Fixes #9897. The dappnode team was running into a curious issue where they were seeing an empty slashing protection history exported, as reported in #9897. They were running their validator with a command like this:

```
validator \
  --prater \
  --datadir=/root/.eth2 \
  --wallet-dir=/root/.eth2validators \
  --rpc-host 0.0.0.0 \
```

and then trying to export their slashing protection history with:
```
validator slashing-protection export --datadir=/root/.eth2validators
```
Note that they set their --datadir as `/root/.eth2` when running, which is different than what they are trying to export. They should have received some kind of warning if this was the case. This PR adds the necessary warning and explanation to users in case this situation happens.

**NOTE TO REVIEWERS**
Currently, if a validator.db is not found in the specified directory when attempting an export, the current code does throw an error. However, seems like it did not in dappnode's case. My belief is that dappnode had an old, probably empty validator.db in their --wallet-dir and their real validator.db in their --datadir, leading to the issue. This is really hard to write a test case for. We will have to confirm this warning is triggered on dappnode's side before merging.

title: Warn Users In Case Slashing Protection Exports are Empty
body:
Resolves #9897, we finally confirmed and were able to reproduce the problem reported by the dappnode team where exporting their slashing protection history would result in an empty JSON history. This was because the wallet was created with an older version of Prysm that would place their `validator.db` in the top-level wallet directory. However, newer versions of Prysm create and use their `validator.db` in the wallet/direct or wallet/derived folder instead.

```
wallet/
  validator.db # This is a faulty DB created in older versions of Prysm!
  direct/
    accounts/
      all-accounts.keystore.json
    validator.db # This is the correct DB
```

The problem and resolution was **confirmed** by the dappnode team today.

We issue a warning to users here and exit early instead:

```
No slashing protection data was found in your database. This is likely because an older version of " +
				"of Prysm would place your validator database in your wallet directory as a validator.db file. Now, " +
				"Prysm keeps its validator database inside the direct/ or derived/ folder in your wallet directory. " +
				"Try running this command again, but add direct/ or derived/ to the path where your wallet " +
				"directory is in and you should obtain your slashing protection history
```

- [x] Rename current Prysm endpoint to `ImportAccounts` to reserve `ImportKeystores` for the standard API
- [x] Define an `Importer` interface that both the derived and imported keymanager implement
- [x] Amend the keymanager logic to support multiple passwords per keystore
- [x] Implement the API endpoint for `ImportKeystores` according to specification, ensuring it works as expected with necessary tests

**Note**: Diff large due to protobuf regeneration.

title: Monitor service
body:
This PR implements a validator monitor within the beacon node. It adds a feature flag --monitor-indices to the beacon-chain command taking a list of validator indices (not necessarily connected to the beacon). The beacon then logs messages and emits metrics in the following events

A beacon block is proposed by a tracked validator
A beacon block includes an attestation by a tracked validator
A beacon block includes a slashing of a tracked validator
A beacon block includes a voluntary exit of a tracked validator
A beacon block includes a sync-committee contribution by a tracked validator
An unaggregated attestation by a tracked validator was processed by the beacon node
An aggregated attestation by a tracked validator was processed by the beacon node
An aggregate attestation where the aggregator was a tracked validator, was processed by the beacon node
A voluntary exit by a tracked validator was processed by the beacon node
It also keeps a structure for aggregated performance since launch, but currently it does not log them

Collaboration with @terencechain

# Notes for reviewers:

-  context and cancel usage in this service may be completely bogus and unnecessary.

title: API Middleware for Keymanager Standard API Endpoints
body:
This PR adds API middleware support for our keymanager standard https://ethereum.github.io/keymanager-APIs/#/ to support translating grpc gateway responses into the expected types, such as hex strings and enums, to align with the 
standard.

### Changes
- [x] Support DELETE requests in the api middleware
- [x] Support DELETE requests in the cors middleware used by the API gateway
- [x] Regenerate protobufs 
- [x] Amend the custom mux used by the validator client to be able to handle the regular gateway, the api middleware, and web requests
- [x] Small fix to delete keystores to return empty response if request has no public keys

### Requirements
- [x] GET request working! Able to return the list of public keys as hex strings being used by the keymanager
- [x] DELETE request working! Able to successfully delete keystores and retrieve their slashing protection history. If key has been deleted before, it will still return slashing protection history and NOT_ACTIVE
- [x] POST request working! It is able to import keystores with the given password and their associated slashing protection history as well. For a script that is able to make this complex POST request, see the Gist prepared
 
https://gist.github.com/rauljordan/89b35a15032dedd77cf14cfec9886c18

title: Ensure Slashing Protection Exports and Keymanager API Work According to Spec
body:
As defined in the validator [keymanager API standard](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/151/files), there are a few intricate details that we must ensure we support and behave as required. This PR adds a few fixes to ensure the behavior is up to spec:

For `ImportKeystores`
- [x] Ensure that every keystore in the `ImportKeystores` endpoint has a corresponding password. Even if using one password to encrypt everything, we should just duplicate that password N times in the request where N = len(keystores)

For `DeleteKeystores`
- [x] If a key is in the DB but not found in the wallet, we should return NOT_ACTIVE
- [x] We should return slashing protection history only for the keys that are in the request

title: Web3signer: Add an HTTP Client Wrapper to Interact with Remote Server
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.
2. Please file an associated tracking issue if this pull request is non-trivial and requires context for our team to understand. All features and most bug fixes should have
   an associated issue with a design discussed and decided upon. Small bug
   fixes and documentation improvements don't need issues.
3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to
   be updated. If you're unsure what to update, send the PR, and we'll discuss
   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**


Feature

Part of #9994


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR is the first in a series that aims to add support for Consensys' [Web3Signer](https://docs.web3signer.consensys.net/en/latest/) remote signing server, supported by various eth2 clients today. Web3signer is an important standard for institutional adoption of staking, and we should support it in Prysm today. 

This first PR introduces a new keymanager type in the Prysm validator known as remote-web3signer, and an HTTP client wrapper used internally by the new keymanager. This defines the necessary methods to perform http calls to the remote signer server according to the API spec they define in their docs [here](https://consensys.github.io/web3signer/web3signer-eth2.html).

**NOTE**: This PR does is scoped only to the http client functionality, and is the first of several remaining PRs

title: support fetching origin sync data from a beacon node
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This is PR 2/3 towards implementing checkpoint sync (aka weak subjectivity sync). This PR adds a new RPC endpoint that enable a client to query for the epoch of the latest finalized block within the weak subjectivity period. Also included is a new cli tool `prysmctl` with subcommands enabling a user to download the block at the first slot of the epoch and the subsequent state that integrates the block into the (ie latest_block_header root = the signed beacon block root).

**Other notes for review**

Currently this branch includes some code that modifies the timeout of calls to the state endpoint. This will be removed once https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/9946 has been merged to develop and updated in this branch.

Note that this branch builds on `cp-sync-origin-root`, so that branch will be used as the target of this PR until the upstream branch is merged, at which time this PR will swap to `develop`.
author: kasey

title: Standardize config overriding in tests across repo
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

We currently have at least 4 different ways of overriding configs in tests:

1. Best option
```
params.SetupTestConfigCleanup(t)
params.OverrideBeaconConfig(params.MainnetConfig())
```
2. Bad because it assumes mainnet is the default
```
params.UseMinimalConfig()
defer params.UseMainnetConfig()
```
3. Bad because it assumes mainnet is the default
```
conf := params.BeaconConfig()
conf.AltairForkEpoch = 5
params.OverrideBeaconConfig(conf)
defer params.UseMainnetConfig()
```
4. OK although explicitly using `OverrideBeaconConfig` is more expressive
```
params.SetupTestConfigCleanup(t)
params.UseMainnetConfig()
```

The purpose of this PR is to standardize the use of (1).

title: WIP: beacon node cli flag for specifying origin block+state
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This adds beacon node cli flags that can be used to specify paths to ssz serialized block and state values to be used in place of a genesis block+state for syncing from a recent subjectivity checkpoint. When these flags are specified, the existing database methods for setting up a beacon node are leveraged to save these values, mark the block as justified, finalized, and head of chain and keep track of the root used to initialize the system in this way. This allows the chain to begin syncing from the weak subjectivity checkpoint, rather than syncing from genesis. 

**Other notes for review**
Note that this targets the `cp-sync-fetch-origin` branch, which this branch builds on top of. It is branch 3/3 to add this feature to the beacon node. Most of the code in play will have already been merged in previous branches (see PR #9976 and #9997), so the key for this branch is testing to make sure the flag is ready for release to end-users. I intend to add some additional tests to this branch after the holiday break, in the meantime I'll mark it WIP.

title: Add is_merge_complete helper
body:
This PR adds `is_merge_complete` helper as defined in the spec:
```python
def is_merge_complete(state: BeaconState) -> bool:
  return state.latest_execution_payload_header != ExecutionPayloadHeader()
```

I've tried two implementations to compare empty payload header along with benchmarks
1. Uses `ssz.DeepEqual` function to compare empty
```
BenchmarkMergeComplete
BenchmarkMergeComplete-12    	   34737	     34638 ns/op
PASS
```
2. Uses handcrafted function to compare empty
```
BenchmarkMergeComplete
BenchmarkMergeComplete-12    	 2778049	       430.9 ns/op
PASS
```

I went with handcrafted function in the PR

Maybe helps with memory usage since this method is very high traffic.

title: Fork Choice Proposer Boost Changes
body:
## Background

An accompanying document explaining the problem and what this PR mitigates can be found [here](https://www.notion.so/prysmaticlabs/Fork-Choice-Proposer-Boost-Design-df50ab6d18ea4af0ae3b2a6837f80bc4). Essentially, there are several issues with the current LMD fork choice rule which do not deal with situations where malicious proposers can withhold blocks to trigger reorgs. This will be exacerbated after the merge, as it is possible people are incentivized to do this in order to extract [MEV](https://research.paradigm.xyz/MEV).

The original PR with changes to the specification can be found [here](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2730/files) and the fork choice spec can be found [here](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/fork-choice.md)

**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR introduces fork choice proposer boosting as a way of dealing with ex-ante attacks, described in our document [here](https://www.notion.so/prysmaticlabs/Fork-Choice-Proposer-Boost-Design-df50ab6d18ea4af0ae3b2a6837f80bc4). It is important to note this PR is **highest risk** as mistakes in here can trigger dangerous forking scenarios on mainnet. It must be reviewed thoroughly and tested until there is enough confidence for shipping to mainnet.

title: Update Batch Verification Routine
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature Improvements

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR introduces some improvements in our batch verification logic. This is based on earlier work on how to reduce the amount of pairings required to verify a batch of signatures along with some more optimizations based on work from other clients(ex: nimbus). Earlier there was experimentation on reducing duplicates when verifying across a batch of signatures. The work was shelved at the time due to higher priority items taking precedence(Altair HF work). Now with the state being bigger with close to 300k validators and other clients also applying similar and other additional optimizations to the process with success it seems like a good time to explore this again. 

- [x] Introduces method to remove duplicate signatures.
- [x] Introduces method to perform a search and aggregation of common messages. This is not without cost as it increases the griefing vector by a peer wanting to pass invalid signatures for messages. The batch size is kept relatively small to prevent the node from re-verifying too many messages in the event this happens. 
- [x] Add unit tests
- [x] Add feature flag to gate this.

title: Fix Fork Choice prunning
body:
This PR fixes the following issue on current fork choice pruning. Given the following diagram of nodes, where the numbers are the indices in the Fork Choice

```
0 -- 1
  \ _ 2
```
And we finalize the block 1, we should be left with only that block, pruning away the older final state `0` and the contentious fork `2`. Currently we keep a dangling node `2` that gets pruned later. 

WARNING: the loop is very fast, but it is a loop over the whole fork choice, this may not be so critical since it's only applied when we are finalizing a node, therefore either we are in a good case, or if we were forked, we are getting away from trouble.

title: Fix off by one in DB
body:
The following issue is caused by an off-by-one in the current reindexing algorithm of prysm, This PR includes a fix and a unit test for the following situation

Consider the following chain of blocks

```
0 -- 1 -- ... -- 62 -- 64 -- 65 -- ... -- 127
                  \
                    -- 63
```
That is, the last block of Epoch 1 is orphaned. 

1. We finalize Epoch 1. At this point all blocks 0 -- 63 should be considered Final, this is currently OK on prysm
2. At this point blocks 64--95 should be considered not final. This is the bug being fixed in this PR, currently prysm would consider those blocks final in the index. 
3. We finalize Epoch 2. At this point all blocks 64 -- 95 should be final, blocks 96 -- 127 should not be final (again same bug being fixed here)
4. After finalizing Epoch 2, we check that block 63 is no longer considered final, while all blocks 0--62 are still considered final

title: State balance cache: handle input zeros
body:
The state balance cache's `get` returns the cached balances when input root matches the cached root.  The cache is initialized with: 
```GO
	balances []uint64
	root     [32]byte
```

When someone inputs `[32]byte{}` the cache will return `[]uint64`. Such behavior is dangerous and could hide away edge cases. Instead, we should disallow returning a default value, and pass the default value to `update` to let it process or fail

title: Engine API Protobuf Definitions
body:
The latest engine API specification has come a long way and it is in a pretty stable state, found [here](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/specification.md#structures). These are maintained as protobufs in `proto/engine/v1` and will be used as the canonical types in Prysm for supporting the "merge" of Ethereum PoS and PoW.

This PR only contains the protobuf definitions and generated Go code from said protobufs.

**NOTE**: Protobuf generates snake_case json tags for the structs, but the JSON-RPC API will require camelCase to unmarshal and marshal propertly. Unfortunately, protobuf does not support customizing the JSON struct tags as mentioned in [here](https://github.com/golang/protobuf/issues/52), so we include a custom implementation of the standard library's json `Marshaler` and `Unmarshaler` interfaces. Unit test has been added to ensure this works properly.

title: Invalid synced tips
body:
This PR handles the situation when a node changes status SYNCING -> INVALID

1- removes the invalid node from fork choice
2- readjusts children/parent relations
3- takes into account weight to readjust best descendant and child
4- updates the synced tips structures to reflect this change.

This last case 4 can only happen in one scenario:

```
0 -- 1 -- 2
        \ 
          -- 3
```
if 3 becomes INVALID, then

a- if 1 was not a synced tip, then there are no changes
b- is 1 was a synced tip only because it was the tip of the branch ending in 3 then it has to be removed. For example, if 2 was a synced tip the 1 needs to be removed, if 2 was not a synced tip, then 1 continues being a synced tip.

title: Implement `is_valid_terminal_pow_block`
body:
Implement `is_valid_terminal_pow_block` from spec

```python
def is_valid_terminal_pow_block(block: PowBlock, parent: PowBlock) -> bool:
    is_total_difficulty_reached = block.total_difficulty >= TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY
    is_parent_total_difficulty_valid = parent.total_difficulty < TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY
    return is_total_difficulty_reached and is_parent_total_difficulty_valid
```

title: Use a doubly linked tree structure as Fork Choice Store
body:
# Summary

This PR implements a doubly linked tree structure as Fork Choice Store instead of the current flat array of nodes, each keeping track of their parent. The main benefits of this approach are

- Simpler, readable code. 
- More maintainable and less bug prone code. 
- Better encapsulation
- No need for synced tips (and other optimistic sync complications)
- Passing pointers to nodes (8 bytes) instead of roots (32 bytes around)

Some trade-offs
- We use recursive functions instead of loops in the set of nodes. 
- In the happy case this design adds 8 bytes per node (not counting the removed 32 bytes from the graffiti) and in addition it adds 8 bytes per fork. 

## Design 
The main difference is in the structure `Node` that node has
```go
type Node struct {
        slot           types.Slot                   // slot of the block converted to the node.
        root           [fieldparams.RootLength]byte // root of the block converted to the node.
        parent         *Node                        // parent index of this node.
        children       []*Node                      // the list of direct children of this Node
        justifiedEpoch types.Epoch                  // justifiedEpoch of this node.
        finalizedEpoch types.Epoch                  // finalizedEpoch of this node.
        balance        uint64                       // the balance that voted for this node directly
        weight         uint64                       // weight of this node: the total balance including children
        bestDescendant *Node                        // bestDescendant node of this node.
        optimistic     bool                         // whether the block has been fully validated or not
}
```
- We keep a pointer to the parent
- We keep a pointer to each child
- We keep track of the optimistic status of each node. 
- We keep the total validator balance (plus proposer Boost) that voted directly for this node. 
- We do not keep the best child

(we also removed the 32 bytes from the graffiti) 

The  `Store` structure is modified as follows
```go
type Store struct {
        treeRoot                   *Node                                  // the root node of the store tree.
        headNode                   *Node                                  // last head Node
        nodeByRoot                 map[[fieldparams.RootLength]byte]*Node // nodes indexed by roots.
        ...
}
```
- We keep a pointer to the root of the tree
- We keep a pointer to the current canonical head
- We keep a map from block roots to nodes. 
- We **do not** keep a list of canonical nodes.
- We **do not** keep any list of indices. 

## Updating weights
The main difference happens when updating weights. There is no `computeDelta` function. Instead, a call to `ForkChoice.Head()` does the following:
1. It updates the balances that voted directly for each node. The tradeoff here is between keeping the extra 8 bytes per node, vs having a list of deltas. These latter ones are integers, which would normally be implemented as 4 bytes, thus we are doubling the size of the balance list, but avoiding completely any integer overflow. 
2. It applies the proposer boost changes
3. It computes recursively the weights 
4. It updates recursively the best descendants. 

As an example of better encapulation, since the node structure is richer, several methods can be taken away from the store structure. For example the updating of the weights is simply:
```go
func (n *Node) applyWeightChanges(ctx context.Context) error {
        if ctx.Err() != nil {
                return ctx.Err()
        }
        // update the children
        childrensWeight := uint64(0)
        for _, child := range n.children {
                if err := child.applyWeightChanges(ctx); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                childrensWeight += child.weight
        }
        if n.root == params.BeaconConfig().ZeroHash {
                return nil
        }
        n.weight = n.balance + childrensWeight
        return nil
}
```
## Other comments
I removed the Tree Handler for the debug endpoint. If needed it can be added again. The main reason to remove it is again encapsulation. In future PRs I would like to minimize the interface exposes by the fork-choice package:

- There should be never a reason to expose the Store, and certainly never a node.
- If there is direct need for node-specific information from outside the fork-choice package (like it's weight), most likely a refactor is in need. Otherwise add a getter to `ForkChoice`. 

:warning: Warning: this is a pretty sensitive and bug-prone area of code. If you are reviewing this please be thorough and assume that the writer has made tons of bugs (surely there are plenty). The reviewer should not only be a coauthor but also co-blamable and get the same credits as the writer.

title: Retrieving state by slot to always apply canonical block at slot, when available
body:
This PR introduces some new types, `stategen.ReplayerBuilder`, which allows callers to describe a desired state to build, and `stategen.Replayer` which gives control over how to build it. Currently the `ReplayerBuilder` interface only allows a slot to be specified:
```
type ReplayerBuilder interface {
	ForSlot(target types.Slot) Replayer
}
```
This slot represents the slot of the last block to apply when rebuilding the state, ie if slot 23 is specified, the resulting `BeaconState` will represent the result of replaying all canonical blocks through the block at slot 23. If there are skipped slots in the chain up to and including slot 23, `process_slots` will be used to advance the state to the specified slot. Sometimes it is desirable to advance the state to the beginning of a subsequent slot. For this use case, the `Replayer` offers a pair of methods that give more fine-grained control:

```
type Replayer interface {
	ReplayBlocks(ctx context.Context) (state.BeaconState, error)
	ReplayToSlot(ctx context.Context, target types.Slot) (state.BeaconState, error)
}
```
`ReplayBlocks` will only recreate the state specified to the `ReplayerBuilder`. `ReplayToSlot` will do the same thing (invoking `ReplayBlocks` under the hood), but will then also use `process_slot` to advance the state to the requested slot.

This PR changes the `StateBySlot` method of `statefetcher.StateProvider` to use `ReplayBlocks`, so that when requesting a state by slot we always get the "post-state". All RPC methods that used `stategen.StateBySlot` have also been updated to use `Replayer`s.

**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**Related issues**
https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/10132
https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/10043
This also impacts weak subjectivity sync. With these changes, the debug endpoint to retrieve state by slot returns the state with the block at the given slot applied, allow us to use the state and block from the same block when initializing the database, which is consistent with other implementations. 

**Other notes for review**
This PR is marked WIP because there is a bug in how canonical blocks are checked (we need to loop over the next-highest block if the first highest blocks turns out to be non-canonical). I'm working on adding some tests to demonstrate the bug + a fix.

This change includes a few somewhat-unrelated changes. The fork epoch processing routines have been relocated to the core transition package.

title: Add `validate_merge_block`
body:
This PR implements `validate_merge_block` from bellatrix spec. 

```python
def validate_merge_block(block: BeaconBlock) -> None:
    """
    Check the parent PoW block of execution payload is a valid terminal PoW block.

    Note: Unavailable PoW block(s) may later become available,
    and a client software MAY delay a call to ``validate_merge_block``
    until the PoW block(s) become available.
    """
    if TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH != Hash32():
        # If `TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH` is used as an override, the activation epoch must be reached.
        assert compute_epoch_at_slot(block.slot) >= TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH_ACTIVATION_EPOCH
        assert block.body.execution_payload.parent_hash == TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH
        return

    pow_block = get_pow_block(block.body.execution_payload.parent_hash)
    # Check if `pow_block` is available
    assert pow_block is not None
    pow_parent = get_pow_block(pow_block.parent_hash)
    # Check if `pow_parent` is available
    assert pow_parent is not None
    # Check if `pow_block` is a valid terminal PoW block
    assert is_valid_terminal_pow_block(pow_block, pow_parent)
```

The goals for this PR were to reduce the switch/case logic through the application and deduplicate tests. - Make full use of wrapped beacon blocks such that proposals have a single code path instead of `n` fork specific code paths

_Validator proposal test changes_

- Make use of table driven tests to deduplicate tests.

**Summary**
This pull request removes approximately 400 lines of duplicated code while making the production code paths more readable.

title: Forkchoice featureflag
body:
This supersedes #10245 and puts this feature behind a feature-flag. Please read the description in #10245 for the design. In addition to that description, some remarks relevant to this PR

- I have made **no attempts** to minimize code duplication: it is the intention that one implementation will eventually win after being sufficiently tested and we should be able to remove the other by simply removing the corresponding subdirectory of `beacon-chain/forkchoice`. 
- Similarly, I've duplicated the tests in the blockchain packages that directly made use of the protoarray package, so that they are also tested with the nodetree package. 
- This PR has a breaking change in the debug RPC endpoint that returns the fork choice store. It now returns roots of nodes instead of indices, since indices do not make sense in the tree version
- This PR removes the methods to save to DB synced tips since they will not be needed anymore, they need to be subsequently replaced with an appropriate method to save the last fully validated synced root and slot 

## Some comments due to a review of @prestonvanloon  and @rauljordan :
- We have many tests that are duplicated because of the two different fork-choices implementations. This was deemed simpler to remove half entirely when we choose a default one. 
- We will simplify the forkchoice interface to avoid the calls to `ProcessBlock` with so many parameters in the future. 
- One of the biggest advantages that this PR brings, in addition to those mentioned in the description of #10245 is that the algorithms to prune and update optimistic status becomes trivial. For example, when a node which was optimistically synced becomes INVALID (the EC declares it's payload is invalid) pruning it and its children (not implemented in this PR yet) becomes trivial, since it involves just removing that node, the children are automatically removed due to the linked nature of the tree. This avoids completely the complicated logic of synced_tips. 

Credits go to @rkapka and @terencechain who are coauthors and reviewed extensively the code in the `beacon-chain/forkchoice/nodetree` directory and found actual implementation bugs. 

cc. @prestonvanloon

title: RPC: add prepare execution payload
body:
This PR implements get payload for proposer RPC. Outlined in spec:
```python
def prepare_execution_payload(state: BeaconState,
                              pow_chain: Dict[Hash32, PowBlock],
                              finalized_block_hash: Hash32,
                              suggested_fee_recipient: ExecutionAddress,
                              execution_engine: ExecutionEngine) -> Optional[PayloadId]:
    if not is_merge_transition_complete(state):
        is_terminal_block_hash_set = TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH != Hash32()
        is_activation_epoch_reached = get_current_epoch(state) >= TERMINAL_BLOCK_HASH_ACTIVATION_EPOCH
        if is_terminal_block_hash_set and not is_activation_epoch_reached:
            # Terminal block hash is set but activation epoch is not yet reached, no prepare payload call is needed
            return None

        terminal_pow_block = get_terminal_pow_block(pow_chain)
        if terminal_pow_block is None:
            # Pre-merge, no prepare payload call is needed
            return None
        # Signify merge via producing on top of the terminal PoW block
        parent_hash = terminal_pow_block.block_hash
    else:
        # Post-merge, normal payload
        parent_hash = state.latest_execution_payload_header.block_hash

    # Set the forkchoice head and initiate the payload build process
    payload_attributes = PayloadAttributes(
        timestamp=compute_timestamp_at_slot(state, state.slot),
        prev_randao=get_randao_mix(state, get_current_epoch(state)),
        suggested_fee_recipient=suggested_fee_recipient,
    )
    return execution_engine.notify_forkchoice_updated(parent_hash, finalized_block_hash, payload_attributes)
```

title: Migrating Keymanager account list functionality into each type
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Refactor

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR takes care of two more instances where we were switching on the keymanager type.

1. `validator/accounts/wallet_edit.go`: In this case, we only support editing the wallet configuration for the remote keymanager type. Rather than switching on each type, I just added a guard clause to return early if the keymanager type is not remote. This was a relatively simple cleanup.
2. `validator/accounts/accounts_list.go`: This was a more involved change. The end result is us calling km.ListKeymanagerAccounts on the keymanager, no matter which type it is. We accomplish this by adding this function to the IKeymanager interface and implementing on each of the real and mock types. This moves all the printing logic from the accounts_list file into each of the specific keymanager implementations. We confirm the correctness of this refactor by the fact that accounts_list_test (which checks a sample output) still passes.

A few notes about (2).
- In order to keep the interface function definition clean, I added a `ListKeymanagerAccountConfig` struct type to the `validator/keymanager/types.go` file. The fields of this struct are data external to the keymanager that are used in the printing (e.g., wallet accounts directory path). Not each implementation of the interface will use each of these fields in the `ListKeymanagerAccounts` function, but the non-used values will simply be ignored no problem. 
- All the output testing still takes place in `accounts_list_test.go`. We just call the new interface function (`ListKeymanagerAccounts`) on the test keymanagers.
- In the case of the `mockRemoteKeymanager` we still need the printing to work (because we are testing against it). We can accomplish this by moving the logic out of the real remote keymanager type into a function that is exported by the remote package (`remote.ListKeymanagerAccountsImpl`). Thus both the real and the mock remote keymanagers can still call this function by importing that package. In order to accomplish this, we need to inject a pointer to the keymanager itself into the `remote.ListKeymanagerAccountsImpl` function (along with the keymanager options). This seems like a much better outcome than duplicating the code.
- The other mock keymanager types (that implement the `IKeymanager` interface) can just return nil on function call, because we aren't testing the printing there.
- `displayRemotePublicKeys` was a shared function used by the remote and the web3 signer account lister. Rather than duplicating the code into each package, I moved it to the `validator/accounts/types.go` file so it could be imported to both packages. 


**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
This is part of the keymanager refactor defined in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883.

title: Cleanup of Keymanager Deleter interface
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Refactor

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR addresses the account deletion code and refactors it as part of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883. 

The key change is making the `Deleter` interface a mandatory part of the `IKeymanager` interface (in `validator/keymanager/types.go`). This is inline with the other changes in this refactor: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10313 & https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10382. 

This addition to the interface cleans up the following pieces of code:
- `validator/accounts/accounts_delete.go`: we no longer have to do the type assertion against the Keymanager into the `keymanager.Deleter` type. Instead we can just call `.DeleteKeystores` on the Keymanager and if that keymanager type doesn't support the operation it will just return an error. 
- `validator/rpc/accounts.go`: we no longer need to conditionally check on the keymanager kind before calling `DeleteAccount`. We know that if it is the wrong keymanager type, it will just fail fast and return the error.
- `validator/rpc/standard_api.go`: we no longer have to do the type assertion against the Keymanager into the `keymanager.Deleter` type. We can just call `.DeleteKeystores` on the keymanager directly. 
- `validator/accounts/accounts.go`: we can rename `Config` to `DeleteConfig` to increase the specificity of the type, because it is only used to configure the delete operation. Additionally, we can remove the `*wallet.Wallet` field from the type because that is unused.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
This is part of the keymanager refactor defined in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883.

title: Move Engine API to Powchain and Consolidate Connection Management
body:
## What does this PR do? Why is it needed?

Closes #10465 

Three things:
1. Move the engine API client abstraction into becoming part of the `powchain` service
2. Consolidate connection management for Prysm to connect to execution nodes in a single place
3. Connect to execution nodes on initialization rather than at service runtime

### Moving the Engine API Client

Previously, we had created an `Engine API Client` abstraction in its own package in Prysm. However, it makes more sense to move this as part of the `powchain` service, as that service already manages an execution client's json-rpc connection. This simplifies our logic and makes things far more concise.

### Consolidating Connection Management for ETH RPC Endpoints 

Ethereum execution clients, such as go-ethereum, expose a json-rpc API on localhost:8545 by default, offering methods in the `eth` RPC namespace. For the Bellatrix hard-fork, Prysm will require a connection to an execution node's `engine` json-rpc API namespace. Originally, go-ethereum had planned to expose this in a totally different port than the normal RPC endpoint. However, this was scrapped and now it is available at localhost:8545 albeit with authentication as a requirement.

### Connecting to ETH RPC on Initialization

For the merge, we need to connect to RPC endpoints on initialization rather than in runtime Start() functions, as we do today. This is a fairly invasive change, and here is how we deal with it:

1. Move the dialing of ETH endpoints to the powchain's `New()` function
2. Ensure we can dial RPC endpoints even if the ETH client is not synced. Previously, we would have complex connection management logic to check sync status of the execution client and disconnect if it fell out of sync
3. Ensure tests are updated to pass these requirements
author: rauljordan

title: Remove synced tips and use last valid hash
body:
This PR removes the use of synced tips in the protoarray fork choice implementation. It also uses the last valid hash returned from the EL when removing invalid blocks from forkchoice. 

## Rationale

The biggest advantage of synced tips is that it provides us with an effective way of tracking optimistic status of block that may be outside of forkchoice (eg. after pruned by finalization from ForkChoice). 

The disadvantage is the increased complexity added and the number of edge cases we have to deal with. 

Prysm is the unique client (currently to my knowledge) that does not prune and serves non-canonical historical blocks. By removing the synced tips structure we lose the hability of knowing their optimistic status. We would have to resort to serve them as optimistic. 

Fixes #10445

title: Remove Ristretto Cache For Public Keys
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The ristretto Cache requires strings as keys, this requires an expensive byte to string conversion each time we want to retrieve the decompressed public key. This PR uses an LRU cache instead and uses the public key in its `[48]byte` form as the key. This has a few advantages, we don't have to allocate a public key string each time we want to access the decompressed public key. 

This is done by taking advantage of a new addition in go 1.17 which allows us to cast an array from a slice provided the slice is of the appropriate size. This is checked at the start of the function, where we make sure that the slice is of the correct size. Given that doing this is essentially zero-cost, this is more memory efficient compared to our current method.
 
**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

title: Save head after FCU
body: In the situation that we switch head to an optimistic block, we will become optimistic immediately and only validate it after FCU has returned. If the validator needs to perform duties in this brief period, it will not because the node is optimistic. In this PR we change this behavior so that the node acts on its previous head until the EE has returned with the execution validation.

title: Sync: don't set block to bad due to timeout
body: Post merge, BN uses EE to verify payload. Under busy conditions, EE could not respond in time, and BN will get a timeout error. It's natural to retry when the verification times out, but we should not immediately set the block to bad. This will halt the beacon node from retrying and processing the same and future blocks built on the block. This PR added a simple filter to accommodate EE times out

title: Proper Connection Management for ETH JSON-RPC Client for Startup and Runtime
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

With the merge around the corner, Prysm will need a connection to an execution client, even on startup. Currently, the connection to the execution client is something that happens in the background and is mostly used to retrieve deposit lgos from the Validator Deposit Contract. This needs to come front and center for the merge. However, we cannot afford to make a **breaking change** to current Prysm users until we ship Prysm v3.

Moreover, we need to make sure that whatever solution we pick, we **do not crash nor shutdown Prysm**. That is, Prysm should be able to continue even if the RPC connection goes down. If this occurs, we should just error where the calls are made to the execution client, and attempt a reconnection and proceed normally.

This PR is tested on both **kiln** and **mainnet**. On mainnet, the behavior remains the same as today. On Kiln, if the RPC connection is not found, the node can continue as normal, but will typically get stuck in a sync loop until the connection is restored. The node can fully sync after the connection is restored.

**IMPORTANT CHANGES**

- For this approach to work, Prysm needs to at least define a default value for an execution endpoint. This PR sets it as localhost:8545

```
save_state_block_to_db (40ms)
set_proposer_boost

notify_new_payload (10ms)
save_block_to_forchoice (1ms)
set_proposer_boost
```

title: Fix Nasty Finalization Bug
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug Fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Previously we were inserting deposits into our finalized trie via our deposit count(voted eth1data) instead of the eth1 deposit index in the state. The side effect of this is that when we do try to fetch non-finalized deposits for our trie we end up using the wrong merkle index, which leads to us fetching insufficient deposits in order to complete the whole trie in the event our deposit count(from voted eth1data) does not match up with the eth1 deposit index in the state. This can lead to proposers rebuilding the trie in periods where there are a lot of large amount of deposits being added in.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

title: Engine API Proxy Utility for Merge Testing
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR adds a proxy server that sits between a consensus client and an execution client to be used in end-to-end testing. This way, we can programmatically modify in-flight requests and responses as needed to test different behaviors as described in a design doc [here](https://www.notion.so/prysmaticlabs/E2E-Integration-With-Proxy-Middleware-7ced91ea03914008893f82c2481248d1).

This PR simplify creates the proxy logic and adds tests. The way requests can be programmatically intercepted is through registering custom handlers based on conditional events in a test.

The proxy allows for adding conditional interceptors for requests via an API that looks like this:
```go
// RPC method to intercept.
method := "eth_syncing"
proxy.AddRequestInterceptor(
	method,
	&syncingResponse{Syncing: false}, // Custom response.
	func() bool {
		return true // Trigger function that decides if interception should occur.
	},
)
```

title: Refactor validator accounts list to remove cli context dependency
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Refactor/code health

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR addresses the account list code and refactors it as part of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883. It copies heavily from https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/9881 which was abandoned due to the scope of the changes. Due to recent refactors of the keymanager functionality (https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10313, https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10382, https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10415), these changes make even more sense. 

The key feature is decoupling the CLI context from the validator code. We do this with the following:

1. `cmd/validator/accounts/list.go`. This file handles the creation of the wallet and keymanager from the `cli.Context` object.
2. `validator/accounts/cli_manager.go`. This file defines the `AccountsCLIManager` struct type and related functions. This object is constructed and parameterized by the parsing of the CLI flags in `cmd/validator/accounts/list.go`.
3. `validator/accounts/cli_options.go`. This file defines the functional options parsed from the CLI. These are used to update the state of the `AccountsCLIManager`.
4. `validator/accounts/accounts_list.go`. This is where we see the elegance of this decoupling. Because the wallet and keymanager initialization is now abstracted into the `AccountsCLIManager` construction, we can just directly call `keymanager.ListKeymanagerAccounts` by making `List` a method of the `AccountsCLIManager` receiver type. 

This change makes the `validator/accounts/accounts_list.go` implementation maximally simple. The same technique will be applied to reduce code complexity and duplication for the other functions in the `validator/accounts` directory. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
This is part of the keymanager refactor defined in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883.
It is also described in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/10339.

title: Consolidate BeaconBlock Wrappers Into Idiomatic Subpackages
body:
This PR uses our new `consensus-types/` package in the top-level folder of Prysm to consolidate our beacon block interface into idiomatic Go subpackages. The folder structure is as follows:

```
consensus-types/
  errors/
  primitives/
   slot.go
   ...
  wrappers/
    beacon_block.go
  forks/
    phase0/
      beacon_block.go
    altair/
      beacon_block.go
    bellatrix/
      beacon_block.go
  interfaces/
    beacon_block.go
```
Importing and using these utilities becomes a lot nicer. Instead of long names such as `wrappers.SignedPhase0BeaconBlock`, we just get `phase0.BeaconBlock`, which conveys a lot of information in a clean-way. Moreover, it gives us a structure for future forks and subpackages where we can maintain fork-specific types.

```go
// WrappedSignedBeaconBlock will wrap a signed beacon block to conform to the
// signed beacon block interface.
func WrappedSignedBeaconBlock(i interface{}) (block.SignedBeaconBlock, error) {
	switch b := i.(type) {
	case *eth.SignedBeaconBlock:
		return phase0.WrappedSignedBeaconBlock(b), nil
	case *eth.SignedBeaconBlockAltair:
		return altair.WrappedSignedBeaconBlock(b)
	case *eth.SignedBeaconBlockBellatrix:
		return bellatrix.WrappedSignedBeaconBlock(b)
	case nil:
		return nil, typeerrors.ErrNilObjectWrapped
	default:
		return nil, errors.Wrapf(typeerrors.ErrUnsupportedSignedBeaconBlock, "unable to wrap block of type %T", i)
	}
}
```

title: Fix URL handling in beacon node api client
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Fixes a bug where URLs with basic auth credentials could not be used to initialize an `api/beacon.Client` (see #10467 ie `beacon-node-host` arguments in prysmctl or checkpoint sync). Previously host and scheme were snatched out of the result of a url.Parse, saved as separate strings and used to construct the URL for any given path. Aside from losing other attributes, like username:password, this is actually more complicated than doing the right thing, which is storing the validated user input as a `*url.URL`, and using `ResolveReference` to construct URL objects for specific API request paths.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #10467

**Other notes for review**
Tested using infura, up to a point - I wasn't able to test syncing a node because I kept getting timeouts for a state by slot query, but the following command uses several authenticated API calls up to that point, so I can confirm the general API interaction is working with basic auth:

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This changes `handleEpochBoundary` so that it runs the equivalent of `process_slots` on the BeaconState before caching committee data. This fixes an issue where we cache incorrect shuffled and sorted validator indices for subsequent epochs, leading to a mismatch of the proposer index when running in E2E, due to the low value for MAX_SEED_LOOKAHED.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

This PR runs process_slots on the BeaconState at the epoch boundary before calling `UpdateCommitteeCache`. This ensures that the validator registry has been updated so that the list of activation eligible validators matches what will be seen in the epochs to be cached.

title: More selective on marking block as bad
body:
Today when we process a block in blockchain service pkg, any error could be returned, and the node would mark the block as bad, which prevents the further processing of children blocks. The correct behavior is only to mark the block bad if it is invalid. This PR attempts to add better separation. Summary:

we want to make the block bad when
- the block itself is bad (invalid state transition)
- the payload is bad (invalid ee response)
- the block violated certain fork choice rules (before finalized slot, not finalized ancestor... etc)

we shouldn't mark the block bad if
- DB returns an error cause it cant find the parent
- fork choice returns an error because something less irreverent

title: Refactor validator accounts delete to remove cli context dependency
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Refactor/code health

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR addresses the account list code and refactors it as part of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883. It follows up on https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10554, which does a similar migration for the accounts list functionality. 

For delete it gets a bit more involved. But I am curious to hear what you think! Here is a high level of whats going on:

1. `cmd/validator/accounts/delete.go`. This is a new file that parses the CLI flags and constructs the CLI manager with the appropriate options. On the CLI manager, it simply calls the `Delete` method with the `context.Context` type (no longer a need for the `cli.Context`.
2. `cmd/validator/accounts/delete_test.go`. This is the new location of the test that was previously `validator/accounts/accounts_delete_test.go`. As written, that test is built for the CLI context interface, so if we are moving the logic for handling that to the `cmd/validator/accounts` directory, it makes sense to also move the test there. I had to copy a few helper test functions into this file to get it to compile. So for now there is a bit of code duplication. I expect this to level out as we start migrating the other CLI tests into this directory. 
3. `cmd/validator/accounts/wallet_utils.go`. This is a new file for shared functionality between list and delete (right now just has `walletWithKeymanager`).
4. `validator/accounts/accounts_delete.go`. This is where we see the benefit of this refactor. We chop out all the CLI parsing stuff from the `DeleteAccountCli` function, and make it a `Delete` method on the AccountsCLIManager pointer receiver.
5. `validator/accounts/accounts_helper.go`. I made a minor change here to separate the `filterPublicKeysFromUserInput` into two pieces for readability. I also made this function exported because we now use it in the `cmd/validator/accounts` package. Since it is still in use for files in the `validator/accounts` package, I thought it would be easier to export it for now, and then once it is  only used in the `cmd/validator/accounts` dir, we can make it non-exported again.
6. `validator/accounts/cli_manager.go` and `validator/accounts/cli_options.go`. I added a few new options that the delete function requires. As we continue refactoring we can tell which of these options are actually needed. If they are only used by a single method on the AccountsCLIManager type, then we can just pass them as arguments for that method.

LMK what you think! This one was certainly a bit more involved than the List functionality, but I still think the separation of concerns (decouple CLI parsing from the actual functions in the validator/accounts package) is a nice improvement and the readability + maintainability of `validator/accounts/accounts_delete.go` is much improved. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

This is part of the keymanager refactor defined in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883.
It is also described in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/10339.

title: Scenario End To End Testing
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

End To End Feature Addition

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR introduces a new feature for our end to end testing. Currently our end to end testing works in a best-case fashion. We run our end to end test suite with a pre-defined setup and the network that is setup is run is expected to pass the designated evaluators. This approach has been very useful in ensuring our builds are reliable and any new PRs being opened do not break anything. However while our end to end testing is very useful tool, it doesn't test how resilient prysm nodes are to faults in the network. (Other nodes going offline, validators going offline,etc). 

*Scenario Testing* introduces the ability for our e2e test runner to introduce faults in the network. The ability to do this is very much needed to test edge cases with the merge coming up. Due to the interactions between the consensus and execution node, the ability to reliably test that prysm can recover from the correctly will be important. Scenario testing now introduces the ability for our test runner to pause/resume/stop any desired process that is currently running. The ability to pause/stop a process can be used to simulate faults in the network and test for any scenarios that we want. 

We now have a special scenario test runner, this test runner is slightly different from our normal test runner in that it doesn't run with a few things enabled(new deposits, weak subjectivity sync, doppelganger checks, etc). If desired these cases can be added to the scenario runner. The reason we haven't added it in so far is for simplicity. 

Once this is merged in, we can start work on introducing a proxy for our execution nodes and use that to modify json-rpc requests and responses. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #10242

title: Do not update forkchoice checkpoints on calls to Head
body:
Currently prysm passes justification information to the forkchoice package on each call to `Head`. This allows the caller to revert finalization/justification by passing previous justification points. Consider for example the following situation
```
    Epoch N - 1        |       Epoch N

  A <-  B <-------------------- C <-- D 
            \ 
              -  E 
 ``` 
If we call Head with justification = finalization N, we would obtain D as valid head, while if we pass N-1 we would obtain E. This is not acceptable as once the forkchoice package has seen a higher justification it should not revert back.

title: add mutex for validator.highestValidSlot
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This bug fixes a potential race condition (read/write) in the validator process. The area of contention is the `validator` struct's `highestValidSlot` field.

**Explanation**

`validator.ReceiveBlocks()` starts a loop that will wait to receive blocks from the bn and processes them as they arrive. This loop [makes a write](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/20ab988a4a7b0fa8d6249751431d021a87e4ed1e/validator/client/validator.go#L361)  to `v.highestValidSlot` (validator/client/validator.go:361) which [can be read](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/20ab988a4a7b0fa8d6249751431d021a87e4ed1e/validator/client/attest.go#L257) at the same time by  `validator.waitOneThirdOrValidBlock()` (validator/client/attest.go:257). This read can be triggered when a validator publishes a regular attestation or a sync committee contribution.

**Fix**

I added a simple mutex around access of `validator.highestValidSlot`. I used a vanilla `Mutex` (vs a `RWMutex`) since there are only two reads of the field and only one of them is in a different critical region from conflicting write. 

**Other notes for review**

This was detected while running a validator client instrumented with ThreadSanitizer (compiled with `go build -race`) on mainnet-shadowfork-5. Here is the TSAN detection output for reference:

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature
related to #10593
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR builds on top of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10669

This PR provides capabilities for users to define fee recipients and gaslimit information on their corresponding validator public keys and send them to the beacon node, which will in turn call the builder APIs. These user-defined configurations are important for custom builders to distribute funds correctly and are signed by the validator key for authenticity. The information used here is similar to the prepare_beacon_proposer APIs which are sent to the execution engine, the register validator API proxies to the builder APIs.

- [x] yaml config parsing support for validator proposer settings
- [x] introduce gas limit to config file
- [x] builds register validator request
- [x] calls register validator beacon API from validator client
- [x] update unit tests


**does not include**

- register validator beacon API implementation internally ( gRPC)
- register validator beacon API externally ( REST)
- caching register validator 
- dynamic gas limit ( does not calculate previous block gaslimit and compare with default gas limit or current gas limit setting)


Reasoning why this is the correct fix. First, let's look at when these errors occur:
It occurs during services initialization
```

time="2022-05-24 16:37:03" level=debug msg="Could not process pending blocks" error="could not validate pending slots: nil checkpoint" prefix=sync**
```

It occurs in between processing deposits
```
time="2022-05-24 16:37:09" level=debug msg="Deposit registered from deposit contract" eth1Block=64 merkleTreeIndex=215 prefix=powchain publicKey=0xadeb5ccef7679c5d26e97ac5d2c8222058bf8b7c5eaebd31db3f3ecbb8d00987e2b921711dc6953eff6852601c57b198

time="2022-05-24 16:37:11" level=debug msg="Latest eth1 chain event" blockHash=0x99db28a97c08e30da0b4f592009a0b557abb0430587bf74ff29fb0230091b762 blockNumber=73 difficulty=2 prefix=powchain
```

title: Do not fill in blocks that are not in the finalized branch
body:
The function `fillInForkChoiceMissingBlocks(ctx, blk, finalizedChkpt, justifiedChkpt)` obtains from DB all blocks starting from the parent of `blk` and goes up the parent chain. It inserts all blocks with slots higher than the last finalized checkpoint plus the parent of the last such slot.

This function does not check that this last parent is the finalized block, if it isn't then the function inserts a contending chain to the finalized block and it should be declared invalid.

In addition, this function has an off-by-one in which it passes also the finalized block to forkchoice, all tests for this functions were wrongfully counting nodes adding the extra finalized checkpoint that should not have been saved.

title: Forkchoice checkpoints
body:
This is the first step towards deprecating `blockchain.store`. In this PR we let `forkchoice` package track accurate justification information and use it's own internal checkpoints to decide head. This is the first point in #10734 

Known issues: the `store` package uses `ethpb.Checkpoint` which uses a slice for roots. `forkchoice` uses `[32]byte` internally. This PR introduces a new type `forkchoicetypes.Checkpoint` which uses `[32]byte` for root. Since the blockchain package uses slices, everytime that there is an interface call between `blockchain` and `forkchoice` to request or update checkpoints, a copy will be made. This will be resolved in the third step of this series of PRs.

**What type of PR is this?**

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR addresses the account backup code and refactors it as part of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883. It follows up on https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10554 and https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10686 which do similar migration for the accounts list and delete.

1. `cmd/validator/accounts/backup.go`. This is a new file that parses the CLI flags and constructs the CLI manager with the appropriate options. On the CLI manager, it simply calls the `Backup` method with the `context.Context` type (no longer a need for the `cli.Context`.
2. `cmd/validator/accounts/backup_test.go`. This is the new location of the test that was previously `validator/accounts/accounts_backup_test.go`. As written, that test is built for the CLI context interface, so if we are moving the logic for handling that to the `cmd/validator/accounts` directory, it makes sense to also move the test there. 
3. `validator/accounts/accounts_backup.go`. Again, this is where we see the benefit of this refactor. We chop out all the CLI parsing stuff from the `BackupAccountCli` function, and make it a `Backup` method on the AccountsCLIManager pointer receiver.
4. `validator/accounts/accounts_helper.go`. I made a minor change here to add `selectAccounts` into this file from the `accounts_backup.go`. This function is only used in `FilterPublicKeysFromUserInput` (which is in this package) so we can leave the function as non-exported.
5. `validator/accounts/cli_manager.go` and `validator/accounts/cli_options.go`. I added a few new options that the backup function requires. As we continue refactoring we can tell which of these options are actually needed. If they are only used by a single method on the AccountsCLIManager type, then we can just pass them as arguments for that method.

title: API's `IsOptimistic` - update `header.StateRoot` only when block is not missing
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

We currently do this routine before checking if a blok's root is optimistic:
```
root, err := st.HashTreeRoot(ctx)
if err != nil {
	return false, errors.Wrap(err, "could not get state root")
}
header.StateRoot = root[:]
headRoot, err := header.HashTreeRoot()
```

Updating the state root is necessary only when we have a non-missing block. This is because when replaying the state (which happens earlier in the API call) for a missing block, we invoke https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/5ee66a4a683398bcda7ffc4a0db24bbe6d05f6ff/beacon-chain/state/stategen/replayer.go#L114. `ReplayProcessSlots` internally calls `process_slots`, and `process_slots` updates the state root, which means we shouldn't do it again. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #10807

title: Remove `wealdtech/go-eth2-util` dependency
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

While working on another feature, I changed the signature of fastssz's `SizeSSZ` function from `SizeSSZ() int` to `SizeSSZ() (int, error)`. After updating fastssz dependency in Prysm, I got the following build error:
```
../pkg/mod/github.com/wealdtech/go-eth2-types/v2@v2.5.2/forkdata_encoding.go:10:24: cannot use f (variable of type *ForkData) as type ssz.Marshaler in argument to ssz.MarshalSSZ:
        *ForkData does not implement ssz.Marshaler (wrong type for SizeSSZ method)
                have SizeSSZ() (size int)
                want SizeSSZ() (int, error)
```
It turns out that the `wealdtech/go-eth2-types` package contains a type generated with fastssz. While we don't use this package directly, it's an indirect dependency.

This PR moves over code from some `wealdtech` packages that is used in Prysm, along with tests. This PR removes the problematic dependency, allowing us moving forward with changes to fastssz.

title: Disallow lower justified epoch to override higher epoch
body:
Assume the following scenario:
`slot`: `95`
`current_target_balance`: `EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT`
`previous_target_balance`: `EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT`
`total_active_balance`: `100 * EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT`
`justification_bits`: `0011`
`state.current_justified_checkpoint.epoch`: `2` 

The above is an impossible scenario unless the client has a bug in manipulating `justification_bits` or `target_balance` calculations because they don't align. In an event of such, we should not allow the updating of the justified checkpoint epoch to a lower number. Prysm looks at `justification_bits` to update checkpoint whereas spec looks at `target_balance` to update checkpoint. They all work but prysm should add on an additional safety filter to disallow epoch to be updated lower than existing epoch

title: Improve Field Trie Recomputation
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature Work

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR introduces some new methods for our field tries to deal with shared states. Instead of copying each time we want to recompute a field, we instead introduce a `transfer` method. This allows us to transfer the contents to another new trie. Other states which hold references to the old trie will simply then lazily re-generate it whenever they need to compute a field. 

The reason this works is that our past state reference objects are mostly kept in memory in our caches. These states aren't used for anything else other than state regeneration in some cases or saving them to disk. Given these are infrequent occurrences, we instead allow callers to generate when they need to on the fly and avoid the full copy for our head state. 

This has a significant saving on our memory usage, our general memory usage of the beacon node has dropped 30% with this change.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

title: Refactor validator accounts import to remove cli context dependency
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Refactor/code health

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR addresses the account import functionality and refactors it as part of https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883. It follows up on https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10554, https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10686, https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10824, https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/10841 which do similar migration for the accounts list, delete, backup, and exit.

1. `cmd/validator/accounts/import.go`. This is a new file that parses the CLI flags and constructs the CLI manager with the appropriate options. On the CLI manager, it simply calls the `Import` method with the `context.Context`(no longer a need for the `cli.Context`). The options specific to the import functionality are: `WithImportPrivateKeys`, `WithPrivateKeyFile`, `WithReadPasswordFile`, `WithPasswordFilePath`, and `WithKeysDir`. Also note that the `walletImport` function handles the construction of the wallet and is migrated to this file.
2. `cmd/validator/accounts/import_test.go`. This is the new location of most of the tests that were in `validator/accounts/accounts_import_test.go`. As written, these tests are built for the CLI context interface, so if we are moving the logic for handling that to the `cmd/validator/accounts` directory, it makes sense to also move the tests there. Tess that don't depend on the CLIctx remain in the `validator/accounts/accounts_import_test.go`.
3. `validator/accounts/accounts_import.go`. This is where we see the benefit of this refactor. We chop out all the CLI parsing stuff from the `ImportAccountCli` function, and make it the `Import` method on the AccountsCLIManager pointer receiver. 
4. `validator/accounts/cli_manager.go` and `validator/accounts/cli_options.go`. I added a few new options that the import function depends on.
6. `validator/accounts/accounts_import_test.go`. I left a few tests here (which don't rely on setting up the cli ctx and just test the non-exported functions in `validator/accounts/accounts_import.go`. 

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
This is part of the keymanager refactor defined in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/9883.
It is also described in https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/10339.

title: Deprecate store in blockchain pkg
body:
In this PR we remove package `store` and let `forkchoice` track all justification and finalization information. 

It removes several functions from the `blockchain` package like `updateJustified` and `updateJustifiedInitSync`. It also simplifies considerably block processing so that functions like `handleBlockAfterBatchVerify` are removed. Justification/Finalization update is purely done on block insertion and on `on_tick` within forkchoice to be more aligned with how the spec does it. 

Future changes that are **not covered** in this PR are:
- deprecation of blockchain's `head` structure. 
- tracking of justified balances within forkchoice
- cleanup of all database accesses within blockchain when they should be handled purely within forkchoice. An example of this is already merged in #10905 


Fixes: #10734

- [x] forkchoice tests
- [x] blockchain tests
- [x] spec tests
- [x] e2e tests

**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Allows the beacon-node to exit more cleanly during initial-sync. Initial-sync can stall during exit when multiple block ranges are requested from the same peer. This happens because we fail to release the peer lock when `f.waitForBandwidth` fails (see L321 and L348) - which happens when the rate limiter kicks in while the block fetcher is being stopped.

This scenario is unlikely in a production network, but it often arises during development.

title: Define a JSON Marshal/Unmarshal Rules for Execution Block With Txs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

As part of dealing with reconstructing Bellatrix beacon blocks from execution payload headers designed [here](https://www.notion.so/prysmaticlabs/Storing-Only-BlindedBeaconBlocks-in-Prysm-Post-Merge-1aed63ab2aa94d00b96c05fbc7d69b5b), we need to retrieve full, execution blocks by hash via our JSON-RPC connection to our execution client. 

Today, we use `eth_blockByHash` requests via JSON-RPC requests. However, we do not request full transaction bodies from the execution client. To do this, we need to define a new Go struct with marshal/unmarshal rules that **can handle full transaction bodies**. This PR introduces a new struct to properly unmarshal and marshal blocks with full txs from JSON-RPC.

The logic in this PR is almost identical to the normal marshal/unmarshal rules except for the transactions field. We use an embedded struct to reduce code duplication as reasonably as possible.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #10589

title: [Feature] - Store Only Blinded Beacon Blocks Post-Merge
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In a design document [here](https://www.notion.so/prysmaticlabs/Storing-Only-BlindedBeaconBlocks-in-Prysm-Post-Merge-1aed63ab2aa94d00b96c05fbc7d69b5b), we outline how important it is that Prysm only stores blinded beacon blocks post-merge in the database. 

if we **do not have this feature,** we foresee the storage requirements of Prysm growing significantly over time. Today, the avg Ethereum block size is 82Kb. Assuming we get a block every 10 seconds, this means 492Kb per minute, or 29.52 Mb per hour. Given there are 8760 hours per year, this could amount to 8760*29.52Mb = 258Gb per year that needs to be stored in Geth *and* in Prysm. It is unreasonable to store this same data twice, which is why this feature is important for us to ship.

[https://etherscan.io/chart/blocksize](https://etherscan.io/chart/blocksize) see here for avg blocksize data at the time of writing, on July 5th, 2022.

This PR adds a feature flag `--enable-only-blinded-beacon-blocks` which stores Bellatrix beacon blocks as blinded format in our database. This will change our behavior with p2p and API requests to reconstruct full Bellatrix blocks from blinded format.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #10589

As part of working on code that uses blinded and full Bellatrix beacon blocks, we noted that these data structures are extremely similar, save for one detail: the transactions. title: Fix counters data races in async tests
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR updates the following `async/debounce` and `async/every` tests to prevent concurrent read and writes:
- `TestDebounce_SingleHandlerInvocation`
- `TestDebounce_MultipleHandlerInvocation`
- `TestTestEveryRuns`

It improves the project tests stability.

Atomic counters have also been added to the rest of the debounce tests to prevent potential data races later on.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

The `timesHandled` counter used in these tests assertions are not protected against concurrent read and writes.
When reading their values for assertion, they can be incremented at the same time in the goroutine right above.

The same goes for the `i` counter in `TestTestEveryRuns`.

When running the tests with race detection (`go test -run TestDebounce_MultipleHandlerInvocation -race -v` for example), the issue is detected.

title: Fix data race in monitoring test
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do ? Why is it needed ?**

This PR fixes a data race condition in one of the monitoring test : `TestStart`.
It uses the existing mutex to prevent this from happening.

**Which issue does this PR fix ?**

In the `TestStart` test, there's the following assertion:
```golang
require.Equal(t, s.isLogging, true, "monitor is not running")
```

But `s.isLogging` value is modified at the same time [it is read by the assertion](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/c33acde64ec230c23b0e5fceebc04ac50c20ead6/beacon-chain/monitor/service_test.go#L175), which leads to a concurrency read/write.
It happens [at the end of the `Service.run()` method](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/c33acde64ec230c23b0e5fceebc04ac50c20ead6/beacon-chain/monitor/service.go#L158). 

Using the `Service` mutex by locking, performing the assertion and then unlocking access to the boolean prevents the race condition.

title: Prysmctl Command to Request Beacon Nodes for Block Ranges Over P2P
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

We lack tooling to spin up a local libp2p host that can peer with beacon nodes and issue proper requests for data. This is important for load testing new features that depend on the p2p stack, such as #11010. This PR adds in a subcommand to `prysmctl` which allows for querying a specific beacon node peer for a range of beacon blocks over p2p. Here's how to use it:

```
go run ./cmd/prysmctl p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range --help
NAME:
   prysmctl p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range - Request a range of blocks from a beacon node via a p2p connection

USAGE:
   prysmctl p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range [command options] [arguments...]

OPTIONS:
   --chain-config-file value    The path to a YAML file with chain config values
   --peer-multiaddrs value      comma-separated, peer multiaddr(s) to connect to for p2p requests
   --client-port value          port to use for the client as a libp2p host (default: 13001)
   --prysm-api-endpoints value  comma-separated, gRPC API endpoint(s) for Prysm beacon node(s) (default: "localhost:4000")
   --start-slot value           start slot for blocks by range request. If unset, will use start_slot(current_epoch-1) (default: 0)
   --count value                number of blocks to request, (default 32) (default: 32)
   --step value                 number of steps of blocks in the range request, (default 1) (default: 1)
   --help, -h                   show help (default: false)
```

This connects to a beacon node via gRPC as well to retrieve the necessary data to handshake with beacon nodes before making proper requests for data. The tool then outputs data to stdout showing the request timing and checking if the request worked or not.

To support custom configs, remember to specify the `--chain-config-file` to the command as well. This is crucial to get the feature to work well with the Sepolia chain, for example.

Example on Sepolia:
```
go run ./cmd/prysmctl p2p send beacon-blocks-by-range --chain-config-file=/Users/zypherpunk/interop/config.yaml

INFO[0000] List of peers                                 peers="[/ip4/10.0.0.74/tcp/13000/p2p/16Uiu2HAkzUiJ2it2cCaW3kKGVDjWCxaR4YNg2ca4YQFdG1RjEZNM]" prefix=prysmctl-p2p
```
