body:
We are using the execution engine blob envelope, which has an extra `Data` attribute holding the actual blob bytes, instead of the ssz container layout the consensus specs specify. This was in spec tests because the ssz-serialized representation of a container with a single byte vector is the same as that byte vector on its own. This change cleans up the difference to remove the extra layer of indirection on the blob bytes outside of the EE API.

hat tip to @james-prysm for noticing the inconsistency in the Beacon API which led us to read through the consensus specs to confirm how the container should look.

title: Use next slot cache in more places
body:
While auditing next slot cache, I am surprised how under utilized next slot cache it is. Most of the usages are still using `ProcessSlotsIfPossible`, which can be using `ProcessSlotsUsingNextSlotCache`. There's no downside to use `ProcessSlotsUsingNextSlotCache`, with miss, it defaults back to the original behavior. 

Please look very carefully at these two things:
- I added `slot > parentState.Slot()` check to `ProcessSlotsUsingNextSlotCache`. It wasn't there before
- I have to pass in a root to `ProcessSlotsUsingNextSlotCache`. Most of the time that's just the head root, and sometimes target root. But check them carefully. Even if they are wrong, it would just be a cache miss

Here are three usages that will greatly benefit from using the next slot cache:
- `getPayloadAttribute`
- `getSyncCommitteeHeadState`
- `getAttPreState`

title: Add flag to boost local block value
body:
This pull request adds a new flag to `local-block-value-boost` that allows the local block value multiplied by the boost value. The resulting value will be used if higher than the original builder's bid value. 
(i.e `builder_bid_value * 100 > local_block_value * (local-block-value-boost + 100`)

By default, the boost value is set to 0. This means that the current behavior remains unchanged. However, if preferred, the value of the boost can be adjusted to shift prioritization to the local block

The proposed change is designed to provide greater flexibility in censorship resistance defense, allowing for more dynamic and potentially more competitive bidding between local builders and mev builders

title: prysmctl using the same genesis func as e2e
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

the `prysmctl testnet generate-genesis` command wasn't generating correct genesis states after phase0. It was trying to create an >= altair state by using the fork transition functions to advance the state to subsequent forks. The problem with this is that these methods copy the block header at each "upgrade", because in regular usage the parent block will be from the previous fork. But when the intent is for the state to be a genesis state at the given fork, the block also needs to be from that fork, so the startup code that infers a genesis block from the genesis state would come up with a block with additional fields added for the fork (`sync_aggregate` for altair, `execution_payload` for bellatrix and so on) leading to a root mismatch.

title: Replace statefeed Initialize
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR replaces the code that watches for the statefeed Initialize event with a simpler, race-free synchronization primitive based around blocking callers in a context-aware select until a sentinel channel is closed. The channel is only closed by a setter method that popualates the genesis data everyone is waiting on, timestamp and validator root. 

The returned type is also a step towards decoupling services from the blockchain service in order to determine the current slot. Instead, the returned type provides a Clock that can give the current time (Now) or current slot (CurrentSlot - which will allow it to satisfy existing interfaces).

One benefit of coupling these things together is that it allows code that uses the wall clock to begin using a synthetic clock instead, giving us a way to inject a global view on the passage of time that can move faster than 1:1 with the wall clock. This could be helpful going forward in building tests that move somewhat faster than realtime, as long as we aren't gated on other performance factors.

title: Validate gossip exit with current slot
body:
Fixes the following error:

```
Apr 15 10:56:32 nishant-NUC8i5BEH beacon-chain[284213]: time="2023-04-15 10:56:32" level=debug msg="Gossip message was rejected" agent="Prysm/v4.0.2/75338dd83d943ed5e13635cd0578c38a3b2d248b" error="expected current epoch >= exit epoch, received 194539 < 194540" 
```

When Prysm nodes validate exit messages over gossip, the head slot won't advance. Using current would cover most of the case. Another idea is to process the head state to the current slot, which might be expensive. 
Something to consider here is this might have a negative impact on processing exit messages across the fork, but the bug would have existed today regardless.

title: Use mock v1alpha1 server in Beacon API's validator functions
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Cleanup + fixes

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

There are 4 `ProduceXXX` methods defined on the Beacon API's validator server. Each of them gets the block to propose from a v1alpha1 server, which is a field of the validator server. Because preparing a proper block is very difficult to set up, the tests are very long and hard to read. The v1alpha1 server and its interface are autogenerated and we use `mockgen` to generate a mock for the interface. Therefore we can replace the type of the v1alpha1 server field from a concrete type to its interface type, and use the mock in tests.

To do this, we have to include `AssignValidatorToSubnet` and `AggregatedSigAndAggregationBits` in the v1alpha1 server's proto definition, so that these methods are available through the interface. We also can no longer use v1alpha1 server's exported fields directly in the validator server because they will be no longer available. Thus they have to be made fields of the validator server.

This PR also fixes some issues in the implementation of `ProduceXXX`:
- `ProduceBlockV2` and `ProduceBlockV2SSZ` didn't check for optimistic status
- `ProduceBlockV2` and `ProduceBlockV2SSZ` didn't handle non-blinded blocks coming from the v1alpha1 server
- `ProduceBlindedBlockSSZ` produced full (!) Bellatrix and Capella blocks

title: Don't delay att processing until next slot
body:
To reorg late block, we make subsequent bets at 10s and 12s mark by processing current slot attestations to see if we need to revert the original bet. Interestingly, `processAttestations` has this condition to delay attestation processing until a subsequent slot (spec condition):
```python
    # Attestations can only affect the fork choice of subsequent slots.
    # Delay consideration in the fork choice until their slot is in the past.
    assert get_current_slot(store) >= attestation.data.slot + 1
```

This contradicts the reorg late block methodology. To fix this, we alter the condition to the following:
```python
    assert get_current_slot(store) >= attestation.data.slot
```

Analysis of why this is ok to do:
**10s:** This is intended because we want to account for attestations at the current slot
**12s:** We may violate the condition here, but this condition is still ok because we'll unlikely receive the current slot attestation at the start slot. Let me know if this is wrong, I can fix it by using the proposed slot of the input argument

title: persistent validator settings in validator client
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
   You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA), which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.
2. Please file an associated tracking issue if this pull request is non-trivial and requires context for our team to understand. All features and most bug fixes should have
   an associated issue with a design discussed and decided upon. Small bug
   fixes and documentation improvements don't need issues.
3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to
   be updated. If you're unsure what to update, send the PR, and we'll discuss
   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

Feature


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently validator settings from `proposer-settings` is never persisted in the validator client. Instead, fee recipients and validator registrations are persisted on the beacon node. 

Downsides to the current approach.
- settings are not persisted on restart if using MEV Boost if [KeymanagerAPIs](https://ethereum.github.io/keymanager-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Fee%20Recipient/setFeeRecipient) are used to populate the settings. This is because the validator registrations will expire after 3 epochs if we stop receiving them. 
- validator settings updated through keymanager API are not immediately active, instead will be scheduled to update every epoch

With the new approach
- validator settings are saved to db in a bucket
- bucket will be overridden if restarted with the proposer settings flag, but will update if restarted with default-fee-recipient or enable builder flags.
- Keymanager APIs will save to bucket

Side Effects
Our gaslimit API was not working in the way that was intended, as it is only used for MEV-related items it will now return an error if those settings are not active or if no proposer settings exist in the first place.

**Flag/DB/API combination effects**
ps = proposer settings, vc = validator client

- no ps in db + vc started with suggested fee recipient flag (+ enable builder flag)= new ps saved to db
- no ps in db + vc started with proposer-settings-file or proposer-settings-url = new ps saved to db
- no ps in db + vc started without flags + set fee recipient via keymanager api = new ps saved to db
- ps in db + vc started without flags = validator starts with proposer settings from db
- ps in db + vc started with suggested fee recipient flag (+ enabled builder flag) = update default settings in ps in db
- ps in db + vc started with proposer-settings-file or proposer-settings-url = new ps saved to db
- ps in db + vc started (with or without flags, see results above) + set fee recipient via keymanager api = update key's values in existing ps in db


Future things to consider
- migrate persistent settings from beacon node to validator client
- delete validator registration db in favor of cache ( currently behind a flag)

There is a subtle bug with the filtering check, or actually with MultipleValidatorStatus . title: Ignore some untimely attestations
body:
When we receive an attestation for an old target, a node needs to regenerate the beacon state at that time in order to validate the attestation. Performing several of these replays at the same time is what stresses the nodes' CPUs and bloats memory usage. A node has a cache of seen attestation targets designed to address this situation. With the increase in validator sizes and the number of this untimely attestation, this cache quickly filled and forced us to replay several times in the same state. This PR implements a heuristic such that when a node receives many unviable checkpoint attestations, a node will simply ignore them if the target of the attestation is known to be old and not have been a checkpoint in any chain known to our node

This PR also made a change to validate aggregated p2p pipeline to not process slots for state used to verify selection proof and signature

title: Add `broadcast_validation` to block publishing
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR implements https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/317, which defines two new endpoints: `publishBlockV2` and `publishBlindedBlockV2`.

Things to keep in mind when reading the code:
- I implemented the new endpoints as HTTP handlers, whereas existing `publishBlock` and `publishBlindedBlock` are implemented as gRPC handlers. To make the code more manageable, it would be a good idea to call the HTTP handler directly from the gRPC handler because the only difference is an additional query parameter. This will be done in a follow-up PR.
- `rpchelpers.ValidateSync` used gRPC-specific constructs, so I renamed it to `ValidateSyncGRPC` and created a new HTTP version `ValidateSyncHTTP`.
- Consensus and equivocation validation is based on @terencechain 's PR https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/pull/12335. Comparing to Terence's code, I reduced the scope of the cache because it is only used in the validator server.
- Example JSON blocks in tests are based on the Beacon API spec.
- I created yet another set of structs in `structs.go`, but maybe it would have been a better idea to reuse the ones from API Middleware. I didn't want to do this because we want to remove all middleware code in the future.
- Both endpoints have a `oneOf` specification, which means that values representing several versions of blocks can be submitted. This makes JSON unmarshalling problematic because missing fields get ignored (as an example, a JSON representing a Phase 0 block will get unmarshalled to a Capella block without errors, but it shouldn't). To fix the issue I imported the https://github.com/go-playground/validator package to validate that fields are not empty. This package looks very useful and we can later extend validations to check for things like the length of a hex string.

4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

the `--enable-registration-cache` currently has expiration logic to ensure timely updates and regular updates to validator registrations. Although validator registrations are sent every epoch, the registration currently has a buffer of 3 epochs before expiration. If a validator client is updated to not use builder settings or there are relay issues for accepting the validator registration for 3 epochs then the registration will expire, returning to local execution.

Assuming the relay is regularly responsive for validator registrations was an error and many relays may not respond to validator registration calls in a timely manner. This resulted in users losing MEV value due to rolling back onto local execution after registration expired.

To lean on the safe side, this PR reverts the expiration logic and the cache will need to be cleared via a beacon node restart.

title: Checkpoint sync: get block using state.latest_block_header.slot
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Background: When checkpoint syncing a node from another beacon api endpoint, the current checkpoint sync code performs the following steps:
- Download the latest finalized state.
- Compute the root of the downloaded state, then fill in the `state_root` field of `state.latest_block_header` with that value. HTR the `latest_block_header` to compute the root of the block the it refers to.
- Request the block by the root derived from `latest_block_header`.

The problem with this approach is that in the case of a checkpoint on a skipped slot, the state root won't match the root used by the latest block, so the block root can't be correctly derived without undoing `process_slots` on the state. Currently we check for this situation by comparing `state.latest_block_header.slot` to `state.slot` and refuse to start a checkpoint sync when they don't match. To deal with that edge case correctly, and the general case consistently with the edge case, it's simpler to always assume the included block will be correctly retrieved by slot, which should be safe since it is finalized by definition. So this PR replaces the previous complicated block root computation with a simple request for the block at `state.latest_block_header.slot`.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #12206

title: Copy All Field Tries For Late Blocks
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Optimization

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In #10884, we added the ability for there to only be one relevant set of field tries held in memory. The main reason this was done was to not have Prysm store outdated field tries in memory as they took up a significant amount of space in the heap. 

However doing this has brought some downsides in that older states will have to recompute all the tries for the fields in the event they are used to process a new block or are being used to advance slots. This causes issues when processing late blocks as you do end up having to regenerate the whole set of tries. To allow the next slot cache to function better, we add the ability to copy all tries for late blocks. This allows late blocks to be processed in an efficient manner along with keeping heap usage manageable.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #12434

title: Proposer RPC: make `setExecutionData` better
body:
`setExecutionData` has gotten too convoluted since Capella with builder payload, withdrawal root, and bid value comparisons. This PR cleans and refactors it to be extensible to future hard fork

Today:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Check if you can use builder]
    A -->|No|B[Get local payload]
    B -->C[Set local payload]
    A -->D[Get builder payload]
    D -->|Fails|B
    D -->|Ok|E[Get local payload]
    E -->F[Get local value]
    F -->G[Get builder value]
    G -->H[Compare withdrawal root]
    H -->|Fail|I[Return. NOTE: THIS IS A BUG]
    H -->|Pass|J[Compare values]
    J -->|Builder>Local and can set|K[Set builder payload and return]
    J -->|Else|L[Set local payload and return]
```

What I propose is the following. Get local payload and builder payload outside of `setExecutionData`. Make `setExecutionData` as minimal as possible by using `getLocalPayload` and `getBuilderPayload` and pass the payloads to `setExecutionData` 
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Check if builder payload is nil]
    A -->|Yes|B[Set local payload and return]
    A -->|No|C[Get local value]
    C -->D[Get builder value]
    D -->E[Compare withdrawal root]
    E -->|Fail|B
    E -->|Pass|F[Compare values]
    F -->|Builder>Local and can set|G[Set builder payload and return]
    F -->|Else|B
```

title: Implements #11616 - EIP-3076 - Minimal database
body:
This PR is easier to review commit by commit. (Useful information are in commit message description)

**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR implements the **minimal slashing protection database**, as specified in [EIP-3076](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3076).

- [ ] `signed_attestations`:
    - [ ] During validator runtime
    - [ ] During JSON import
    - [ ] During JSON export

- [ ] `signed_blocks`:
    - [ ] During validator runtime
    - [ ] During JSON import
    - [ ] During JSON export

- [ ] Tests

In term of data, the minimal slashing database can be seen as a subset of the complete slashing database, as it has the exact same schema, but contains only the block with the maximum slot and attestations with the maximum source and target for each validator.

=> There is no need to have a database interface and 2 implementations of this interface (complete and minimal), since the minimal database can be simply handled by removing, for each validator, all but the latest message (atomically with the new insertion).

A new `--enable-minimal-slashing-protection-database` flag is defined in the validator client.

Design choices about complete/minimal interoperability:
------------
1. The validator client **cannot** start if the `--enable-minimal-slashing-protection-database` flag is set while a pre-existing complete database is found. (The opposite is possible).
2. The validator client **can** import a complete JSON interchange file into a minimal database. However, only block with the maximum slot and attestations with the maximum source and target for each validator will be imported in the minimal database. (By design, it's also possible to import a minimal JSON interchange file into a complete database, since the JSON interchange file with a list of `signed_blocks` or `signed_attestations` with only `1` element can be both considered as a minimal JSON interchange file or as a complete JSON interchange file, but with only 1 attestation/block per validator.)

Because of `1.`, Prysm validator client should provide a tool to convert a complete database to a minimal one.
Example:
```
prysm.sh validator slashing-protection-history convert-to-minimal
```

Notes about the current antislashing database:
---------------
```
"pubkeys-bucket"  -> <pubkey> -> "att-signing-roots-bucket" -> <target epoch> -> <signing root>
                              |
                              -> "att-source-epoch-bucket"  -> <source epoch> -> []<target epoch>
                              |
                              -> "att-target-epoch-bucket"  -> <target epoch> -> []<source epoch>

"lowest-signed-source-bucket" -> <pubkey> -> <lowest signed source epoch>
"lowest-signed-target-bucket  -> <pubkey> -> <lowest signed target epoch>
```

 [EIP-3076 condition 3](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3076#conditions) (attestation slashing rules):
---------------------------
Same source, different target ==> ✅
```
old attestation: S ----------------> T (whatever the signing root is)
new attestation: S -----------> T (whatever the signing root is)

or

old attestation: S -------------> T (whatever the signing root is)
new attestation: S ------> T (whatever the signing root is)
```

Same source, same target, same root ==> ✅
```
old attestation: S ----------------> T (signing root A)
new attestation: S ----------------> T (signing root A)
```

Same source, same target, different root ==> ❌ (LMD Ghost and/or Casper FFG violation)
```
old attestation: S ----------------> T (signing root A)
new attestation: S ----------------> T (signing root B)
```

Different source, same target ==> ❌ (LMD Ghost and/or Casper FFG violation)
```
old attestation:      S -----------> T (whatever the root is)
new attestation: S ----------------> T (whatever the root is)
```

Surrounding ==> ❌ (Casper FFG violation)
```
old attestation:      S -----> T (whatever the signing root is)
new attestation: S ----------------> T (whatever the signing root is)
```

Surrounded ==> ❌ (Casper FFG violation)
```
old attestation: S ----------------> T (whatever the signing root is)
new attestation:      S -----> T (whatever the signing root is)
```

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
Fixes #11616

title: Threadsafe LRU With Non-Blocking Reads for Concurrent Readers
body:
This PR adds a simple LRU cache based on [hashicorp's implementation](https://github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/blob/master/simplelru/lru.go) that adds thread-safety and makes it non-blocking for multiple, concurrent readers. This can be used by our public keys cache in order to avoid lock contention being observed on mainnet today. The modifications are:

- Adding a mutex for the items in the LRU, and a separate mutex for the evict list
- On `Get()`, spin off a goroutine to update the evict list. Because we only acquire a read lock to read the item, Get() will not block for multiple, concurrent readers, as the update of the evict list will happen in a goroutine that acquires an exclusive lock to the evict list

title: Cache next epoch proposers at epoch boundary
body:
Alternative to #12482

We have been observing the proposer at slot 0 call `GetBlock` 500ms after the slot start time. This is because `GetDuty` takes > 500ms. `GetDuty` takes a long because it needs to retrieve the epoch+1 proposer indices to fill in the proposer ID cache. Unfortunately, the cache entry for this is cold, so `GetDuty` becomes the first hit. 

To optimize this, we make refactor `UpdateProposerIndicesInCache` to allow input epoch separate from state and update the cache for the target input epoch. This is called as part of `handleEpochBoundary`

Note: This does not handle the skip slot scenario. If slot 31 is skipped, then `GetDuty` will be another 500ms. One way to resolve this is to call `handleEpochBoundary` at `lateBlockTask` with a few refactors in mind.

**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

when the current pubkeys used are in pending status it triggers a search for last active validator in the overall set to find the position in the queue. this is done for every single pub key but the last active validator index is only needed once per state. for large operators this a bit of a strain running the validator client. 
This pr moves the check for last active validator to once per call on the state and will reuse it for the validator keys. 

**note** : A major drawback on this approach, is we are introducing checking for the last active validator even if there are no pending validators ( this is only done once at least). The pros of this change may outway the drawbacks.

a binary search does not work in this case as statuses are not sorted.

In the future we may consider removing the position in queue check all together to reduce this strain.

Fixes #12457

title: Remove `handleEpochBoundary` and move shuffling caches to post next slot cache fill
body:
Review and merge #12484 first

There are a few issues concerning how Prysm updates shuffling caches (attester committee + proposer)
- Missing skip slot case. If slot 31 is missed, then the next epoch slot 0/1/2 cache usages will be slow 
- Independent of next slot cache update. This means we are doing the work twice 
- The usage of `s.nextEpochBoundarySlot` is not reorg resistant 

This PR addresses the above by removing `handleEpochBoundary` and moving the shuffling caches update function next to updating the next slot cache under a go routine. It also add an `updateShufflingCachesOnReorg` as soon as reorg is detected in `onBlock`. `updateShufflingCachesOnReorg` fills the cache based on head state

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

I've set it to 5 minutes instead of the initially proposed 2 just to give some extra time in case of higher latency or slower beacon node (happy to set it to 2 if you think this is too much).

I've removed the test `TestUpdateProposerSettingsAt_EpochEndExceeded` which was passing because of the "deadline exceeded" error during startup, not at epoch end (the slot sent in `ticker <- slot` was the second from the last so it wasn't triggering the periodical push that only happens on first slot of the epoch).

title: feat: aggregate atts using fixed pool of go routines
body:
This PR optimizes the performance of attestation aggregation, which is currently limited by CPU usage. The proposed solution is to introduce parallelization to improve its efficiency. With the use of Go routines that spun up to the value specified by `runtime.GOMAXPROCS` which represents the maximum number of CPUs that can be utilized. It is important to note that there is no need to spin up more Go routines than this value, as doing so may result in increased scheduling and context-switching time, which could outweigh the benefits of parallelization. This is gated behind a feature flag
Initial testing of the optimized code has shown significant improvements, reducing the run time from 600 ms to 180 ms. This indicates a 3-4 times speedup compared to the previous implementation.

![image](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/assets/21316537/71ff315f-ec36-4408-adae-c8fc74ab302c)
author: terencechain

title: feat(deneb): proposer rpc to handle builder flow
body:
This PR updates the proposer RPC to handle builder flow for Deneb.

`GetBeaconBlock` highlights:
- `getBuilderPayload` returns `blindBlobsBundle` to align symmetric with `getLocalPayload`
- `setKzgCommitments` takes in `blindBlobsBundle` alongside `blobsBundle` and choose accordingly 
- new helper `blindBlobsBundleToSidecars` to convert blind bundles to blind sidecars
- `GenericBeaconBlock_BlindedDeneb` gets returned to the validator client is the block is blind

`ProposeBeaconBlock` highlights:
- `newUnblinder` takes in blinded blobs to call `SubmitBlindBlock`
- new helper `unblindBlobsSidecars` to convert blind sidecars and full bundle to unblinded sidecars
- `unblindBuilderBlock` returns unblinded sidecars
author: terencechain

title: fix(aggregator): remove single bit aggregation
body:
A single-bit attestation aggregation by slot and index is useless for aggregator RPC. It doesn't aggregate the single-bit attestation with pre-aggregated attestation at 6.5s mark. It aggregates a single-bit attestation under a brand new batch, which will never be considered between 6.5s - 8s. It's best to remove it to avoid further code confusion. 
Do we care about aggregating a single bit into an existing batch? Probably not, at that point we should just aggregate attestations as they come

title: Shorten fc lock
body:
This PR removes the lock held during the whole of block processing. 

On the good side: 
- It does not lock forkchoice during consensus and execution validation which is the biggest part of the process. 
- It cleans up a little bit the order or operations on `onBlock`. 

On the bad side: 
- Code writers of the blockchain package need to remember to acquire locks appropriately. In particular, locking a function that calls the `chain-info.go` functions (like this PR wiill do) will result in a deadlock.

**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR introduces a new bucket `block-roots` to store state root to block root mapping. It is used to support arbitrary state root to block root resolution so that we can use `stategen.StateManager.StateByRoot(blockRoot)` to retrieve the beacon state.

This mapping is stored when gossip block(s) are received and verified.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Part of #12053

**Other notes for review**
- On top of unit tests, I have updated `exploredb` to check the contents of the new `block-roots` bucket manually. For all `stateRoot`->`blockRoot` pairs in the `block-roots` bucket, it retrieves the matching block in `blocks` bucket and checks if `block.Block().StateRoot()` == `stateRoot`. Command to run:
```
bazel run //tools/exploredb:exploredb -- --datadir <beaconchaindata dir path> --dbname <beaonchain db name> --command check-bucket --bucket-name block-roots --limit <num of keys to check>
```

 
- Once this PR is merged, I will submit another PR to update existing beacon APIs with `{state_id}` parameter to use the `block-roots` bucket to retrieve the matching `blockRoot` for beacon state generation.

title: Handle Epoch Boundary Misses
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug Fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In certain situations in the network, we can miss saving the epoch boundary state into our boundary cache. This can cause issues in future epochs, as if we need to fetch the justified/finalized state we end up having to regenerating it from scratch. Instead of doing that, we have now decided to add an optimization to always save epoch boundary states into our cache. 

We also handle the edge case where the incorrect epoch boundary state is saved into our cache in the event of shallow re-orgs(1 slot) at the start of an epoch. Both these cases have test cases added in along with bug fixes in the deletion of values for the boundary cache.

If we receive a new block and the block fails at `NewPayload`, the block has not been inserted into the forkchoice store, so there's enough to prune, in this case, we shouldn't prune and instead return the original error which messes with the intent of the original error

Another option is to remove `pruneInvalidBlock` usage for `NewPayload` rather than the condition

title: Move consensus and execution validation outside of onBlock
body:
This is a simpler alternative to #12561 

It moves consensus and execution validation outside of `onBlock` and acquires thus the forkchoice lock after validation. This allows for a simpler lock logic while still not keeping the lock during the bulk of the processing. 

This method also cleans up the path to parallelizing consensus and execution validation 

Locking during init sync stays the same, the node is essentially locked to do anything else while processing batches.

title: Integrate Read-Only-Lock-on-Get LRU Cache for Public Keys
body: **What type of PR is this?** > Other **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** This replaces our public keys cache used in our crypto/blst/ package #12476 to a slightly modified one that is thread-safe across concurrent readers that only acquire a read-lock instead of a read-write-lock. This is a considerable improvement, as concurrent readers have to all wait for a lock to `Get()` a public key, and is noticeable during the pipelines of multiple signature verification. This is far worse when running with a lot of subnets, for example, and shows up in pprof for a beacon node on mainnet. The LRU cache introduced is the same as before, except it has a few core modifications in that it uses a mutex.RLock for Get() calls instead of a mutex.Lock and adds greater thread-safety and nil checks. Aside from that, it still the same LRU being used as before. **Other notes for review* With the cache: paths related to public key fetching from the cache are not as visible Without the cache: the multiple aggregate verify pipeline shows up a lot in the profile as it needs public keys from the cache

title: feat: update caches when 31 is a skip slot
body:
**The problem:**
If 31 is a skip slot, we will not update caches for the next epoch. Due to cache miss, slot 0 proposer will perform poorly with an extra 500ms-1s latency incurred to block the proposal.

**The solution:**
- Refactor `handleEpochBoundary `, calling `UpdateCommitteeCache` and `UpdateProposerIndicesInCache` into its own function to be reused. Call this helper `updateEpochBoundaryCaches`
- Use `updateEpochBoundaryCaches` for `lateBlockTasks` when the current slot equals 31. This involves a copy and processing head state to 31 before feeding it to `updateEpochBoundaryCaches`
- Considered moving this to background routine to FCU faster. I didn't do this because `UpdateProposerIndicesInCache` is already a background

title: update shuffling caches at epoch boundary
body:
This is an alternative to #12651 It does the following

- It removes the updating of caches at the start of epochs (this is handled now on late block tasks)
- It updates the cache both on skipped slots 31 (at 4 seconds) and on incoming blocks 31 performing a copy in both cases. 
- It refactors the function `handleEpochBoundaries`  so that it can be used both from `postBlockProcess`  and within `lateBlockTasks` 
- Fixes an existing bug: we should update the cache with the headState, not the incoming block state. 
- Moves epoch reporting away from the hot forkchoice lock to `ReceiveBlock`. 
- Removes the variable from the service that tracks the next epoch boundary slot
- It adds some missing locks

There is the problem of the extra copy done whenever slot 31 comes late, but this is unavoidable: we never reorg blocks 31 if the incoming block is head, so even if it's late we should update the caches reflecting this.

title: only handle epoch boundary on canonical blocks
body:
This PR handles the following situations

The current behavior is this
- A block for slot 31 comes in but it is not canonical (say it's based on slot 16 for some reason)
- We do not update the NSC, but later on `handleEpochBoundary` we update the shuffling committee and this requires an epoch transition (bug number 1) 
- Later in `lateBlockTasks` we call again `handleEpochBoundary` to update the committees again (bug number 2). 

This PR removes the first call since it will happen anyway in `lateBlockTasks`. Notice that this doesn't affect the scenario when block 31 comes in and is late: 

- If it is canonical then we will call `handleEpochBoundary` at block processing. 
- If it is not, then already `lateBlockTasks` took care of it.

title: fix: update committee cache epoch + 1
body:
When we call `UpdateCommitteeCache`, we update `epoch` and `epoch+1`. If `epoch` exists, the function returns `nil` instead of `continue`. This means in the happy case, `epoch+1` never gets updated

Besides the inefficiency, here is what the real bug is:
1.) Start beacon node, at the end of epoch 1, we update the cache for epochs 2, and 3
2.) At end of epoch 2, epoch 3 is pre-cached, we skip updating epoch 4 because of the return nil 
3.) We then call `UpdateProposerIndicesInCache` for epoch 4. `UpdateProposerIndicesInCache` calls `ActiveValidatorIndices` which fills on the miss. Because epoch 4 doesn't have an entry, it caches epoch 4 and epoch 5(!)
4.) Here is the bug. At the end of epoch 2, the committee cache creates an entry for epoch 5


Another consideration is to remove fill on miss for `ActiveValidatorIndices` and `ActiveValidatorCount` but we should fill those for initial sync. It can be another PR

title: update NSC together with epoch boundary caches
body:
This PR touches two points of block processing
- moves the updating of the NSC during `postBlockProcess` towards the end of it, 
- It calls `handleEpochBoundary` in the background and in the same thread as the update of the NSC. 

This way we avoid a second epoch transition if the NSC hadn't finished by the time we call `handleEpochBoundary`. 

This is safe because:
1. The only method between `updateNextSlotCache` and `handleEpochBoundary` is FCU which does not use the NSC, hence it's safe to move the call down (notice that anyway it was happening in the background so it was unpredictable if we actually needed the NSC). 
2. `handleEpochBoundary` is only needed during the next slot as the only thing it does is update the committee caches and the proposer indices caches. Thus it's safe to do this in the background. 
3. `handleEpochBoundary` is a noop unless we are in slot 31, thus there is no problem in putting it in the same thread as the NSC update. 

There are a couple of edge cases, most notably the situation of syncing a very late slot 31. In this case we would have already updated the shuffling and proposing indices caches during `lateBlockTasks` and they are very unlikely to be changed by the late block. However, in this situation we would now **not block** during block processing. It may happen that the next slot proposer will reach its turn before `handleEpochBoundary` finished. In this scenario, we may be introducing a different behavior:

a) if head was saved on time then we will propose on top of the very late block 31 (as we do not reorg on epoch boundaries). 
b) if head was not saved that means that we didn't finished processing the block on time and we will propose on top of 30 without behavior changes.

title: Prevent Pubkey Cache From Overwhelming the Go Runtime
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug Fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In the event we fetch a pubkey from our cache we spin off a new goroutine for each fetch. However this can cause problems 
if we are retrieving a large number of pubkeys in a short amount of time ( processing a block, processing many aggregates over gossip, etc). With the active validator set hitting 700000 keys, you would essentially be spinning up 700,000 goroutines here. While the go runtime can handle many routines being spun up, pushing it to 700,000 can potentially overwhelm it and push up CPU usage. 

This PR sends all these requests to a separate goroutine in the background, to prevent a goroutine from being spun up for each pubkey fetch.

body:
When the proposer verifies attestations in the pool, it calls `ProcessAttestationNoVerifySignature`, which does 1.) verifying and 2.) processing by mutating the state. We do not need to do 2 to verify attestation for block inclusion. After capturing 50+ profiles on the proposer proposal > 250ms. The following path shows up on the majority of the flame:

![image](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/assets/21316537/82a58719-66fb-41bd-989b-b7d13bca8b24)


This PR replaces `ProcessAttestationNoVerifySignature` with `VerifyAttestationNoVerifySignature` which also cleans up the code given there's no fork difference between phase 0 and altair

title: Fix: writeBlockBatchToStream when genesis block fork version is Capella
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

prysmctl testnet generate-genesis comes with --fork flag, which allows to generate a genesis of a specific fork such as capella

Example command
`./prysmctl testnet generate-genesis --fork=capella --num-validators=64 --geth-genesis-json-in=genesis.json --output-ssz=genesis.ssz --chain-config-file=config.yml --genesis-time=1691623218
`
If a genesis block is generated with capella fork version, then the initial-sync will not work for other nodes, as the other nodes who will try to sync with the node building blocks, will fail to deserialize the genesis block. 

The node who will be sending genesis block along with other blocks to the other node who requested for the block by range will call the ReconstructFullBellatrixBlockBatch in the following line

https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/7aa043892bf5983ab41c5182fa4346846deb32da/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_beacon_blocks_by_range.go#L150

followed by the following line

https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/7aa043892bf5983ab41c5182fa4346846deb32da/beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go#L608

This line generates the empty payload for the genesis block which is of type Bellatrix without checking the version of the genesis block which could be of version Capella. 

And because of this the other node, who is syncing will not be able to UnmarshalSSZ to the genesis block and will be throwing error **invalid ssz encoding. first variable element offset indexes into fixed value data** and thus stalling the initial-sync.

Following is the exact line where the error will trigger on the other node who is trying to sync with genesis having fork version Capella

https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/7aa043892bf5983ab41c5182fa4346846deb32da/beacon-chain/p2p/encoder/ssz.go#L79

title: Fix logic for checking whether newly covered bits has at least one un…
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
MaxCoverAttestationAggregation iterate several rounds (maximum len(atts)/2), and
each round it finds 'greedy selected candidates' and updates coveredBitsSoFar.

https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/a85b4445fc6dcbc066fa375b0e77befae8b02c8a/proto/prysm/v1alpha1/attestation/aggregation/attestations/maxcover.go#L71
`xc, err := coveredBitsSoFar.XorCount(coverage)`
coveredBitsSoFar is used for checking whether newly selected candidates have at least one unknown bit. (xc > 0)
However XorCount just produces the count of different bits, not the newly included bits found from new round.

This can be simply checked using Contains method whether there's any newly included bits.

Let me provide a simple example when the new round has no newly covered bit, but
XorCount tells it has.

```
coveredBitsSoFar := bitfield.NewBitlist64(3)
coveredBitsSoFar.SetBitAt(0, true)
coveredBitsSoFar.SetBitAt(1, true)
// [0, 1, 1]

coverage := bitfield.NewBitlist64(3)
coverage.SetBitAt(0, true)
// [0, 0, 1] -> this has no unknown bit !!!

xc, _ := coveredBitsSoFar.XorCount(coverage)
// xc : 1
// xc > 0 : true (wrong decision)

contains, _ := coveredBitsSoFar.Contains(coverage)
// !contains : false (correct decision)
```

tested in play ground
https://go.dev/play/p/oPihQ1h7mmM

title: feat: save blobs to db for subscriber
body:
When we receive a blob over a subscriber, it must be saved to the DB later for `isDataAvailable` in the blockchain pkg. This allowed a beacon node to process consensus and execution checks in parallel. The beacon node should not block the processing of a block until it has received all the blobs. Instead, it should process the block as soon as it gets it. 

This PR implements the following 
- DB pkg `SaveBlobSidecar` allows merging blobs and only delete blobs if the key is older than the retention period. Removed blob index check
- Blockchain pkg `removeInvalidBlockAndState` also removes the blob for block root
- Sync pkg `blobSubscriber` saves the blob to the DB

This PR does not touch the following but needs to be discussed (separate issues?)
- DB pkg `SaveBlobSidecar` inputs a list of blob sidecars. Should this be singular? It seems to me plural is better for initial syncing and proposer. But singular is better for regular syncing. It's 2 vs. 1
- Blockchain pkg `isDataAvailable` needs to consider not all the blobs have arrived and wait / edge cases handling

title: Fix filterContained
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

filterContained is checking 'contains' between the 'last element of filtered' and new attestation from given attestation list.
So what I'm worrying is like below case.

let the given attestation list has 3 attestations and aggregation bits are like below.
(Just assumed aggregation bits are 6 bits for convenience)

attestation[0].AggregationBits = [1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0]
attestation[1].AggregationBits = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1]
attestation[2].AggregationBits = [0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0]

Here I expect all the 3 elements will be included in the final returned list, filtered.

At the first iteration,
attestation[1] will be appended because attestation[0].AggregationBits does not contain attestation[1].AggregationBits.

At the second iteration,
attestation[2] will be appended because attestation[1].AggregationBits (which is the final element of filtered) does not contain attestation[2].AggregationBits.

Like this, all 3 elements will be included in filtered list even though attestation[0].AggregationBits contains attestation[2].AggregationBits.

So this fix stores coveredBits for holding the bits covered so far during the iteration, and
use this for checking 'contains' instead of the 'last element of filtered'.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**
https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/discussions/12727

title: binary search is the wrong tool for the job, derp
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This fixes a bug in the `lowestSlotNeedsBlob` func. This method was trying to use binary search to find the first block in the sorted list that contained commitments. **Other notes for review**

DO NOT MERGE

The plan for this branch is to provide a reference point for a more reviewable deneb-integration diff - a 3rd branch `deneb-integration-remaining` is on the way, which will be set up in a PR against this branch (`deneb-integration-proto`). If `deneb-integration-remaining` diffs cleanly against `deneb-integration`, we can confidently fast-forward merge deneb-integration knowing that it has had this extra round of final review.

This will break attribution/history and likely cause a messy rebase. This is a second attempt after trying to also integrate consensus-types and gateway changes, which spiraled out into other areas of the code.

title: db: fix save blob sidecar using wrong prefix
body:
**Background:**

Bolt DB struggles with pruning, which has been evident during the development of the slasher. With the introduction of EIP-4844 in Prysm, there will be a significant amount of blob data. In the last design, we implemented a rotating buffer database schema for blobs. This schema will overwrite old data once the expiration period for blobs is reached, eliminating the need for pruning or deletion routines.

**How It Works:**

- Store a maximum of N epochs worth of blobs.
- Once epoch N is reached, overwrite the contents of epoch 0 using a modulo operation.
- Given the possibility of multiple blob sidecars per slot, a straightforward overwriting algorithm won't suffice.
Saving blobs involves:
- Convert the slot using a modulo operator to a range of `[0, maxSlots]`, where `maxSlots = MAX_BLOB_EPOCHS * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH`
- Compute the key for the blob using the formula: `bytes(slot_to_rotating_buffer(blob.slot)) + bytes(blob.slot) + blob.block_root`.
- Overwrite all elements if the incoming blob has a slot more significant than the last saved slot in the rotating keys buffer.
This PR ensures efficient data storage and retrieval without frequent pruning, thus keeping the database size bounded.


**Bug fix:**

When checking for a pre-existing blob sidecar to override (ex: if blob sidecar slot is > 4096 epoch),
it is supposed to use `bytes(blob.slot)`, which is `[8:16]`. 
The bug is it was using: `[:8]`, which is `bytes(slot_to_rotating_buffer(blob.slot))`

title: db: Log a warning if the genesis state is smaller than 1Kb
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

With the upcoming Holesky testnet and the use of git lfs, we are seeing some users hit the following
error:

```
unable to start beacon node: could not load genesis from file: version=0x363a3736 not found in any known fork choice schedule: unable to find requested BeaconChainConfig
```

This error is rather confusing and typically the user believes their config is wrong. The actual
problem is that they were trying to load a genesis state from the git lfs metadata file which is an
invalid genesis state and really small (134 bytes).

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Prysm will now log a warning just before this crash to give the user some clues as to what their
root problem is.

This PR also adds a general log "Loading genesis state from disk" with the sha256sum hash of the state. This is helpful for ensuring the state is byte for byte similar when issues occur. (Thanks for the suggestion @kasey)

```
[2023-09-13 15:27:20]  INFO genesis: Loading genesis state from disk. hash=0xcb233c7a9e94818b2f3a3a66c0bfc177103ed2e62463966d164462dce3d2a672
[2023-09-13 15:27:20]  WARN db: Genesis state is smaller than one 1Kb. This could be an empty file, git lfs metadata file, or corrupt genesis state. size=134 bytes
unable to start beacon node: could not load genesis from file: version=0x363a3736 not found in any known fork choice schedule: unable to find requested BeaconChainConfig
```

**Other notes for review**

Consider this workflow:

```sh
# User checks out the Holesky testnet
cd /tmp
git clone https://github.com/eth-clients/holesky.git 

# Then they try to run prysm without fetching / checking out the LFS files from github lfs.
bazel run //cmd/beacon-chain -- --datadir=/tmp/holeksy \ 
  --holesky \
  --genesis-state=/tmp/holesky/custom_config_data/genesis.ssz

# They see a fork schedule not found error and think that the holesky config is messed up.
# Actually, they need to go fetch and checkout that file.
cd /tmp/holesky/custom_config_data
git lfs fetch genesis.ssz
git lfs checkout genesis.ssz

# Then they can see that the genesis.ssz is 197Mb
stat -c '%s' genesis.ssz
# Prints 205677169 (bytes)

# Now prysm can load this genesis state!
```

title: Add a flag to configure blob retention epoch period
body:
Resolves #12934 

### Summary
This pull request introduces a new flag called `extend-blob-retention-epoch` that allows users to extend the blob retention epoch period beyond its default value of 4096 epochs (~18 days). This feature provides greater flexibility in managing blob data storage.

### Background
The current blob retention system defaults to a period of 4096 epochs (~18 days) for retaining blob data. While this default may be sufficient for most use-cases, some users may require a more extended blob retention period for specific reasons, such as long-term data storage or compliance.

### Changes
- Added new beacon node command-line flag `--extend-blob-retention-epoch`
- Which sets local DB variable `maxEpochsToPersistBlobs`
- Added validation to ensure the value entered is not less than the default 4096 epochs

Note, there is an existing check-in `checkEpochsForBlobSidecarsRequestBucket` to ensure retention window doesn't change across reboots unless the DB is wiped

This change aligns with the consensus spec as outlined in [PR #3350](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3350).

title: Proposer: better handling of blobs bundle
body:
### Summary
This PR refactors how `blindBlobsBundle` and `fullBlobsBundle` are managed, transitioning them from function parameters to package-level variables. Additionally, it introduces new helper methods that embed `setKzgCommitments` logic, improving the cohesiveness of payload-related operations.

### Background
Previously, `blindBlobsBundle` and `fullBlobsBundle` were passed around as parameters in multiple functions. This led to unwieldy function signatures and decreased code readability. Separately, the `setKzgCommitments` functionality was distanced from where the payload was set, creating potential issues for future development.

### Changes
1. Move `blindBlobsBundle` and `fullBlobsBundle` to package-level variables.
    - Reduces the number of parameters in several functions like `BuildBlockParallel`.
   
2. Introduce new helper methods `setExecution`, `setLocalExecution`, and `setBuilderExecution`.
    - These methods internally call `setKzgCommitments`, ensuring that it is invoked whenever a payload is set.

3. Refactor `setExecutionData` to use the new helper methods based on the execution context.

title: Block backfilling
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR implements backfilling for blocks. When a node starts from checkpoint sync, a database record is created to track the slot and root of the origin root. If `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` is an earlier epoch than the lowest slot recorded in this db entry, the backfill service will initialize and start back-filling blocks until we have coverage over the `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` span.

Note that this PR does not include deneb blob syncing, which will be implemented in a follow-up PR.

**Other notes for review**

~~This is a draft PR. I will update this section with notes on issues that need to be addressed before this can be merged.~~
- ~~clean up crufty things that are obvious for a full PR, like exported defs without comments, typos, TODOs in comments~~
- ~~peer downscoring for bad batches~~
- ~~backfill should be disabled by default while this feature is in testing. Add a flag like `--enable-experimental-backfill` so that we can merge this branch sooner without turning it on by default.~~
- ~~There are a few parameters that we want to be able to tune with cli flags. The number of p2p workers and the size of the batches are top of mind.~~
- follow-up issues:
  - [blob backfilling](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/13029)
  - [optimize for faster downloading ](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/13028)
  - [move signature checking to a single thread](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/13030)
  - [Add a flag like --backfill-to-epochs](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/13031) that allows the user to specify an earlier backfill target than MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS. [requires some ux discussion](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/issues/13003)
  
Some commentary on the design to help with review:
- `backfill.Store` exposes db methods needed to manage the backfill. A new db method has been added to update the finalized index based on imported blocks. I added the proto/dbval package for values like BackfillStatus that represent some structured data we want to store in the db. I'm ambivalent about adding another sort of protobuf dependency, maybe json would be better?
- `verifier` exploits the fact that all blocks to be backfilled were signed by validators that are present in the checkpoint sync origin state. At startup the public keys for the validator registry are copied from the origin state.
- `batch` is the unit of work for backfill. It encapsulates everything a worker needs to process it, and state information etc that other components can use to act on the results (retry, import blocks etc).
- `peers.Assigner` is an attempt to extricate the initial-sync peer selection logic to be used by other components. It is used by the backfill pool to pick the next best peer when routing a batch to be worked on.
- `pool` manages peer selection for batches and plumbing batches between the Service and the workers. It handles issues like persistently trying to find peers when one can't immediately be found, ensuring that the same peer doesn't receive multiple requests concurrently, and handling the special case where all batches have completed, shutting down the worker pool and telling the Service that everything is done.
- `worker` is the simplest component. It represents a worker loop that runs in a separate goroutine, reading from a shared fan-out channel until it receives a batch, then does the work described by that batch.
- `backfill.Service` reading the `Start` method of Service is probably the best way to get an overview of how the pieces come together. The run loop there orchestrates the overall backfill process. It uses `batcherSequencer.sequence` to populate the worker pool's todo queue, receives completed batches from the pool, updates batcher to notify it of state changes, requests importable batches from batcher, imports them, calls update with the results, rinse and repeat.

title: Fix `GetBeaconBlock` to use `skip-mev-boost`
body:
This PR fixes issue #12950 where `GetBeaconBlock` in the beacon API does not correctly utilize the `skip-mev-boost` parameter when making a call to the underlying prysm API.

#### Background:
In the beacon API, there are distinct endpoints for requesting a full block or a blind block. However, the prysm API does not make this distinction, instead relying on a `skip-mev-boost` parameter. The issue arises because the `skip-mev-boost` parameter was not being recognized or used within the `GetBeaconBlock` function in the beacon API. Here is the beacon API request:
```
v1alpha1req := &ethpbalpha.BlockRequest{
		Slot:         req.Slot,
		RandaoReveal: req.RandaoReveal,
		Graffiti:     req.Graffiti,
		SkipMevBoost: true, // Skip mev-boost and relayer network
	}
```

#### Changes:
This PR rectifies this oversight by incorporating the `skip-mev-boost` parameter. When this parameter is set to `true`, the payload construction for MEV Boost is skipped, effectively mimicking the behavior as if an override builder was applied from the engine API.

title: refactor Payload Id caches
body:
This PR breaks the duties of the PayloadID caches into two separate caches while removing a database one:
- It creates a `TrackedValidators` cache that the beacon node uses to keep track of all validator indices it's serving. It will not forget these validators while it is running. 
- It removes the validator index from the payload ID cache. 
- It does not remove the DB methods dealing with the fee recipient, however, those are no longer used and will be removed in a subsequent PR. 


The rationale is that by breaking the responsibility this way, the beacon can request a payload only when it knows that the next proposer is tracked, and then the payload ID is only saved based on the headroot. 

The VC (both REST and grpc) no longer are in charge of pruning the payload ID cache (this is now done every time the payload ID cache is updated) and they simply populate the cache when they call to prepare the beacon proposers, which happens every epoch.

title: Remove remote slashing protection feature
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

- On the validator side it is not possible to turn on remote slashing protection:
```
if ctx.Bool(enableExternalSlasherProtectionFlag.Name) {
	log.Fatal(
		"Remote slashing protection has currently been disabled in Prysm due to safety concerns. " +
			"We appreciate your understanding in our desire to keep Prysm validators safe.",
	)
}
```

- On the beacon node side, the slasher server is never initialized, and the generated grpc-gateway file never has its `Register` function called.

Because of this the remote slashing feature is currently unusable. This is by design as the feature introduces a liveness risk - slasher reporting something is slashable when it isn't. It therefore makes sense to remove the feature entirely at this point.

title: Add pending blobs queue for missing parent block
body:
This PR introduces an on-demand pending blobs queue for handling gossip blobs that arrive with missing parent blocks. The design of this queue varies significantly from the existing pending attestation queue, which operates on a timer-based mechanism. In contrast, the proposed on-demand approach is both cleaner and more efficient.

#### Summary

- **Parent Block Request:** When a blob arrives, and its parent block is missing, we request the parent block by invoking `sendBatchRootRequest`.

- **Pending Blobs Queue:** Subsequently, the blob is placed into a pending blobs queue represented as `map[[32]byte][]*eth.SignedBlobSidecar`. The arrival time is also inserted. The key for this map is the parent root of the blob.

- **Background Routine:** A background routine, `processPendingBlobs`, is initiated at startup and listens for two types of events:
  1. **New Processed Block:** Upon receiving this event, the routine checks if any blobs in the map can be processed. If so, these blobs are verified against the standard gossip rules using `validateBlobPostSeenParent` and are then passed to the blockchain service via `s.cfg.chain.ReceiveBlob`.
  2. **Time ticker (at 11s mark):** When this event occurs, the routine checks for blobs in a cache older than 12s. That means on average, a blob arrives at slot N, it will get pruned at the end of slot N+1 (11s) mark

This fixes #13004

This PR enhances blob retrieval from peers by first checking if the blobs are already present in the DB before requesting. It also includes refactoring of the `requestPendingBlobs` function to improve code clarity.

Inside `requestPendingBlobs`, the PR introduces two steps:
  - **`constructPendingBlobsRequest`**: This function constructs the request object by filtering out known indices through a db call.   
  - **`sendAndSaveBlobSidecars`**: Utilizes the request object from `constructPendingBlobsRequest` to request blobs by their root and subsequently save them to the DB.
author: terencechain

title: Check block exists in pending queue before requesting from peer
body:
Fixes an issue where redundant requests were made to peers for blocks already present in the pending queue, adversely affecting peer scoring.

#### Changes:

1. **Pending Attestation Queue**: Check if the block exists in the queue before appending pending roots.
2. **Batch Root Request**: Similar to `BlockBeingSynced`, removes the root from the request list if it's already seen.

This PR adds checks in both places for future-proofing.

title: Exit early if blob by root request is empty
body:
This PR introduces a length check for the blob request parameter at the function level. The aim is to prevent errors that get triggered and subsequently propagated upstream when the parameter's length is 0.

This check could be added at the caller level, implementing it at the function level centralizes the logic, thereby making the code easier to maintain and less prone to errors.

body:
This PR adds a test to verify that block insertion is constant time in forkchoice and that head computation is linear with the number of nodes (equivalently with the time since non-finality). title: Set Better Slice Capacities in the State
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Optimization

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In #12832 , we made appending values to slices more efficient by not having to allocate a whole new slice when appending a new value. However due to how the state transition function works along with how many deposits are included in a block, this PR optimizes this further by allocating a new slice along with the number of max deposits as additional capacity. 

The reason this is done is that we allocate a new slice in each state transition for a block. And if a block has 16 deposits, we would allocate 16 elements to each of the respective slices. However the previous slice only gave an additional capacity for one. Since this is insufficient for a block filled with deposits, this PR sets the excess capacity to be an even larger value.

Removing the cancel function would not change any outcome under the current implementation.

title: sync only up to previous epoch on phase 1
body:
When syncing to the finalized checkpoint on init sync (what we call phase 1) we sync blocks in batches until we reach an epoch that is strictly higher than the finalized checkpoint's epoch. That is, if our finalized checkpoint is for epoch 1, we skip this step when the head slot is 64 or higher. 

This PR changes this behavior to skip this step starting when the head slot is within the finalized checkpoint epoch, that is 32 in the example above. This is so that we skip stage 1 syncing during checkpoint sync.

title: Better Beacon API evaluator part 1
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Tests

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This is the first of a series of PRs to make the Beacon API e2e evaluator more trustworthy. Currently it only tests a handful of GET endpoints.

I added GET endpoints for all sections except https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator. I also didn't implement reward endpoints which are inside the `Experimental` section, but might do it in the next PR.

IRREGULAR ENDPOINT OVERVIEW

A regular endpoint is an endpoint where we directly compare responses between Prysm and LH. This list contains endpoints where this is not the case.

- [/eth/v2/beacon/blocks/{block_id}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getBlockV2) - in addition to regular comparison, we check if SSZ response is valid in `postEvaluation`
- [/eth/v1/beacon/blinded_blocks/{block_id}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getBlindedBlock) - in addition to regular comparison, we check if SSZ response is valid in `postEvaluation`
- [/eth/v1/beacon/pool/attestations](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getPoolAttestations) - only check if response is not nil because Prysm and LH might have different atts in their respective pools
- [/eth/v1/beacon/pool/attester_slashings](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getPoolAttesterSlashings) - same as above
- [/eth/v1/beacon/pool/proposer_slashings](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getPoolProposerSlashings) - same as above
- [/eth/v1/beacon/pool/voluntary_exits](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getPoolVoluntaryExits) - same as above
- [/eth/v1/beacon/pool/bls_to_execution_changes](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getPoolBLSToExecutionChanges) - same as above
- [/eth/v1/config/fork_schedule](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Config/getForkSchedule) - remove forks with far-future epoch set before comparing responses. Without this the evaluator fails because Prysm returns Deneb fork and LH doesn't.
- [/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{state_id}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Debug/getStateV2) - this endpoint will be updated in the next PR, I left it as-is
- [/eth/v1/node/identity](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Node/getNetworkIdentity) - only check if response is not nil because Prysm and LH identity will be different
- [/eth/v1/node/peers](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Node/getPeers) - only check if response is not nil because Prysm and LH peers will be different
- [/eth/v1/node/peers/{peer_id}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Node/getPeer) - this is executed in `postEvaluation`. We query for the first peer returned from `getPeers`.
- [/eth/v1/node/peer_count](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Node/getPeerCount) - only check if response is not nil, although maybe peer count will always be the same?
- [/eth/v1/node/version](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Node/getNodeVersion) - check if version response contains client name

UNIMPLEMENTED ENDPOINTS

- [/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/{block_id}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Beacon/getBlobSidecars) - Deneb-related
- all light client endpoints
- [/eth/v1/builder/states/{state_id}/expected_withdrawals](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Builder/getNextWithdrawals) - not supported by LH
- [/eth/v1/config/spec](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Config/getSpec) - Prysm and LH responses differ, but should theoretically be the same. After inspecting the resulting JSON values, it looks like both clients are missing some values. I am worried that it will be hard to maintain the response from this endpoint equal between clients. Maybe only check if it's not nil?
- [/eth/v1/debug/fork_choice](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Debug/getDebugForkChoice) - not supported by LH

OTHER

I sometimes see this error when trying to fetch the first Prysm peer in `postEvaluation`, not sure why:
> Evaluation failed for epoch 1: prysm request failed with response code: 500 with response body map[code:%!s(float64=500) message:Could not obtain ENR: could not serialize nil record]

title: Handle minor race condition when validating blobs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Theoretically, if two blobs for the same block root & index started validation at the same time it's possible both will pass validation and make it to the blob subscriber. This PR changes `setSeenBlobIndex` to check if the blob has already been seen, in a locked operation. If it has already been seen here, we can skip `ReceiveBlob` and sending the event. This couldn't have been abused because `ReceiveBlob` will properly filter duplicate indices. So this is just a cheap way to save some potentially unnecessary work.

Also, noticed that `seenBlockSize` is based on the old max number of blobs per block (4). And the worst case size calculation was incorrect, not that it makes much of a difference. It should have been 256kB.

title: Fix block proposals in the REST validator client
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

When the REST validator client requests a block from the beacon node, it always tries to unmarshal it into a full block. The correct thing to do is to request the block from the `/v3/validator/blocks` endpoint and read the `ExecutionPayloadBlinded` field in the response to determine whether the requested block is blinded or not. This allows us to propose blinded blocks. If a node does not support the `v3` endpoint, we do the following:
- execute `v1/validator/blinded_blocks` and, if the request is successful, marshal the result into a blinded block
- if the previous request is unsuccessful, execute `v2/validator/blocks` and marshal the result into a full block

**Other notes for review**

- I added a new e2e test which runs both the builder and the REST VC. Without the fix this test fails.
- I modified `getGraffiti` to always return 32-byte values. The `v3` endpoint checks if graffiti has the correct length, and our current e2e setup sends a shorter graffiti.
- I updated the validator client to use structs defined next to HTTP handlers rather than the ones from API Middleware.

title: Check that blobs count is correct when unblinding
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR adds a check to `unblindBlobsSidecars` that ensures the number of blobs in the bundle from the builder equals the number of blinded sidecars. I can imagine a scenario in which a malicious builder returns a bundle which has fewer than expected blobs. When processed, I believe this is would cause a panic when `bundle.Blobs[i]` is accessed. If you're using a good relay this shouldn't be a problem, but better safe than sorry.

Also, noticed a version check that checked for Bellatrix when it should have checked for Deneb.

title: Blob filesystem: Save Blobs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR is the first part in the new blob filesystem and is the portion responsible for saving blobs.

In order to maintain data integrity and prevent Prysm from reading a blob before it has completed writing it, we will first write to a temporary file `{slot}_{block_root}_{blob_index}_{commitment}.blob.partial` and then atomically rename the file.

Once the file has been renamed, it will be available for reads. The data integrity aspect of this implementation prevents corrupted writes in the event that Prysm is killed unexpectedly.

This PR introduces a new flag `--validator-registration-batch-size` to the Prysm validator client.

The added help line is the following:

--validator-registration-batch-size value      Sets the maximum size for one batch of validator registrations. Use a non-positive value to disable batching. (default: 0)

When activated (with a positive `<value>`), this flag will batch registration requests to the Builder API [/eth/v1/builder/validators](https://ethereum.github.io/builder-specs/#/Builder/registerValidator) into multiple, smaller requests of `<value>` items maximum.

title: Enhance Validation for Block by Root RPC Requests
body:
This PR introduces an improved validation mechanism for handling block-by-root RPC requests. Previously, when a peer responded to such a request, there was no immediate verification to ensure that the received block matched the requested root. This lack of validation could lead to potential issues where the caller might receive incorrect or mismatched blocks.

With the changes introduced in this PR, we add a straightforward yet effective check. Upon receiving a block in response to a block-by-root RPC request, we now perform a hash tree root operation on the received block. This hash is then compared against the initially requested root. If there's a mismatch, the block is not included in the return.

title: Update proposer RPC to new blob sidecar format
body:
This PR updates the Prysm Proposer RPC to utilize the new blob sidecar format. Key changes include:

- The passing of blobs has been removed. Consequently, blobs are no longer required to be signed.
- The `GenericSignedBeaconBlock` now uses `SignedBeaconBlockDeneb`, replacing the previous `SignedBeaconBlockDeneb` usage.
- The exact change applies to `GenericBeaconBlock`, aligning with the new format.
- Blobsidecar is constructed before broadcast. Opt'ed this way because of simpler code. Added a note to measure latency because this is a hot path. If slow, we can look into an optimized approach where we call Merkle root construction in the background

Note to the reviewer: blind blob signing remains unchanged in this PR
author: terencechain

title: Verified roblobs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR sets some pieces on the board for a move towards consolidated blob verification and block signature caching.
- Adds `VerifiedROBlob` type to represent blobs that have undergone full verification (signed block header, inclusion proof valid, commitments verified). This allows us to leverage the type system to specify which paths deal with unverified vs verified values.
- Add `verification` package stub with eg `verification.BlobSidecarNoop` method to fake verification. This punts the overhaul of verification to a subsequent PR so we can make progress with the type system changes first and reduce the scope of the later verification PR.
- Refactor `BlobStorage`:
  -  Add a `Get`, and `Indices` helper method.
  - Simplify on-disk storage of blob data to reduce the number of system calls needed for the most common storage operations. 
  - Wire up storage in the node init with a flag to specify the path (default to a subdirectory in bolt data dir).
  - Use afero for simplified basepath handling and in-memory test db feature.
- Replace usages of boltdb blob methods with `BlobStorage` methods. Note that these methods only deal with `VerifiedROBlobs`, guaranteeing that anything we write/read from storage is verified.
- Replace numerous instances of `DepreatedBlobSidecar` with `ROBlob` or `VerifiedROBlob`.
- Fixes to unit tests to deal with these changes.
- Simplify `BlobAlignsWithBlock` because it had a ton of unit tests that weren't relevant with block fields moved into the header, which were also tricky to port, so it was just easier to fast-forward to replacing most of those with a block root check.

title: Implement Slot-Dependent Caching for Blobs Bundle
body:
**Background:**
There's an issue with the proposer RPC mechanism in serving the blob sidecar. The proposer's duty is split into two phases: building and broadcasting the block. The beacon node first calls the local execution client to obtain the payload and blobs bundle (building phase). This blob bundle is then utilized in the broadcasting phase. The challenge lies in managing the blobs bundle's lifecycle between these two API calls. Currently, the proposer RPC uses a global variable localBlobsBundle, reassigned with each build phase. This setup presumes synchronicity between the building and broadcasting phases. It works well for sequential operations (e.g., build:100 -> broadcast:100 -> build:101 -> broadcast:101) but fails for interleaved sequences (e.g., build:100 -> build:101 -> broadcast:100 -> broadcast:101).

**Proposed Fix:**
The proposed solution is to transform localBlobsBundle into a map indexed by slot numbers. The map entries will be deleted after broadcasting. This approach introduces full pruning, which occurs only during subsequent update and retrieval calls. As well as every 6s into the slot. We don't want to prune any earlier to avoid lock contention
