title: Run payload envelope DA check concurrently
body:
When processing an execution payload envelope, the data availability (DA) check previously ran sequentially after consensus verification and EL validation had both completed. This moves the DA check into the same `errgroup` so it runs concurrently with payload verification and EL `newPayload` validation.

- The DA check only runs when the latest bid carries blob KZG commitments (unchanged behavior).
- Uses the group context (`gCtx`) so a failure in any of the three cancels the others.

This enables https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/588 to emit `execution_payload_available`

title: Prototype for SSZ-REST Engine
body:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/793 > [!NOTE] > This work assumes the devnet will start from **Fusaka** due to reducing boilerplate code. If a devnet starts the fork prior to Fusaka, the engine API won't work. This PR implements SSZ-REST Engine API, which will replace current JSON-RPC `engine_*` methods that require hex-encoded JSON encoding between EL and CL. Adding a flag(`--engine-ssz-http`) will enable SSZ-REST engine. As the following panels show, this will bring a lot of benefit including: - Payload body size: For example, a request for `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHashV1` becomes much smaller (**4.7x improvement**) in average. - Latency: For example, a req-resp roundtrip has **improved 17x** for `engine_getBlobsV2` in average. Current caveat on implementation: - `engine_forkchoiceUpdated*` method often shows poor latency. This is because 1) now CL is responsible for serialising fork choice update (See the [rationale](https://github.com/MariusVanDerWijden/execution-apis/blob/4e0fed12d3ebc9d1ca8829331a82b97b1d1bd154/src/engine/refactor.md#message-ordering--idempotency).) and 2) the current implementation in this PR uses mutex for this. We might expect better latency using `singleflight`. See Appendix for config and scripts. ### Design Principal #### Files and packages - `beacon-chain/execution/enginehttp`: Implements h2c client and wires SSZ-REST APIs. - `engine_client.go`: Now only holds interfaces like `Reconstructor` and `EngineCaller`. Didn't move reconstructor methods in this file though. - `engine_transport.go`: Defines core interface (`engineTransport`) with a wrapper for observability (`instrumentedEngine`). - `engine_jsonrpc.go`: All legacy JSON-RPC method callers are located. `jsonrpc_error.go` has util functions for handling error from JSON-RPC Engine. - `engine_ssz.go`: All SSZ-REST method callers are located. - `execution_block.go`: All `eth` namespace callers are located. #### Additional notes - `engineTransport` interface: Abstracts the wire transport for the `engine` namespace. This enables us to decouple the execution service from `rpcClient`. The service now holds two transport: `sszTransport` and `jsonTransport`. Note that `jsonTransport` is a fallback for `sszTransport` in case the EL doesn't support SSZ-REST Engine API. - Abstraction for Engine transport makes us achieve the goal without much code change outside of `beacon-chain/execution` package. - An execution service originally holds `rpcClient` and calls it with context. `rpcClient` cannot be fully removed as methods under `eth` namespace are still widely used. `jsonTransport` has a pointer to `s.rpcClient` as a primary client. - Directly calling `rpcClient` for `engine` methods is now discouraged: See refactoring for reconstructing block and payload. - `instrumentedEngine` is for observability: It observes the latency for each call. ### Plan
✅ Implementation Plan - ✅ Build a HTTP/2 client - ✅ Wire newly added [SSZ containers](https://github.com/MariusVanDerWijden/execution-apis/blob/4e0fed12d3ebc9d1ca8829331a82b97b1d1bd154/src/engine/refactor-ssz.md) for communicating with EL - ✅ Add a feature flag `--engine-ssz-http ` - ✅ Abstraction: leverage `EngineCaller`/`Reconstructor` interface. New transport will implement both interfaces, and the caller will call on the interface. - ✅ Endpoints implementation - ✅ Interop: Currently, it seems [Erigon](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/21729/), [Nethermind](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/11887) and [Ethrex](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/pull/6770) has ongoing implementation. Interop was done with Erigon at this moment.
### Appendix #### Kurtosis config (with [Erigon#21729](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/pull/21729)) ```yaml participants: - el_type: erigon el_image: test/erigon:engine-ssz-793 cl_type: prysm cl_image: prysm-bn-custom-image:engine-ssz vc_image: prysm-vc-custom-image:engine-ssz supernode: true count: 2 cl_extra_params: - --subscribe-all-subnets - --verbosity=debug vc_extra_params: - --verbosity=debug - el_type: erigon el_image: test/erigon:engine-ssz-793 cl_type: prysm cl_image: prysm-bn-custom-image:engine-ssz vc_image: prysm-vc-custom-image:engine-ssz supernode: false count: 1 prometheus_config: scrape_interval: 15s labels: variant: ssz-rest cl_extra_params: - title: Start presubmit e2e tests from a Fulu genesis
body:
The minimal and state-diff presubmit e2e tests started from an earlier fork and exercised fork transitions mid-run. Fork transitions are the dominant source of e2e flakiness: participation and sync-committee participation dip at every boundary, which is why the evaluators are full of skip-the-fork-slot workarounds.

Start both tests from a Fulu genesis so all forks are active at epoch 0 and no in-test transition occurs. Add types.WithExtraEvaluators so the BPO evaluator can still be registered under a Fulu genesis (addIfForkSet skips fork-gated evaluators when the fork epoch is 0).

title: Request parent payload envelopes in parallel with parent blocks
body:
- When filling pending block gaps, request the parent's execution payload envelope by root in parallel with the parent block by root, instead of waiting for the block stream to finish first.
- Saves one round-trip sycning to head: a child building on a full parent needs the parent payload, and previously we only requested it after`sendBeaconBlocksRequest` returned
- Replaces the per-block pending-queue slot gate with a chain-level `CurrentSlot() >= gloasStartSlot` check so the envelope request no longer depends on the block already being queued. Removes the now-unused `pendingBlockByRoot` helper.
author: terencechain

title: Queue payload attestations received before the beacon block
body:
PTC attestations gossiped before the node has the referenced beacon block were dropped (ValidationIgnore), instead of being held and processed once the block arrived. This pr adds a bounded pending queue for those attestations, mirroring the existing pending payload-envelope queue.

- Queue an attestation whose beacon_block_root is not yet in forkchoice, keyed by block root.
- At queue time, verify committee membership and signature against the current head state. The head state is not authoritative for the missing block's branch, so a committee miss, or a committee the head state cannot compute, is ignored and dropped rather than rejected, which avoids penalizing peers. An invalid signature is still rejected, since the validator key is authoritative once the index is confirmed in the head PTC. Only attestations that pass both checks are queued.
- Request the missing block by root.
- Drain when the block is processed (both the gossip block subscriber and the pending-blocks queue), re-checking the block-slot match, then process and re-broadcast.
- Stale entries pruned every slot.

title: Move state defragmentation off the block-import hot path
body:
Closes #16700.

`ReceiveBlock` called `s.defragmentState(postState)` synchronously right before taking the forkchoice write lock; defragmentation walks the whole state tree and added directly to block-import latency.

This moves it into a goroutine that runs after the block is fully imported. It is intentionally placed after the synchronous import work rather than simply wrapping the original call in `go` — a goroutine at the original site would contend with `postBlockProcess` on the state lock and merely relocate the latency.

Safety: `Defragment()` takes the state's write lock and only mutates the given state object's own multi-value-slice references (each shared slice is itself `RWMutex`-guarded), so it is safe to run concurrently with readers of the now-imported state. One behavioral note: `StateGen.SaveState` now persists the pre-defrag state, which is harmless since the serialized form is flattened regardless; the in-memory head object is still compacted.

Verified with `go build ./beacon-chain/blockchain/...` and `go test -tags develop -run ReceiveBlock ./beacon-chain/blockchain/`.

The sibling hot-path defrag cases (#16702 / #16691 / #16692) can follow the same pattern in separate PRs if you'd like.

body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`go fix` is a static analyzer introduced in Go 1.26 which automatically scans and silently changes the codebase. ([Blog](https://go.dev/blog/gofix))

Available analyzers (version: 1.26.4):

```
    any          replace interface{} with any
    buildtag     check //go:build and // +build directives
    fmtappendf   replace []byte(fmt.Sprintf) with fmt.Appendf
    forvar       remove redundant re-declaration of loop variables
    hostport     check format of addresses passed to net.Dial
    inline       apply fixes based on 'go:fix inline' comment directives
    mapsloop     replace explicit loops over maps with calls to maps package
    minmax       replace if/else statements with calls to min or max
    newexpr      simplify code by using go1.26's new(expr)
    omitzero     suggest replacing omitempty with omitzero for struct fields
    plusbuild    remove obsolete //+build comments
    rangeint     replace 3-clause for loops with for-range over integers
    reflecttypefor replace reflect.TypeOf(x) with TypeFor[T]()
    slicescontains replace loops with slices.Contains or slices.ContainsFunc
    slicessort   replace sort.Slice with slices.Sort for basic types
    stditerators use iterators instead of Len/At-style APIs
    stringsbuilder replace += with strings.Builder
    stringscut   replace strings.Index etc. with strings.Cut
    stringscutprefix replace HasPrefix/TrimPrefix with CutPrefix
    stringsseq   replace ranging over Split/Fields with SplitSeq/FieldsSeq
    testingcontext replace context.WithCancel with t.Context in tests
    waitgroup    replace wg.Add(1)/go/wg.Done() with wg.Go
```

It turns out `//beacon-chain/sync/initial-sync:` wastes over 10 seconds just for waiting *something* to happen. With `synctest`, we can advance when the goroutine is *durably* blocked (not including I/O, for example).

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

As most of the diff includes whitespaces, so I'd recommend to toggle "hide whitespace" option when you're trying to review this PR in Github UI.

Use this command for the numbers that suggested above:

```
$ bazel test //beacon-chain/sync/... \
  --test_filter="TestService_InitStartStop|TestService_Start_DoesNotMarkSyncedWhenStillBehindInSameEpoch|TestService_waitForStateInitialization|TestService_markSynced|TestExpirationCache_PruneOldBlocksCorrectly" \
  --nocache_test_results
```

Note that there are tons of spots that `synctest` can be leveraged in our `beacon-chain/sync` code, but I think I need to setup testing helpers to simulate. Reference: https://go.dev/blog/synctest#testing-networked-code

title: Hook up payload attestation message in fork choice spec tests
body:
The gloas `on_payload_attestation_message` fork choice spec tests were silently passing because the runner's `Step`/`Check` types had no fields for `payload_attestation_message` steps or the `payload_timeliness_vote` / `payload_data_availability_vote` checks, so YAML unmarshalling silently dropped both.

  - Add `payload_attestation_message` step support: unmarshals the message and feeds it through `ReceivePayloadAttestationMessage`, asserting acceptance/rejection per the step's`valid` field
  - Add `payload_timeliness_vote` / `payload_data_availability_vote` check support, comparing the per-seat PTC vote bitvectors in forkchoice (`null` = no vote, `true`/`false` = recorded value)
  - Add a `PTCVotes` getter on the doubly-linked-tree forkchoice to expose the vote bit vectors
  - Convert the skip list to `map[string]string` so each skip logs its rationale

  With the steps actually wired up, 2 of 7 test cases pass (`from_block`, `not_ptc_member`). The remaining 5 are skipped with rationales:

  | Test | Reason |
  |---|---|
  | `valid`, `multiple_ptc_members_vote_independently` | PTC votes are only recorded at the validator's first committee seat [consensus-specs#5222](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5222) requires recording at every duplicate seat (balance-weighted committee) |
  | `current_slot_and_signature` | Signature and current-slot checks live in gossip validation (`validate_payload_attestation.go`), not the fork choice handler |
  | `unknown_block_root` | Unknown block root check lives in gossip validation (`VerifyBlockRootSeen`) |
  | `slot_mismatch` | Block slot match check lives in gossip validation (`VerifyBlockSlotMatches`) |

title: Harden Gloas pending data column queue against penalty-free flooding
body:
The problem:
  Today a peer can flood the gloas pending data-column queue for cheap:
  - Columns for a not-yet-seen block root are queued unverified and the validator returns ValidationIgnore, which doesn't propagate or penalize. So flooding costs the attacker nothing at ingest time.
  - The deferred check (processPendingGloasColumns) applied just one downscore per peer, no matter how many bad columns they sent.
  - Columns queued for a root that never showed up were never penalized at all.

  Make the penalties proportional to the abuse:
  1. Downscore per bad column.
  2. Penalize stale roots at prune time, that is roots never had block

title: Test-only flag to simulate partial EL blobs in kurtosis
body:
## What changed

Adds a hidden, test-only beacon node flag `--simulate-partial-el-blobs` (commit "drop blobs if flag is enabled"):

- When enabled, the node drops a subset (~half) of the blobs returned by `engine_getBlobs`, so the missing cells must be recovered from peers via the partial data column protocol.
- The drop is applied on both the engine client fetch path (`beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go`) and the proposer path (`beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator/proposer.go`), with corresponding handling in the partial data column broadcaster.
- The flag is `Hidden` and logs a warning when enabled — it is for kurtosis/devnet simulation only, not for production use.

## Why

To exercise the peer-to-peer partial-column cell exchange path from #16733 in kurtosis simulations: with all blobs available locally via `engine_getBlobs`, the partial-message recovery path never triggers. Dropping blobs artificially forces nodes to fetch the missing cells from peers, validating the partial data column dissemination end to end.

## Notes for reviewers

- This PR targets `partialmsg-gloas-integration` (the branch behind #16733) rather than `develop`, so the diff is scoped to the simulation change only.
- Test/debug tooling only — no changelog fragment, since the changelog check applies to PRs targeting `develop`.

title: Remove bazel
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

## Bazel ==> Go-toolchain Migration Plan

Goal: remove Bazel entirely from Prysm, replacing each task with the Go toolchain
where possible, and Docker / small purpose-built Go tools where not.


### How the tricky mechanisms work today (so we can replicate them)

#### SSZ codegen + network variants
- `.proto` files contain template placeholders (e.g. `{block_roots.size}`).
- `proto/ssz_proto_library.bzl` holds two dicts, `mainnet` and `minimal`, and does text
  substitution on the `.proto` before compilation (`ssz_proto_files` rule).
- After protoc produces `*.pb.go`, the `ssz_gen_marshal` rule (`tools/ssz.bzl`) runs
  `fastssz/sszgen` over the package to emit `*.ssz.go`.
- `bazel build --config=minimal` sets **both** `--//proto:network=minimal` and the Go
  build tag `minimal` (`.bazelrc:30-31`).
- Hand-written variant files already use Go build tags today:
  `sync_committee_{mainnet,minimal}.go`, `config/fieldparams/minimal.go`, etc.
- **Only the mainnet `*.ssz.go` is committed.** Minimal is regenerated on the fly by
  Bazel. This is the one real design gap for a pure-Go flow (Phase 2).

#### Proto plugins
- Custom compiler `protoc-gen-go-cast` (+ `_grpc`) supports the `(ext.cast_type)` options
  used throughout the protos. A normal Go protoc plugin (installable via `go install`).

#### nogo
- One Bazel-internal binary running staticcheck + golang.org/x/tools passes + ~30 custom
  analyzers in `tools/analyzers/`. Config/exclusions in `nogo_config.json`.

#### Phase 1 — Makefile creation + code generation without Bazel

Scaffolding:
- Add the root `Makefile` as the new task entrypoint. It starts with **only the `gen`
  target** (+ `gen-proto`/`gen-ssz`/`gen-mocks`), wired to the `tools/cmd/gen` orchestrator.

Code generation: A Go orchestrator (`tools/cmd/gen`, buildable with the Go toolchain),
replacing `hack/update-go-pbs.sh`, `hack/update-go-ssz.sh`, `hack/update-mockgen.sh`:
1. **Template substitution**: port the `mainnet`/`minimal` dicts from
   `proto/ssz_proto_library.bzl` into Go and expand the `{...}` placeholders in `.proto`
   into a temp dir. Generator must support **both** dicts now.
2. **Proto compile**: `protoc` with local plugins — `go install protoc-gen-go-cast@<pin>`,
   `protoc --go-cast_out=… --go-cast-grpc_out=…` (google/api include path resolved from
   vendored `third_party/googleapis`).
3. **SSZ compile**: `fastssz/sszgen` per package over the generated `*.pb.go`, honoring the
   per-package `objs`/`exclude_objs` lists currently in each `BUILD.bazel` (ported into
   generator config). Strip the `// Hash:` line.
4. **Mocks**: `mockgen` (optionally via `//go:generate`).

Tooling: **`protoc` + plugins driven by a Go orchestrator** (not `buf` — the pre-compile
template substitution doesn't fit buf's in-place model cleanly).

go.mod `tool` block gains: sszgen, mockgen, goimports (+ the protoc-gen-go-cast pin).

**Acceptance / baseline (verification, not a commit artifact):** before starting, capture
`bazel`-regenerated `*.pb.go`/`*.ssz.go` as golden; regenerated files must be
byte-identical to the committed Bazel-generated ones.

## Phase 2 — Build & version stamping + minimal/mainnet as a pure Go build tag
**Commit:** "Phase 2: go build + version stamping + minimal/mainnet build tags"

Build & stamping:
- Add the Makefile `build` target — `go build` for all binaries (beacon-chain, validator,
  prysmctl, client-stats, tools).
- Replace `--stamp`/`workspace_status.sh` with
  `-ldflags "-X .../runtime/version.gitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD) -X …=$TAG -X …=$DATE"`
  pointed at the existing stamped vars in `runtime/version` (today fed by a Bazel
  `version_file` genrule).
- `-trimpath` + fixed ldflags for reproducibility.
- PGO: pass `-pgo=pprof.beacon-chain.samples.cpu.pb.gz` (native Go PGO, replaces Bazel's
  `pgoprofile`).

Minimal vs mainnet (the one genuine design change — Go can't regenerate mid-build):
- **Commit both variants behind build tags.** Run Phase 1's orchestrator with both dicts
  and commit `*.ssz.go` for mainnet (`//go:build !minimal`) and the ~13 minimal files
  (`//go:build minimal`). `go build` = mainnet; `go build -tags=minimal` = minimal —
  matching the existing hand-written tagged files.
- Golden-diff the committed minimal files against `bazel build --config=minimal` output.

## Phase 3 — Tests, spec tests, e2e
**Commit:** "Phase 3: tests, spec tests and e2e under go test"

- **Unit tests** (`build/test` → `make test`): gotestsum, mainnet + minimal passes
  (`-tags=develop` / `develop,minimal`), flake reruns, `mode=race`. go.mod `tool` += gotestsum.
- Makefile targets added this phase: `test`, `testdata`, `e2e`.
- **Spec tests**: `build/externaldata` replaces `download_spectests.bzl` (same
  `v1.7.0-alpha.8` pins, sha256-verified, lazy + `make testdata` eager). Add the pure-Go
  `build/bazel` runfiles helper here (`non_bazel.go` — resolves vectors, fetch-on-miss);
  its `//go:build bazel` rules_go wrapper stays until Phase 9. Spec tests run inside the
  `make test` passes.
- **E2E** (`build/e2e` → `make e2e [kind]`):
  - Import swap: `testing/endtoend/{components,params}` import Prysm's `build/bazel` instead
    of `rules_go/go/tools/bazel` (same `FindBinary`/`Runfile`/`TestTmpDir` API; resolves
    from `$PRYSM_BIN` then `dist/`). `E2E_LOG_PATH` fallback added.
  - `build/e2e` builds the launched binaries (`beacon-chain`, `validator`, `bootnode` —
    `-tags=minimal` for minimal scenarios) + `geth`, provisions `lighthouse`/`web3signer`
    when needed, then `go test -tags=develop[,minimal] -run <Test> ./testing/endtoend`
    with `PRYSM_BIN=dist`.
  - External binaries (`lighthouse v7.0.0-beta.0`, `web3signer 25.9.1`) ported from
    `testing/endtoend/deps.bzl` into `build/externaldata` as opt-in (out of `FetchAll`).
  - **Teardown safeguard:** `build/e2e` pkills stale devnet binaries before start and runs
    each scenario in its own process group, killed on exit/SIGINT/SIGTERM (Bazel got this
    free from its sandbox process-wrapper).
  - Suites map 1:1 to the old Bazel `test_suite`s:
    `make e2e presubmit|postsubmit|scenario_tests`, plus single scenarios
    (`minimal builder web3signer slasher slashing scenario postmerge statediff mainnet multiclient`).
  - `testing/endtoend` stays excluded from `make test` (heavy).
- Fix the Makefile `$(POSITIONAL):` ordering bug (must sit after `TEST_KINDS`/`E2E_KINDS`).

Note: this phase depends only on `go build`/`go test` for the host — **not** on Phase 4
cross-compilation — so it correctly precedes it. It does depend on Phase 2's `-tags=minimal`.

## Phase 4 — CGO cross-compilation
**Commit:** "Phase 4: cross-compilation via zig / osxcross / mingw"

No new Makefile target — cross-compilation is a `platforms=` flag on the existing `build`
target: `make build platforms=all` (+ `tools/cross-toolchain/install-zig.sh`). Five
distributed run-targets (linux/{amd64,arm64}, darwin/{amd64,arm64}, windows/amd64) for the
shipped set (beacon-chain, validator, client-stats, prysmctl — **not** bootnode).

CGO surface: **blst** (C), **herumi `bls-eth-go-binary`** (prebuilt C++ static libs,
imported unconditionally by `crypto/bls/bls.go`), a small **prometheus/client_golang**
darwin mach cgo file. `gohashtree` is pure Go + Go-asm (not cgo). The herumi C++ libs +
darwin mach headers are what break full hermeticity.

Single Linux x86_64 host builds all five (as Bazel's RBE worker did). `make build
platforms=all` auto-provisions each toolchain via idempotent scripts under
`tools/cross-toolchain/`: `install-zig.sh` (pinned **0.14.1**, user cache), `install-mingw.sh`
(gcc+g++ mingw-w64, POSIX threads), `install-osxcross.sh` (osxcross, MacOSX12.3 SDK). Linux
targets use zig and build from any host (incl. macOS); darwin/windows need a Linux host.

Per-OS toolchain:
```
linux   amd64  CC="zig cc -target x86_64-linux-gnu.2.31"
linux   arm64  CC="zig cc -target aarch64-linux-gnu.2.31"  CGO_CFLAGS+=-ftree-vectorize -funsafe-math-optimizations -fomit-frame-pointer
darwin  amd64  CC="o64-clang"               # osxcross, MacOSX12.3 SDK
darwin  arm64  CC="oa64-clang"              # osxcross, MacOSX12.3 SDK
windows amd64  CC="x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc"  # mingw-w64; zig windows-gnu can't link herumi's libstdc++
```
- glibc 2.31 pinned via the `.2.31` triple suffix (Bazel's Ubuntu-20.04 baseline).
- `-march=armv8-a` dropped (aarch64 baseline; `zig cc` rejects the name).
- **blst:** `-D__BLST_PORTABLE__` by default (matches Bazel's shipped portable images); the
  `…-modern-…-amd64` artifact omits it (ADX, x86-only).
- Path to full hermeticity: dropping the unconditional herumi import lets windows build
  under zig; darwin still needs osxcross/macOS for the prometheus mach cgo.

## Phase 5 — Docker / OCI images
**Commit:** "Phase 5: Docker/OCI images via buildx"

No new Makefile target — Docker is a `docker=true` flag on the existing `build` target.
Replace `rules_oci` + `prysm_image.bzl` with one parameterized multi-stage Dockerfile
(`tools/docker/Dockerfile`) + `docker buildx`, driven by `make build docker=true [push=true]`
(the `build/docker` command). Images embed the portable binaries from Phase 4.
- Faithful base: final stage `FROM` the pinned `gcr.io/.../distroless/cc-debian11@sha256:55a5…`,
  with a `rootfs` builder (`debian:bullseye-slim`) that downloads+verifies+extracts the exact
  Debian-11 userland via `tools/docker/debian-pkgs.sh` (port of `tools/image_deps.bzl`; fixes
  the latent arm64 `libtinfo6` `deb11u1`→`deb11u2` bug), writes `/etc/passwd` (root+nonroot),
  and the `/bin/sh`→bash, `/app/cmd/<bin>/<bin>`→`/<bin>`, `/entrypoint`→`/<bin>` symlinks.
- Images (unchanged set): beacon-chain, validator, prysmctl. Tags faithful to Bazel:
  beacon-chain → `$TAG` **and** `$TAG-portable`; validator → `$TAG`; prysmctl → `$TAG`.
  Repos `gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/{beacon-chain,validator,cmd/prysmctl}`;
  `org.opencontainers.image.source` label preserved.
- `docker=true` builds host-arch and `--load`s locally; `push=true` builds the
  linux/amd64+arm64 manifest and `--push`es (auto-creates a `docker-container` buildx builder).
  `mode=dev` (fast/unstripped) vs `mode=release` (stamped/stripped/PGO).
- Self-contained root `Dockerfile` for one-command dev builds (`docker build . -t <name>`,
  `--build-arg BIN=…`) compiling in-container with the pinned zig toolchain.
- Replaces `hack/build_and_upload_docker.sh` (rewritten in Phase 8, deleted in Phase 9).

## Phase 6 — `.deb` packaging
**Commit:** "Phase 6: .deb packaging via nfpm"

Add the Makefile `deb` target. Replace `rules_pkg` (`pkg_deb`/`pkg_tar`) with **`nfpm`**
(go.mod `tool` block, `go tool nfpm`), driven by `make deb` (the `build/deb` + `build/debpkg`
commands, mirroring `build/docker`⇄`build/crossbuild`).
- Packages (unchanged): `prysm-beacon-chain`, `prysm-validator` — one `nfpm.yaml` each at
  `beacon-chain/package/` / `validator/package/`, reusing the existing config YAML, systemd
  unit, `preinst.sh`/`postinst.sh` verbatim.
- Faithful layout (byte-checked vs old `pkg_deb`): `/usr/bin/<bin>` (0755),
  `/etc/prysm/<bin>.yaml` (0640, `type: config` → conffile),
  `/usr/lib/systemd/system/prysm-<name>.service` (0640); same name/description/maintainer/
  homepage; no depends/prerm/postrm. Version = `GIT_TAG` with leading `v` stripped
  (`version_schema: none`).
- **Build both amd64 + arm64** (Bazel shipped amd64 only) — free, Phase 4 already cross-builds
  both linux binaries. Output `dist/prysm-{beacon-chain,validator}_<ver>_{amd64,arm64}.deb`.
- nfpm gotcha: content `src`/`dst` are env-expanded only with `expand: true` on that entry.

## Phase 7 — Static analysis (nogo → standalone vettool)
**Commit:** "Phase 7: static analysis via prysm-vet multichecker"

Add the Makefile `lint` target. Replace `nogo` with a single `multichecker` binary
(`tools/cmd/prysm-vet`, from `golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/multichecker`), run via
`make lint` (`go run ./tools/cmd/prysm-vet ./...`).
- Faithful analyzer set (ported from `BUILD.bazel:69-273`): all custom analyzers under
  `tools/analyzers/` (18 top-level + 17 `modernize/*`; `modernize/newexpr` + `/slicesdelete`
  disabled), the enabled `x/tools/.../passes/*` (40 + `composite`/`lostcancel`;
  `cgocall`/`fieldalignment`/`shadow` omitted), and all `staticcheck` SA\* **except SA1019**.
  honnef + x/tools version-pinned → deterministic set.
- Exclusions reproduced from `nogo_config.json`, read at runtime (default `nogo_config.json`,
  override `PRYSM_VET_CONFIG`). Each analyzer's `Run` is wrapped to filter `pass.Report` by
  per-analyzer `only_files`/`exclude_files` regexes (exclude wins, then only restricts).
- First-party guard: drop any diagnostic under `$GOMODCACHE`/`GOROOT` (nogo's `external/.*`
  exclusions are no-ops in the module world).
- Standalone multichecker, not a `-vettool` (a unitchecker can't read a central config cleanly).
- `golangci-lint` + `gosec` remain separate CI steps, unchanged.
- Includes a small commit-companion: any in-tree lint findings surfaced by prysm-vet that
  Bazel's nogo also flagged are fixed here.
- **`nogo_config.json` is retained** as prysm-vet's config — do not delete it in Phase 9.

## Phase 8 — CI/CD rewiring
**Commit:** "Phase 8: CI/CD rewiring (GitHub Actions + hack scripts)"

GitHub Actions (the only in-repo CI):
- `check-generated-go.yml`: drop `bazelisk`; install pinned `protoc` (21.7) and run `make gen`
  then `git status` exit-1. (sszgen/mockgen/goimports run from the module; googleapis vendored.)
- `go.yml`: add a `vet` job running `make lint` (portable-blst cgo flag). golangci-lint,
  gosec, `go build ./...`, fuzz, gomodtidy stay.
- New `e2e.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` (default `presubmit`) + nightly cron, `make e2e <target>`
  on linux/amd64 with Go + Java + portable-blst cgo.
- New `release.yml`: on `v*` tag + dispatch. `artifacts` job → `make build platforms=all
  mode=release` + `make deb`, upload to the GH Release via `gh`. `docker` job →
  `hack/build_and_upload_docker.sh <tag>`, gated on a new `GCR_SA_KEY` secret.
- Unit tests stay in Buildkite (no GHA test job).

Bazel-based `hack/` scripts the Buildkite pipeline calls — rewritten Bazel-free:
- `spectest-report.sh`: `bazel test //testing/spectest/...` → `go test` over
  general+mainnet (`-tags=develop`) and minimal (`-tags=develop,minimal`).
- `build_and_upload_docker.sh`: 5 `bazel run …push_oci_image` → one
  `make build docker=true push=true mode=release DOCKER_TAG=<tag>`.
- `ci-coverage.sh`: `bazel coverage //...` → `go test -coverprofile` over mainnet+minimal,
  merged with `go run ./tools/gocovmerge`, then deepsource + `hack/codecov.sh`.

**Out-of-repo (cannot be a commit):** Buildkite's web-UI pipeline must be edited manually —
`bazel test //...` → `make test`; stop running `hack/check_gazelle.sh` (the generated-code
gate is now the GHA `check-generated-go` job); spec/coverage/docker steps call the rewritten
scripts above.

## Phase 9 — Delete Bazel
**Commit:** "Phase 9: delete Bazel"

Bazel fully removed; Go toolchain + `make` is the only build system.
- Delete all **465 `BUILD.bazel`** + 3 bare `BUILD` + all **17 `*.bzl`**
  (`deps.bzl`, `distroless_deps.bzl`, `proto/ssz_proto_library.bzl`, `tools/*.bzl`,
  `tools/go/def.bzl`, `third_party/herumi/herumi.bzl`, cross-toolchain `*.bzl`, …).
- Delete root Bazel files: `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, `MODULE.bazel.lock`, `.bazelrc`,
  `.bazelversion`, `.buildkite-bazelrc`, `bazel.sh`, `build/bazelrc/`, and the Bazel-only CI
  scripts (`hack/check_gazelle.sh`, `hack/workspace_status*.sh`).
- Delete `tools/nogo_config/` and `build/bazel/{bazel,bazel_test}.go` (the `//go:build bazel`
  rules_go runfiles wrapper) — the only Go importers of `bazelbuild/rules_go`; drop that dep
  via `go mod tidy`. The pure-Go `build/bazel` helper stays (now with no build tag).
- **Dependents fixed:** `check-specrefs.yml` reads the spec version from
  `build/externaldata/externaldata.go` (was `WORKSPACE`); `CODEOWNERS` drops `*.bzl`/`deps.bzl`
  lines; docs that gave `bazel run/build/test` instructions are converted to `go run`/`make`:
  `INTEROP.md`, `DEPENDENCIES.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
  `testing/spectest/README.md`, `tools/cross-toolchain/README.md`, several `tools/*/README.md`.
- **Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry** under Changed/Removed recording the Bazel→Make migration.
- **Kept** (NOT Bazel-only): `nogo_config.json`, `tools/cross-toolchain/*.sh`,
  `tools/gocovmerge`, the rewritten `hack/{spectest-report,build_and_upload_docker,ci-coverage}.sh`,
  `build/`.
- Verify: `git ls-files '*.bzl' '*BUILD.bazel'` empty; `go build ./...` + `go test ./build/...`
  green; `go.mod` no longer lists `bazelbuild/rules_go`;
  `make {build,test,gen,lint,deb,e2e}` all dispatch.
- Remove `hack/update-{go-pbs.sh,go-ssz.sh,mockgen.sh}`

---

## Gaps / things easy to forget

Nothing in the original 11-phase plan is *dropped* by the 9-phase regrouping, but these are
not visible in the 9-line phase list and must be tracked:

1. **`CHANGELOG.md` entry** — the original plan never mentioned it; Prysm ships release notes
   from CHANGELOG.md. Land it in Phase 9.
2. **Doc + CODEOWNERS + `check-specrefs.yml` updates** — folded into Phase 9 (delete); they
   are the long tail of `bazel …` references. (INTEROP.md is one of them.)
3. **`go.mod` `tool` block is distributed across phases** — codegen tools land in Phase 1,
   gotestsum in Phase 3, nfpm in Phase 6, the prysm-vet libs in Phase 7. Each commit must
   still `go build`/`go test`; add a tool only in the phase that first uses it.
4. **Buildkite UI changes are out-of-repo** — Phase 8's commit only covers GitHub Actions +
   `hack/` scripts; the Buildkite web-UI pipeline edits happen outside git and won't appear
   in any commit.
5. **Phase 1 golden-reference baseline is a verification step, not a commit** — capture Bazel
   outputs and byte-diff against the new codegen; nothing committed, but it gates Phases 1–2.
6. **Generator/output split across Phases 1–2** — Phase 1 must already teach `tools/cmd/gen`
   the minimal dict even though the minimal `*.ssz.go` files are only committed in Phase 2.

## Commit-partitioning strategy (one commit per phase)

The 19 commits on `remove-bazel-origin` interleave codegen/test/lint work and do **not**
align to these 9 boundaries. Do **not** cherry-pick them. Instead, treat the *final tree* of
`remove-bazel-origin` as the target and re-partition its cumulative diff vs `develop` by
file-set into the 9 commits above:
- Phases 1–8 are additive (new `Makefile`, `build/`, `tools/cmd/*`, `tools/docker/`,
  `*/package/nfpm.yaml`, `.github/workflows/*`, rewritten `hack/*.sh`) plus a handful of
  `.go` edits (the minimal-tag SSZ split → P2, the e2e import swap → P3, prysm-vet lint
  fixes → P7). They coexist with the still-present Bazel files.
- Phase 9 is the only deletion commit.
- After staging each phase's file-set, confirm `go build ./...` + the phase's own `make`
  target are green before committing, so every commit is independently shippable.

## Risk register
| Area | Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Proto codegen | byte drift vs Bazel output | pin protoc + plugin versions; golden-diff (P1) |
| SSZ minimal | no committed minimal variant today | P2 build-tag variants; golden-diff vs `--config=minimal` |
| CGO cross | blst SIMD / herumi link errors per target | validate each GOOS/GOARCH early; zig/osxcross/mingw as Bazel did |
| nogo parity | losing a custom check silently | multichecker embeds the same analyzers; keep CI gate until P9 |
| Reproducible builds | `-trimpath`/ldflags differences | `-trimpath` + fixed ldflags; compare binary metadata |
| Commit hygiene | a phase commit doesn't build | stage by file-set, run that phase's `make` target before committing |


**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

title: e2e: Reliability improvements
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This fixes a group of issues that were making `//testing/endtoend:presubmit` unreliable. The goal is to fix the actual harness/evaluator issues instead of marking the target flaky.

The main changes are:

1. Make e2e evaluators wait for stable state instead of failing on transient reads. This includes head convergence checks, deterministic eth1 vote expectations, Fulu participation decoding, and a narrow startup skip for sync participation through slot 3. Slot 4 and later are still checked.

2. Fix eth1 transaction generation under fork and txpool pressure. Blob tx generation is now fork-aware, sender nonce/gas price state is tracked across iterations, blob modes use separate funded accounts across the Fulu boundary, and local geth is started with `--rpc.txfeecap=0`.

3. Use `HeadETH1Data()` instead of random eth1data when `BlockByTimestamp(latestValidTime)` fails. Random eth1data is still used for the disconnected case, but short EL lag should not introduce avoidable nondeterminism.

4. Fix harness false negatives. Checkpoint sync now waits for matching heads instead of a specific log string. Doppelganger detection reads the existing validator log instead of truncating it, uses the direct wait result, and the log scanner can handle long lines.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

**Other notes for review**

Testing:

- `//testing/endtoend/evaluators:go_default_test`
- `//testing/endtoend/components/eth1:go_default_test`
- `//beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator:go_default_test`
- `//testing/endtoend:presubmit`
- `//testing/endtoend:presubmit --runs_per_test=10`

The runs_per_test=10 was sufficient evidence that the changes were a significant improvement, but Buildkite found one more CI-only startup case at epoch 0 slot 3 in `validator_sync_participation_0`. The final boundary fix keeps that skip limited to startup and keeps slot 4+ enforced.

title: Check network size before computing subnet topic scoring params
body:
Computing subnet topic scoring params on a network with fewer than AttestationSubnetCount × SlotsPerEpoch × D/2 (= 8192) active validators truncates the expected message rate to zero, so every node logged ~64 "Skipping initializing topic scoring because rate is 0" warnings per topic subscription on small networks.

Check the minimum validator count up front in the subnet param functions and replace the per-subnet warnings with a single debug line (active vs required count) logged once when the active validator count is first cached. Mainnet behavior is unchanged.

author: Inspector-Butters

title: Make FullBeatsEmpty fork-agnostic
body:
`FullBeatsEmpty` returned `false` for pre-gloas blocks, but pre-gloas blocks always carry their payload, so head saves were inconsistent: `UpdateAndSaveHeadWithBalances` saved `full = false` pre-gloas while the post-block FCU path and the `FullHead`-derived paths saved `true`, letting a same-root save spuriously register as a head change.

Rather than special-case the fork, this drops the slot/epoch branch entirely: `choosePayloadContent` already resolves to the full node pre-gloas (all pre-gloas votes carry `payloadStatus = true` so weight accrues to the full node, and pre-gloas children build on it), so the helper now works the same across forks.
author: terencechain

title: Key payload ID cache by parent payload status
body:
- The payload ID cache was keyed only by `(slot, head root)`, but in gloas the same root exists as empty or full. At second 0 an empty/full flip without a root change could return a payload ID prepared against the wrong parent hash, producing an invalid proposal (`bid.parent_block_hash != state.latest_block_hash`). The UpdateHead FCU also runs in a goroutine, so last-write-wins could leave a stale entry.
- Key the cache by `(slot, root, full)`. Writers record the payload status the FCU was prepared against (envelope processing → full, late payload tasks → empty, reorg FCU → status from `FullHead`, late block tasks → `HasFullNode`); the proposer looks up with `FullBeatsEmpty`. A status mismatch is now a cache miss that falls back to a fresh synchronous FCU instead of a wrong hit.

title: adding gossip validation on envelope api and block api default
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

resolves one of our todos which is default to gossip validations on rest apis for envelope: spec found here 

https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/580

This approach takes the shortest path which is just reapplying the steps but a greater refactor is needed to share the actual gossip validation function as something shared.

```
participants:
  # Stateless VC: requests block + envelope inline (include_payload=true) and
  # publishes SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelopeContents (blobs + KZG proofs).
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-4
    el_extra_params:
      - --http.api=eth,net,web3,admin
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    supernode: true
    count: 1
    validator_count: 32
    cl_extra_params:
      - --subscribe-all-subnets
      - --verbosity=debug
    vc_extra_params:
      - --enable-beacon-rest-api
      - --stateless
      - --verbosity=debug

  # Stateful VC: BN caches the envelope (include_payload=false) and the VC
  # publishes the spec-wire SignedBlindedExecutionPayloadEnvelope.
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-4
    el_extra_params:
      - --http.api=eth,net,web3,admin
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    supernode: true
    count: 1
    validator_count: 32
    cl_extra_params:
      - --subscribe-all-subnets
      - --verbosity=debug
    vc_extra_params:
      - --enable-beacon-rest-api
      - --verbosity=debug

network_params:
  fulu_fork_epoch: 0
  gloas_fork_epoch: 2
  seconds_per_slot: 6
  genesis_delay: 40

additional_services:
  - dora
  - spamoor

# spamoor generates load so payloads are non-empty: eoatx for normal EL txs,
# blobs to exercise the blob/KZG path through the stateless envelope Contents flow.
spamoor_params:
  spammers:
    - scenario: eoatx
      config:
        throughput: 10
    - scenario: blobs
      config:
        throughput: 2

global_log_level: debug
```

title: Emit proposer_preferences SSE event for locally submitted preferences
body: The `proposer_preferences` SSE event only fired from the gossip-receive path, so a node never emitted its own validators' preferences (gossip doesn't loop back to the publisher). Builders and relays consuming a single node's event stream therefore missed that node's proposers' preferences; this also emits the event when preferences are submitted locally via the validator client.
author: terencechain

title: Emit execution_payload_bid event on the beacon node event stream
body: The `execution_payload_bid` SSE topic was registered as subscribable but had no producer, so subscribers never received anything. This emits it from the gossip subscriber once a bid passes validation, mirroring how `proposer_preferences` is wired, so builders and relays can observe bids over the event stream.
author: terencechain

title: Emit payload_attributes SSE event after the Gloas fork
body: The `payload_attributes` event only fired from the pre-Gloas `notifyForkchoiceUpdate` path, so the stream went silent the moment Gloas activated — which blocks external builders and relays that drive payload building off this event. This fires it from the Gloas envelope and forkchoice-update paths, and sources the parent execution block hash from the head state for Gloas blocks (the payload lives in the envelope, not the block body).

title: Don't request data columns for empty slots in initial sync
body:
In Gloas the column-fetch decision keyed off block.Body().BlobKzgCommitments(), which returns the bid's committed commitments (the builder's promise). For a payload-absent slot the payload (and its data columns) is never revealed, so the node requested columns that no peer can serve, looped on respondedSidecars=0, and never synced past the slot.

Drive the decision off the revealed execution payload envelopes instead:
- Fetch payloads before sidecars so the envelope set is available.
- Select columns per revealed payload via columnFetchBlocks: Gloas blocks only when an envelope exists for the block root; pre-Gloas (Fulu) blocks always (payload is in the block). Request the out-of-batch payload the first block builds on by its beacon block root (loaded from the DB) and persist those columns via the queue consumer.
- Gate the import-side availability check (areSidecarsAvailable) on payload presence so payload-absent Gloas blocks don't poll for nonexistent columns.

title: Bound data-column availability wait during batch sync
body:
## Problem

During block-batch (initial) sync, `areDataColumnsAvailable` waits **indefinitely** for a block's custody data columns — its `slotEnd` case only logs and then keeps waiting; the only exits are "enough columns arrived" or `ctx.Done()`. Because round-robin imports batches **sequentially**, a single block whose columns are momentarily unavailable blocks the whole import pipeline forever and sync **dead-ends at a batch boundary** (no further blocks imported, no error). For a near-tip block whose slot has already passed, `slotEnd` is never even armed, so it stalls silently with no log.

## Fix

Bound the wait to **one slot**, scoped to the **sync/batch path only** (`areSidecarsAvailable`, reached from `onBlockBatch`). On timeout the batch returns an error and is retried by round-robin, which re-fetches the columns — turning a hard dead-end into a recoverable retry. The head/gossip and execution-payload-envelope DA paths (`process_block.go` head check and `receive_execution_payload_envelope.go`) call `areDataColumnsAvailable` directly and are intentionally left unchanged.

## Testing

- `go build ./beacon-chain/blockchain/`, `go test -tags develop ./beacon-chain/blockchain/ -run TestStore_OnBlockBatch` pass.
- Validated on **glamsterdam-devnet-5**: before the change a local Prysm+Nethermind node repeatedly dead-ended at a batch boundary near the tip; with this change the node syncs through and reaches head.

title: Recover Payload insertion
body:
While this PR still applies as recovery from the previous situation, the actual error mode seen on devnets is at startup in which the initial forkchoice tree insertion is up to an empty node, and the subsequent batches want to build on top of full. This is better fixed in fillInMissingBlocks

When the beacon node syncs a batch it does not apply the last payload if
it's not canonical. This leads to a situation in which the payload may
be on db but the corresponding node in forkchoice is not set. In this PR
we recover from a failure mode in which, when about to sync a batch, the
first block builds on full, we have the payload in db, but we do not
have the corresponding full node on forkchoice, in this case we simply
insert the payload to forkchoice without repeating its validation.

title: Fail fast on data column availability check for past-slot blocks during sync
body: areDataColumnsAvailable blocks on a subscription fed by gossip storage writes. During sync that channel never fires for historical roots (columns arrive via range requests, already saved before import), so the wait could only end on context expiry. This skips the wait for past-slot blocks and envelopes, returning an error so the caller refetches instead of blocking the import path. The live path (current/future slot) is unchanged.

title: Fail execution payload envelope data column check during sync instead of blocking
body: During initial sync data columns are fetched via range requests, so the gossip-fed subscription wait in areDataColumnsAvailable never makes progress for an envelope and only blocks the import path. When not in regular sync, this checks data column availability synchronously and returns an error if columns are missing so the caller refetches, instead of blocking. The live gossip path is unchanged.

title: Fix unbounded growth of engine_exchangeCapabilities requested method list
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`ExchangeCapabilities` appends the fork-specific engine endpoints (Electra/Fulu/Gloas) to the **package-level** `supportedEngineEndpoints` slice on every invocation:

```go
if params.FuluEnabled() {
    supportedEngineEndpoints = append(supportedEngineEndpoints, fuluEngineEndpoints...)
}
```

`ExchangeCapabilities` is called from `pollConnectionStatus` on every execution-client (re)connection, and `pollConnectionStatus` is re-invoked from the run loop on every failed `eth1HeadTicker` header fetch (and via `retryExecutionClientConnection` from several error paths). Each call therefore re-appends the fork endpoints to the shared slice, so the slice grows without bound.

Because the requested-but-unsupported set is then computed from that ever-growing slice, the resulting warning grows on every reconnect:

```
WARN execution: Connected execution client does not support some requested engine methods
  methods=[engine_getBlobsV3 engine_getBlobsV3 engine_getBlobsV3 ... (hundreds)]
```

This is most visible on execution clients that don't yet implement `engine_getBlobsV3`/`engine_getBlobsV2`, and on nodes that reconnect to the EL frequently.

The fix builds a fresh local endpoint list on each call instead of mutating the shared package-level slice. The set of requested engine methods is now stable across calls, so the warning is constant-length (and duplicate-free) rather than monotonically growing. The shared `supportedEngineEndpoints` slice is left read-only.

**Other notes for review**

Testing plan: added `Test_ExchangeCapabilities_StableAcrossCalls`, which enables all forks, captures the engine-method list the EL receives via a stub HTTP handler, calls `ExchangeCapabilities` twice, and asserts the two requested method lists are identical and contain no duplicates. The test fails on the previous code (`22` methods on the first call, `32` on the second) and passes with this change. The full `//beacon-chain/execution:go_default_test` package passes.

This change only affects the request list sent to the EL and the warning log; it does not change which capabilities are cached or how they are used. The warning will still appear once per reconnect when the EL genuinely lacks a requested method — it simply no longer accumulates.

title: Ignore payload attestations outside the head state's PTC window, don't reject
body: When the node's head lags the attestation slot, the pending-queue path could no longer resolve the slot's PTC against the head state and rejected the sender, disconnecting, through gossip scoring, every peer forwarding current-slot payload attestations. It now drops those (ignore) via a shared `helpers.PayloadCommitteeAvailable` check (also reused by `ptcWindowOffset`), while still rejecting genuine not-in-committee or bad-signature messages.
author: terencechain

title: Resolve payload attestation committee against the slot-covering state
body: `processPayloadAttestationMessage` resolved the PTC committee index from the head state, which on a lagging node errored with `ptc window out of range` and silently dropped the vote. It now uses `PtcLookupState` — the same slot-covering state the gossip validation path uses — and skips cleanly when no covering state is available.

title: Dedupe Gloas pending-column downscore to once per peer per root
body: Under blob load a Gloas data column can be queued before its block arrives. If the block is still missing when the pending entry is pruned, every queued column's forwarder is downscored once per column. A single peer that relayed many columns for one block then takes up to 128 hits and instantly blows past the bad responses threshold of 5. That disconnects an otherwise healthy peer, and under sustained load it cascades into losing most peers. This change downscores each forwarder at most once per orphaned root.

title: making duties failures independent of each other
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 Feature


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**


#16421 split validator-client duty fetching across gRPC/REST and introduced **promotion** — instead of re-pulling both current and next epoch every boundary, the cached next-epoch duties are promoted into the current epoch and only the new next-epoch is fetched.

This PR finishes the two follow-ups #16928 left open:

1. **Next-epoch duties are always optional.** Previously a next-epoch *attester* fetch failure was a hard error that aborted the whole update — disrupting the *current* epoch too. Now every next-epoch duty type fails softly (flagged, not fatal), so a next-epoch problem never breaks the current epoch.
2. **Failures are retried per-type, not bundled.** Previously any single missing next-epoch duty forced a full re-pull of *all four* duty types at the next boundary. Now the missing types are re-fetched **individually, mid-epoch**, and merged in — so promotion stays cheap and a single transient failure doesn't cascade.

A third, related change keeps the dependent-root (reorg) handling consistent with the new soft-failure model.

## What changed

### Next-epoch duties optional
`missingNextDuties` gains a `missingNextAttester` bit. In both the full-fetch and promotion paths, a failed next-epoch attester is logged and flagged (not returned as an error), exactly like proposer/sync/ptc already were. Current-epoch attester/proposer remain required.

### Per-type mid-epoch retry
- `RetryMissingNextDuties` re-fetches **only** the duty types flagged missing and overlays them onto the existing next-epoch duties (`overlayNextDuties`), leaving the types that already succeeded untouched. If the **attester spine** itself is missing (the attester assignment is what creates each validator's duty row, so without it there are no rows to overlay onto), it rebuilds the whole next epoch instead.
- `MaybeRetryMissingNextDuties` is what the run loop calls each non-epoch-start slot. It runs the retry in its **own goroutine** so the current slot's attestation/proposal isn't blocked, but only when there's actually missing work (`needsNextRetry`) and no retry is already in flight (`retryInFlight` CAS) — so we don't spawn goroutines for nothing or pile them up.
- Writes are guarded by a store **revision** counter: if an epoch-boundary or head-event update lands while a retry goroutine is mid-fetch, the now-stale write is dropped (`replaceNextDuties` applies only if the store is still at the revision the fetch was based on).

### Dependent-root / reorg handling
`checkDependentRoots` no longer treats an *unknown* (nil) current dependent root as "needs update" — that state only arises after a soft next-epoch attester failure, and forcing a full `UpdateDuties` on every head event while it's nil is wasteful. Recovery is instead owned by the epoch boundary and the per-slot retry. Current-epoch reorg detection (the `prev` dependent-root path) is unchanged.

## Before / after

### Per-duty-type fetch failure

| Duty type | Current epoch fails | Next epoch fails — **before** | Next epoch fails — **now** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Attester** | hard error → keep cached duties, retry next tick | **hard error → aborts the whole update, breaking the current epoch** | soft: flag `missingNextAttester`; spine rebuilt by the mid-epoch retry |
| **Proposer** | hard error → keep cache | soft, but forced a full 4-type re-pull next boundary | soft: flag; overlaid by the mid-epoch retry |
| **Sync** | soft (logged) | soft, forced a full 4-type re-pull | soft: flag; overlaid by the mid-epoch retry |
| **PTC** | soft (logged) | soft, forced a full 4-type re-pull | soft: flag; overlaid by the mid-epoch retry |

### Triggers → action

| Trigger | **Before** | **Now** |
|---|---|---|
| Epoch boundary, no failures + same validators + stable dep root | promote next→current, fetch next epoch only | same |
| Epoch boundary, can't promote (first run / validator-set drift) | full fetch (current + next, all types) | same |
| Epoch boundary, a next-epoch type failed last cycle | **forced full re-pull of all 4 types** | **promote** — the gap was already filled mid-epoch |
| Mid-epoch slot | *(nothing — wait for next boundary)* | **retry only the missing next-epoch types**, in a goroutine off the slot critical path; no-op when nothing is missing |
| Head event, dependent root changed | `UpdateDuties` | same |
| Head event, current dependent root **unknown (nil)** | **trigger `UpdateDuties`** | **skip** — let the boundary + per-slot retry recover |

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16928

title: Reject empty Gloas block access lists
body:
## What changed

This rejects zero-length Gloas block access lists before Prysm caches or publishes an execution payload envelope, and while decoding Gloas engine JSON payloads. A zero-length BAL serializes as `0x`, which ELs reject as invalid RLP; the valid empty RLP list encoding is `0xc0`.

The guard is applied in:
- `ExecutionBundleGloas` JSON decoding
- `ExecutionBlock` JSON decoding
- self-built execution payload envelope caching
- `PublishExecutionPayloadEnvelope` request validation

## Why

On `glamsterdam-devnet-6`, block `0xe52da835...f491fa` at slot 13961 / execution block 12609 was imported successfully through non-Prysm paths, but Prysm-connected ELs rejected the replayed/published payload envelope with BAL decode failures:

- Besu: `Invalid block access list encoding`
- Geth: `failed to decode BAL: EOF`

The Prysm-side logs showed the beacon node processing the same payload envelope while sending an empty BAL (`0x`) to the EL, which explains the EL-specific rejection without requiring the original built block to be globally invalid.

## Tests

- `go test ./proto/engine/v1`
- `go test ./beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator -run 'Test(StoreExecutionPayloadEnvelope|ExtractExecutionPayloadGloas|PublishExecutionPayloadEnvelope)'`\n\nI also tried `go test ./proto/engine/v1 ./beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator`; `proto/engine/v1` passed, while the full validator package hit unrelated existing failures in stream/duties tests and a `Bitvector32` go-cmp panic.\n\n## Note\n\nAI-assisted investigation and patch by @lodekeeper.

title: Drain pending Gloas data columns for our own proposed block
body:
Our own proposed block is imported via the RPC path (ProposeBeaconBlock -> ReceiveBlock) and never re-enters the gossip/by-root ingest paths that drain pending Gloas columns. Columns peers reconstruct and gossip back to us arrive before our local import, get queued as "block not yet seen", and are never drained -- so the payload's data columns are declared unavailable at slot end.

Subscribe sync to the statefeed BlockProcessed event (which fires on every import path, including our own block) and drain the pending Gloas columns for the processed root. Gated on regular sync to avoid needless work on the initial-sync batch path.

title: Remove Bazel: Phase 3/9 - Part 1
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This pull request implements the first part of **Phase 3** of:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16982

> [!NOTE]
>  Phase 3 covers both unit tests and end to end tests. However this pull request is already big enough, so we chose to split Phase 3 in 2 parts: unit tests (this one), and then end to end tests (to be implemented).

This pull requests implements `make test`, and `make testdata`.

Main design changes:
- Bazel supports flaky tests. This is not the case for `go test`. To support flaky tests, we use [gotestsum](https://github.com/gotestyourself/gotestsum) as a test harness.
- Some tests (eg: spectests), require to fetch external data. This was handled by Bazel. This PR handles this as well.

`make test` runs tests. External data are lazily fetched directly into the tests, and are cached.
With this PR, all unit tests (even the ones than previously used to depend on Bazel) can be ran with `go test` directly. This also means that those tests can be run with a classical go debugger in an IDE.

`make testdata` only fetches the test data. This is **not** a requirement before running `make test`. It's only a convenience tool if human eyes on the test data are needed.


> [!IMPORTANT]
>  **Main difference with Bazel tests:**
> Bazel tests support retrying panicking tests. This is not the case for [gotestsum](https://github.com/gotestyourself/gotestsum).
> Because of that, this PR starts by some commits fixing panicking tests, or converting panicking tests to erroring tests.

If needed, we probably can do some extra work to support panicking tests as well, but I think it's not a bad thing not to support panicking tests.

This PR also runs `make test` in the CI as **info only**. A failing `make test` won't fail the whole CI.

The `Makefile` has been updated as:
```
Prysm - Ethereum consensus client

Commands:
  make run <bin> [flags=...] [-- <args>]       Run a binary
  make build [<bin>...] [flags=...]            Build a binary (default: all)
  make gen [<kind>...] [mode=force|no-force]   Create generated code (default: all,no-force)
  make test [<kind>...] [mode=no-race|race]    Run unit tests (default: all,no-race)
  make testdata                                Pre-fetch external spec-test data
  make clean                                   Clean everything
  make help                                    Show this help

Options:
  <bin>:         beacon-chain client-stats prysmctl validator
  gen <kind>:    proto ssz mocks
  test <kind>:   mainnet mainnet-spectest minimal minimal-spectest

Notes:
  After '--', pass '--flag value' (not '--flag=value')
```

title: making proposer preferences repush on reconnection to different node
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

proposer preferences has a feature to deduplicate sends as it checks each slot , but if the validator disconnects from a beacon node it won't send to the new beacon node as a fresh push because of the local deduplication.

this pr adds a counter instead of pure host comparisons so that it adresses reconnection to the same node, along with a check if we did reconnect to a new bn and force pushes the pr. this issue was found while reviewing https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17063

**note**: this has not been applied to builder preferences yet so something similar should be reviewed there.

## Testing

Verifies that when the VC fails over to a different beacon node **without** the runner restarting (health never flips), the connection counter still forces a re-push so the new node receives our proposer preferences. This is the path the health-recovery force cannot cover.

**1. Build validator + beacon images** from this branch and tag them for Kurtosis:
`gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest` and `gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest`.

**2. Launch a post-Gloas devnet where one VC has a 2-beacon fallback list.** Save as `gloas-fallback-test.yml`:

```yaml
participants:
  # TARGET VC: primary cl-1, fallback cl-2
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    vc_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
      - --beacon-rpc-provider=cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000,cl-2-prysm-ethrex:4000
    count: 1
  # backdrop: keeps the chain healthy, provides cl-2..cl-4
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    vc_extra_params: [--verbosity=debug]
    count: 3
network_params:
  fulu_fork_epoch: 0
  gloas_fork_epoch: 1
  seconds_per_slot: 6
  genesis_delay: 30
global_log_level: debug
```

```
kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --args-file gloas-fallback-test.yml --enclave gloas-fallback
```

**3. Verify the fallback list took effect** (the package sets its own `--beacon-rpc-provider`; ours is appended and wins):

```
cid=$(docker ps --filter name=vc-1-ethrex-prysm -q)
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | grep "Initialized gRPC connection provider"
# expect: count=2 endpoints=[cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000 cl-2-prysm-ethrex:4000]
```

**4. Wait for Gloas** (head slot >= 32) and confirm steady state (`prefsBuilt=0` on quiet slots):

```
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep "Build proposer preferences result" | tail
```

> Use `docker logs`, not `kurtosis service logs` — the latter only returns ~200 lines (startup).

**5. Kill the primary beacon during a quiet mid-epoch slot** (not epoch-start, not mid-epoch, so the re-push is unambiguous):

```
kurtosis service stop gloas-fallback cl-1-prysm-ethrex
```

**6. Observe** in the target VC log:

```
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
  | grep -iE "Switched (gRPC endpoint|to responsive)|Build proposer preferences result|unhealthy|Starting validator runner"
```

**Expected (PASS):**
- `Switched gRPC endpoint newHost=cl-2... previousHost=cl-1...` and `Switched to responsive beacon node`.
- **No** `Beacon node unhealthy, stopping runner` and **no** new `Starting validator runner` — health did not flip and the runner did not restart, so this exercises the connection-counter path (not the restart path).
- The next `Build proposer preferences result` on a normally-quiet slot shows `alreadySubmitted` dropping (cache cleared) and **`prefsBuilt` > 0** (the re-push), followed by a `SubmitSignedProposerPreferences` RPC to cl-2.

**FAIL (regression):** after the switch `prefsBuilt` stays `0` — the new beacon never receives the preferences.

**Cleanup:**

```
kurtosis enclave rm -f gloas-fallback
```

<details><summary>Observed run (2026-07-01)</summary>

Killed `cl-1-prysm-ethrex` at 14:58:26, chain slot ~250 (epoch 7, quiet window):

```
slot 250-254 (pre-kill):  prefsBuilt=0  alreadySubmitted=12      # steady state
14:58:40  Switched gRPC endpoint             newHost=cl-2  previousHost=cl-1
14:58:40  Switched to responsive beacon node current=cl-2  previous=cl-1  tried=[cl-1]
slot 255 (14:58:45):      prefsBuilt=6  alreadySubmitted=6       # cache cleared + re-push
14:58:48  gRPC SubmitSignedProposerPreferences -> cl-2           # re-push on the wire
```

No `unhealthy` / `stopping runner`; only the original `Starting validator runner` (14:32:30). Slot 255 is off-cadence (not epoch start, not mid-epoch); in steady state it was `0`. The 12->6 `alreadySubmitted` drop is `submittedPrefSlots` being cleared by `forceFullPush`, and `prefsBuilt=6` is the re-push to cl-2.

</details>


**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

title: Gate partial column decode on subscription to protect the gossip loop
body:
`onIncomingRPC` runs on the shared pubsub `processLoop` and SSZ decodes the attacker sized `PartialMessage` (up to ~8MB) before the subscription check, so a peer can force multi-MB decodes on the loop that also carries blocks and attestations, including for subnets we do not custody.

How an attacker triggers it against a node running `--partial-data-columns`:
1. Connect and negotiate the partial messages extension.
2. Send a `PartialMessagesExtension` RPC with `TopicID` `data_column_sidecar_37` (a subnet the victim does not custody), a 33 byte `GroupID`, and a `PartialMessage` padded to roughly 4096 cells of 2048 bytes of garbage cells that are never KZG verified.
3. Stream these in a loop, reusing a few already established group IDs so the library per group cap does not reject them
author: terencechain

title: Implement the active-active mode in the REST validator client.
body: **What type of PR is this?** Feature Depends on: - https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17143 ### The active-passive connection scheme Currently, a Prysm validator client can connect to multiple beacon nodes via REST, but only one node is actively used for SSE events and HTTP requests at any given time. This is called the **active** beacon node, while the others are **passive**. If the active node fails or goes offline, the validator client automatically switches to one of the passive nodes, which then becomes active. This is the **active-passive** connection scheme. While this approach generally works well, it has limitations in certain situations. Consider a validator client connected to BN-1, BN-2, and BN-3, with only BN-1 active. If BN-1 experiences issues (such as poor peering or slow block execution due to disk constraints) and fails to import a block within the 4-second deadline, while BN-2 and BN-3 successfully import it, the validator client faces a problem. Because the validator client only listens to BN-1's SSE events, it will not receive the head event for the new block before the deadline. Consequently, when it requests attestation data from BN-1, it receives stale data corresponding to the previous block. The validator client signs and broadcasts this attestation through BN-1, which means the validator misses the head vote, and potentially the source and target votes if this is the first block of an epoch. This situation could have been avoided if the validator client could listen to SSE events from all connected beacon nodes (not just the active one) and request fresh attestation data from any of them (not just the active one). Here enters the **active-active** connection scheme. ### The active-active connection scheme With the **active-active** connection scheme, a validator client actively listens to and requests data from all connected beacon nodes. When responses differ between beacon nodes, the validator client selects the best one based on the context. This pull request implements the **active-active** connection scheme. To implement this connection scheme, we introduce four new concepts: **The multi-event stream** The validator client needs to listen to SSE events from multiple beacon nodes. The multi-event stream: - connects to (and reconnects to, if needed) each beacon node's event stream, - merges these streams into a single stream, - removes potential duplicates, and - sends the result to an output stream. ``` host-1 --\ host-2 ---+--> merged --> deduper --> out host-3 --/ ``` **The multi-handler** The multi-handler is a framework that defines how HTTP requests are sent to connected beacon nodes and which response is selected. It provides the following options: - `WithRace`: Should requests be sent sequentially or concurrently to the beacon nodes? - `WithAccept/WithSSZAccept`: Should all 2xx responses from any beacon node be accepted, or should additional acceptance criteria be applied? - `WithDeadline`: How long should the validator client wait if no acceptable response is returned? - `WithRepoll`: Should the validator client retry if no acceptable response is returned? `WithRepoll` takes a **re-poll mode** that decides what stops the re-polling: - `UntilAccepted`: keep re-polling until an *accept-passing* (fresh) response arrives, or the deadline fires. - `UntilAny2xx`: re-poll only while *no usable response at all* has arrived, stopping as soon as any node returns one. **The freshness options** Now that we've implemented the multi-handler, we need to define how to use it (which options to set) for the 4 objects that require it. | Function | Endpoint | Object requested | |---|---|---| | `attestationFreshnessOptions` | [/eth/v1/validator/attestation_data](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Validator/produceAttestationData) | `AttestationData` | | `syncCommitteeFreshnessOptions` | [/eth/v1/beacon/blocks/head/root](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Beacon/getBlockRoot) | `BlockRootResponse` | | `blockFreshnessOptions` | [/eth/v3/validator/blocks/{slot}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Validator/produceBlockV3) (or [/eth/v4/validator/blocks/{slot}](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/produceBlockV4) for Gloas) | `BeaconBlock` | | `payloadAttestationFreshnessOptions` | [/eth/v1/validator/payload_attestation_data](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/?urls.primaryName=dev#/Validator/producePayloadAttestationData) | `PayloadAttestationData` | **`attestationFreshnessOptions`, `syncCommitteeFreshnessOptions` and `payloadAttestationFreshnessOptions`** use `WithRace`, an accept criterion, `WithDeadline`, and `WithRepoll(UntilAccepted)`. - `WithRace` queries all beacon nodes concurrently. - The accept criterion (`WithAccept` for the JSON reads, `WithSSZAccept` for the SSZ payload-attestation read) prioritizes any response whose root matches the expected head root. If the deadline is reached without a matching response, the validator client falls back to the first response received. (Voting for a stale block is preferable to not voting at all.) - `WithDeadline` works together with the accept criterion to decide when to use the fallback response. It is floored to `readFreshnessBudget` so that a lagging node still gets time to import the announced head. - `WithRepoll(UntilAccepted)` continuously re-queries all beacon nodes until either a matching response is received or the deadline is reached. **`blockFreshnessOptions`** uses `WithRace`, `WithSSZAccept`, `WithRepoll(UntilAny2xx)`, and `WithDeadline`. - `WithRace` queries all beacon nodes concurrently. - `WithSSZAccept` prioritizes the block that is *built on top of* the expected head, i.e. the block whose **parent** root matches the expected head root. - `WithRepoll(UntilAny2xx)` keeps re-polling until at least one node returns a block (any 2xx). - `WithDeadline` is the caller's context deadline (the slot deadline). **The head tracker** The freshness options above all steer requests toward the node that already imported the *expected head*. Something has to decide what that expected head is. This is the head tracker. The head tracker records the latest head (block root and its slot) the validator client has learned about from the head events of *all* connected beacon nodes (fed by the multi-event stream). On each head event, it keeps the head with the highest slot and ignores any event for an older slot. So the "expected head" is the most advanced head announced by any single beacon node. When the validator client is about to attest, participate in a sync committee, propose a block or attest to a payload, it attaches the tracked head (the expected head root, plus a deadline) to the request context as a freshness *hint*. The freshness options then read that hint to build their accept criteria. This is what closes the loop and solves the problem described at the top: even if a node is lagging, a head event from any other node advances the head tracker, so the validator client knows which head to expect and can request fresh data from whichever node already imported it. ``` head events (all nodes) --> head tracker (best head) --> hint on ctx --> freshness options ``` ### To test Use a validator client with the `--enable-beacon-rest-api` flag and more than one beacon node: ``` --beacon-rest-api-provider=http://beacon-1,http://beacon-2,http://beacon-3 ``` Test by powering down all beacon nodes except 1 (regardless the chosen beacon node is). Also, the interesting case is the following: If, amongst all the connected beacon node, at least one imported the block before the 4 seconds deadline, then all the votes (head, source, target) should be correct. To ensure the correct behavior of all configurations, I tested with 3 VCs at the same time - 1 REST VC connected in active-mode to 2 BNs - 1 gRPC VC - 1 REST VC connected to a single BN Results from https://github.com/nalepae/validators-effectiveness are displayed below: **REST VC connected in active-mode to 2 BNs** **1 gRPC VC** **1 REST VC connected to a single BN** > [!NOTE] > The 4 `not submitted` attestations are due to the "migrate to cold" process locking the DB for a long time, unrelated to the current PR. **Other notes for review** > [!NOTE] > Please read commit by commit, with commit messages. > Only the REST validator client is impacted. No change on gRPC. > [!IMPORTANT] > As the `--enable-beacon-rest-api` flag is still in the experimental mode, we chose to replace the current active-passive connection scheme by the new proposed active-active connection scheme. **Acknowledgements** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have included a uniquely named [changelog fragment file](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-changelogmd). - [x] I have added a description with sufficient context for reviewers to understand this PR. - [x] I have tested that my changes work as expected and I added a testing plan to the PR description (if applicable).

title: Fix attestation ideal rewards for Electra balances
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Fixes the attestation rewards API `ideal_rewards` response for Electra compounding validators with effective balances above 32 ETH.

This PR updates ideal reward generation to derive distinct effective-balance buckets from the requested validators and sort them before calculating rewards. It also adds a regression test for a 2048 ETH compounding validator with exact expected reward values.

title: Accept builder preferences without the builder endpoint flag
body: `SubmitBuilderPreferences` was gated on the legacy `--http-mev-relay` flag via `Configured()`, while the gloas bid path already dials builders per URL from the request auth. Flag-less deployments rejected every preference push with `FailedPrecondition`, so `maxExecutionPayments` stayed empty and payment-carrying bids were discarded.
author: terencechain

title: Submit block to winning builder before the broadcast error check
body: ProposeBeaconBlock returned on a broadcast/receive error before reaching the builder submission, so a block that was already broadcast to gossip but failed local processing never reached the winning builder and the envelope was never revealed. The submission now runs before the error check.
author: terencechain

title: Fall back to Builder-API bids when the local payload is unavailable
body: When `getLocalPayload` fails, Gloas block production only consulted the cached P2P bid even with valid builder request auths in hand, because the builder query took its parent hash from the local payload. The fallback now queries authed builders using `getParentBlockHash`, picks the best of the cached P2P and Builder-API bids, and records the bid source so a winning builder still receives the signed block
