title: Enforce ProgressiveList limits defined on STF during unmarshal
body: ## Background and rationale EIP-7688 and EIP-7916 define a replacement for the `List` family of ssz collection types supporting progressive merkleization: ProgressiveList, ProgressiveBitlist, ProgressiveByteList. Unlike the base ssz design, progressive collection types do not have a strict maximum size defined in their spec type definition. Previously the definition not only changed how the fields were merkleized, but also moved validation as early in the p2p pipeline as possible, to happen at the unmarshal step. We still have limits we want to enforce (e.g. `MAX_ATTESTATIONS_ELECTRA`), but those limit checks have migrated from the unmarshal step to a validation function on the STF. When upstream specs moved to this scheme, spectest generators stopped limiting the size of test inputs according to the limits, requiring implementations to accept inputs that were outside the bounds. In prysm's codegen we dropped the validation previously performed at the unmarshal step to accept these fixtures. However this change unnecessarily defers validation that we could perform up front, potentially spreading the responsibility for checking these lengths to various parts of the application in ways that could lead to bugs. It could also open us up to limited griefing from malicious inputs that cause extra memory allocation for values that the decoder can easily determine are invalid. So I've asked @jtraglia for a compromise: modify specs so that spectest generation is aware of the valid range of values for these types with limits enforced at the STF, so that fixtures can avoid exceeding those ranges. That allows us to pass ssz-static spectests using types where we have restored input size validation to our unmarshal methods. This also gives spectest generators a convenient place to pick a size for values to exceed in fixtures where the STF checks are being tested (the spectest generator can use `> $LIMIT` for invalid inputs, and `== $LIMIT` for valid inputs). The upstream changes are in [consensus-specs PR 5564](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5564). This PR should update to the version pin including that PR once it merges (and will fail with length validation errors in the meantime). **Acknowledgements** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have included a uniquely named [changelog fragment file](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-changelogmd). - [x] I have added a description with sufficient context for reviewers to understand this PR. - [x] I have tested that my changes work as expected and I added a testing plan to the PR description (if applicable). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`SlashableAttestationCheck` and `SlashableProposalCheck` both have two arguments: a metric (`ValidatorAttestFailVec`, `ValidatorProposeFailVec`) and a flag (`v.emitAccountMetrics`).  `Validator*FailVec` is incremented *conditionally* (and bit inconsistently) inside those methods. 

This PR completely moves failure metrics out of `ValidatorDB`, and handles them consistently, after each call. This PR also removes double counting problem for `ValidatorProposeFailVec`: It can be first incremented in `SlashableProposalCheck` and then incremented again at the caller side.

- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/13360#discussion_r1442003600

I guess it was a mechnical change in order to preserve the same semantics regarding metrics, but as 1) we already have the double counting issue in proposal metrics 2) for sake of consistency and 3) it should be considered as "failure" when slashing protection check fails, I'd suggest to handle like this PR.

title: Persist execution payload envelope before emitting execution_payload_available
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`ReceiveExecutionPayloadEnvelope` emits `execution_payload_available` before `savePostPayload` writes the envelope to the DB (the save only happened after EL validation). `GET /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes/{block_id}` reads from the DB, so a client that fetches the envelope in reaction to the event gets a 404 for a few milliseconds.

Observed on a gloas devnet with Dora (which fetches on `execution_payload_available` and treats 404 as "no envelope"): ~90% of unfinalized slots showed the payload as unavailable, and Prysm's `http_request_count{endpoint="beacon.GetExecutionPayloadEnvelope",code="404"}` grew by ~2 per slot per node. Trace with a proxy between Dora and the BN (same root, same node):

```
11:51:25.078 SSE execution_payload_available slot=317 root=0xd2c946b6
11:51:25.079 GET /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes/0xd2c946b6… -> 404
```

This PR saves the envelope right after consensus verification and data availability succeed, then emits the event (its timing is unchanged, it still does not wait for EL validation), and deletes the envelope again if EL validation fails so nothing invalid is left behind.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A (no existing issue)

title: Add `--submit-blacklisted-builder-bids` feature flag
body:
## What

`SubmitSignedExecutionPayloadBid` rejects a bid whose builder this node's circuit breaker has blacklisted, on the grounds that we should not broadcast something we would ourselves ignore on gossip:

```
{"message":"builder 0 is blacklisted by the circuit breaker","code":400}
```

That check also makes the gossip-side behavior untestable: a blacklisted builder cannot get its bid onto the wire at all, so there is no way to observe that peers refuse to propagate it.

This adds a hidden `--submit-blacklisted-builder-bids` flag that skips the check on the **submit path only**. A builder can then broadcast while blacklisted, and we can verify its peers drop the bid.

## Scope

- Only `SubmitSignedExecutionPayloadBid` is gated. The `[IGNORE]` check in `validateExecutionPayloadBidPubSub` is untouched, so receiving peers still ignore the bid — that is the behavior under test.
- The rest of `validateSubmittedBid` still runs (signature, builder active/version, fee recipient vs. proposer preferences, gas limit, parent hash, …), so the bid must otherwise be valid to be broadcast. This isolates the circuit breaker as the single reason peers drop it.
- Hidden flag, consistent with other testing-only flags such as `--reorg-late-payloads`. Testing only; not intended for mainnet.

## Note

With the flag on, the blacklisted bid is also recorded in the local `HighestBidCache`, so a node that is both the flagged builder and a proposer in that slot could select its own blacklisted builder's bid. That is out of scope here — the flag is meant for a builder-only node — but happy to gate that too if reviewers prefer.

## Tests

- `TestSubmitSignedExecutionPayloadBid_Blacklisted` — rejected, no broadcast, with the flag off.
- `TestSubmitSignedExecutionPayloadBid_BlacklistedWithFeatureFlag` — broadcast succeeds with the flag on.

title: Fix data race on the shared err in the REST duties fetch
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`dutiesForEpoch` fetches attester and proposer duties concurrently through an `errgroup`, but both goroutines assigned the same function-scoped `err`, declared once above them:

```go
var attesterDutiesContainer *structs.GetAttesterDutiesResponse
var err error                                                    // <- shared
wg.Go(func() error {
    attesterDutiesContainer, err = c.dutiesProvider.AttesterDuties(ctx, epoch, indices)
    if err != nil { ... }
    ...
})
...
wg.Go(func() error {
    proposerDutiesContainer, err = c.dutiesProvider.ProposerDuties(ctx, epoch)   // <- same err
    if err != nil { ... }
```

The sync duties goroutine in between uses `:=` and was already safe; these two use `=`.

Beyond the race itself, the two goroutines can observe each other's result in the window between the assignment and the `if err != nil` on the next line:

- a proposer failure seen by the attester goroutine is reported as `failed to get attester duties for epoch N`, blaming the wrong request;
- in the other direction an attester failure overwritten by the proposer's `nil` is dropped, and the goroutine then falls through to `attesterDutiesContainer.Data` with a nil response.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

None — filing directly as a small bug fix, per the template note.

**Other notes for review**

No new test: the existing `TestGetDutiesForEpoch_Error/get_attester_duties_failed` already reproduces it. Before the change:

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0004130a0 by goroutine 74:
  ...dutiesForEpoch.func3()
      validator/client/beacon-api/duties.go:174

Previous write at 0x00c0004130a0 by goroutine 72:
  ...dutiesForEpoch.func1()
      validator/client/beacon-api/duties.go:114

--- FAIL: TestGetDutiesForEpoch_Error/get_attester_duties_failed
    testing.go:1712: race detected during execution of test
```

After it, `go test -race ./validator/client/beacon-api/ -count=1` passes for the whole package. Happy to add a dedicated regression test if you would rather have one that names the behaviour explicitly.

Worth flagging separately: this is invisible to CI today. The Makefile defaults to `TEST_MODE := no-race` and the workflows run plain `make test mainnet`, so `mode=race` is never exercised. That is why a race reachable from an existing unit test has survived.

title: Don't wait on gossip sidecars for a slot that has already passed
body:
## What

`isDataAvailable` and `ReceiveExecutionPayloadEnvelope` choose between a blocking wait on the sidecar notifier and a synchronous storage read based on `inRegularSync()`. That predicate says nothing about whether the sidecars for the slot being imported could still be in flight, so a node that is *in* regular sync but whose head has fallen behind takes the blocking branch for a slot whose gossip window closed long ago, and only gives up when the caller's context expires.

For the pending payload envelope that context is `SlotDuration` (`pending_payload_envelope.go`), so every queued slot costs a full 12s before the by-root fetcher backfills the columns in well under a second. The backlog then drains slower than the chain advances and the node never recovers.

Gate on slot recency instead. `slot+1` stays eligible because an envelope for slot N routinely lands early in slot N+1 with its columns still in flight.

Second change: the pending blocks queue called `processPendingPayloadEnvelope` before `processPendingGloasColumns`, so the envelope's availability check ran while the columns gossiped for that root were still sitting unsaved in `pendingGloasColumns`. Swapped — the dependency runs the other way.

## Observed on glamsterdam-devnet-8

`prysm-nethermind-1` and `prysm-nethermind-2` after their EL was redeployed (~3 min outage) at 21:21 UTC on 2026-08-29. Both resumed with a ~17 slot backlog and never caught up; lag grew monotonically 16 → 24 → 36 slots.

Per-slot, on repeat:

```
21:38:46.79  Synced new block slot=118067
21:38:58.79  Could not process pending payload envelope error=data availability check failed …   (T+12.00s)
21:38:58.79  Processed pending block and cleared it in cache duration=12.369s slot=118067 slotIndex=1/27
21:38:59.65  Requested direct data column sidecars from peers duration=861ms initialMissingCount=128
21:39:00.13  Synced execution payload envelope slot=118067
```

40 consecutive samples landed in 12.05–12.43s. Over 20 minutes, against healthy peers:

| node | direct col fetches | envelope DA failures | blocks applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| prysm-geth-1 | 0 | 0 | 99 |
| prysm-besu-1 | 0 | 0 | 99 |
| prysm-nethermind-1 | 71 | 71 | 79 |
| prysm-nethermind-2 | 78 | 78 | 86 |

Downstream effect: at proposal time the head was 18–32 slots stale, so both proposals went out on a very old parent, self-built, and were orphaned — slot 118041 with `headSlot=118023`, slot 118106 with `headSlot=118074`.

## Tests

- `TestIsDataAvailable_BehindHead` — regression test; blocks for the full bound without the fix.
- `TestCanWaitForGossipSidecars` — table test for the predicate.
- `testIsAvailableSetup` now puts the generated block at the head of the clock. The fixture had it 127 slots in the past while the subtests meant to exercise the blocking wait, which only happens at the current slot.

## Not addressed here

Two related weaknesses turned up while tracing this, left out because they are judgment calls rather than clear wins:

- `pruneStaleGloasColumns` drops entries older than `currentSlot-1` and `maxPendingGloasRoots` is 8, so a node even two slots behind discards every column it receives and pays a full 128-column refetch per slot (`initialMissingCount=128` above). Widening retention costs roughly 2.3MB/slot; it should probably be bounded by bytes rather than root count.
- `shouldReSync` requires `syncedEpoch < currentEpoch-1`, so a node stuck 20–35 slots behind straddles the threshold and flip-flops in and out of initial sync.

title: Cap self-built payload envelopes at one per valid proposer per slot
body:
## Problem

In `queuePendingPayloadEnvelope`, both capacity caps (`maxPendingPayloadRoots=128`, `maxPendingBuildersPerRoot=2`) are gated behind `!isSelfBuild`, and all self-build envelopes share one builder-index constant (`BuilderIndexSelfBuild`) so the per-root `inner[builderIdx]` dedup never fires across roots.

A malicious current-slot proposer holds the proposer key and can sign an unbounded number of self-build envelopes, each with a **different** `beacon_block_root`, all validly signed. Each new root both adds a pending-map entry and fires a `sendBatchRootRequest` goroutine to fetch the unknown block. The resulting flood of spurious block-by-root requests gets **us banned by our peers**.

## Fix

Cap self-build at **one queued payload per valid proposer index per slot**, keyed on the head-state proposer for the current slot (`helpers.BeaconProposerIndexAtSlot`). A valid self-build signature already ties the envelope to exactly that proposer, so the key is deterministic and not attacker-controlled.

- The seen-proposer entry is recorded **only after** a successful signature verification, so a non-proposer peer cannot reserve or block the real proposer's slot with a bad envelope.
- Keying per proposer (not globally per slot) still admits one payload per **distinct valid proposer** in a forked scenario where the head reorgs to a branch with a different slot proposer — bounded by our own reorgs, not the attacker.
- The existing per-slot `maxSelfBuildSigFailures` budget is retained to bound bad-signature floods from non-proposers.
- `queuePendingPayloadEnvelopeFromRootRequest` needs no change — it already enforces the caps and never fires a root request.

## Tests

Added to `pending_payload_envelope_test.go`:
- **Flood** (one proposer, many distinct roots) → exactly one queued payload.
- **Distinct fork proposers** (head reorg to a different valid slot proposer) → two queued payloads.
- **Bad-sig-does-not-reserve** → a bad-signature envelope neither reserves the proposer's slot nor blocks the subsequent valid one.

Pre-existing `SelfBuildBypasses*` tests still pass, confirming honest self-build is never starved by the external-builder caps; the new per-proposer bound is orthogonal.

title: Gate `getFFG()` precompute for epoch start & "already-head" case
body: **What type of PR is this?** > Other: FCR optimization **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** FCR duration is much longer in every epoch boundary (= first slot of the epoch). Flamegraph above shows the anatomy there, and this PR resolves the **second part** (= `confirmation.OnFastConfirmation.OnceValue...`). `getFFG()` is called for sake of precomputing, when certain conditions met. One of the condition is `slots.ToEpoch(confirmedSlot) < slots.ToEpoch(currentSlot)`. It is always true in epoch boundary, as `confirmedSlot` would always be the previous epoch. So, we can say `getFFG()` is always called (which takes ~110ms for the Hoodi testnet in my machine). The only consumer of `getFFG()` is `honest()` call which is wrapped with `sync.OnceValues` for memoization purpose. If `honest()` isn't called, then `getFFG()` doesn't have to be eagerly called. There are three places where `honest()` is consumed, and new variable `honestReachable` gates `getFFG()` when it isn't needed: ```go // honest() is only reachable at an epoch start once the slot's own block is already head. honestReachable := !slots.IsEpochStart(currentSlot) || headSlot >= currentSlot ``` https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/1e307c23a3f8ac693123864addeeadca9d40cca2/beacon-chain/confirmation/confirmation.go#L588-L598 1. `pass1GateOpen`: If the current slot is epoch start, it returns true. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/1e307c23a3f8ac693123864addeeadca9d40cca2/beacon-chain/confirmation/confirmation.go#L692-L694 2. `applyPass2SafetyGate`: Same as `pass1GateOpen`. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/1e307c23a3f8ac693123864addeeadca9d40cca2/beacon-chain/confirmation/confirmation.go#L650-L654 3. `confirmCurrentEpochBlocks`: When `headSlot < currentSlot`, `slots.ToEpoch(blockSlot) > slots.ToEpoch(tentativeSlot)` is always false. - `blockSlot <= `headSlot` & `headSlot < currentSlot` => `slots.ToEpoch(blockSlot) <= previous epoch` - `tentativeSlot` comes from `confirmedRoot`, thus `slots.ToEpoch(tentativeSlot) >= previous epoch` - Therefore, `slots.ToEpoch(blockSlot) <= slots.ToEpoch(tentativeSlot)`. **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?** N/A **Other notes for review** **Acknowledgements** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have included a uniquely named [changelog fragment file](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-changelogmd). - [x] I have added a description with sufficient context for reviewers to understand this PR. - [x] I have tested that my changes work as expected and I added a testing plan to the PR description (if applicable).

title: Pre-warm pending deposit signatures before the Gloas fork
body:
## What

`onboard_builders_from_pending_deposits` walks the **entire** pending deposit queue — no churn limit, no finalization gate, no `MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH` cap — verifying BLS signatures inline while holding the state write lock. The spec asks us to pre-verify and cache in the slots before the fork:

> *Note*: In the slots leading up to the fork, implementations SHOULD validate pending deposit signatures and cache the results. The pending deposit queue might be large and verifying many signatures at the fork could be slow.
>
> *Note*: This function naively revalidates deposit signatures on every call [`is_pending_validator`]. Implementations SHOULD cache verification results to avoid repeated work.

This does that, and removes two superlinear terms that the cache alone would not have covered.

## Why caching is sound here

`is_valid_deposit_signature` uses `compute_domain(DOMAIN_DEPOSIT)` with a nil fork version *and* a nil genesis validators root, so it resolves to `GenesisForkVersion` + `ZeroHash` (`beacon-chain/core/signing/signing_root.go:230`; every deposit call site passes `nil, nil`). Validity is therefore a pure function of `(pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, signature)` — independent of state, of the fork, and even of the chain's real `genesis_validators_root`. Results computed before the fork are exactly valid after it, and never expire.

Not to be confused with post-fork `BuilderDepositRequest`, which signs under `DOMAIN_BUILDER_DEPOSIT` and is a separate path.

## Changes

- **`beacon-chain/cache/deposit_signature.go`** — plain map keyed by the `Deposit_Data` HTR, with a hard insert cap that *refuses rather than evicts*, so a warmed entry is never displaced. An LRU would let the warm-up evict its own earliest entries and converge to nothing.
- **`helpers.IsValidDepositSignature`** consults it. One change covers both fork-time call sites. A cache miss falls back to a direct verify and is **never** treated as invalid.
- **`helpers.PendingValidatorIndex`** replaces the `is_pending_validator` rescan. Each accumulated deposit is examined at most once. Exact because the accumulator only grows and validity is pure, so a `true` result is permanent and an invalid prefix never needs rescanning.
- **`builderInsertionIndex`** takes a cursor for the onboarding pass, where inserts only fill slots and none frees one. Not applied post-fork, where exits free earlier slots and the full rescan is required.
- **`ForEachPendingDeposit`** so the warm-up does not deep-copy the queue every slot.
- **Warm-up routine** over the two epochs before the fork, bounded per-slot budget, worker pool, readiness metrics with a projection warning, cache cleared one epoch *after* the fork (the upgrade runs several times around the boundary and needs the entries).

## The quadratic

Enqueue *k* deposits with pubkey `P` + non-builder credentials + invalid signatures (these accumulate in the kept list), then *k* with pubkey `P` + `0xB0` credentials + invalid signatures. Each of the latter rescanned all *k* accumulated entries, re-verified every one, then was **dropped without becoming a builder** — so the next one rescanned again. That is *k*² pairings for 2*k* deposits at `MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT` = 1 ETH each.

Measured: at k=2000 (4,000 deposits) verifications now scale as 2*k* = 4,000, taking 1.9s. The old code's 4M pairings would be **~32 minutes**. This shape is in the spec pseudocode too, so it likely affects other clients — worth reporting upstream.

## Measurements

M4 Pro, 14 cores, against the pre-fork scenarios in [jtraglia/kurtosis-devnets/gloas-deposits](https://github.com/jtraglia/kurtosis-devnets/tree/master/gloas-deposits). Invalid signatures are **well-formed signatures over the wrong message**, so each costs a full pairing (~476µs) — malformed byte strings fail G2 decompression at ~9µs and understate the cost by ~50x.

| Scenario | Cold onboard | Warm onboard | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| **s2** — 262,144 valid builder deposits, unique pubkeys | **2m12s** | **214ms** | 618x |
| **s3** — 50,000 invalid builder + 1 valid, same pubkey | **23.8s** | **40ms** | 591x |
| **s5** — 50,000 invalid validator + 1 valid builder, same pubkey | **23.9s** | **25ms** | 953x |

- Single verify: 476–512µs cold, **0.6µs** warm.
- The insertion cursor is worth **69s of s2 on its own** — 239ms vs 1m9s, measured by direct A/B, not projection. The signature cache alone would have left s2 over a minute.
- Warming s2 costs **138 core-seconds** ≈ 308ms/slot across the two epochs at 7 workers. On 4 cores (2 workers) it is ~975ms/slot, still inside the budget.
- Cache holds all 262,144 s2 entries with 2x headroom, zero rejections. 80 B/entry measured → 20MB at s2 scale, 40MB at the cap.
- s5 is why the warm-up candidate set is **per public key, not per deposit**: a builder-credential-only filter would warm 1 deposit and leave 50,000 cold.

title: gloas checkpoint sync withheld payload fix
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

A node checkpoint-syncing from a Gloas finalized checkpoint never leaves initial sync when the checkpoint block's bid lists blob commitments but the builder withheld the payload. It spins at 100% CPU re-requesting the origin's data columns by root (5M+ attempts in 7 minutes on the devnet) and downscores every peer on each attempt.

Why this only happens in Gloas: before Gloas, the payload and its blob commitments are in the block, so a checkpoint block that lists commitments guarantees the blobs or columns exist and can be fetched by root. In Gloas the block only carries the builder's bid. The payload and the blobs arrive later in a separate envelope, and the builder can withhold it. The origin column prefetch (`fetchOriginDataColumnSidecars`) still treats commitments in the block as proof that columns exist and retries with no exit condition. For a withheld payload no peer will ever have them.

Changes:

1. **Skip the origin column prefetch for Gloas origins** (`fetchOriginSidecars`). Forward sync settles the origin's data availability instead: the first batch requests envelopes starting one slot before its first block, so a revealed origin envelope is imported with its columns, and a withheld one has nothing to fetch. Pre-Gloas origins keep the existing prefetch.

2. **Keep the origin's columns when they arrive in the first batch** (`fetchSidecars`). The block queue starts fetching a few slots behind head, so the first response includes the already-imported origin. Those blocks are stripped before the per-block save loop, which dropped their columns. They are now carried in `columnsToSave` and persisted by `saveCarriedColumns`. This is what stores the origin's 128 columns in scenarios B and E below.

3. **Match the parent envelope by beacon block root, not only by execution hash** (new `BlockBuiltOnParentEnvelope`, used by `getBatchPrestate` and `envelopesForBlocks`). When a block's parent had no payload, the block's bid `parent_block_hash` points at the last revealed payload further back, so a hash-only match picks that ancestor's envelope and treats the parent as full. For a withheld origin at slot 32 this applied the slot-31 envelope to the checkpoint state and failed with `signature 'execution payload envelope signature' is invalid`. On develop the queue recovered after one failed batch, so this was not the stall on its own, but it is the same code path and the same root cause.

4. **Validate the envelope slot against the latest block header slot instead of the state slot** (`validatePayloadConsistency`). A checkpoint state can be advanced through empty slots past its latest block, and the origin envelope carries the block's slot. Timestamp derivation uses the header slot for the same reason. Not exercised on the devnet (see Not covered).

Not changed: pre-Gloas origin blob and column prefetch, processing of non-origin blocks and envelopes, peer scoring.

Follow-ups: rename `BlockBuiltOnEnvelope` to `BlockBuiltOnPayloadHash`; generalized parent-payload recovery for arbitrary batches was split out to its own PR.

## How this was tested

Devnet: 4 geth/prysm supernodes, Gloas at epoch 0, 6 s slots, blob spam. All four chain nodes ran the branch beacon. Checkpoint-syncing nodes were launched by hand on the enclave network in pairs (develop control vs branch) with their own fresh geth.

Version stamps of the images that ran:

```
prysm-beacon:ckpt-fix     -> beacon-chain version Prysm/v7.1.8/dcf508dbf8c7c71e91ca658d4135b094212f4ec5
prysm-beacon:ckpt-develop -> beacon-chain version Prysm/v7.1.8/6c7106c668091b55a81d66417adc8dc79c3be187
prysm-validator:withhold  -> validator version Prysm/v7.1.8/dcf508dbf8c7c71e91ca658d4135b094212f4ec5 (+ devnet-only fault below)
```

Withheld payloads were produced with a devnet-only validator patch, not part of this PR: with `--graffiti=WITHHOLD` the VC skips `proposeSelfBuildEnvelope` at the first slot of every odd epoch and logs `DEVNET FAULT: withholding self-build payload envelope`. So odd-epoch checkpoints have a withheld origin payload and even-epoch checkpoints a revealed one.

```go
	if devnetWithholdEnvelope(v.graffiti, slot) {
		log.WithField("slot", slot).Warn("DEVNET FAULT: withholding self-build payload envelope")
	} else if err := v.proposeSelfBuildEnvelope(ctx, slot, pubKey, blk); err != nil {
	…
func devnetWithholdEnvelope(graffiti []byte, slot primitives.Slot) bool {
	if len(graffiti) < 8 || string(graffiti[:8]) != "WITHHOLD" {
		return false
	}
	return slots.IsEpochStart(slot) && slots.ToEpoch(slot)%2 == 1
}
```

Spamoor's child wallets were unfunded after launch; `docker restart` of the spamoor container fixed it and blocks carried 2 to 4 blobs from slot 65 on.

Fault confirmation at slot 32 and 96 (cl-1 REST on `kurtosis port print ckpt-withhold cl-1-prysm-geth http`):

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' $P/eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes/0x356c68c9c7ad…26bea   # slot 32
404

slot 96 root=0x87f405c092b9 blobs=2 envelope_http=404
```

Syncing nodes were started with cl-1's launch args plus `--min-sync-peers=1 --bootstrap-node=<cl-1 ENR> --execution-endpoint=http://el-sync-<name>:8551` and either `--checkpoint-sync-url=http://cl-1-prysm-geth:3500` (scenarios A, B) or `--checkpoint-state=/cp/state.ssz --checkpoint-block=/cp/block.ssz` with files fetched from `GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/<slot>` and `GET /eth/v2/beacon/blocks/<slot>` as `application/octet-stream` (scenarios C, D, E). Files force the batch path (`syncToFinalizedEpoch`) because the peers' finalized epoch is already ahead; the URL variant landed on the regular path (`Already synced to finalized epoch`).

Status was sampled every 20 s from each node's `GET /eth/v1/node/syncing` together with `docker logs` counts.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | slot 96, withheld, blobs | URL, regular | stalled at 96 for 7 min, 100% CPU, peers downscored | synced to head |
| B | slot 128, revealed, blobs | URL, regular | synced to head | synced to head, origin envelope imported, 128 columns stored |

- A revealed origin payload where the first child builds on the empty parent.
- The Fulu to Gloas fork boundary inside the first batch (Gloas was active from genesis here).

title: Cancel sidecar parent-block fetches on sync service shutdown
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

When a blob or data column sidecar arrives over gossip before its parent block, the (blob/data column) validator spawns a goroutine that requests the parent by root (`sendBatchRootRequest`). 
Since #13061 that goroutine ran on `context.Background()`, so it never observed beacon node shutdown, and a cancelled context was not honored mid-request either.

This PR:

- Runs the sidecar parent fetch on the sync service context (`s.ctx`) instead of `context.Background()`.
- Registers `context.AfterFunc(ctx, stream.Reset)` in `SendBeaconBlocksByRootRequest` and `SendExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRootRequest`, so cancellation interrupts a blocked response read instead of waiting for the next chunk deadline.
- Checks `ctx.Err()` at the top of each retry and after each attempt in `sendBatchRootRequest`, so a cancelled request returns immediately instead of burning the remaining `numOfTries` attempts.
- Bounds the optimistic payload envelope fetch with `respTimeout` per attempt, the same bound `sendBeaconBlocksRequest` already applies to the block request. Previously the envelope request inherited the caller's context with no timeout of its own.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

title: FCR spectest for `v1.7.0-beta.0`
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

## Goal

Currently, FCR spectests are red in the `develop` branch. For non-gloas, there are 34 tests are failing, and for gloas, all FCR tests are failing. This PR makes FCR spectest green.

## Commit walkthrough

1. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17467/commits/30ecbcd636af93e2c20c4733b0d1d82c7f66ac59

This reverts commit 055ad523543c0961e516e71c2238eb0ea1eae6a5. (in #17122)

The stub aggregate pubkey only matched vectors generated before consensus-specs#5489. From v1.7.0-alpha.13 the pyspec computes real aggregate pubkeys with BLS disabled, so the stub diverges from `next_sync_committee.aggregate_pubkey` on every fast_confirmation case that crosses a sync committee period.

This unlocks two state-mismatch cases for Electra and Fulu:

- `is_one_confirmed_fails_recently_activated_validator_voting_in_empty_slot`
- `is_one_confirmed_passes_with_new_validator_activated_in_head_state`

2. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17467/commits/6b7667e9c2808df3d034aed4e46f55e046a55478

This enables `SafeBlockHash` return zero hash, which wasn't possible previously because it always falls back to unrealized justifed hash when lookup returns zero hash. This is implausible in mainnet, but with the context of spectest, it is possible as it often starts from genesis (zero hash).

This unlocks six `safe_execution_block_hash mismatch` cases from Bellatrix to Fulu:

- `fcr_no_restart_if_head_gu_is_stale`
- `fcr_no_restart_to_gu_because_gu_too_old`
- `fcr_no_restart_to_gu_mid_epoch`
- `fcr_reverts_to_finalized_when_confirmed_not_canonical_mid_epoch`
- `fcr_reverts_to_finalized_when_confirmed_too_old_lower_participation`
- `reset_to_finality_but_no_restart_to_gu_because_gu_too_old_epoch`

3. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17467/commits/6172a0671e53677b10475f3b5d7ae76cbc99134d

```python
def get_safe_execution_block_hash(fcr_store: FastConfirmationStore) -> Hash32:
    safe_block = fcr_store.store.blocks[fcr_store.confirmed_root]
    # [Modified in Gloas:EIP7732]
    return safe_block.body.signed_execution_payload_bid.message.parent_block_hash
```

In Gloas, the safe execution block hash is the confirmed block's bid `parent_block_hash`. Spectests setup has a Gloas genesis with non-zero `parent_block_hash`, which Prysm currently cannot accommodate as it returns zero byte when it is the tree root node.

Add a new field in FC store (`treeRootParentHash`) that records the payload hash that tree root's bid builds on, and return it when the walk finds no full ancestor.

This makes all 184 FCR tests for Gloas pass.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

title: Make fuzzer happy & Harden hdiff decoding
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix & CI

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Our CI for fuzzing has been mostly red these days: https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml. Most of them are complaining the out-of-bound issue that we currently have in fuzzing harness. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17470/commits/ccfc94a273206cf9ef9071683cc06204a7da2037 exactly fixes this.

Otherwise, it oftentime fails with this unknown status ([example run](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/actions/runs/32725115585/job/97425742241)):

```
  --- FAIL: FuzzApplyDiff (419.54s)
      fuzzing process hung or terminated unexpectedly: exit status 2
      Failing input written to testdata/fuzz/FuzzApplyDiff/52bafb783381e056
      To re-run:
      go test -run=FuzzApplyDiff/52bafb783381e056
```

and I (and Astra) strongly believe this was due to OOM as `snappy.Decode` will anyway allocate some crazy bytes from the fuzzed input. https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17470/commits/f79bb748c6456713bfc01d34046c62b448b90ea7 uses `DecodedLen` so it **never** allocates an implausibly excessive memory, which will save our fuzzer run.

This PR also includes some hardening hdiff decoding (or reading) across few commits (https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17470/commits/8bf5291cbdfcdaa81b7ce500a4460531942ea895, https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17470/commits/115e550b8a0b17c93726e0becaa81cfd22318a92), including multiplication overflow.

title: Replace EF bootstrap nodes with NodeOps fleet
body:
I am on the Ethereum Foundation's Node Infrastructure team (NodeOps). We run the bootnodes
that ship in this repository as the "EF" entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. We are
replacing that fleet, and we would like the new records in a release before the Glamsterdam
client releases.

### What changes

- Add five new EF bootnodes per network. Every node serves all three networks.
- Remove the legacy EF entries. The new set is a replacement, not an addition.
- Third-party bootnodes and DNS discovery roots are untouched.

### The new fleet

Five bootnodes, each serving mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. They are geographically distributed,
multi-cloud, and dual stack (IPv4 + IPv6). Each node runs discv4 and discv5 on the EL port and
discv5 on the CL port, and the fleet spreads across several discovery implementations so one
implementation bug cannot take the whole set down.

### About the records

- The ENRs are generic bootnode records: no `eth2` field, no `tcp`, sequence number 1. Clients
  dial configured bootnodes regardless of fork, and a static list cannot be re-signed every
  fork, so we do not include fork data on purpose.
- Where an EL list accepts ENRs, we list the ENR. It covers discv4 and discv5 and carries the
  IPv6 endpoint. Enodes appear only where a list needs them, in the discovery-only form
  `enode://<pubkey>@<ip>:0?discport=<port>` (no RLPx listener).
- The records are derived from the node keys and are byte-identical across all the client
  PRs. The canonical copies are the eth-clients PRs (`metadata/bootstrap_nodes.yaml` and
  `metadata/enodes.yaml` for mainnet, sepolia and hoodi).

### Verification

- Each node answers discv4 and discv5 pings from the public internet on the advertised ports.
- The relevant tests in this repository pass with the new lists (details below).
- The legacy nodes stay online until client releases with the new records are widely deployed.
  We will announce the shutdown separately.

### Contact

Chase Wright, EF Node Infrastructure. Discord `MysticRyuujin` (ETH R&D and STEEL servers), or
chase.wright@ethereum.org.

### This repository

**Files:** `config/params/{mainnet,testnet_sepolia,testnet_hoodi}_config.go`,
`changelog/mysticryuujin_nodeops-bootnodes.md`.

**Semantics:** `BootstrapNodes` swaps the EF ENRs (4 / 5 / 6) for the five new CL ENRs per
network.

**Tests:** `go test -tags develop ./config/params/`.

title: Gloas datacolumn boundary validation
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

During Gloas initial sync, the first block of a batch can build on the payload of a block from before the batch. When the range response does not carry that parent envelope, develop imports the batch anyway and never fetches, verifies, or stores the envelope. When the parent envelope is supplied, develop applies it after checking only its signature, and does not check that its data columns are available.

Now the node checks for the parent envelope before it imports a batch. If the envelope is not stored and not in the range response, the node requests it by root from up to three peers, starting with the peer that served the batch. It also fetches the parent's data columns when they are within the retention window. Batch import verifies the parent envelope against the pre-state and rejects the batch when the parent payload's data columns are not available. This applies to both finalized and head sync.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

**Other notes for review**

**Testing plan**

Kurtosis devnet (config below): 4 geth/prysm supernodes, Gloas at genesis, 6 s slots. A devnet-only validator fault skips the last slot of every epoch, so every 64-slot initial-sync batch (96, 160, 224, …) starts after an empty slot. A devnet-only patch on the two syncing nodes drops the last envelope from each batch's range response. As a result, no range response carries the next batch's parent envelope. Branch `Prysm/v7.2.1/60585a8fbc` and develop `Prysm/v7.2.1/4b5b0b85e1`, both with that patch, checkpoint-synced from the slot-64 state at finalized epoch 9 on 2026-10-08. After both reached head 611, each node was queried with `GET /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes/{slot}`.

title: Ignore bids from builders exited by the parent's payload
body:
- Adds the `[IGNORE]` condition from [consensus-specs#5580](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5580) to execution payload bid gossip validation.
- The parent's builder exits are applied by the child block, so the parent's post-state still shows the builder as active. A bid accepted here sinks the proposal that includes it.
- The parent envelope is only read when the bid builds on the parent's revealed payload, and the check runs after signature verification.
- That read is cheap. The DB stores the envelope blinded, so the transactions are already gone and only the execution requests are decoded: ~3us for a typical payload (4 KB stored) and ~64us for an unusually request-heavy one.

title: Ignore proposer preferences for pre-Gloas proposal slots
body:
- Adds the `[IGNORE]` condition from [consensus-specs#5559](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5559) to `proposer_preferences` gossip validation.
- Matters while nodes subscribe to the topic an epoch ahead of the fork, where a proposal slot can still fall before `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH`.
- The test setup now pins `GloasForkEpoch` to 0, which the existing cases need once the check exists.
author: terencechain

title: Reject proposer preferences pointing past the shuffling dependent slot
body:
- Adds the `[REJECT]` condition from [consensus-specs#5582](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5582) to `proposer_preferences` gossip validation.
- Adds `compute_shuffling_dependent_slot` as `slots.ShufflingDependentSlot`, clamped to the genesis slot for `epoch <= MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD`.
- A dependent block at or after the start of the lookahead epoch cannot be the block the shuffling depends on, so it is provably the sender's fault.
author: terencechain

title: Add the dependent root check to proposer preferences gossip
body:
- Adds `is_valid_dependent_root` from [consensus-specs#5443](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5443) to `proposer_preferences` gossip validation.
- Prysm required the dependent root to equal the head's. That ignores valid preferences on a competing branch, and then ignores every bid for that slot, since bid gossip keys the preferences cache on the bid's own branch rather than on the head.
- The check is expressed over the forkchoice tips: a block has a child crossing the epoch start exactly when some tip's dependent root for that epoch is that block. The head clause falls out of the caller's fast path.
- Off the head branch the proposer lookahead is now read from the dependent block's own state, and only when that state is already cached, never from a regeneration.
- Note: the existing one-epoch advance guard is kept, so a dependent block separated by empty epochs is still ignored rather than accepted.

title: Eip 8333
body:
**What type of PR is this?** Feature **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** This PR implements [EIP-8333: Align checkpoint with epoch boundary block](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8333) behind a new `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` config parameter. ### The change in one picture Ethereum finalizes in epochs of 32 slots. Every epoch, validators vote for one block, the "checkpoint" (their FFG target). Today that block is the epoch's **first** block. From the Heze fork it becomes the **last block before the epoch**, the epoch boundary block: ```text epoch 1 epoch 2 ... ───┬─────────┬─────────╫─────────┬─────────┬─── ... │ slot 62 │ slot 63 ║ slot 64 │ slot 65 │ ... ───┴─────────┴─────────╫─────────┴─────────┴─── ... ▲ ║ ▲ │ epoch │ │ boundary │ from Heze ──────────┘ └────────── before Heze checkpoint for epoch 2 checkpoint for epoch 2 = block at slot 63 = block at slot 64 (the boundary block) (the epoch's first block) ``` | | Checkpoint root for epoch N | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Before Heze | Latest block at or before the **first slot of epoch N** | | From Heze | Latest block at or before the **last slot of epoch N-1** (boundary block) | | Genesis epoch | Always the genesis block (unchanged) | **Why:** today the epoch's first proposer effectively picks the target the whole epoch votes on, and validators attesting in that same slot must decide within seconds whether the block arrived. Anchoring one slot earlier means the target is already known when the epoch begins, so a late or missing first block no longer splits target votes. ### How the implementation is shaped Everything funnels through one pair of helpers, gated on the fork epoch. Below `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` they return the epoch start slot, exactly what the old code used, so **every gated call site is provably a no-op until the fork activates** (mainnet and minimal default: far future). ```mermaid flowchart TD G["HEZE_FORK_EPOCH
config/params/config.go:212"] S["slots.CheckpointSlot
time/slots/slottime.go:127
(which slot anchors epoch N)"] R["helpers.CheckpointRoot
beacon-chain/core/helpers/block.go:116
(the block root at that slot)"] G --> S S --> R R --> A["State transition:
target matching + justification"] S --> B["Fork choice:
targets, viability, pruning"] S --> C["P2P bounds:
gossip floors, peer status"] S --> D["API:
finalized / justified state ids"] B --> E["Justified balances
at the checkpoint epoch"] ``` ### Two behavior changes before the fork (please look here first) Two changes are deliberately **not** gated. They fix pre-existing issues that today only show up when an epoch's first slot is empty, and that would break every checkpoint sync after Heze: 1. **Checkpoint sync origin epoch** (`beacon-chain/db/kv/wss.go:107`). We recorded the finalized checkpoint's epoch from the origin block's slot. When the checkpoint block is older than the checkpoint epoch, that label came out too small (it self-healed on the first finality update, which is why it went unnoticed). The epoch now comes from the state slot, which is always in the checkpoint epoch. 2. **Justified balances** (`beacon-chain/state/stategen/getter.go:104`). Fork choice weights now come from the checkpoint state advanced to the checkpoint epoch, matching the spec's `checkpoint_states`. Before, we read balances from the checkpoint block's own state, which is one epoch stale when the first slot is empty. Everything else in the PR does nothing until `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` is scheduled. ### Every place that changed **New building blocks** - `config/params/config.go:212`: new `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` parameter (wired through the loader, mainnet, and minimal configs; defaults to far future). - `time/slots/slottime.go:127`: new `slots.CheckpointSlot`, the slot anchoring an epoch's checkpoint. - `beacon-chain/core/helpers/block.go:116`: new `helpers.CheckpointRoot`, the spec's `get_checkpoint_root`. **State transition** - `beacon-chain/core/altair/attestation.go:344`: attestation target matching (rewards and participation flags) compares against the checkpoint root. - `beacon-chain/core/epoch/precompute/attestation.go:121`: same for the phase0 precompute path. - `beacon-chain/core/epoch/precompute/justification_finalization.go:164` and `:172`: newly justified checkpoints record the checkpoint root. **Fork choice** - `beacon-chain/forkchoice/doubly-linked-tree/store.go:134`: after the fork, an epoch-start block is no longer its own target; targets point back to the boundary block. - `beacon-chain/forkchoice/doubly-linked-tree/forkchoice.go:257`: checkpoint viability uses the checkpoint slot. - `beacon-chain/forkchoice/doubly-linked-tree/store.go:309`: pruning after finalization keeps children past the checkpoint slot (the finalized epoch's first block is now a child of the checkpoint, not a competitor). - `beacon-chain/forkchoice/doubly-linked-tree/forkchoice.go:489`: proposer-root bookkeeping clears up to the checkpoint slot. - `beacon-chain/forkchoice/interfaces.go:18` and `beacon-chain/forkchoice/doubly-linked-tree/forkchoice.go:768`: justified balance lookups carry the checkpoint epoch. **Blockchain service** - `beacon-chain/blockchain/process_block_helpers.go:383`: filling missing fork choice ancestors stops at the checkpoint slot. - `beacon-chain/blockchain/weak_subjectivity_checks.go:44`: the weak subjectivity search window shifts to the epoch of slots ending at the boundary. **P2P and gossip bounds** (every "is this already final?" check moves one slot earlier after the fork) - `beacon-chain/sync/validate_beacon_blocks.go:156`: block gossip. - `beacon-chain/verification/blob.go:148`: blob sidecar gossip. - `beacon-chain/verification/data_column.go:268`: data column sidecar gossip. - `beacon-chain/verification/execution_payload_envelope.go:109`: payload envelope gossip. - `beacon-chain/sync/rpc_execution_payload_envelopes_by_root.go:62`: oldest slot a peer may request. - `beacon-chain/sync/rpc_status.go:474`: peer status validation accepts boundary-anchored finalized checkpoints, and keeps the old loose check for pre-fork epochs so existing peers stay compatible. **HTTP API** - `beacon-chain/rpc/lookup/stater.go:152` and `:170`: `state_id=finalized` and `state_id=justified` resolve through the checkpoint slot, so a served checkpoint sync origin always descends from the checkpoint root. **Checkpoint sync and justified balances** (the two ungated fixes described above) - `beacon-chain/db/kv/wss.go:107` and `beacon-chain/state/stategen/getter.go:104`. **Tests, e2e, docs** - `testing/util/attestation.go:200`: generated test attestations vote for the checkpoint root. - `testing/endtoend/minimal_e2e_test.go:32`: the minimal e2e schedules Heze at epoch 2, so the run starts under the old anchoring, crosses the fork, and holds finality under the new one. - `testing/endtoend/endtoend_test.go:284`: the checkpoint sync wait retries transient errors instead of aborting. - `docs/eip-8333-design.md`: design doc with the full reasoning, alternatives considered, and cross-client notes. - New unit tests in every touched area (slots, helpers, state transition, fork choice, stategen, blockchain, sync, verification, db). **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?** Part of EIP-8333 (Heze) support. **Other notes for review** - The branch is 14 self-contained commits in dependency order; it should read well commit by commit. - The first two commits are fork-independent fixes that apply to today's mainnet behavior; happy to split them into their own PRs if preferred. - `HEZE_FORK_VERSION` (fork digest plumbing) is intentionally out of scope; it is only needed once the fork is actually scheduled. - A changelog fragment is included. **Acknowledgements** - [ ] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - title: Fix backfill nil panic in columnsNeeded when a batch needs no columns
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

- Backfill panicked with a nil pointer SIGSEGV in batch.columnsNeeded when a batch had no column work (e.g. all blocks pre-Fulu or outside the column retention window), because newColumnSync returns a non-nil &columnSync{} whose embedded *columnBatch is nil, and the wrapper called the promoted (*columnBatch).needed() instead of the nil-guarded (*columnSync).columnsNeeded(). 
- This PR routes the call through the guarded method and adds a regression test that reproduces the crash without the fix.

title: Gloas late head payloads
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

After a restart, forkchoice is rebuilt without the payload envelopes already sitting in the DB,
and initial sync treated "envelope in DB" as "envelope processed" — so nothing re-imported them.
The node gets stuck optimistic at its checkpoint slot, failing batches:

```
WARN  initial-sync: Block processing failure error=post block process: could not process block: could not insert block 98 to fork choice store: invalid parent root firstSlot=64 lastSlot=98
WARN  initial-sync: Execution payload envelope processing failure error=beacon block root 0xea6457... not found in forkchoice firstSlot=129
```

With this change the same restart recovers in ~40s with no warnings (43 envelope re-imports in
the first minute vs 0 on a control node without the fix).

- `isProcessedPayload` now requires the forkchoice full node in addition to the persisted
  envelope, so envelopes persisted before forkchoice insertion completed are re-imported.
- An all-known batch no longer drops the head's unimported envelope, and data columns of
  filtered known blocks are saved instead of discarded.
- The per-slot late-payload requester from #16904 only fired while the head was the current
  slot's block; it now also retries a stale head's missing envelope, covering a payload-less
  head at the initial-sync → regular-sync handoff. Existing guards (present/known-bad
  short-circuit, singleflight) keep healthy-node request volume unchanged.
  
  ## How this was tested

4-node kurtosis devnet: Gloas from genesis, 6s slots, blob spam, fault VC (`WITHHOLD` graffiti)
that skips epoch-boundary slots and withholds envelopes at the first slot of odd epochs — so
justified checkpoints land on withheld/skipped slots. cl-1..cl-3 ran the branch
(`Prysm/v7.1.8/5ad989eae3...`, verified via `--version`), cl-4 the base stack without the fix
(`Prysm/v7.1.8/f712acc6b9...`) as control.

```yaml
    vc_image: prysm-validator:ppv-fault
    cl_log_level: debug
    vc_log_level: info
    cl_extra_params:
      - --min-sync-peers=1
    vc_extra_params:

    supernode: true
```

title: Serve available historical Gloas payload envelopes by root
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The execution payload envelopes ByRoot handler silently omits available envelopes older than the serving node's finalized epoch. A lagging requester can still need those envelopes to process blocks newer than its own finalized checkpoint.

removing the finalized epoch cuttoff so available historical envelopes can be constructed and served by root. This follows the expanded ByRoot serving window introduced in [consensus-specs #4950](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4950)

 # How this was tested

Two 4-node kurtosis devnets, Gloas from genesis, `WITHHOLD` fault VC. Because this PR only changes
what a node *serves*, the requesting nodes are held fixed and the peers are swapped between runs:

- **Two block-producing nodes holding all validators** — on this PR (`Prysm/v7.1.8/bf4e6298ed...`)
  in one run, on develop (`Prysm/v7.1.8/7730c643fe...`) in the other.
- **Requesting nodes with no validators, running develop** (`Prysm/v7.1.8/7730c643fe...`) — the
  same image in both runs, two of them against PR peers and one against develop peers. No stake
  means the network keeps finalizing while they are down, and a develop requester has no recovery
  path of its own, so anything it recovers came from the peer that served it.
- **Two devnet-only patches on the requesting nodes, neither part of this PR**: `resyncIfBehind`
  disabled, since resync otherwise rescues them within ~2 min and closes the window; and the
  stale-head envelope requester from the `gloas-late-head-payloads` stack, which asks for the
  envelope.

Procedure, identical in both runs: restart both requesters at slot 168 — head lands on the epoch-4
checkpoint block, slot 126 (slot 128 was skipped) — and they fetch its envelope normally, since the
servers' finalized epoch is still 3 and the old cutoff sits at slot 96. Then stop both, wait for
the network to finalize past that block (epoch 3 → 5, moving the old cutoff to slot 160), and start
them again. Against PR peers, ~4 s from start to import:

```
14:43:29.49  INFO blockchain: Initialized head block from DB root=0x4a2a61a3c7d7... slot=126
14:43:33.43  INFO blockchain: Synced execution payload envelope blockHash=0xb4a6e865f524 blockRoot=0x4a2a61a3c7d7 parentHash=0x9376378ecee6 slot=126
```

Counted from container logs over the three minutes after start, per requester:

| | peers on this PR | peers on develop |
|---|---|---|
| by-root envelope requests | 46 | 103 |
| envelopes imported | 1 | 0 |
| `is_optimistic` afterwards | false | true |

The two requesters facing PR peers behaved identically; the develop-peers column is the single
develop requester in that run. Against develop peers a requester never recovers and keeps asking
every slot indefinitely; against PR peers it stops once the envelope lands, which is why its
request count is lower.

Their only two ERROR lines (`could not get duty dependent root`, geth's `Too deep reorg`) are
pre-existing behavior of marking a stale head full, unrelated to this change: the same pair appears
in both runs, and also on develop nodes importing the same envelope through the ordinary path
before the window opens.

```yaml
participants:
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master-101035a
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-beacon:msp-develop
    vc_image: prysm-validator:ppv-fault
    cl_log_level: debug
    vc_log_level: info
    vc_extra_params:
      - --graffiti=WITHHOLD
    supernode: true
    validator_count: 128
    count: 2
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master-101035a
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-beacon:msp-fix-probe
    cl_log_level: debug
    cl_extra_params:
      - --disable-peer-scorer
    supernode: true
    validator_count: 0
    count: 1
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master-101035a
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-beacon:msp-develop-probe
    cl_log_level: debug
    cl_extra_params:

  spammers:
    - scenario: eoatx
      name: "EOA spam"
```

title: grpc use execution_payload_available event
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

gRPC validator clients never received `execution_payload_available` — the gRPC event stream only
carried the head topic — so every PTC vote waited out the deadline: 4.51s into a 6s slot, versus
0.23s for a REST client on the same chain.

- New deprecated-tagged `StreamExecutionPayloadAvailable` RPC on `BeaconNodeValidator` forwards the
  existing `statefeed.ExecutionPayloadAvailable` event as `{slot, block_root}` — the same signal the
  REST SSE topic serves. A 16-deep outbox with its own sender goroutine returns `ResourceExhausted`
  rather than letting a slow client stall envelope processing.
- The gRPC VC's `StartEventStream` runs it alongside `StreamSlots`, emitting the same event JSON as
  REST. `ProcessEvent` and the `payloadAvailability` waiter are unchanged.
- Against an older beacon node the stream returns `Unimplemented`; the VC warns once per bind
  (`Beacon node does not support payload availability streaming; gRPC PTC votes will wait for the
  deadline. Upgrade the beacon node or use --beacon-rest-api-provider for on-arrival voting`) and
  keeps deadline voting on the head stream. Any other stream failure tears both down and the runner
  re-binds as before.
- Not changed: the REST path; head_v2 over gRPC still downgrades to v1 head (#13563).

# Follow-ups, deliberately separate

- **Deadline-path tolerance differs.** With no event, REST re-polls for 500ms past the due mark;
  gRPC asks once. Only matters if the node's clock trails the VC's; zero occurrences observed. The
  right fix is server-side — `Service.PayloadAttestationData` waiting out its own deadline instead
  of returning `Unavailable` — which makes both transports identical with no client code.
- **REST logged empty slots as errors**, dropping the node's `204` during re-poll. Found in this run,
  fixed on `ptc-no-content-classification`; not caused here. this pr try to fix it https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17510
- **`payloadAvailability` is pruned only on `notify`**, so a node that never emits the event (the
  compat path above) grows it unbounded. Small standalone fix.


## How this was tested

4-node geth/prysm kurtosis devnet, gloas from genesis, 6s slots, spamoor, slots 0–319, images
`Prysm/v7.1.8/d85408468c…`. The package forces Prysm VCs into REST mode, so the gRPC VCs were
started by hand reusing the kurtosis volumes. Same VC binary everywhere: `grpc-vc-1` → cl-1 (PR),
`vc-2`/`vc-3` REST → cl-2/cl-3 (PR), `grpc-vc-4` → cl-4 running develop `7730c643fe` with no
`StreamExecutionPayloadAvailable` — the A/B control.

<details><summary>args-file and gRPC VC command</summary>

```yaml

  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master-101035a
    cl_type: prysm

    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest      # d85408468c
    cl_log_level: debug
    vc_log_level: debug
    supernode: true
    validator_count: 64
    count: 3
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:master-101035a
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-beacon:msp-develop                        # 7730c643fe
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    cl_log_level: debug
    vc_log_level: debug
```

title: Limit V3 codec coverage to pre-Gloas forks
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The validator V3 block API supports forks before Gloas; Gloas uses V4. Its codec coverage test currently uses `version.All()`, which would incorrectly require a V3 Gloas codec once Gloas is included in that list.

Add `version.Before(cutoff)` to return supported forks strictly before the cutoff, and use `version.Before(version.Gloas)` for V3 codec coverage. Add tests for cutoff boundaries, fork ordering, and appending without overwriting the supported fork list, plus a `pvl-` changelog fragment.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

None.

title: archive node: fix startup panic for non initialized statediffcache in saveGenesisData
body:
#17292 is initializing stateDiffCache only after `StartDB` in node startup, but `StartDB` calls `SaveGenesisData` which in turn calls `HasState` and then we panic for a fresh db because cache is not initialized. 

this patch fixes two things:
- makes `hasStateUsingStateDiff` return false and not panic when cache is not initialized.
- changes the `SaveHeadBlockRoot` so we won't call `HasState` if `HasStateSummary` already returned true. this should save us a bunch of reads from the tree.

title: ExecutionBlockHashProof for lightclient
body: Adds Gloas-compatible light-client proof generation for progressive SSZ containers. Introduces the execution block hash proof, fork-aware generalized indices, and version/container-specific active-field schemas, while preventing legacy payload proofs from being used for Gloas.
author: Inspector-Butters

title: hdiff optimization: Sparse ApplyValidatorsDiff
body:
Apply validator state diffs using sparse per-index updates and appends instead of materializing and rebuilding the entire validator registry.

This reduces memory spikes during state reconstruction, especially when validator diffs are empty or affect only a small subset of validators. Diffs are fully index-validated before mutation, with a compatibility fallback for existing public-key changes.

title: fixing 204 handling for rest ptc attestation
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

On a Gloas devnet, REST validator clients logged an error for every ordinary empty slot:

```
ERROR client: Could not request payload attestation data error=could not get execution payload
attestation data: query until accepted: context deadline exceeded retried=false slot=317
```

Nothing was wrong. The beacon node had answered `204 No Content` — which
`GetPayloadAttestationData` returns explicitly "to signal the validator not to cast a payload
attestation". An expected condition was being reported as a hard failure.

No votes were lost either way — both transports abstain correctly on an empty slot — so this is a
reporting and metrics defect, not a voting one.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

title: Decouple `BuilderService` with DB
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR is based on the fact that `v4.0.7` was released over [three years ago](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/releases/tag/v4.0.7). And in our [documentation for builder](https://prysm.offchainlabs.com/docs/configure-prysm/builder/#registration-cache), it says:

> Validator registrations for Builder APIs are stored in a cache by default as of 4.0.7 instead of bolt db when starting the beacon node. ... In the future the db used to store registrations will be removed completely and the flag will no longer be required for this feature. Validator settings will be persisted on the validator client side.

This PR in one line: Remove all legacy DB usage for builder service. This requires to deprecate one flag: `--disable-registration-cache`. I think it's worth doing at this moment because we're aheading Gloas which requires significant change for proposer settings and by giving up this niche flag code complexity and dependency graph gets much simpler.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

Each commit incrementally applies the change.

- [Deprecate flag: --disable-registration-cache](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17515/commits/148af46c7e6112ee9e96b401f19d4cdebfdf2829): Move the flag into deprecated zone.
- [Remove the validator registration DB path](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17515/commits/12510b8bb1670af4b415ec9f80dae65f896559b6): `RegisterValidator` and `RegistrationByValidatorID` only checks the registration cache which is our hot path at this point.
- [Read fee recipients from the proposer preferences cache](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17515/commits/5634468c99ee0e29774b4edc920f00063e314c8b): `GetFeeRecipientByPubKey` (which has no production caller in the codebase but anyway) now checks the cache instead of calling `BeaconDB.FeeRecipientByValidatorID`. Thus we now don't have any `Fee recipients operations.` in our DB.

title: Marshal states directly behind their DB version key when saving
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: Optimization

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR uses `MarshalSSZTo` instead of `MarshalSSZ`, which requires one more copy for the SSZ object. The size of buffer is expected as we have `SizeSSZ` API, so it makes sense to set the capacity with this size getter.

With this PR, state saving would be much more efficient, and it has a high impact for the nodes with lower `slots-per-archive-point` (e.g., 32). This can be a good memory optimization before we make hdiff in production.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

title: adding builder settings flags for proposer settings
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Operators can now configure Gloas builders for all validators from the command line, the way `--suggested-fee-recipient` sets the default fee recipient, instead of needing a proposer settings file, URL, or keymanager API call:

- `--builder-urls` — comma-separated builder URLs; auth data may be appended as a hex fragment (`https://builder.example#0x0123`), otherwise the URL's UTF-8 bytes are used.
- `--builder-min-bid`, `--builder-boost-factor`, `--builder-max-execution-payment` — Gwei / percentage / Gwei, written only when set so an explicit `0` stays distinct from "inherit".

How the flags behave, in three rules:

1. **The flags set the default builder settings for this run only.** Pass them on every start, like `--enable-builder`. A start without them clears any default builders list left in the DB by an earlier run and warns once. Without `--suggested-fee-recipient`, the flags keep the default fee recipient already in the DB.
2. **Everything else keeps its precedence.** A settings file or URL `default_config` replaces the flag default and warns which flags it overrode. Per-key settings from a file, URL, or the keymanager API win over the flag default and are never touched.
3. **Before Gloas, a non-empty `--builder-urls` list turns builder registration on**, the way `--enable-builder` does, for every key that resolves a fee recipient. A per-key `builders: []` opts that key out. `--enable-builder` behaves as before.
4. **`--suggested-gas-limit` now applies from Gloas onward too.** It sets the default gas limit that pre-Gloas registrations and post-Gloas proposer preferences both read, so after the fork it overrides the network gas limit schedule (EIP-8261). Operators should remove it once Gloas is live to follow the schedule. Startup warns when the flag is set on a network with Gloas scheduled, and separately when the value exceeds the highest scheduled gas limit; the existing per-epoch warning covers the active schedule value. Like the builder defaults, the default gas limit applies per run: a start without the flag drops the persisted one and warns once.

Keys inherit from the flag default field by field: a key with only a fee recipient uses the flag builders; a key with its own list keeps it and inherits unset preferences such as `min_bid`. A run whose only default content is builder flags persists nothing and no longer logs the "proposer settings are empty" warning.

Schema handling: any builder flag stamps the flag source with the highest supported schema version (`MaxSchemaVersion`, currently 2); an unversioned file with v2 fields is still inferred as version 2. The merge dispatches on `version < 2` for the legacy path, so later schema versions take the current path by default. `--enable-builder` still applies as legacy pre-Gloas content and is scrubbed at the Gloas cutover as before; on version 1 databases `--suggested-gas-limit` also keeps writing the legacy builder-level gas limit, which the cutover scrubs while the option-level default carries over. On a network with no Gloas fork scheduled the flags are accepted with a warning.

The help text of every defaults-only flag, `--suggested-fee-recipient` included, now ends with "Per-key settings from a proposer settings file, URL, or the keymanager API take precedence." The one new startup log is a Warn that fires once when a restart drops a persisted default builders list because neither builder flags nor a settings source configured one:

```
Dropped the default builder settings a previous run stored in the validator DB because neither builder flags nor a settings source configured a builders list this run; pass --builder-urls or the settings file on every start
```

Not changed: settings-file and keymanager behavior, the runtime `EffectiveBuilderConfig` resolution, bid selection on the beacon node, and the version 1 builder merge. The flagless behavior changes are the version 2 switch rule above, which applies to a DB that an earlier run already stamped version 2, and the per-run default gas limit in rule 4.

## How the flags work together

All six flags set the defaults for this start, the `default_config` of the proposer settings. Per-key settings from a settings file, URL, or the keymanager API always win over them. A file or URL `default_config` replaces the flag defaults as a whole.

| Flag | Sets | Before Gloas | From Gloas | Restart without it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--suggested-fee-recipient` | default fee recipient | fee recipient for proposals and builder registrations | fee recipient in proposer preferences | kept from the DB |
| `--suggested-gas-limit` | default gas limit | gas limit in builder registrations, sent only while registration is on | gas limit in proposer preferences for every key; overrides the network schedule, remove it to follow the schedule | dropped, one warning |
| `--enable-builder` | legacy builder toggle | turns builder registration on for keys with a fee recipient | no effect, warned, cleared at the fork | dropped, as today |
| `--builder-urls` | default builders list | a non-empty list turns registration on, like `--enable-builder` | builders to request bids from | dropped, one warning |
| `--builder-min-bid` | default minimum bid | none | floor for builder and gossip bids | dropped |
| `--builder-boost-factor` | default boost factor | none | weight of bids against the local payload; 100 is neutral, 0 always builds locally | dropped |
| `--builder-max-execution-payment` | default payment cap | none | execution payment counted for bids from the listed builders | dropped |

| Combination | Result |
|---|---|
| `--builder-urls` with `--enable-builder` | Redundant before Gloas. `--enable-builder` still logs its legacy warning. |
| `--builder-urls` without `--suggested-gas-limit` | Registrations and preferences use the network default gas limit, or the schedule once one is active. Nothing is carried over from an earlier start. |
| `--suggested-gas-limit` without `--enable-builder` or `--builder-urls` | Before Gloas nothing sends it. From Gloas it is the preference gas limit for every key. |
| `--builder-min-bid` or `--builder-boost-factor` without `--builder-urls` | Still apply to gossip bids, and per-key builder lists inherit them. |
| `--builder-max-execution-payment` without `--builder-urls` | No effect until a builders list exists. Per-key lists inherit it. |
| Builder flags without `--suggested-fee-recipient` | The stored default fee recipient stays. Without one anywhere, only keys with their own fee recipient register before Gloas. |
| Any flag with a file or URL that has `default_config` | The source's `default_config` wins whole. Overridden builder flags are named in a warning; the fee recipient and gas limit flags are replaced silently. Kept from today: with a version 1 file, `--suggested-gas-limit` still sets the builder gas limit used for registrations. |
| Any flag with a file or URL without `default_config` | The flag defaults stay and the source's per-key entries apply. |
| Per-key settings through the keymanager API | Win over every flag and survive restarts, unless a file or URL with per-key entries is configured, which replaces them. |


**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

title: recover missing dependent root during startup
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`head` and `head_v2` events carry two dependent roots that validator clients compare against
their cached duties to decide whether to refetch. Prysm derives both by walking forkchoice back
to the last block before the epoch. At startup forkchoice is rooted at the finalized checkpoint
block (the anchor) and has no ancestors, so a dependent root that lies before the anchor cannot
be resolved. Two failure modes, both hit on every checkpoint sync and every restart:

- **Head in the anchor's epoch F** (checkpoint sync: the catch-up blocks between the anchor and
  the network head are processed through `ReceiveBlock`, so each one produces a head event).
  The previous-epoch root is before the anchor, forkchoice returns `ErrNilNode`, and the event
  is dropped:
  ```
  ERROR blockchain: Could not notify event feed of new chain head error=could not get duty dependent root: invalid nil or unknown node
  ERROR blockchain: Could not notify event feed of new chain head_v2 error=could not get duty dependent root: invalid nil or unknown node
  ```
  No `head`/`head_v2` event reaches subscribers for the whole epoch.
- **Head in epoch F+1** (checkpoint sync catch-up, and restart, which starts with the justified
  block as head). The previous-epoch root is the anchor's parent. Forkchoice substitutes
  `finalizedDependentRoot`, which is zero until the first prune, and the zero-root fallback then
  emitted the origin block root, i.e. the anchor itself, as `previous_duty_dependent_root`. A
  wrong root, silently, for a full epoch.
  
  This PR keeps the forkchoice lookup as the primary source and adds a fallback for the two cases
above (`ErrNilNode` or a zero root): the dependent root for epoch E is read from the head
state's `block_roots` at slot `start(E) - 1`, the same derivation `core.ProposalDependentRoot`
uses for the duties endpoints. The head state is fetched at most once per event and only when
forkchoice misses, so the steady-state path is unchanged. Epoch 0 keeps the origin root.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Raised by @potuz from the same symptom in crysm (dependent root unavailable at startup
after checkpoint sync).

**What type of PR is this?**

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`chain_reorg` SSE topic has no deduplication logic for payload status flip (from empty -> full), so this PR adds a simple gate for reorg checking.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**
