title: Remove `BeaconState` proto message
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: (Very nice) cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR removes `beacon_state.proto` and automatically generated `*.pb.go` files corresponds to it. Instead, we now replaces all proto message definition of `BeaconState{Fork}` with native Go struct.

**Before**:

```proto
message BeaconState {
  // Versioning [1001-2000]
  uint64 genesis_time = 1001;
  // ... and so on
}
```

- Add new `BeaconState` per fork in `beacon_state.proto` file
- Run `make gen` for executing `protoc`, so that we have a Go struct.
- This system enforces us to have few converter functions from/to proto, as well as slice type even though it is completely fine to use array type for fixed bytevector.

**After**:

```go
// in beacon_state_mainnet.go
// BeaconState is the Phase0 SSZ state.
type BeaconState struct {
	GenesisTime                 uint64
	GenesisValidatorsRoot       []byte `ssz-size:"32"`
	Slot                        primitives.Slot
	Fork                        *Fork
	LatestBlockHeader           *BeaconBlockHeader
// and so on
```

- Add new `BeaconState` per fork in `beacon_state_{mainnet|minimal}.go` file
- No need to generate `*.pb.go` files related to the state. Plus we remove over 9K lines of generated files which is awesome.
- Note that we don't need few entries in `ssz_proto_library.bzl` as it is now natively maintained in native Go struct definition.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17503

**Other notes for review**

### How to review this PR

This PR is designed to review commit by commit. It consists of three parts:

#### Revisit the testing harness

Until [fix(ssz): derive query field names without json tags](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/1d108c7df7ce5706143346267706dd69ba884bf2), these are collections of groundwork for the later work. First commit ([test(state): support non-protobuf states in SSZ harness](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/e5684be8e28493ceab7f06ebb15fed5fd07da825)) is note-worthy - as it touches our equality check. Main purpose is dropping proto dependency on equality check.

#### Mechanical change from Altair to Gloas, and then Phase0

From [refactor(state): replace Altair protobuf with SSZ struct](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/27f63deac9d8f5e7f5e88b022d94d32c850fa03b) to [refactor(state): replace Phase0 protobuf with SSZ struct](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/4d8c2f5c6087e4f8df7db7d5c2c36bfb29bce9d8),
each commit mechanically migrates to native struct per fork. Most of the diff of each commit is regenerated `*.pb.go` files and some equality check in our spectest runner.

Phase0 is deliberately done after Gloas as it has different wire format and pattern when saving in the storage.

#### Cleanups

From [refactor(state): drop protobuf from beacon-chain/state](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/217be0feaabf9456e5a2b0fea1be9349cd5ba77f), commits are mostly cleaning things up which are now unused or dead. [refactor(proto): remove beacon_state.proto](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/69d9f54a3694b2a89a7f26cf999cbb135083a22d) is note-worthy, as it retires `beacon_state.proto` and moves each proto message into separate parts in the codebase, so please read the description.

### Production Risk

Before #17523, there was a very tiny production risk on DB migration, but now we don't have. I _believe_ this PR doesn't bring any production risk and should work well without any problems, but here's some notes:

- DB compatability: We save `BeaconState` in SSZ format, so it doesn't need to be considered. Same behavior.
- `CopySlice(nil)` returns `nil` instead of `[]`.
- SSZ Query package changes are not considered as production IMO.

### Follow-ups

- Move state-related definition and function into dedicated package. `proto/` package is not proper location now.
- Rename `*Proto*` methods. I deliberately omitted it in this PR because it covers almost entire codebase.
- Delegate SSZ List limit and SSZ Vector length to `fieldparams` configuration which is considered as canonical.
- Better memory allocation and no more Proto conversion.
  - As `methodical-ssz` doesn't support yet for array type, we need a patch there.

title: add grpc retry to parity rest for PTC votes
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

 Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

A gRPC validator client could drop its PTC vote after one failed request. It asked the beacon node once when the payload-availability event arrived and, if that failed, once more at the PTC due time. When that second answer was also `Unavailable`, for example because the beacon node's clock trails the validator's and it has not reached its own due time yet, the slot was skipped. A first request that began at or after the due time was never retried at all. REST clients already re-polled for 500ms past the due mark inside the REST transport, so the two transports tolerated the same lag differently.

**Semantic change:** after the first failed request, the shared validator code waits until the PTC due time if necessary, then retries with a 50ms pause after each failed attempt for up to 500ms, bounded by the parent context. If the first failure arrives after due, the retry window starts then. A successful response proceeds to signing and submission; expiry or parent cancellation ends the retries.

Exact total read-time parity is left to #17552: this PR retains REST's internal polling, so REST can consume its own polling window before the shared retry window begins.

**How this was tested**

4-node geth/Prysm kurtosis devnet, gloas from genesis, 6s slots, spamoor, slots 20–274 (2026-09-24 14:33–14:58 UTC). The fix only shows on slots whose payload is not final at the validator's due time, so two image-only faults were induced (patches in the collapsed block): cl-1 runs its PTC deadline check 300ms behind real time, standing in for a beacon node whose clock trails the validator's, and vc-4 withholds its self-built payload on even slots. Three validators read PTC data from cl-1: `grpc-branch` (a1934ef7b8, this PR) and `grpc-control` (b7e659a7a8, its parent commit, the control) hand-started in gRPC mode, plus the kurtosis REST validator vc-1 on the PR image.

-	if err := v.proposeSelfBuildEnvelope(ctx, slot, pubKey, blk); err != nil {
+	if devnetWithholdEnvelope(g, slot) {

@@ -630,3 +637,18 @@ func blockLogFields(pubKey [fieldparams.BLSPubkeyLength]byte, blk interfaces.Rea

 }

29 slots were withheld and cl-1 held the data back on every one (26 inside the window). Per validator, on the induced slots where it had a PTC duty and on the healthy slots:

| validator | induced slots | healthy slots |
|---|---|---|
| grpc-control (parent) | 24 skipped with `retried=false`, 0 votes | 212 votes, p50 222ms, max 287ms |
| grpc-branch (PR) | 25 votes, all `payloadPresent=false`, p50 4845ms | 207 votes, p50 223ms, max 286ms |
| rest-branch (PR, REST) | 21 votes, all `payloadPresent=false`, p50 4844ms | 213 votes, p50 223ms, max 281ms |

Slot 64, verbatim (due at 4.5s, cl-1 serves from 4.8s):

```
vc-4         14:37:35.19 WARN  DEVNET FAULT: withholding self-build payload envelope slot=64
cl-1         14:37:39.50 WARN  DEVNET FAULT: PTC data held past the real deadline by clock lag sinceDeadline=2.719538ms slot=64
grpc-control 14:37:39.51 INFO  Skipping payload attestation: data unavailable error=PayloadAttestationData: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = payload attestation data not yet final for slot 64 retried=false slot=64
grpc-branch  14:37:39.51 DEBUG Payload attestation data not final yet, polling from the deadline error=... not yet final for slot 64 slot=64
grpc-branch  14:37:39.85 DEBUG Submitted new payload attestation blobDataAvailable=true blockRoot=0xed5a785ac23d payloadPresent=false slot=64 timeSinceSlotStart=4.859442126s
rest-vc-1    14:37:39.83 DEBUG Submitted new payload attestation blobDataAvailable=true blockRoot=0xed5a785ac23d payloadPresent=false slot=64 timeSinceSlotStart=4.839259538s
```

The following blocks carried the payload-absent aggregate (blocks 65/91/111/175: 381/446/453/438 of 512 bits set) against 511 after healthy slots. Finalized epoch 6 at slot 267, 0 `Verification of aggregate failed` on any node. Counters at slot 267: grpc-branch `validator_payload_attestation_data_retry_total{outcome="recovered"} 56` and no skips; grpc-control `validator_payload_attestation_submission_total{result="skipped_unavailable"} 49`.

**Not covered:** real clock skew (emulated only inside the PTC data handler); a payload arriving between the due time and due+300ms (every induced slot was payload-absent); a stalled REST beacon node, which is #17552's scope. cl-1 logged two 12-line `Failed to find peers` bursts (14:42, 14:48) with all three peers connected; beacon p2p, not touched here.

**Other notes for review**

#17552 is stacked on this PR and finishes the parity work. It:

- Bounds the initial request and every retry by the earlier of the parent deadline and 500ms after the later of PTC due or read start. Failed requests retry with a 50ms pause, including before due.
- Polls REST beacon nodes independently, with at most one outstanding request per node, so a stalled node cannot prevent a responsive node from retrying. REST uses the common cutoff instead of adding another grace window.
- Keeps root preference and the latest usable fallback inside REST. gRPC accepts its first successful response immediately. REST validates each response with the endpoint decoder before it can become a winner or replace a fallback.
- Adds real gRPC, REST JSON and REST SSZ transport coverage for timing, failure recovery and stalled peers.

It is separate because it changes the multi-node REST query machinery in `api/rest`, which this minimal fix does not need. Review this PR on its own; the follow-up rebases onto develop once this merges.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Closes the "deadline-path tolerance differs" follow-up noted in #17500.

title: Unify PTC reads and retry REST nodes independently
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

 Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

After #17550 the two transports reach the same result by different paths. The gRPC client polls in the validator layer from the due time. The REST transport polls on its own until the due time plus 500ms, and the validator layer polls around it again. A REST validator with several beacon nodes also polls them in rounds, and a round waits for every node, so one stalled node holds the answer from a responsive one until the round's deadline. On the devnet below that cost a quarter of the healthy-slot votes 4.7 seconds each.

Now the validator layer owns one cutoff for both transports: the PTC due time, or now if that has passed, plus 500ms. It asks every 50ms until a request succeeds or the cutoff passes. A request that fails before the due time is retried on that cadence instead of waiting for the due time. The REST transport takes that cutoff from the caller, polls each beacon node on its own loop, and rejects responses it cannot decode before choosing one. Preferring the node that reports the announced head stays inside the REST transport as before.

Unchanged: when a request succeeds, gRPC votes on it as is. The retry counter counts validator-layer retries only, so REST-internal polling of individual nodes does not move it. No beacon node code changes.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Follow-up to #17550.

**How this was tested**

5-node geth/Prysm kurtosis devnet, gloas from genesis, 6s slots, spamoor, slots 18–258 (2026-09-24 20:50–21:14 UTC). Two image-only faults (patches in the collapsed block): cl-1 checks the PTC deadline 150ms late, standing in for a beacon node whose clock trails the validator's, and cl-3 holds every PTC data request open until the caller gives up. vc-4 withholds its self-built payload on even slots so some slots are not final at the due time. Four validators: `rest-base-2n` (ef3dceeba1, #17550 on the same develop, the control) and `rest-follow-2n` (2a4266ee35, this PR) both REST against cl-1 and cl-3; `grpc-follow` and `rest-follow` on this PR against cl-1 alone.

title: Apply block PTC votes to every seat and skip votes for older blocks
body: Block-carried payload attestations now write each voter's vote to every PTC seat it holds, matching on_payload_attestation_message and the gossip path. Votes whose data.slot does not match the voted block's slot are skipped, as the spec returns early for them after a skipped slot.

title: Reject Builder-API bids whose block hash equals the parent block hash
body: validateBuilderBid now enforces bid.block_hash != bid.parent_block_hash, which process_execution_payload_bid and bid gossip already check, so a builder can no longer make the proposer build an invalid block.

title: Reject by-root Gloas column sidecars whose slot does not match the block
body: Gloas sidecars have no signed block header, so the by-root path accepted any slot and stored the column under it, which could push the pruner cutoff forward. The sidecar slot is now checked against the local block's slot.

title: Unfinalized checkpoint sync
body:
This PR fakes a finalized checkpoint on forkchoice and allows the node to start from an arbitrary state. 

Tested on KT as follows: 

- Start a run with 7 nodes, 3 prysm, 2 Lighthouse, 2 Lodestar. 
- Wait for finalization. 
- Stop the PRysm nodes. 
- Wait 6 epochs without finalizing. 
- Grab a checkpoint state from either LH or Lodestar. 
- Restart the Prysm nodes with an empty db and from the unfinalized checkpoint. 

The node immediately catches up and starts attesting.

title: Accept late previous-fork attestations on the current fork's subnet topic
body: Unaggregated attestation topic validation derived the expected digest from the attestation's slot, so after a fork boundary a late attestation from the previous fork's epoch published on the current fork's topic was rejected. The subscriber already ignores messages on non-current digests, so the check now compares against the current fork digest, matching the spec which only checks the subnet.

title: E2E: tolerate network-wide skipped slots in the metrics head-slot check
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`TestEndToEnd_MainnetConfig_MultiClient` fails `metrics_check_epoch_N` on most develop postsubmit runs with `expected metrics slot to equal chain head slot, expected 176, received 174` (Buildkite build 107074, both attempts: 176 vs 174 and 145 vs 143). The check in `metricsTest` asserted that every node's head slot is within one slot of the wall clock, sampled once in the middle of each epoch. That is not a sync check: any two consecutive slots without an imported block right before the sample fail a fully synced node.

What actually produced the gaps in build 107074 (from the beacon/validator stderr the harness dumps on failure):

- Attempt 2 (145 vs 143): the Prysm proposers for slots 144 **and** 145 both failed with `Could not get local payload: timeout from http.Client`, i.e. `engine_getPayload` exceeded Prysm's fixed 1 s deadline (`defaultEngineTimeout`, unchanged since 2022). The same attempt logged 7 such timeouts (slots 130, 135, 136, 141, 144, 145, 152), 31 `Beacon node is not respecting the follow distance. EL client is syncing.` warnings and 69 validator `DeadlineExceeded` errors: geth and the beacon node were starved on the agent.
- Attempt 1 (176 vs 174): no Prysm build failure at 175 or 176 (its 7 timeouts were at 148, 167, 168, 170, 181, 182, 184); those two slots were either Lighthouse proposals or import lag. Logs from sibling runs of this test the same night show a third of the 12-blob blocks waiting 1 to 3 s for data columns (`Data columns still missing at slot end`) and Lighthouse blocks arriving up to 3 s late.
- The passing run 107053 has the same rates (14 and 11 getPayload timeouts on its two Prysm nodes, 35% of blocks with a data-availability wait over 1 s), so pass or fail only depends on where the mid-epoch sample lands.

This makes the head-slot check skipped-slot-aware and moves it into its own helper:

- A head at the wall-clock slot, or one slot behind it, still passes unconditionally (the current slot's block may still be propagating).
- A head that trails by more passes only when it is at, or within one slot of, the highest head across all nodes and the shortfall is at most `SlotsPerEpoch / 4` (8 slots on mainnet, 2 on minimal). No node has a block for the missing slots, so they were skipped network-wide, not missed by that node. A node that trails the highest head still fails, and so does a chain that stalls for longer than the tolerance.
- The check polls all nodes concurrently for up to one slot before failing (same pattern as `waitForMatchingHeads`), so a block that is still on its way when the evaluator starts can arrive. The wall-clock slot is read after the heads, so a slot boundary crossed during the fetch can only make the clock later.
- The failure message names the node, its head, the clock slot, the highest head and the tolerance.

Replaying both rules over the block-import timelines of three real runs (mid-epoch sample per epoch, both Prysm nodes): the old rule fails the sample where both nodes sit two slots behind the clock after two skipped slots; the new rule passes it and still fails the end-of-run sample where the chain stops (lag 16). The metrics page checks are unchanged. The `metricCheckComparison` no-op (#17043) is deliberately left alone.

Not addressed here, worth their own issues: Lighthouse (v8.2.0 in e2e) rejecting its own validators' blocks with `InvalidCellProofLength { expected: 768, actual: 6 }` in the first two epochs of every run (27 to 39 failed block productions per run, real missed proposals); the 1 s `engine_getPayload` budget on a saturated agent with 6 s slots; and the postsubmit job uploading stale `outputs.zip` artifacts from an earlier run on the same agent (the bundles attached to build 107074 are from 00:24 and 00:44 UTC, while its attempts ran 01:51 to 02:26).

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A (postsubmit flake; #17043 is related but not addressed here)

**Other notes for review**

Testing: new unit tests for `compareHeadSlots` (table) and `waitForHeadsNearClock` (gomock: retries until a lagging node catches up, returns the last comparison error on timeout, accepts network-wide skipped slots). `go test ./testing/endtoend/evaluators/` and `go vet ./testing/endtoend/...` pass locally. The e2e presubmit exercises the evaluator on the minimal config; the mainnet multi-client postsubmit run is the target.

**What type of PR is this?**

> Uncomment one line below and remove others.
>
> Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR synchronizes proposer settings snapshot publication and retrieval.

`UpdateProposerSettings` already serializes clone-then-swap updates, but `ProposerSettings` previously read the pointer without synchronization. `Graffiti` also accessed the field directly. Runtime keymanager/API updates could therefore race with validator slot processing.

This change:

- changes `proposerSettingsMu` to an `RWMutex`;
- protects snapshot retrieval with `RLock`;
- makes `Graffiti` retrieve one synchronized snapshot instead of accessing the field directly;
- extends the concurrency regression test to exercise updates concurrently with `ProposerSettings` and `Graffiti` reads.

The read lock only protects retrieval of the pointer. Continuing to read the returned snapshot after releasing the lock is safe because updates clone the settings and never mutate previously published snapshots.


**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17568

title: Fix --max-health-checks off-by-one
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`--max-health-checks=N` shut the validator down on the **N+1-th** consecutive failed health check instead of the N-th. `updateStatus` compared the counter before incrementing it, so `fails` first had to reach `maxFails` and then take one more failed check to reach the shutdown branch:

```go
} else if m.maxFails > 0 && m.fails < m.maxFails {
    m.fails++                                    // #1: 0 -> 1, #2: 1 -> 2, #3: 2 -> 3
} else if m.maxFails > 0 && m.fails >= m.maxFails {
    m.cancel()                                   // #4: 3 >= 3, shutdown
}
```

That contradicts the flag's own documentation, which describes a failure count rather than "N retries after the first failure":

> Maximum number of consecutive failed health checks before exiting. A health
> check fails when no connected beacon node is ready. Set to 0 or a negative
> number for indefinite checks.

The changelog entries from #15401, which added the flag, read the same way ("after the given number of health check failures").

This PR increments the counter first and then compares, so N failed checks means N. The `maxFails <= 0` indefinite-retry path is untouched, and the counter still resets on a healthy check, so the "consecutive" part of the documentation stays accurate.



**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #<issue number>

**Other notes for review**

The existing test encoded the off-by-one (`initialFails: 2` with `maxFails: 2` expected the cancel on the third failure), so it is corrected here along with two new table cases: `maxFails=1` cancelling on the first failure, and one failure short of the limit staying alive.

New `TestHealthMonitor_CancelsOnMaxConsecutiveFails` probes step by step for `maxFails` of 1, 2 and 3 and asserts the shutdown happens on exactly the `maxFails`-th consecutive failure, plus a subtest covering that a healthy check in between resets the count. Both fail on `develop` and pass with this change; `go test ./validator/client/ -count=1` passes.

body:
Gossip validation for index 1 attestations only checked that the payload envelope was seen and not invalid, so it accepted and forwarded votes for a payload the EL has not validated yet. This adds the missing `[IGNORE]` for an optimistic payload per `verify_attestation_payload_status` in the Gloas p2p spec.

title: Reject Gloas blocks whose bid does not build on the parent's execution head
body:
Block gossip only checked the bid's parent block root and blob count, so a block whose bid named an unknown parent block hash was accepted and forwarded until the state transition caught it. This adds the missing `[REJECT]` from `validate_beacon_block_gossip` using the same `HasPayloadBlockHash` check the bid topic already applies.

Spec reference: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5294
author: terencechain

title: Apply gossip clock disparity to Gloas payload attestation, bid, and proposer preferences slot checks
body:
The Gloas gossip slot checks for payload attestations, bids, and proposer preferences compared raw slot numbers, so honest messages arriving within `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` of a slot boundary were ignored. This adds a shared `withinSlotRange` helper mirroring the spec's `is_within_slot_range` and uses it for `is_current_slot`, `is_current_or_next_slot`, and `is_past_slot`.

Spec reference: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5294

title: fix(eth1exporter): validate address entries before reloading
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The address loader assumes every scanned line has both fields, allowing malformed configuration to bypass its error-return path. Validate entries before updating the exporter's watched addresses: ignore blank lines, trim surrounding whitespace, and return line-numbered errors for missing separators, empty names, or invalid Ethereum addresses.

Only replace the watched addresses after the entire file has been read successfully. Failed reloads therefore preserve the previous addresses and balances, and use the existing HTTP 500 response. Address-loading failures at startup are logged before exiting with a nonzero status. File-close errors are logged rather than panicking.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

No associated issue; this is a small bug fix covered by the PR template's exception.

**Other notes for review**

Invalid hexadecimal addresses were previously skipped silently; this change rejects them explicitly. Entries with additional separators are also rejected. Empty and whitespace-only files successfully load an empty address list.

Added tests covering valid entries, whitespace and CRLF, malformed entries and physical line numbers, scanner errors, missing files, preservation of the previous configuration on failure, and successful and failed reload responses. Added a Bazel test target and a changelog fragment.

title: Optimize ExecutionPayload Transactions representation
body:
# ExecutionPayload.Transactions Optimization

Currently we represent the Transactions list in an ExecutionPayload as 2D byte array (`[][]byte`). We don't need to interact with the individual transactions other than to ensure they are non-zero values, so the overhead of looping over and allocating slices for the individual txns when unmarshaling, marshaling and merkleizing is really not worth it. We can avoid quite a bit of computation, gc pressure etc etc by just validating the encoded form of the bytes list and keeping it in that representation for all operations in the beacon node and validator. This PR adds a custom type for the transactions list to accomplish that goal and makes the necessary changes across the grpc boundary to support the change.

## Note re Backwards-Compatibility

Both the struct generated by protoc and the wire format of ExecutionPayload will change with this PR. 

### Wire format

At the level of the wire format, this represents a breaking change. A new protobuf field number was used for the new tx list format, and the old field will be ignored by the beacon node. This means that validators running releases without this change, expecting the old wire format and unaware of the new field, need to be protected from accidentally signing an empty transaction list. 

The change only impacts the gloas `ExecutionPayload`; pre-gloas types are unaffected. To ensure that we fail loudly if a validator tries to interact with gloas endpoints using the old method/schema, a new grpc endpoint version (v2) was added, and the v1 version will return an error when the validator requests a payload. The intention is to force validators to upgrade if attempting to connect to an incompatible node.

For any networks that haven't forked into gloas yet (mainnet and all testnets except Sepolia), this change should have no impact. However special care should be taken in Sepolia. Ideally operators will get new beacon nodes running on the release including this change, then restart validators with the new version to point at the upgraded nodes. Upgraded validators talking to old beacon nodes will get an error due to the unknown v2 route, and any validator (particularly un-upgraded ones) talking to upgraded nodes will get an error if attempting to use the v1 gloas methods.

### If your code interacts with the struct (unlikely!)

I believe few if any users of prysm have custom code interacting with the go struct. Any code that does will be impacted and should be updated to use the `TransactionListBuilder` for initializing or mutating transactions lists, and the `Transactions() [][]byte` helper for reading them. The latter returns slices that are shared references to the underlying data byte slice, which is fine for prysm's purposes as we never mutate these values, but other users should take care to copy values if this mutation would be harmful. You can use the test support methods in this PR as an example of how to use the builder for populating the transactions slice.

title: Gloas: keep payload status right with several beacon nodes
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

**The issue:**

 With several beacon nodes, the REST validator client could vote with a beacon node that had not seen the payload yet:
 - The payload attestation data only had to match the block root. A beacon node that had the block but not the payload could win, and the validator voted the payload absent.
 - A beacon node announces a Gloas head twice: empty, then full. A slow beacon node's "empty" event could overwrite a "full" head reported by another beacon node, so the attestation data read preferred stale data.

 **The fix:**

 - When a beacon node already announced the payload, only accept payload attestation data with `payload_present` set.
 - The head tracker no longer changes the same head from full back to empty.

# Purpose
This PR implements a **mock** directly in the beacon node (via a new beacon API) to allow changing validator sweep threshold on the fly.

When an EL supports this EIP, this "cheat code" won't be needed any more, and this PR can be directly deleted.

# How to test it

## Setup

**Kurtosis configuration file**
```yaml
participants:
  - cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn-custom-image:latest
    vc_type: prysm
    vc_image: prysm-vc-custom-image:latest
    count: 3

network_params:
  gloas_fork_epoch: 1
  seconds_per_slot: 4

  withdrawal_type: "0x02"
  withdrawal_address: "0x8943545177806ED17B9F23F0a21ee5948eCaa776"
  validator_balance: 32

additional_services:
  - dora
  - spamoor
  - assertoor

spamoor_params:
  image: ethpandaops/spamoor:master
  spammers:
    - scenario: eoatx
      config:
        throughput: 10
    - scenario: blobs
      config:
        throughput: 6

dora_params:
  image: dora-custom-image:latest

global_log_level: debug
```

The Dora docker image **must be** built from https://github.com/nalepae/dora.
```
docker build -t dora-custom-image:latest .
```

Run the devnet with Kurtosis. Once the Gloas fork epoch is reached, you can check the `validator_sweep_thresholds` values in the beacon state:
```
curl <beacon-url>/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/head | jq '.data.validator_sweep_thresholds'
[
  "2048000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  ...
]
```

Everything should be set at 2048 ETH.

## Case 2: Modify the threshold for an already existing validator

Send a fake `2048 ETH -> 33 ETH` sweep threshold change request for validators 0 and 1 to the beacon node with:
```
curl -X POST <beacon-url>/prysm/v1/debug/beacon/sweep_threshold_requests \
    -d '{
      "requests": [
        {
          "source_address":   "0x8943545177806ed17b9f23f0a21ee5948ecaa776",
          "validator_pubkey": "0xaaf6c1251e73fb600624937760fef218aace5b253bf068ed45398aeb29d821e4d2899343ddcbbe37cb3f6cf500dff26c",
          "threshold":        "33000000000"
        },
        {
          "source_address":   "0x8943545177806ed17b9f23f0a21ee5948ecaa776",
          "validator_pubkey": "0x8aa5bbee21e98c7b9e7a4c8ea45aa99f89e22992fa4fc2d73869d77da4cc8a05b25b61931ff521986677dd7f7159e8e6",
          "threshold":        "33000000000"
        }
      ]
    }' | jq
```

You should see in the beacon logs:
```
[2026-08-11 14:20:57.22]  INFO gloas: Processing EIP-8148 set sweep threshold requests from the parent payload count=2 slot=56
[2026-08-11 14:20:57.22]  INFO gloas: Applied EIP-8148 set sweep threshold request balance=32000899755 effectiveSweeps=will sweep once balance and effective balance both exceed the threshold previous=2048000000000 pubkey=0xaaf6c1251e73fb600624937760fef218aace5b253bf068ed45398aeb29d821e4d2899343ddcbbe37cb3f6cf500dff26c threshold=33000000000 validatorIndex=0
[2026-08-11 14:20:57.22]  INFO gloas: Applied EIP-8148 set sweep threshold request balance=32000046970 effectiveSweeps=will sweep once balance and effective balance both exceed the threshold previous=2048000000000 pubkey=0x8aa5bbee21e98c7b9e7a4c8ea45aa99f89e22992fa4fc2d73869d77da4cc8a05b25b61931ff521986677dd7f7159e8e6 threshold=33000000000 validatorIndex=1
```

then:
```
curl <beacon-url>/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/head | jq '.data.validator_sweep_thresholds'
[
  "33000000000",
  "33000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  "2048000000000",
  ...
]
```

The values of `validator_sweep_thresholds` in the beacon state for validators 0 and 1 are now 33 ETH. The rest is still 2048 ETH.

Now, you can wait for a long time for the effective balance of validators 0 and 1 to reach 33.25 ETH, or you can make a deposit.

To make a deposit, copy this test file on your system:
```yaml
id: eip8148-topup-deposit
name: "EIP-8148: top-up deposit to trigger a custom-threshold sweep"
timeout: 30m
config:
  validatorPubkey: ""
  topUpAmount: 2
  depositContract: "0x00000000219ab540356cBB839Cbe05303d7705Fa"
tasks:
  - name: check_clients_are_healthy
    timeout: 5m
  - name: generate_deposits
    timeout: 10m
    config:
      limitTotal: 1
      limitPerSlot: 1
      topUpDeposit: true
      awaitReceipt: true
      failOnReject: true
    configVars:
      publicKey: "validatorPubkey"
      depositAmount: "topUpAmount"
      depositContract: "depositContract"
      walletPrivkey: "walletPrivkey"
```
and register it to Assertoor with:

```
curl -X POST <assertoor-url>/api/v1/tests/register -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' --data-binary @<path-to-the-test-yaml-file> | jq
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Don't forget the `@` before the file path.

Once done, trigger a **2 ETH** deposit for the validator 0 with:

```
curl  -X POST <assertoor-url>/api/v1/test_runs/schedule \
  -d '{"test_id":"eip8148-topup-deposit",
        "config":{
       "validatorPubkey":"0xaaf6c1251e73fb600624937760fef218aace5b253bf068ed45398aeb29d821e4d2899343ddcbbe37cb3f6cf500dff26c",
          "topUpAmount":2
        }}' | jq
```

Once the sweep is done for this validator, you should see:
```
curl http://<beacon-url>/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators/0xaaf6c1251e73fb600624937760fef218aace5b253bf068ed45398aeb29d821e4d2899343ddcbbe37cb3f6cf500dff26c | jq '{index: .data.index, balance: .data.balance, effective_balance: .data.validator.effective_balance, status: .data.status}'
{
  "index": "0",
  "balance": "33000000427",
  "effective_balance": "34000000000",
  "status": "active_ongoing"
}
```

(`balance` is slightly higher than 33 ETH and `effective_balance` is exactly 34 ETH)

After the start of the next epoch, the same request should return:
```
{
  "index": "0",
  "balance": "33000000427",
  "effective_balance": "33000000000",
  "status": "active_ongoing"
}
```

(`balance` is slightly higher than 33 ETH and `effective_balance` is exactly 33 ETH)

title: fix(db): replay missing historical hdiff states without repeated snapshot decoding
body:
# Fix missing historical hdiff lookup and avoid repeated snapshot decoding

Draft for author review; please leave in draft until the author requests team review.

**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix and historical-lookup performance improvement.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Historical state reads can fail with a generic missing-diff error even when an earlier state and retained canonical blocks permit replay. This PR classifies absent state, validator and balance diffs as `ErrNotFoundState`, and translates absent snapshots at the historical-read boundary so the existing replay path can recover. Startup snapshot validation remains strict. Empty or undecodable diff records are not reclassified as missing.

Every distinct ancestor diff is required; an empty cache level does not make that ancestor optional. Required diffs are loaded before the full snapshot, avoiding repeated large snapshot decodes during searches across incomplete history.

The two commits separate correctness and lookup efficiency. This PR contains no repair utility, database migration, persistent backfill or multi-value-slice changes, and does not modify the historical-diff writer.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

No linked tracking issue. The behavior was reproduced on a local mainnet archive; the historical writer that created its gaps is unknown.

**Other notes for review**

Regression tests cover missing ancestor components, leaves and snapshots, nonzero offsets, empty levels, malformed records, canonical replay through a real database with state-root equality, and checking missing diffs before decoding snapshots. A missing-history benchmark is included.

Independent validation on this PR's own tree, based on `develop` at `9ad1bee498613b7c5d0b70c7d7d2f3c3536c5b16`:

- All five affected Bazel test targets executed successfully with test-result caching disabled: KV, stategen, native state, hdiff and multi-value-slice.
- gofmt, goimports, Gazelle and native `make build` passed. Native checks used an isolated source archive with VCS stamping disabled to avoid the existing generator scanning nested local workspaces.
- Release-mode Bazel builds of beacon-chain and validator passed.
- The release-mode missing-history benchmark passed (`GOMAXPROCS=2`, three measurements).

Earlier live validation used this change together with the separately proposed append optimization. Those end-to-end timings must not be attributed to this PR alone. Large gaps can still cause long ancestry walks or replay; the March 2026 control exceeded 60 seconds in that combined run. This PR does not persistently repair missing records.

During self-review, the KV and stategen Bazel suites were rerun uncached and passed.

Three fresh read-only historical API probes against the unchanged combined live binary returned HTTP 200 and exactly matched prior response payloads. The node remained synced. This is combined runtime evidence, not an independent deployment of this branch.

Self-review found no blocking defect. I traced error classification through canonical replay and startup validation, checked offset-relative ancestor deduplication and the read-order change, and reviewed corruption and state-root regression coverage. No source changes were needed.

Both branches merge cleanly into upstream `develop` at `1ca08be9c5a31e8b8bcc331700facba173954f39`. The companion append optimization is #17591; these are independent PRs, not a stack. The full repository and network end-to-end suites were not run.

**Acknowledgements**

- [x] Read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] Included a uniquely named changelog fragment.
- [x] Added reviewer context and regression tests.
- [x] Tested the changes independently and documented the remaining limitation.

title: perf(state): avoid quadratic scans in multi-value-slice append
body:
# Avoid quadratic scans in multi-value-slice append

**What type of PR is this?**

Performance improvement.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`multi-value-slice.Append` previously scanned existing appended positions to find the next position for an object. Repeated appends therefore rescanned an increasingly long prefix, causing quadratic work when reconstructing a state with many appended validators.

Use the object's existing cached length to locate its next appended position directly. Value sharing at that position, copy isolation, detach/reuse behavior and locking are preserved. This removes the prefix scan; it does not remove the checks among values sharing the destination position.

This PR changes only the multi-value-slice implementation, its tests and its changelog fragment. It is based directly on `develop` and has no dependency on the historical-diff lookup PR or repair utility.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

No linked tracking issue. The original append loop was identified as a dominant CPU bottleneck while reconstructing historical mainnet states.

**Other notes for review**

Tests exercise copied objects with shared and divergent values, detach/reuse, a seeded operation model and concurrent appends to copied objects. A benchmark measures batches of 1,000, 10,000 and 50,000 appends.

Independent validation on this PR's own tree, based on `develop` at `9ad1bee498613b7c5d0b70c7d7d2f3c3536c5b16`:

- All five affected Bazel test targets executed successfully with test-result caching disabled: KV, stategen, native state, hdiff and multi-value-slice.
- gofmt, goimports, Gazelle and native `make build` passed. Native checks used an isolated source archive with VCS stamping disabled to avoid the existing generator scanning nested local workspaces.
- Release-mode Bazel builds of beacon-chain and validator passed.
- The multi-value-slice test suite also executed successfully with the race detector.
- The release-mode append-scaling benchmark passed (`GOMAXPROCS=2`, three measurements per size).

Earlier live-node testing had both this optimization and the separate historical-diff lookup changes applied. Those endpoint timings are combined evidence, not an isolated latency claim for this PR. This change does not address missing historical records or alter database serialization.

During self-review, the multi-value-slice suite was rerun uncached with the race detector and `-test.count=10`; all repetitions passed.

Three fresh read-only historical API probes against the unchanged combined live binary returned HTTP 200 and exactly matched prior response payloads. The node remained synced. This is combined runtime evidence, not an independent deployment of this branch.

Self-review found no blocking defect. I checked cached-length maintenance across Init, Copy, Detach, UpdateAt and Reset, the fresh-identifier native-state callers, destination value sharing and locking. No source changes were needed.

Both branches merge cleanly into upstream `develop` at `1ca08be9c5a31e8b8bcc331700facba173954f39`. The companion historical-lookup fix is #17590; these are independent PRs, not a stack. The full repository and network end-to-end suites were not run.

**Acknowledgements**

- [x] Included a uniquely named changelog fragment.
- [x] Added reviewer context, regression tests and benchmarks.
- [x] Tested the changes independently, including concurrency behavior.

title: Fix validator client startup retry loop to honour context cancellation
body:
**What type of PR this is** — Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`initialize()` retried the startup handshake on connection errors by checking `ctx.Err()` and then blocking on `<-ticker.C`. A cancellation landing between those two statements was invisible until the ticker fired, so the loop could keep running for up to the 10 second `backOffPeriod` after the context was cancelled. `runner.run` in the same file already returns immediately on `ctx.Done()`.

The retry wait now selects on the ticker and the context together:

```go
select {
case <-ticker.C:
case <-ctx.Done():
    log.Info("Context canceled, stopping validator")
    return ctx.Err()
}
```

This mirrors `pollConnectionStatus` in `beacon-chain/execution/rpc_connection.go`, which already waits this way. The preceding `ctx.Err()` check is removed because the `select` covers it, and `ctx.Err()` replaces `errors.New("context canceled")` — the message is unchanged, but callers can now use `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17596

**Other notes for review**

Added `TestInitialize_ExitsPromptlyOnCancelledContext`, which pins `backOffPeriod` to 10 seconds, drives `WaitForChainStart` into the retry path via `io.EOF` (mapped to `client.ErrConnectionIssue`), waits for the loop to park on the backoff, cancels, and asserts both a bounded return time and `require.ErrorIs(err, context.Canceled)`.

Validation:

- `go test ./validator/client/ -run 'TestInitialize|TestRetry_On_ConnectionError' -count=1 -v` — passed, including the new test.
- With `runner.go` reverted to the pre-fix version the new test fails at 2.29s with `initialize did not return on a cancelled context until the backoff expired`.
- `go test ./validator/client/ -count=1 -skip TestEIP3076SpecTests` — ok, 116.232s. (`TestEIP3076SpecTests` downloads an external archive and fails on a network error in this environment, unrelated to this change.)
- `gofmt -l`, `git diff --check` — clean. `go vet` reports only pre-existing context-leak warnings outside this change.

title: fix(sync): requester honours a peer's advertised earliest_available_slot
body:
Fixes #17567.

## Problem

Peer selection for `*_by_range` requests never consults the `earliest_available_slot` a peer advertises in its Fulu Status v2 handshake. The field is stored on the requester but not read, so a peer that cannot serve the requested range stays in the candidate list and is scored on exactly the same footing as one that can.

That produces requests the peer can only answer `ResourceUnavailable` (error code 3) with — visible in the report as `startSlot=309423` against `earliestAvailableSlot=313312`, roughly 121 epochs below the peer's serve range.

## Cause

`filterPeers` ranked peers purely on block-provider score and rate-limiter capacity:

```go
peers = scorer.WeightSorted(f.rand, peers, func(peerID peer.ID, blockProviderScore float64) float64 {
    remaining, capacity := float64(f.rateLimiter.Remaining(peerID.String())), float64(f.rateLimiter.Capacity())
    ...
})
```

Confirmed on `develop` at `a32764072`: `GetEarliestAvailableSlot()` has **zero** call sites outside the generated protobuf, and no requester path in `beacon-chain/sync` or `beacon-chain/p2p` reads a peer's `EarliestAvailableSlot`.

## Change

`filterPeers` now receives the range's start slot and drops peers that advertise an `earliest_available_slot` above it, before scoring and trimming:

```go
func (f *blocksFetcher) peersServingSlot(peers []peer.ID, startSlot primitives.Slot) []peer.ID {
	if startSlot == 0 {
		return peers
	}
	serving := make([]peer.ID, 0, len(peers))
	for _, pid := range peers {
		state, err := f.p2p.Peers().ChainState(pid)
		if err == nil && state != nil && state.EarliestAvailableSlot > startSlot {
			continue
		}
		serving = append(serving, pid)
	}
	return serving
}
```

All four call sites already had the start slot in scope, so no new plumbing was needed:

| call site | slot used |
| --- | --- |
| `fetchBlocksFromPeer` | `r.start` |
| `fetchPayloadEnvelopesFromPeer` | `start` |
| `fetchBlobsFromPeer` | `blobWindowStart` |
| `nonSkippedSlotAfter` | `slot` |

Two cases deliberately keep the peer rather than exclude it:

- **Zero or absent `earliest_available_slot`** — a peer only advertises the field once it has one, so a zero value must not be read as "cannot serve".
- **Chain state unreadable** — matches how the existing selection paths (`BestFinalized`, `BestNonFinalized`, `blocks_fetcher_utils.go:261`) already treat an unavailable status. Dropping those peers would turn a transient status gap into a sync stall.

## Verification

`TestBlocksFetcher_filterPeers_EarliestAvailableSlot` builds two peers with equal provider score and equal capacity, differing only in the advertised serve range, and asserts over 50 passes that the peer advertising an earliest slot above the request start is never returned. Repeated passes matter because selection is weighted and probabilistic.

Without the filter the test fails on the peer being selected:

```
--- FAIL: TestBlocksFetcher_filterPeers_EarliestAvailableSlot (0.44s)
    peer advertising earliest_available_slot above the request start slot must
    not be selected, both values are equal: 12D3KooWGpht8aZ9yvyyiHxF14tDLaXhoeMEKkb61VVd6BUDGp9b
```

With it:

```
--- PASS: TestBlocksFetcher_filterPeers (1.42s)
--- PASS: TestBlocksFetcher_filterPeers_EarliestAvailableSlot (0.39s)
ok  github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/v7/beacon-chain/sync/initial-sync  310.817s
```

The full `./beacon-chain/sync/initial-sync/...` package passes (310s) and `gofmt` is clean.

## Scope

This addresses requester-side selection only, which is what the report describes. It does not touch the serving side, does not clamp or split request ranges, and does not add the peer descoring the spec mentions as a possibility for such peers.

Open question for the maintainers, matching the one in the issue: whether this belongs in the Post-Fulu backfill work instead, or as its own change. Happy to rebase or rescope either way.

title: fix(time/slots): stop SlotTicker and SlotIntervalTicker goroutine leaks
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`SlotTicker.Done()` and `SlotIntervalTicker.Done()` cannot stop a ticker that is already
delivering a tick, and each redundant call leaks a goroutine.

Both tickers hand their tick to an unbuffered channel from *outside* the `select`:

```go
case <-after(waitTime):
	s.c <- slot      // not cancellable
	slot++
	nextTickTime = nextTickTime.Add(d)
case <-s.done:
	return
```

`Done()` signals shutdown by spawning a goroutine that sends on `s.done`:

```go
func (s *SlotTicker) Done() {
	go func() { s.done <- struct{}{} }()
}
```

`done` is unbuffered, so that send only completes when the ticker goroutine reaches
`case <-s.done`. If the consumer has stopped reading `C()`, the ticker goroutine is parked
inside `s.c <- slot` and never gets there. The result is two permanently blocked goroutines —
the ticker, and the goroutine `Done()` just spawned — that no shutdown path can reclaim.

This is reachable on a path the code already documents. `validator/client/runner.go` stops
consuming `v.NextSlot()` while it sits in `onAccountsChanged` → `WaitForActivation`, and
`SetTicker()` then calls `Done()` on the old ticker. The comment above that call spells the
situation out:

	// 2. loop stops consuming on slot 10 due to accounts changed tigger with no active keys
	// 3. new active keys are added in slot 20 resolving wait for activation

and there is no bound on how long `WaitForActivation` runs. The same window exists on
shutdown in `beacon-chain/slasher/service.go` `Stop()`, which calls `Done()` only after
`s.wg.Wait()` has already let the consumer goroutines return.

Separately, because `Done()` spawns a goroutine per call and only the first is ever
received, `Done(); Done()` leaks one goroutine per redundant call. `Done()` is an exported
interface method with no "call once" contract and `defer ticker.Done()` is the dominant
idiom in the tree, so this is a trap worth removing.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes # — no tracking issue; this is a small self-contained bug fix, so it is opened
directly per the PR template.

**Other notes for review**

This is not a duplicate of #16241. That PR added the missing `ticker.Done()` calls at two
consumer call sites and is correct as far as it goes, but it works around this root cause
rather than removing it: once the ticker is blocked in `s.c <- slot`, calling `Done()` cannot
rescue it, as described above. This change is what makes those call sites actually effective.

Changes:
- `done` is closed under a `sync.Once` instead of being sent a value from a spawned
  goroutine, so `Done()` is idempotent, spawns no goroutine, and is visible to the ticker
  even while it is blocked in the send.
- Both ticker loops now wait for the timer in their own cancellable `select`, then send the
  tick in a second cancellable `select`. The success path is unchanged; the only difference
  is that a shutdown is now observed at either blocking point.

Alternatives considered:
- Keeping the single nested `select` and guarding only the send — same behaviour, slightly
  smaller diff at the send site. Happy to switch to that shape.
- Taking a `context.Context` instead of a done channel would be cleaner, but it changes the
  `Ticker`/`IntervalTicker` interfaces and all their call sites, so it belongs in a separate
  change.

Not included: `testing/endtoend/helpers/epochTimer.go` `EpochTicker` repeats the identical
`Done()`/send pattern. It is an end-to-end test helper rather than a production primitive, so
I left it out to keep this diff focused — happy to apply the same change there if you would
like it in this PR. A sweep for the pattern (`done <- struct{}{}` and `<-s.done`) found no
other occurrences.

Also noticed but not touched: the `C()` godoc on both tickers says "Call Cancel afterwards",
but the method has been named `Done` for a while. Left out as an unrelated doc edit.

**Testing**

Added four regression tests in `time/slots/slotticker_test.go`, built on the package's
existing `synctest` idiom and its injectable `since`/`until`/`after` seams:

- `TestSlotTickerDoneUnblocksTickerStuckOnSend` / `TestSlotIntervalTickerDoneUnblocksTickerStuckOnSend`
  — fire one tick with nothing reading `C()`, let the goroutine settle into the send, then call
  `Done()` and assert the goroutine count drops back.
- `TestSlotTickerDoneIsIdempotent` / `TestSlotIntervalTickerDoneIsIdempotent` — call `Done()`
  three times and assert no goroutines leak.

`synctest.Wait()` is what makes these deterministic rather than timing-based: it returns only
once the ticker is durably blocked, so the test knows the goroutine is parked inside the send
before calling `Done()`.

Verified non-vacuous by reverting only `time/slots/slotticker.go` and re-running:

	--- FAIL: TestSlotTickerDoneUnblocksTickerStuckOnSend
	    "6" is not less than or equal to "5"
	    Done() did not stop a ticker stuck in its send
	goroutine 24 [chan send (durable), synctest bubble 1]:
	    slots.(*SlotTicker).start.func1()   slotticker.go:143   # s.c <- slot
	goroutine 25 [chan send (durable), synctest bubble 1]:
	    slots.(*SlotTicker).Done.func1()    slotticker.go:66    # s.done <- struct{}{}

The runtime names both leaked goroutines. All four pass with the fix.

Commands run:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `gofmt -l time/slots/` | clean |
| `go build` on `time/slots` + the 10 packages that call `Done()` | OK |
| `go vet ./time/slots` | clean |
| `go test ./time/slots/ -count=1` and `-race` | ok |
| `go test ./validator/client/ -count=1` | ok |

Pre-existing `go vet` warnings in `validator/client/runner.go` and
`beacon-chain/sync/sync_fuzz_test.go` are identical on a pristine checkout and unrelated to
this diff.

title: `ComputeCommittee`: Copy the committee out instead of returning subslice
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: Optimization

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`ComputeCommittee` is a pure helper function returning the committee after unshuffling the indices. It copies active indices into `shuffledIndices`, and finally returns subslice of `shuffledList`. As subslicing preserves the backing array which is 9.1MB in today's Hoodi testnet, this makes our heap space saturate with inused objects.

In most of the happy paths, this is very marginal change as the global `committeeCache` will be hit. It becomes problematic when there's a lot of committee cache miss, for example, at epoch boundary or long non-finalization. GC considers these backing arrays as referenced ones, so the node would suffer from the memory issue.

Found while tackling OOM issue in #17292. Archive node somehow reveals one of our memory issues as it is stress-testing our replaying mechanism and committee cache miss. I believe it's valuable to open a separate PR.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A, related to #17292

title: Fix genesis time validation in slot tickers
body:
**What type of PR is this?**​

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**​

`NewSlotTicker` checks `genesisTime.IsZero()`, but `NewSlotTickerWithOffset` and
`NewSlotTickerWithIntervals` check `genesisTime.Unix() == 0`. These are not
equivalent:

- `time.Time{}` is January 1, year 1 and has `Unix() == -62135596800`, so a genuine
  zero genesis time slips past the guard and starts a ticker with a garbage genesis.
- `time.Unix(0, 0)` is a perfectly valid, non-zero time.Time and is wrongly rejected.

This aligns the two constructors with `NewSlotTicker` by using `IsZero()`.

The existing `TestSlotTickerWithIntervalsInputValidation` did not actually cover this:
it passed a zero `genesisTime` *and* an empty interval list, so the panic came from
`len(intervals) == 0`. (`require.Panics`'s third argument is a failure message, not an
assertion on the panic value.) The test now passes a valid interval list for the zero
genesis case, and assertions use `require.PanicsWithValue` so the panic identity is
checked. Two regression tests were added:

- `TestSlotTickerZeroGenesisTime`: `time.Time{}` panics for all three constructors.
- `TestSlotTickerUnixEpochGenesisTime`: `time.Unix(0, 0)` is accepted by all three.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**​

Fixes #

**Other notes for review**

Verified by reverting the fix: all three tests fail without it, and pass with it.
No production caller passes a zero genesis time (`s.genesisTime` /
`clock.GenesisTime()`), so there is no behavior change on real code paths.

title: Fix data column warm cache indexing on Windows
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Fix data-column `WarmCache()` not indexing existing `.sszs` files on Windows.

PR #15899 correctly fixed the original Windows case reported in #15898. At that time `WarmCache()` used `afero.Walk()`, which returned native `\` paths on Windows, so `extractFileMetadata()` was changed to split using `filepath.Separator`. The same change kept `/` paths working on Linux/Unix and added tests for both native path styles.

PR #16207 later replaced the walk with manual traversal and now builds the relative paths using `path.Join()`. `path.Join()` uses `/` on every platform, so Windows now receives paths such as `116/477978/0x....sszs` while `extractFileMetadata()` is looking for `\`. This causes `extract file metadata: unexpected file ...` and prevents the existing files from being indexed.

Normalize the path using `filepath.ToSlash()` before splitting it on `/`. This keeps the cross-platform intent of #15899: native Windows `\` paths and the `/` paths currently produced by `WarmCache()` both work on Windows. On Linux/Unix, `filepath.ToSlash()` leaves `/` unchanged, so the existing behavior there is not changed. A Windows-style backslash also remains a normal character rather than a path separator on Unix, as before.

Updated only the Unix-style test expectation because the current `WarmCache()` produces `/` paths on every platform. The Windows-style test remains platform-specific, keeping the original native-separator coverage from #15899.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A - this is a small regression follow-up to #15899 after #16207 changed the `WarmCache()` path construction.

Tested on Windows amd64:

`go test ./beacon-chain/db/filesystem -run 'Test(WarmCache|ExtractFileMetadata)$' -count=1` , I can also run a couple tests on a Linux based system - Just lmk.

title: Postpone the validator client shutdown until a restart misses no rewarded duty
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
Postpone the validator client shutdown until a restart misses no rewarded duty

#### The issue
A restarted validator client only performs the duties of slots starting
after it is ready. But on SIGINT or SIGTERM, the validator client stops
right away, whatever the moment in the slot. So even a quick restart can
cut off the duties in progress, or miss the duties of the next slot.

#### The feature
On the first interrupt, the validator client keeps running until a restart
would not miss any rewarded duty:
1. If the current slot has rewarded duties, it waits for them to be done.
2. Then it shuts down if at least 3 seconds are left before the next slot,
    or if the next slot has no rewarded duty.
3. Otherwise, it waits for the next slot, and checks again.

Rewarded duties are attestations, sync committee messages and block
proposals (including the Gloas self-build envelope). Aggregations, sync
committee contributions and payload attestations earn no reward, so they
are not waited for.

A second interrupt shuts down immediately.

```
--disable-duty-aware-shutdown      Stop the validator client immediately on SIGINT/SIGTERM, instead of waiting for the moment in the slot where a restart would not miss any rewarded duty. (default: false)
```
restores the previous behavior.

**How to test it**

**Case 1: No rewarded duty in the current slot or the next slot**
Stop the validator client. It should stop immediately.

**Case 2: Some not yet done rewarded duty in the current slot. (Typically, `ctrl-c` in the first 4 seconds of the slot where a validator has to attest in the current slot)**

Stop the validator client. Is should wait for the duty to be done before shutting down.
```
[2026-10-04 20:09:36.39]  INFO node: Got interrupt, shutting down...
[2026-10-04 20:09:36.39]  INFO client: Waiting for the rewarded duties of the slot to be done before shutting down. Interrupt again to shut down immediately slot=15360046
...
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0x125d9aee6685 committeeIndices=[25 6] pubkeys=[xxxx] sinceSlotStartTime=2.433s slot=15360046 sourceEpoch=480000 sourceRoot=0xd3df2690cbbd targetEpoch=480001 targetRoot=0x36de206d0177
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Stopping service
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Context canceled, stopping validator
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Validator service context canceled, stopping
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO node: Stopping Prysm validator
```

**Case 3: Trying to stop the validator client too late in slot N, while slot N+1 has some rewarded duties. (Typically, `ctrl-c` in the last 3 seconds of the slot where a validator has to attest during the next slot)**
```
[10:11 PM][2026-10-04 20:10:46.06]  INFO node: Got interrupt, shutting down...
[2026-10-04 20:10:46.06]  INFO client: Too late in the slot to restart before the next one, waiting for the rewarded duties of the next slot to be done before shutting down. Interrupt again to shut down immediately slot=15360051 timeLeftBeforeNextSlot=932ms
...
[2026-10-04 20:10:48.90]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0xdfcf873c1ae7 committeeIndices=[59] pubkeys=[xxx] sinceSlotStartTime=1.908s slot=15360052 sourceEpoch=480000 sourceRoot=0xd3df2690cbbd targetEpoch=480001 targetRoot=0x36de206d0177
[2026-10-04 20:10:48.90]  INFO client: Stopping service
[2026-10-04 20:10:48.90]  INFO client: Context canceled, stopping validator
[2026-10-04 20:10:48.90]  INFO node: Stopping Prysm validator
[2026-10-04 20:10:48.90]  INFO client: Validator service context canceled, stopping
```

**Case 4: At least a validator has some rewarded duties during the current slot and the next slot, but the validator client is stopped after the current slot duties, and more than 3 seconds are left before the next slot**
Stop the validator client. It should stop immediately.

title: Reject duplicate data column sidecars in by-range and by-root responses
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

A peer can repeat a data column sidecar in a `DataColumnSidecarsByRange` or `DataColumnSidecarsByRoot` response, and the requester accepts every copy.

For example, we request columns `[1, 2, 3]` for slots `[10, 11]`, so we expect 6 sidecars and read at most 6 chunks. The peer replies with `(10,1) (10,2) (10,2) (11,1) (11,2) (11,3)`. All 6 pass validation, `(10,3)` is never received, and the caller gets `(10,2)` twice.

Why we have this issue:

- By range: [`areSidecarsOrdered`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/fea24b41265542905352ab45fe2291d8eea010cc/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_send_request.go#L609-L627) only rejects `sidecar.Index() < prevIdx` ([L621](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/fea24b41265542905352ab45fe2291d8eea010cc/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_send_request.go#L621)), so a repeated `(slot, column_index)` passes.
- By root: [`isSidecarIndexRootRequested`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/fea24b41265542905352ab45fe2291d8eea010cc/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_send_request.go#L746-L774) only checks that the `(block_root, index)` was requested ([L768](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/fea24b41265542905352ab45fe2291d8eea010cc/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_send_request.go#L768)) and never records what was received. It is also constructed for every chunk inside the read loop of `SendDataColumnSidecarsByRootRequest` ([L711](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/fea24b41265542905352ab45fe2291d8eea010cc/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_send_request.go#L711)), so it could not keep state anyway.

This PR:

- By range: makes the `(slot, column_index)` order strict. A `hasPrev` flag keeps the first sidecar at `(slot 0, index 0)` valid.
- By root: builds the validators once per request, marks each `(block_root, index)` as received, and rejects a repeat with `errSidecarDuplicated`.

The [Fulu spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#datacolumnsidecarsbyrange-v1) requires by-range responses to follow `(slot, column_index)` order and come from a single chain, where each pair identifies at most one sidecar. Right now, Lighthouse rejects duplicates with `LookupVerifyError::DuplicatedData` in both [by-range](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/2da239d15db117af5d4d75f3bd6d6371194342d0/beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/data_columns_by_range.rs#L41-L48) and [by-root](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/2da239d15db117af5d4d75f3bd6d6371194342d0/beacon_node/network/src/sync/network_context/requests/data_columns_by_root.rs#L71-L80) responses.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

No tracking issue. Related: #16711 covers the same goal, but its by-root validator is still constructed inside the read loop of `SendDataColumnSidecarsByRootRequest`, so its counters reset on every chunk.

**Other notes for review**

- I also fixed the by-root test helper to use `Slot`. It previously ignored that field, giving all sidecars the same block root, so even the “perfect match” test contained duplicates.
- Testing:
  - `go test ./beacon-chain/sync/ -run 'TestAreSidecarsOrdered|TestSendDataColumnSidecarsByRangeRequest|TestSendDataColumnSidecarsByRootRequest|TestIsSidecarIndexRootRequested'`: the new duplicate cases fail on `develop` and pass with this change.
  - `go test ./beacon-chain/sync/` passes.
  - `golangci-lint` v2.12 reports no new issues.

title: REST VC: wait past the attestation due time when no node has answered
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
**The issue**
When the REST validator client reads attestation data or a sync committee block root, it stops at the hint deadline, which is the attestation due time. If no beacon node has answered by then, for example because a late block is still being processed, the read fails. The attestation or sync committee message for that slot is then dropped.

**The fix**
When the caller's context has a deadline, it now bounds the read, and the hint deadline becomes a fallback deadline:
- If a node returns a usable answer that does not match the announced head, the read stops waiting for a matching answer at the hint deadline and uses the usable one. This is the same as before.
- If no node has answered at all, the read keeps waiting, up to the caller's deadline. A slow answer is better than no answer.

In `queryUntilAccepted`, the fallback deadline now also ends re-polling and later rounds once a usable answer is in hand, not just the wait for nodes that have not answered yet.

Without a caller deadline, nothing changes.
**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17619

title: Fix goroutine leak in payload_attributes event reader
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`payloadAttributesReader` computes the `payload_attributes` event in a goroutine that sends its result on an unbuffered channel (`edc`). The send only completes if the lazy reader receives it. Two paths leave it blocked forever:

1. The reader is never called: the stream exits and drops the queued reader without invoking it.
2. The reader runs but returns on `ctx.Done()` (client disconnect or deadline) before the worker finishes.

In both cases the worker goroutine leaks, one per disconnect/timeout during that window, for the life of the node.

The fix buffers `edc` by one. The worker sends exactly one value, so the send always completes and the goroutine exits whether or not anyone reads the result. The only cost is an unread result left for GC.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A (small bug fix)

**Other notes for review**

`TestPayloadAttributesReader_DoesNotLeakGoroutine` counts the worker goroutines by stack frame and covers both paths. It fails on `develop` (fea24b4126) and passes with the fix. `go test -race ./beacon-chain/rpc/eth/events/` passes.

An alternative is a `select` on `ctx.Done()` in the worker's send, but in path 1 nothing calls `cancel()`, so the worker would still wait until the deadline. The buffer releases it immediately.

title: Avoid nested read tx in LastValidatedCheckpoint
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

When `lastValidatedCheckpointKey` is absent, `LastValidatedCheckpoint` calls `FinalizedCheckpoint` inside its own `View`, opening a nested read transaction in the same goroutine. As described in #17366, if a concurrent commit must remap the DB, the remap waits for the outer read tx while the nested `View` waits behind the pending remap, and the DB deadlocks.

This reads the finalized checkpoint from the same transaction, following the pattern already used in `DeleteState` (`state.go`). Behaviour is unchanged, including the zero-hash default and the genesis-root substitution.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #17366

**Other notes for review**

Existing `LastValidatedCheckpoint`/`FinalizedCheckpoint` tests and `go test ./beacon-chain/db/kv/` pass.

Added `TestStore_LastValidatedCheckpoint_NoDeadlockWithConcurrentRemap`. It fails on `develop` with the deadlock and passes with this change in about 0.5s. Reproduction steps below.

### How to reproduce

**When it can happen.** On a checkpoint-synced node, `SaveOrigin` (`wss.go`) stores the finalized checkpoint but not the last validated one. Until the first `SaveLastValidatedCheckpoint`, `LastValidatedCheckpoint` takes the fallback branch that opens the nested `View`. The deadlock needs a write whose commit grows the bolt mmap to land between the outer and the nested `View`, so the window is small. I have not hit it on a live node or with kurtosis; the test forces that ordering.

**Steps**

1. On this branch, revert only the fix and keep the test:
   ```
   git checkout develop -- beacon-chain/db/kv/validated_checkpoint.go
   ```
2. Run the test:
   ```
   go test ./beacon-chain/db/kv/ -run TestStore_LastValidatedCheckpoint_NoDeadlockWithConcurrentRemap -count=1 -v
   ```
   It fails after 5s:
   ```
   validated_checkpoint_test.go:196: LastValidatedCheckpoint deadlocked with a concurrent mmap-growing write
   ```
3. To see the stuck goroutines, run it with `-timeout 4s`. `go test` panics before the test's own timeout and prints every stack (trimmed below).
4. Restore the fix (`git checkout HEAD -- beacon-chain/db/kv/validated_checkpoint.go`). The test passes in about 0.5s.

**How the test works**

- **DB setup.** It opens a fresh bolt file with the default (small) initial mmap and wraps it as `&Store{db: boltDB}`, the same way `state_diff_benchmark_test.go` does. `NewKVStore` maps 512 MiB up front, so the test would have to write over 512 MiB before any commit remaps. With the small mmap, a single 4 MiB write is enough. Only the finalized checkpoint is stored, which matches a checkpoint-synced DB.
- **Getting inside the read tx.** There is no hook inside `LastValidatedCheckpoint`, so the test uses tracing. It sets `trace.TracingEnabled` and installs a tracer provider whose `Start` calls back into the test. The callback skips the `BeaconDB.LastValidatedCheckpoint` span (started before the `View`) and fires once, on the next span. That span is always inside the read tx: on `develop` it is `BeaconDB.FinalizedCheckpoint`, just before the nested `View`; with the fix it is `BeaconDB.decode`. So both versions run with a remapping writer waiting.
- **The writer.** From the callback, the test starts the 4 MiB write in a goroutine and sleeps 500ms so the writer reaches `mmaplock.Lock`. bbolt gives no way to observe that, so the sleep only orders the goroutines. It cannot make the test fail with the fix: there is no nested `View` left to block.
- **Assertions.** `LastValidatedCheckpoint` must return within 5s with the stored finalized checkpoint. The test also checks that the callback fired (so it really ran inside the read tx) and that the write succeeded. On timeout it fails without closing the DB, because `Close` would hang on the same lock.
- **Cleanup.** The previous tracer provider and `TracingEnabled = false` are restored when the test ends. No other test in the package enables tracing.

<details>
<summary>Goroutine dump on develop (trimmed)</summary>

Goroutine 88 holds the outer `View` (`validated_checkpoint.go:18`) and is waiting on `RLock` for the nested `View` in `FinalizedCheckpoint` (`checkpoint.go:41`). Goroutine 89 is the commit, waiting on `Lock` in `db.mmap`, which needs goroutine 88's read tx to close first.

title: fix(p2p): read tcp6/udp6/quic6 ENR entries for IPv6 peers
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`getPort` in `beacon-chain/p2p/discovery.go` loaded only the `tcp`, `udp` and `quic` ENR entries, while `retrieveMultiAddrsFromNode` pairs the returned port with `node.IP()`. For an IPv6 endpoint that is wrong twice over:

- an IPv6-only peer (`ip6` + `tcp6`, no `tcp`) produced no dial address at all and was never dialed;
- a dual-stack peer whose `tcp6` differs from `tcp` was dialed on the IPv4 port (the reporter's `/ip6/2001:db8::2/tcp/30304` connection-refused case).

`getPort` now selects the port entry by the family of the node's selected IP: for an IPv6 endpoint the `tcp6`/`udp6`/`quic6` entry takes precedence, falling back to the IPv4 entry when no IPv6-specific entry is present. This mirrors go-ethereum's `enode.Node` port selection (`setIP6` loads `TCP6`/`UDP6` with `TCP`/`UDP` fallback), so a peer that publishes only `tcp` alongside `ip6` keeps working exactly as before.

`convertToUdpMultiAddr` had the same family mix-up in the other direction: it paired both the `ip4` and the `ip6` address with `node.UDP()`, which resolves against the selected family only (so the non-selected family's address could get the other family's port). Each address now takes its own family's UDP entry (`udp` for IPv4, `udp6` when present for IPv6, with the previous `node.UDP()` value as fallback).

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #17613

**Other notes for review**

Testing (Go 1.26.5, `go test ./beacon-chain/p2p/`):

- New tests in `discovery_test.go`, all failing on the unpatched logic and passing with this PR (the two fallback/control cases pass both ways, as intended):
  - `TestGetPort_IPv6OnlyPeer` — `ip6`-only record: tcp/udp/quic resolve from `tcp6`/`udp6`/`quic6` (unpatched: not found).
  - `TestGetPort_DualStackPrefersIPv6Ports` — the reporter's exact case (192.168.77.2/tcp 30304 + 2001:db8::2/tcp6 30324) resolves 30324 (unpatched: 30304).
  - `TestRetrieveMultiAddrsFromNode_IPv6OnlyPeer` — an IPv6-only peer now yields `/ip6/2001:db8::2/tcp/30324/...` (unpatched: no addresses).
  - `TestConvertToUdpMultiAddr_PairsPortsByFamily` — ip4 gets `udp`, ip6 gets `udp6` (unpatched: both got the selected family's port).
  - `TestGetPort_IPv6FallsBackToIPv4Entries`, `TestGetPort_IPv4IgnoresIPv6Entries` — controls.
- Full package run: the only failures are 8 network-dependent tests (`TestStartDiscV5_*`, `TestListenForNewNodes`, `TestHostIsResolved`, `TestVerifyConnectivity`, `TestCreateLocalNode`, `TestPeer_BelowMaxLimit`, `TestService_BroadcastAttestationWithDiscoveryAttempts`) that fail identically on unpatched `develop` (fea24b4) in my sandbox, which has no usable external networking; two of them are already on the repo's known-flaky list. title: REST VC: return from PostSSZWithFallback on the first node that accepts
body:
**What type of PR is this?**​

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**​

`multiHandler.PostSSZWithFallback` is documented as "succeeding as soon as one node
accepts", but it broadcast with `broadcastWriteAll`, which waits for every handler. A
slow or unreachable node therefore held up the call even after another node had already
accepted:

| node | response | today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BN-1 | 200 in 20 ms | first success |
| BN-2 | 200 in 40 ms | first success |
| BN-3 | still writing | the call waits for it |

The helper this contract calls for already exists in the same file. `broadcastWrite`
returns the first success and detaches the remaining writes with `context.WithoutCancel`,
so they still reach every node after the caller has moved on — `Post()` has used it for
this exact contract all along.

`PostSSZ` keeps `broadcastWriteAll`, because it genuinely has to see a 415 from *any*
node before deciding to re-broadcast as JSON. `PostSSZWithFallback` does not: its
`postWithFallbackFn` already downgrades a 415 to JSON per node and memoizes that node's
SSZ support, so there is nothing global left to learn by waiting.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**​

Fixes #

**Other notes for review**

- The doc comment is unchanged — it was already correct. This makes the body match it.
- New subtest `first success returns without waiting for the slow node` parks one node
  mid-request, asserts the call returns while that node is still parked, then releases it
  and asserts the detached write still completes. So the latency win does not cost the
  broadcast semantics. Reverting only `api/rest/multi_handler.go` makes it fail with
  `PostSSZWithFallback waited for every node instead of the first success`.
- `tracks support per node and endpoint` had to be adapted. It asserted exact per-node
  request counts, which only held while the call blocked on the node that needs the JSON
  fallback. Under the new semantics those counters settle asynchronously *and* the per-node
  415 cache may not be warm before the next call, so the expected counts are no longer
  deterministic; the test now waits for each call's writes to settle using the existing
  `waitFor` helper.
- The only difference on error paths is the cancellation branch: `broadcastWrite` returns
  `ctx.Err()`, where the wait-all version joined the collected node errors. Both are
  non-nil, and the new form makes `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` work.
