title: Backfill: Fix Gloas
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
There is some issues with backfill on Gloas.
This PR contains multiple commits. Each commit is a fix of a specific issue.
The corresponding commit message explains the issue and the fix.

**Other notes for review**
To reproduce the issue, just run the `--backfill` flag on Sepolia.
You'll get something like [these logs](https://gist.github.com/nalepae/716eb538d94dd71b80237c193f974382).

```
[2026-10-06 19:40:13.17] DEBUG backfill: Backfill batch failed to import batchId=11298368:11298400 begin=11298368 blobPid= blockPid=16Uiu2HAkyewYrfxiSkZFCgqZr5uCMcbFUcCArbPHMBj7tADM5w44 busyPid=16Uiu2HAkyewYrfxiSkZFCgqZr5uCMcbFUcCArbPHMBj7tADM5w44 colPid= end=11298400 error=IsDataAvailable: column store availability check failed: entry filter: root=&0xf9804a89181daebe324d221b3d709e147527da76ef46e7e20ba8217d702be1a3, index=0x5: no sidecar in cache for block commitment retries=131 retryAfter=2026-10-06 19:40:11.668479912 +0000 UTC m=+286.427116517 scheduled=2026-10-06 19:40:10.668541072 +0000 UTC m=+285.427177637 seq=390 state=importable
```

After the fix, the backfill should run smoothly.

Tested ✅ on 2 full (Gloas + Fulu transition) Sepolia backfills.

Copy of the commit messages.

**Backfill: Do not check columns of Gloas blocks with an empty payload**
The issue
On Gloas, when the payload of a block is never revealed, the block has no
data columns. Backfill knows this: it does not download columns for such a
block, and peers do not serve them anyway.

However, the data availability check still requires columns for every block
with blob commitments in its bid. The check fails with "no sidecar in cache
for block commitment", the batch is retried forever, and backfill is stuck.

The fix
When building the column batch, record which blocks have an empty payload.
The availability check then skips these blocks, the same way backfill skips
downloading their columns.

**Backfill: Decide the payload of the last block of a batch once its child is known**
The issue
On Gloas, backfill finds out whether the payload of a block was revealed by
looking at its child. The child of the last block of a batch is in the batch
above, so backfill could not see it and assumed the payload was revealed.

When that payload was in fact empty, backfill kept asking peers for the
columns of this block. Peers never serve columns of a block with an empty
payload, so the batch never finished and backfill was stuck.

The fix
The payload of the last block of a batch is now undecided until its child is
known. Backfill does not wait for the columns of an undecided block, but keeps
them if peers send them.

The child is the lowest block already backfilled. Backfill reads it from the
database when the batch is built, if the batch above is already imported, and
otherwise when the batch is imported. Then:
- if the payload is empty, the columns of the block are not checked;
- if the payload is full and its columns are missing, the import fails and
  the batch is retried, this time downloading the columns.

title: Read head and forkchoice node under one lock in GetAttestationData
body:
`GetAttestationData` read the cached head before taking the forkchoice lock, which block import holds through `saveHead`. A request arriving mid import got head N-1 with block N's payload bit and voted one slot stale. On Sepolia after Gloas this hit 7% of requests on the node that imports last.

Read the head and the canonical forkchoice node under one forkchoice read lock, so a mid-import request waits for the import and returns N with N's bit.

title: Fix backfill service deadlock when waiting for completion
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Current backfill service termination relies on whether `endSeq` slice is appended for `maxBatches` time (== `--backfill-worker-count`, defaults to 2). This condition can be broken when the batches are arrived in order. See below for the scenario.

This PR makes the termination condition more declarative. It claims that the backfill is complete iff every batches reach to `batchEndSequence` state (See `allEnded` method). 

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #17282
Alternative of #17223 ([context](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17223#discussion_r4205337202))

**Other notes for review**

### Scenario

Consider the origin (= floor) is slot 4037888. Last two batches:
- A = [4037920, 4037952)
- B = [4037888, 4037920)

The deadlock happens when the batch B arrives earlier than batch A. When B arrives, this log is emitted:

```
DEBUG backfill: Waiting for descendent batch to complete
```

And it is not "importable", so waiting for the arrival of A. 

When A arrives, A is first imported, and then B is imported. `scheduleTodos` calls `s.batchSeq.sequence()`, and `sequence()` will return a slice of single element because of this condition (`len(s)` is 1 for the second iteration):

```go
		if c.seq[i].state == batchEndSequence && len(s) == 0 {
			s = append(s, c.seq[i])
			continue
		}
```

`todo` method is used to append `endSeq` after that, but it only appends once in this scenario. Thus, `len(endSeq) == 1` while the completion is waiting for it to be two.

title: Use the slot deadline for the duties of the first slot of an epoch
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
**The issue**
At the first slot of an epoch, the runner overwrites `deadline` with the deadline of the last slot of the epoch, to give more time to the duties update. The context of the duties of the slot is then created from this overwritten value, so these duties may run until the end of the epoch instead of the end of the slot.

**The fix**
The duties update uses its own `dutiesDeadline` variable, so `deadline` stays the deadline of the slot.

title: Replace the per-call `Broadcasted data column sidecars` debug log with a `Broadcasted data column sidecars summary` log, aggregated per block root and emitted once no column was broadcast for this root during 100 ms.
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Since partial data columns are enabled by default, nodes log many `Broadcasted data column sidecars` debug lines with `count=1`. A single slot could produces one line per custody column:


      [2026-10-07 22:33:12.30] DEBUG p2p: Broadcasted data column sidecars summary count=8 indices=18,46,69,71,92-93,116,121 root=0x57ea81eb... sinceStartTime=[min: 203.84536ms, avg: 204.182433ms, max: 204.700129ms] slot=11306566

**Before, without partial columns:**
`engine_getBlobsV2` was all or nothing.
- If the execution client has all the blobs, the node builds all its custody columns at once and broadcasts them in a **single call**: one **single, grouped** log line per block.
- Otherwise, the node gets full columns from gossip. gossipsub forwards them itself, and Prysm logs nothing.

**Now, with partial data columns enabled by default:**
`engine_getBlobsV3` can return only some of the blobs. The node then publishes partial columns, and peers send the missing cells. Each column is on its own gossip topic, so each one is completed at a different moment. When a column is complete, the node re-broadcasts it as a full sidecar for peers that don't support partial messages. That broadcast holds one column, so it logs one `count=1` line.

This pull request groups broadcasts per block root and write one `Broadcasted data column sidecars summary` line per root. The line is written once no column has been broadcast for that root for 100 ms. The format matches the already existing `Accepted data column sidecars summary` log.

      DEBUG p2p: Broadcasted data column sidecars summary count=8 indices=18,46,69,71,92,93,116,121 root=0x… sinceStartTime=[min: 216ms, avg: 260ms, max: 284ms] slot=11305599

title: Fix/cache block headers timeout skip
body:
> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**​

`cacheBlockHeaders` can silently skip a range of eth1 block headers when the
execution client times out on a batch request. On a timeout the batch size is
halved and the `for` loop's post-statement steps the cursor forward by the
*new, smaller* batch size. When the current starting block is no larger than the
reduced batch size, the `i -= batchSize` correction does not apply, so the
`[start, start+reducedBatchSize)` prefix is never re-fetched. The function then
returns `nil`, falsely reporting the whole range was cached — a correctness bug,
not just a performance issue.

This is masked by the existing test, which only exercises `start=1000`
(larger than the reduced batch size of 500).

**Fix:**​ advance the cursor only after a successful fetch; on a timeout, retry the
same starting block with the smaller batch instead of stepping the cursor forward
by the shrunk batch size.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**​

Fixes # (none required — small bug fix)

**Other notes for review**
- Non-timeout behavior is unchanged: with no timeouts the cursor advances by exactly
  `batchSize`, identical to before. `TestService_CacheBlockHeaders` still passes
  (expects 5 calls for `cacheBlockHeaders(1000, 3000)` with limit 1001).
- Added `TestService_CacheBlockHeaders_TimeoutDoesNotSkipRange`: times out once on
  `start=1` (smaller than the reduced batch size) and asserts every block in
  `[1, 2000)` is present in the header cache. On the old code it fails because
  blocks 1–500 are missing. Verified red on the buggy version, green on the fix.

Testing plan:
1. `go test -run TestService_CacheBlockHeaders ./beacon-chain/execution/ -count=1 -v`
2. Both `TestService_CacheBlockHeaders` and
   `TestService_CacheBlockHeaders_TimeoutDoesNotSkipRange` should pass.

title: Use the target's shuffling dependent root in getRecentPreState
body:
### Problem

`getRecentPreState` decides whether the head state can validate an attestation for checkpoint `c` by comparing `DependentRootForEpoch(headRoot, headEpoch-1)` against `DependentRootForEpoch(c.Root, headEpoch-1)`. `DependentRootForEpoch(root, E)` returns the last block before epoch `E`.

The committees of `c.Epoch` are fixed by the last block before `c.Epoch-1`. The current comparison is only correct when `c.Epoch == headEpoch`:

- **`c.Epoch == headEpoch-1`:** it compares the last block before `c.Epoch`, which is one epoch too strict.
  - Example: head in epoch 11, attestation target `{10, R@slot 303}` from a node that didn't see R310.
  - The head chain's last block of epoch 9 is R310 while the target's is R303, so the check fails.
  - Epoch 10's committees only depend on the last block of epoch 8, which both chains share, so the head state was usable and we needlessly regenerated a state.
- **`c.Epoch == headEpoch+1`:** it compares the last block before `c.Epoch-2`, which is one epoch too loose. This was only safe because the function also required `c.Root == headRoot`.

### Fix

- Compare `DependentRootForEpoch(·, c.Epoch-1)` for both roots. This is exactly the block that fixes `c.Epoch`'s shuffling, for every `c.Epoch` that reaches the check: `headEpoch-1`, `headEpoch` or `headEpoch+1`.
- Since the comparison is now exact for the next epoch, return the head state without advancing it whenever the fork version doesn't change, even if `c.Root != headRoot`.
- `c.Root == headRoot` is still required before the path that advances the head state with `ProcessSlotsIfNeeded` and caches it under `c`.
- If the head is several epochs behind the target, both dependent roots resolve to the roots themselves. The check then already implies `c.Root == headRoot`.

### Why equal dependent roots are reliable

Both lookups go through forkchoice. A root that isn't in forkchoice returns `ErrNilNode`, and we fall back to the slow path. Let `F` be the finalized block (the root of the forkchoice tree) and `E = c.Epoch-1`.

**The dependent block is not finalized.** That is, it's at or after `F`, so it's still a forkchoice node.
- Forkchoice walks each chain's target pointers back to that exact node.
- Equal results mean both chains share the same last block before `start(E)`.
- Different results mean the shufflings may really differ, and we fall back.

This includes chains that branch off `F` before the finalized epoch's start because of skipped slots. Example: finalized `{9, R280}` with a late sibling R285, a child of R280. R285 is a real node, so its lookup returns R285 while the canonical chain returns R280, and the comparison fails as it should.

**The dependent block is finalized.** That is, `F` is at or after `start(E)`.
- The last block before `start(E)` is a strict ancestor of `F`.
- Every node in forkchoice descends from `F`, so both chains share that block, and the shuffling is the same.
- Forkchoice answers either with `finalizedDependentRoot` (the parent of `F`) or with a zero root, if the walk reaches `F` after pruning cleared its target. Both lookups follow the same path through `F`, so they return the same value.
- If they ever disagreed, the result is a false negative, i.e. the slow path, never a wrong state.

In both cases a match is never wrong; at worst we miss a chance to use the head state.

### Why the head state is valid

Every caller of `AttestationTargetState` uses the returned state only for the following. None of them reads balances, proposer data, sync committees or the PTC.
- the committees of `c.Epoch` (`BeaconCommitteeFromState` / `AttestationCommitteesFromState`);
- the active validator count, for the committee count and subnet;
- validator public keys;
- `Fork()` and `GenesisValidatorsRoot()` for signature domains.

**Committees.** `compute_committee` depends only on the seed and on `get_active_validator_indices(state, c.Epoch)`, not on balances.
- **Seed:** it uses the randao mix of epoch `c.Epoch-2`, which is final after the last block before `start(c.Epoch-1)`. That's exactly the block we compare. Later blocks only change the mixes for later epochs, and the mixes buffer keeps 65536 epochs, so the head state still has it.
- **Active set:** any activation, exit, slashing or consolidation processed after that block gets an epoch of at least `current + 1 + MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD`, which is after `c.Epoch`. New deposits are appended as inactive. So the active set at `c.Epoch` is the same on both chains.

**Range of epochs.**
- `c.Epoch` is the head state's previous or current epoch: the mix and the registry are already in the state.
- `c.Epoch` is the next epoch: the mix for `c.Epoch-2 = headEpoch-1` is already final in the head state. We only return it unadvanced when the fork version doesn't change at the boundary.

**Public keys.** Validator indices and keys never change. Every member of a `c.Epoch` committee exists at the same index with the same key in both registries.

**Signature domain.** `get_domain` uses `fork.previous_version` for epochs before `fork.epoch`. So a head state one epoch ahead, even right after a fork, gives the correct domain for the target's epoch. The genesis validators root is the same on both chains.

title: Verify gossip payload envelope signatures without loading state
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Gossip validation of execution payload envelopes retrieved the block's verifying state (`blockVerifyingState`) before checking the envelope signature. For blocks whose state is not cached (e.g. older unfinalized blocks), this triggers a state replay for every envelope received, even ones with an invalid signature.

The signature only needs a pubkey and a domain, so this PR removes the state retrieval:

- The forkchoice `Node` now records the bid's builder pubkey (`*[48]byte`, nil for self-built and pre-Gloas blocks). It is set from the post-state in `InsertNode`, and via `BlockAndCheckpoints.BuilderPubkey` in `InsertChain` (filled in batch sync).
- Self-built envelopes are verified against the proposer's pubkey (`block.ProposerIndex()`) from the head state. Validator index to pubkey is consistent across branches since validators are only added from finalized deposits.
- Builder envelopes are verified against the pubkey stored in forkchoice. Builder indices can be reused across branches, so the head state can't be used for these.
- New `VerifySignatureWithPubkey` on the envelope verifier computes the domain from the fork schedule at the envelope's epoch and the genesis validators root.
- If no pubkey is available, the envelope is ignored (not rejected).
- The builder pubkey is cleared once the full node is created (`InsertPayload`, `MarkFullNode`, `InsertChain` with `HasPayload`), and gossip envelopes whose root already has a full node are ignored early.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

**Other notes for review**

- `fillInForkChoiceMissingBlocks` and the startup forkchoice rebuild don't have per-block post-states, so they leave the builder pubkey nil; builder envelopes for those blocks are ignored on gossip.
- `InsertNode` skips setting the pubkey if the state lookup fails (e.g. Gloas genesis) instead of failing insertion.

title: Verify proposer preferences signature before advancing the dependent state
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

On the `proposer_preferences` gossip topic, when the proposal epoch is two epochs past the dependent state, the validator advances a copy of that state across the epoch boundary to read the proposer lookahead. This is the only state advance the validator performs, and it ran before the signature check.

The signature needs only the validator's public key and the genesis validators root, neither of which changes when slots are advanced. So a message with an invalid signature paid for a full epoch transition before being rejected, and because invalid messages are never added to the seen cache, every copy paid again. A peer that finds a qualifying off-head fork-choice tip can repeat this until it is graylisted.

This PR checks the signature against the un-advanced dependent state first, then advances only to check the proposal slot against the lookahead. A forged message is rejected before any state transition.

Accept, reject, and ignore outcomes are unchanged for every message:

- The two checks that swapped places are both `[REJECT]`.
- The "state epoch cannot verify proposal epoch" bound check stays ahead of the signature, so a message our state cannot cover still returns `[IGNORE]` without any BLS work. Its condition is unchanged: the old `else if` only fired for gaps of three or more epochs.

Also in this PR:

- `VerifySignature` gets a doc comment stating it needs no slot advancement, so a future caller does not reintroduce the ordering.
- The test mock now records the state slot each check received separately and whether the proposal-slot check ran. The old shared `lastStateSlot` field was written but never read.
- A new test pins the order in both directions: a forged signature on an epoch-plus-two message is rejected against the un-advanced state with the proposal-slot check never called, and a valid signature is checked at the dependent state's slot while the proposal-slot check sees the boundary state.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

**Other notes for review**

Two edge cases change which check produces the result, but not the result itself:

- A validator index that only enters the registry during the boundary transition's pending-deposit processing now fails at the signature step instead of the lookahead step. Both are `[REJECT]`. Such a validator cannot be in the lookahead anyway, since activation is at least `MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1` epochs out.
- A forged message whose state advance would have failed used to return `[IGNORE]` from the advance error. It now returns `[REJECT]` from the signature, which is the correct result for a bad signature.

Spec: the reference `validate_proposer_preferences_gossip` in `specs/gloas/p2p-interface.md` on consensus-specs master advances the state and then checks the signature, the same order Prysm had. Its signature inputs are state-independent: the domain uses `compute_fork_version(proposal_epoch)` from config plus `state.genesis_validators_root`, and the pubkey is `state.validators[validator_index].pubkey`. Prysm already computes the domain from config via `params.Fork(epoch)`, which matches master and is covered by `TestProposerPreferencesVerifier_VerifySignature_ForkBoundary`. The pinned v1.7.0-beta.0 used `get_domain(lookahead_state, ...)`, which would have read the fork from the advanced state; master moved away from that.

Other clients: Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus, Grandine, and Lodestar all keep the signature last, all derive the domain's fork from config at the proposal epoch, and all read the pubkey by validator index from a state or an index-keyed cache, so none of their signature inputs depend on the advanced state either. Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus, and Grandine bound the repeat cost of the boundary advance with a cache keyed by dependent root and epoch (16 to 32 entry LRUs), and Lodestar refuses to compute the lookahead on a cache miss. Prysm's analogue is the blockchain service's checkpoint-state cache, keyed by epoch and root and reached through `AttestationTargetState`, but this validator advances with `transition.ProcessSlotsIfNeeded` directly and does not consult it. Routing the boundary advance through that cache would make repeated valid messages for the same dependent root cheap and is a reasonable follow-up. It is not a drop-in: `AttestationTargetState` has a head-state shortcut that returns a state one epoch behind the checkpoint, which is fine for committees but not for the proposer lookahead, so it would need a dedicated accessor or a slot check. Reordering the signature check is needed regardless, since a cache still pays on every miss and forged messages should not reach it.

Testing plan:

```
go test ./beacon-chain/sync/ -run TestValidateSignedProposerPreferencesGossip -count=1
go test ./beacon-chain/verification/ -run TestProposerPreferencesVerifier -count=1
```

The new test was also run against the pre-fix validator and fails there. The forged-signature case errors with `advance state to boundary: could not process gloas epoch`, showing the transition ran before the signature check, and the valid-signature case observes slot 32 at the signature check instead of slot 0.

title: [EIP-8025] Implement optional execution proofs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This pull request implements a POC of EIP-8025
- [EIP](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8025)
- [Consensus specification](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/master/specs/_features/eip8025)

**Added flags:**
- `--zkvm` (alias: `--proof-engine`): Use it to signal the node has to subscribe to execution proofs subnets, and to verify incoming proofs.
- `--min-execution-proofs` (default: 1): If `--zkvm` is used, then at least this number of proofs is needed (additionally to the EL validity) for this payload to consider the corresponding forkchoice node as valid (aka, non-optimistic). Note: this is a deviation from the specification. Use `--min-execution-proofs=0` to stick to the specification.
- `--zkvm-mock-proofs`: If `--zkvm` is used, use this when the network's provers run zkboost's mock zkVMs. The node then accepts mock proofs without checking them cryptographically, but still checks their public values against the payload. For each mock proof, the node also verifies a real proof of the same type that is built into the binary, and ignores the result. (This way the node still pays the CPU and memory cost of a real verification).

**Additional deviations from the spec:**

- In consensus-specs Gloas, `NewPayloadRequest` is a [ProgressiveContainer](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L988).
- However, for ere-guests (used by zk-boost), it is a plain [SSZContainer](https://github.com/eth-act/ere-guests/blob/main/crates/stateless-validator-common/src/guest/input/new_payload_request.rs#L236-L242) (aka NO `#[ssz(progressive_container)]` attribute) .

==> `hash_tree_root(new_payload_request)` mismatches.
To be able to run with ZK-boost, Prysm, at the moment, considers `NewPayloadRequest` as a plain `SSZContainer`, deviating from the specification.


Also,  Prysm considers a proof as recursive, aka a valid proof of a payload also attests to the validity of all its ancestors. Once a payload is validated (EL validity plus `--min-execution-proofs` proofs), Prysm marks it in forkchoice as valid together with all its ancestors, and with the empty blocks built on top of it, even if those ancestors did not receive enough proofs themselves.

**Added metrics:**
- `execution_proof_arrival_delay_seconds`: Time between the insertion of a payload in forkchoice and the import of a verified EIP-8025 execution proof of this type for it.
- `payload_proof_validation_delay_seconds`: Time between the insertion of a payload in forkchoice and the moment it is no longer optimistic, once validated by the EL and at least --min-execution-proofs execution proof types. Ancestors validated along with the payload are not counted.
- `execution_proof_verification_seconds`: Time to verify an EIP-8025 execution proof with the zkVM verifier.

**Kurtosis configuration file:**
```yaml

  # Standard node
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:glamsterdam-devnet-8-aa1f2fc
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn-custom-image:latest
    vc_image: prysm-vc-custom-image:latest
    count: 1

  # Proving node.
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:glamsterdam-devnet-8-aa1f2fc
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn-custom-image:latest
    vc_image: prysm-vc-custom-image:latest
    cl_extra_params:
      - --proof-engine
      - --zkvm-mock-proofs
      - --execution-endpoint=http://zkboost-1:3000
    count: 1

  # Standard node that does not need proofs.
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:glamsterdam-devnet-8-aa1f2fc
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn-custom-image:latest
    vc_image: prysm-vc-custom-image:latest
    count: 1

  # Verifying nodes.
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethpandaops/geth:glamsterdam-devnet-8-aa1f2fc
```

title: `BeaconState`: Add generic functions instead of hand-written constructors/extractors
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

> [!NOTE]
> Review commit by commit. Commits 2 ~ 4 are scripted and scripts are attached in the commit body.

Thanks to #17535, each `BeaconState` type is now native Go struct. We still have legacy function names though:

- 18 constructors: `InitializeFromProto<Fork>` (deep copy) & `InitializeFromProtoUnsafe<Fork>` (takes ownership), Phase0 to Heze.
- 9 extractors: `ProtobufBeaconState<Fork>(s any)`

This PR replaces the 27 functions with three generic functions:

```go
type Container interface {
	*ethpb.BeaconState | *ethpb.BeaconStateAltair | ... | *ethpb.BeaconStateGloas
}

func New[T Container](st T) (state.BeaconState, error)       // deep copy of st
func NewUnsafe[T Container](st T) (state.BeaconState, error) // takes ownership of st
func ContainerFrom[T Container](v any) (T, error)            // v is usually ToProto() or ToProtoUnsafe()
```

Before & After:

```go
// before
st, err := state_native.InitializeFromProtoUnsafeElectra(pb)
pb, err := state_native.ProtobufBeaconStateElectra(st.ToProtoUnsafe())
// after
st, err := state_native.NewUnsafe(pb)
pb, err := state_native.ContainerFrom[*ethpb.BeaconStateElectra](st.ToProtoUnsafe())
```

(Note: Things like `pb`, `ToProtoUnsafe`, etc that are specific to protobuf context are deliberately skipped in this PR.

There's no behavior change. One exception on the error text of `ContainerFrom` (`input is <got>, not <want>`) Also I think the production risk is low.

title: `BeaconState`: Rename proto to container
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: Cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

> [!NOTE]
> Review commit by commit.

Since #17535, each `BeaconState<Fork>` type is a hand-written Go struct, not a protobuf message. The previous PR (#17659) added `state_native.New`, `NewUnsafe` and `ContainerFrom[T Container]`. The state API still had two methods with protobuf names:

```go
ToProtoUnsafe() any // returns a state container that shares fields with the state
ToProto() any       // returns a copy of the state as a state container
```

This PR renames them to match the `Container` naming:

| Old name | New name | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `ReadOnlyBeaconState.ToProtoUnsafe` | `ToContainerUnsafe` | `beacon-chain/state/interfaces.go`, `state-native/getters_state.go` |
| `ReadOnlyBeaconState.ToProto` | `ToContainer` | same |
| `encodeProtoWithKey` (unexported) | `encodeContainerWithKey` | `beacon-chain/db/kv/state_diff_helpers.go` |
| `gloasStateProtoForProgressiveSSZTests` (test) | `gloasContainerForProgressiveSSZTests` | `state-native/progressive_ssz_test.go` |
| `TestBeaconState_ProtoBeaconStateCompatibility` | `TestBeaconState_ContainerCompatibility` | `state-native/types_test.go` |
| locals `protoState`, `stProto`, one `statePb`, `proto` | `container`, `st`, `c` | state-native tests and `ssz.go` (hand-picked, commit 2) |
| locals with a pb/proto name that hold a state container: `pbState`, `protoState`, `stateProto`, `stProto`, `spb`, `pb`, `pbb`, `stPb`, `gloasStateProto`, `pbState1`, `pbstate`, `sourceProto`, `targetProto` | `container` (`c` on a conflict), `container1`, `container2`, `sourceContainer`, `targetContainer` | 74 files, found by pattern (commit 3) |
| locals `statePb`, `pbSt` that hold the state built from a container | `beaconState` | `state-native/setters_gloas_test.go`, `core/gloas/pending_payment_test.go` (commit 3) |
| `BenchmarkEncodeProtoWithKey` | `BenchmarkEncodeContainerWithKey` | `db/kv/state_diff_helpers_test.go` |

```go

pb, err := state_native.ContainerFrom[*ethpb.BeaconStateElectra](st.ToProtoUnsafe())
// after
pb, err := state_native.ContainerFrom[*ethpb.BeaconStateElectra](st.ToContainerUnsafe())
```

Follow-up 2 of #17535.

title: Improve the "No responsive beacon node found" log
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

  Bug fix

  **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

  The validator client logs `No responsive beacon node found` whenever no beacon node is ready. That includes the case where the beacon node is reachable but syncing, or synced but optimistic because its execution client is not synced yet. Operators are pointed at the wrong problem.

  This PR has two commits:

  1. **Report optimistic beacon nodes as optimistic in gRPC health** (beacon node)
     `GetHealth` checked `Syncing() || Initialized()` before the optimistic status. `Initialized()` is true on almost every running node, so a synced but optimistic node answered `node is syncing`. The checks are reordered so it now answers `node is optimistic`.

  2. **Log why no beacon node is ready** (validator client)
     The health check now returns a status (`ready`, `syncing`, `optimistic`, `unavailable`) instead of a boolean:
     The health check now returns a status (`ready`, `syncing`, `optimistic`, `unavailable`) instead of a boolean:
     - gRPC: read from the `GetHealth` error reason.
     - REST: a `206` from `/eth/v1/node/health` is split into syncing or optimistic using `/eth/v1/node/syncing`.

     When no node is ready, the log names the cause shared by every node and lists each node's status:

     | All nodes are… | Log |
     |---|---|
     | optimistic | `Beacon node is optimistic, waiting for its execution client to sync before performing duties` |
     | syncing | `Beacon node is syncing, waiting for it to sync before performing duties` |
     | unreachable | `No reachable beacon node found` |
     | mixed | `No ready beacon node found` |

     Example: `nodes="http://bn1:4000=optimistic, http://bn2:4000=unavailable"`

  **How to test it**
For example, start at the same time an empty EL/BN (from checkpoint). Connect a VC to it.
The VC logs should start with:
```
[2026-10-12 09:25:03.24]  WARN fallback: No reachable beacon node found nodes=beacon:4000=unavailable
```

Then, when the BN node is syncing:

```
[2026-10-12 09:25:27.24]  WARN fallback: Beacon node is syncing, waiting for it to sync before performing duties nodes=beacon:4000=syncing
```

Then, when the BN node is synced but the EL is syncing:
```
[2026-10-12 09:28:51.26]  WARN fallback: Beacon node is optimistic, waiting for its execution client to sync before performing duties nodes=beacon:4000=optimistic
```

Then, when both are synced:
Normal logs.

title: Implement EIP-8365: disallow new 0x00 validators
body:
Part of #17673 (Heze devnet tracking).

Implements the EIP-8365 guard from the Heze `apply_pending_deposit` spec (consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4): pending deposits that would create a new validator with BLS (`0x00`) withdrawal credentials are skipped before signature verification, in both the batch processing path (`ProcessPendingDeposits`) and `ApplyPendingDeposit`. Top-ups to existing validators, including existing `0x00` validators, are unaffected. Skipped deposits still consume churn and leave the queue, matching the spec.

The first commit adds `HEZE_FORK_VERSION`/`HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` config placeholders (far-future on all networks), mirroring how Gloas started in #16291. The guard is gated on `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` rather than a state version because the Heze state type does not exist yet; once Heze scaffolding lands, the gate can flip to `st.Version() >= version.Heze` as a one-line change. Inert on all networks until a config schedules the fork.
author: satushh

title: Add Heze fork config placeholders
body:
Part of #17673 (Heze devnet tracking). Split out of #17677.

Adds `HEZE_FORK_VERSION` and `HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` config placeholders, set to far-future on all networks, with per-network version bytes following each network's existing numbering scheme. Mirrors how Gloas started in #16291: configuration only, no version enum, state types, or fork schedule entries yet.

This is shared fork setup for the upcoming Heze work (EIP-7805 FOCIL rework, EIP-8015, EIP-8365, EIP-8198), letting features be gated on the fork epoch before the full Heze scaffolding lands.

title: `heze-devnet-2`
body:
Works for #17673.
 
 ## Tags in each commit
 
 This branch is supposed to be separated by each interest via commit tag.
 
 - `Heze`: Scaffolding works for Heze preparation. Each commit is good for opening a separate PR on current `develop`.
- `Gloas`: Even though these commits are in the stack, it mechanically changes codes for Gloas, so like `Heze`, it's a good PR candidate as well.
-  `FOCIL` / `EIP-8015` / `EIP-8365`: Self-explanatory.
- `Spectest`: Commits for spectest runner.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR supports EIP-8198, which was removed from `heze-devnet-2`. However, it is possible to set shorter slot time in it (see the kurtosis config).
> Seen with Barnabas: Because `heze-devnet-3` will be `heze-devnet-2` + shorter slot time, and because LH, Teku and Lodestar already support EIP-8198 in their `heze-devnet-2` branch, we can keep this branch for devnet 3.

## Kurtosis Config

```yaml
participants_matrix:
  el:
    - el_type: ethrex
      el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:heze-devnet-2
  cl:
    - cl_type: lodestar
      cl_image: ethpandaops/lodestar:unstable

    - cl_type: teku
      cl_image: ethpandaops/teku:heze-devnet-2
      supernode: true
    - cl_type: lighthouse
      cl_image: ethpandaops/lighthouse:heze-devnet-2
      supernode: true
    - cl_type: prysm
      cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:heze-devnet-2-minimal
      vc_image: ethpandaops/prysm-validator:heze-devnet-2-minimal
      supernode: true
      vc_extra_params:
        - --enable-beacon-rest-api
  count: 1

network_params:
  preset: minimal
  gloas_fork_epoch: 0
  heze_fork_epoch: 1
  slot_duration_ms_heze: 5000

additional_services:
  - spamoor
  - dora

global_log_level: debug

dora_params:
  image: ethpandaops/dora:masterndaops/dora:master
```

## Extra Notes

- For calculating HTR of `ProgressiveContainer`, we need a patch for `methodical-ssz` (See https://github.com/OffchainLabs/methodical-ssz/pull/23). `Heze: Bump methodical-ssz...` commit only pins the head for the patch and reruns codegen.

title: Deprecate some flags
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

  Other

  **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

  Several flags and aliases are outdated, but the `--help` output still shows them as normal options. This PR moves them to the `deprecated` section of the help. **Every deprecated flag and alias still works exactly as before**: only the help
  changes.

  This PR has one commit per item:
  - **`--dev`** (beacon node): today it only turns on `--enable-backfill`.
  - **`--holesky`** (beacon node and validator client): the Holesky testnet has been shut down.
  - **Merge transition flags** (beacon node): `--terminal-total-difficulty-override`, `--terminal-block-hash-override` and `--terminal-block-hash-epoch-override`. The merge is complete, so the `merge` help section is removed.
  - **Beacon node aliases**: `--subscribe-all-data-subnets`, `--enable-experimental-backfill`, `--extend-blob-retention-epoch` and `--max-goroutines`.

  How the aliases are handled: the flags stay registered with their aliases, so the old names keep working on the command line, in the config file and in subcommands. For the help only, these flags are shown without the deprecated alias, and
  each deprecated alias gets its own entry in the `deprecated` section:

  ```
  deprecated OPTIONS:
     ...
     --max-goroutines value  Deprecated alias of --healthz-max-goroutines. (default: 5000)
     ... 
 ```

  Only the listed aliases are deprecated. The `--grpc-gateway-*` aliases and the validator client aliases are not changed.

  New helpers in `config/features/filter_flags.go`:
  - `WithoutFlags` removes the deprecated flags from the `features` help section.
  - `SplitAliases` builds, for the given deprecated aliases, the copies of the flags used only for the help.

  The beacon node usage test now compares flags by name, including aliases, so it fails if an alias is missing from the help.

title: Clamp zero-root checkpoints for the engine payload hashes
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix - but only for local testnet started from Gloas genesis

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Besu rejects fcu from Prysm for the first two epoch from Gloas genesis. Prysm sends fcu with `safeBlockHash = 0x0`, from genesis until the first unrealized justification. (Meanwhile Reth and Ethrex accept the zero hash.)

This PR aims to be much more consistent on the zero-root checkpoints using `clampCheckpointRoot`. For the Gloas tree root, `checkpointPayloadHashForRoot` returns `treeRootParentHash`, which is the genesis bid `parent_block_hash`.

Note that this PR will not have any behavior changes on mainnet/testnets.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A - found when locally testing with Besu.

title: [EIP-8025] Implement optional execution proofs
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This pull request implements a POC of EIP-8025
- [EIP](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8025)
- [Consensus specification](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/master/specs/_features/eip8025)

> [!CAUTION]
> This branch is based on the not (yet) merged
> - https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/660

**Added flags:**
- `--zkvm` (alias: `--proof-engine`): Use it to signal the node has to subscribe to execution proofs subnets, and to verify incoming proofs.
- `--min-execution-proofs` (default: 2): If `--zkvm` is used, then at least this number of proofs is needed (additionally to the EL validity) for this payload to consider the corresponding forkchoice node as valid (aka, non-optimistic). Note: this is a deviation from the specification. Use `--min-execution-proofs=0` to stick to the specification.
- `--zkvm-mock-proofs`: If `--zkvm` is used, use this when the network's provers run zkboost's mock zkVMs. The node then accepts mock proofs without checking them cryptographically, but still checks their public values against the payload. For each mock proof, the node also verifies a real proof of the same type that is built into the binary, and ignores the result. (This way the node still pays the CPU and memory cost of a real verification).

**Additional deviations from the spec:**

- In consensus-specs Gloas, `NewPayloadRequest` is a [ProgressiveContainer](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md?plain=1#L988).
- However, for ere-guests (used by zk-boost), it is a plain [SSZContainer](https://github.com/eth-act/ere-guests/blob/main/crates/stateless-validator-common/src/guest/input/new_payload_request.rs#L236-L242) (aka NO `#[ssz(progressive_container)]` attribute) .

==> `hash_tree_root(new_payload_request)` mismatches.
To be able to run with ZK-boost, Prysm, at the moment, considers `NewPayloadRequest` as a plain `SSZContainer`, deviating from the specification.


Also,  Prysm considers a proof as recursive, aka a valid proof of a payload also attests to the validity of all its ancestors. Once a payload is validated (EL validity plus `--min-execution-proofs` proofs), Prysm marks it in forkchoice as valid together with all its ancestors, and with the empty blocks built on top of it, even if those ancestors did not receive enough proofs themselves.

**Added metrics:**
- `payload_synced_since_slot_start_seconds`: Time between the start of the slot of a payload and the end of its processing.
- `execution_proof_verification_milliseconds` (label: `proof_type`): Time to verify an EIP-8025 execution proof with the zkVM verifier, for proofs that pass verification. Buckets: every 10ms, from 10ms to 100ms.
- `execution_proof_verified_since_slot_start_seconds` (label: `proof_type`): Time between the start of the slot of a payload and the verification of a gossiped execution proof of it.
- `payload_proof_validated_since_slot_start_seconds`: Time between the start of the slot of a payload and its validation by the EL and at least `--min-execution-proofs` execution proof types.


**Logs to expect:**
On the prover side:
```
[2026-10-13 13:50:11.18]  INFO blockchain: Synced optimistic execution payload envelope blockHash=0x0dee73d4142e blockRoot=0xedb3d11063f5 gasUtilized=0.00% parentHash=0xd9260c811eae slot=43
[2026-10-13 13:50:13.24]  INFO blockchain: Payload validated by the EL and execution proofs blockRoot=0xedb3d11063f5 proofTypeCount=1 slot=43
[2026-10-13 13:50:13.24]  INFO prover: Broadcast execution proof blockRoot=0xedb3d11063f5 proofSize=262 kB proofType=ethrex-openvm prover=243 slot=43
[2026-10-13 13:50:14.27]  INFO prover: Broadcast execution proof blockRoot=0xedb3d11063f5 proofSize=262 kB proofType=ethrex-sp1 prover=243 slot=43
```

On the verifier side:
```
[2026-10-27 17:51:48.29]  INFO blockchain: Synced optimistic execution payload envelope blockHash=0x63c4e6e1f305 blockRoot=0x23ae9451ce15 gasUtilized=26.69% parentHash=0x4372fa87ada9 sinceSlotStart=296.744685ms slot=11449159
[2026-10-27 17:51:53.18] DEBUG sync: Received and verified execution proof blockRoot=0x23ae9451ce15 proofSize=268 kB proofType=reth-openvm prover=2088 sinceSlotStart=5.19s slot=11449159
[2026-10-27 17:51:53.75] DEBUG sync: Received and verified execution proof blockRoot=0x23ae9451ce15 proofSize=268 kB proofType=ethrex-openvm prover=2088 sinceSlotStart=5.758s slot=11449159
[2026-10-27 17:51:53.75]  INFO blockchain: Payload validated by the EL and execution proofs blockRoot=0x23ae9451ce15 proofTypeCount=2 sinceSlotStart=5.758625406s slot=11449159
```

**Kurtosis configuration file:**
```yaml
participants:
  # Standard node
  - el_type: geth
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:optional-proofs
    vc_image: ethpandaops/prysm-validator:optional-proofs
    count: 1

  # Proving node.
  - el_type: geth
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:optional-proofs
    vc_image: ethpandaops/prysm-validator:optional-proofs
    cl_extra_params:
      - --proof-engine
      - --zkvm-mock-proofs
      - --execution-endpoint=http://zkboost-1:3000
    count: 1

  # Standard node that does not need proofs.
  - el_type: geth
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:optional-proofs
    vc_image: ethpandaops/prysm-validator:optional-proofs
    count: 1

  # Verifying nodes.
  - el_type: geth
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: ethpandaops/prysm-beacon-chain:optional-proofs
    vc_image: ethpandaops/prysm-validator:optional-proofs
    cl_extra_params:
      - --zkvm
      - --zkvm-mock-proofs
      - --min-execution-proofs=2
    count: 2

network_params:
  gloas_fork_epoch: 0

additional_services:
  - zkboost
  - dora

zkboost_params:
  image: ghcr.io/eth-act/zkboost/zkboost:0.12.0
  instances:
    - name: zkboost-1
  zkvms:
    - kind: mock
      proof_type: ethrex-openvm
      mock_proving_time:
        kind: constant
        ms: 2000
    - kind: mock
      proof_type: ethrex-sp1
      mock_proving_time:
        kind: constant
        ms: 3000

global_log_level: debug
```

title: Add Kurtosis smoke CI on every `develop` push
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: CI

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR adds a new CI using Kurtosis & `ethereum-package`. From this PR, for every push event on `develop`, Github Action is triggered to spin up a so-called "default" devnet consisted of two Prysm+Geth nodes. 

Two checks take place:

```yaml
assertoor_params:
  run_stability_check: true
  run_block_proposal_check: true
```

<details>
<summary>Explanations for each flag (from [`ethereum-package` repo](https://github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package))</summary>

```yaml
  # Check chain stability
  # This check monitors the chain and succeeds if:
  # - all clients are synced
  # - chain is finalizing for min. 2 epochs
  # - >= 98% correct target votes
  # - >= 80% correct head votes
  # - no reorgs with distance > 2 blocks
  # - no more than 2 reorgs per epoch
  run_stability_check: false

  # Check block proposals
  # This check monitors the chain and succeeds if:
  # - all client pairs have proposed a block
  run_block_proposal_check: false
```
</details>

And the result can be shown like:

title: REST VC: Use the slot+1 epoch for sync subcommittee duties
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/d230aa4d5f0f920544215bd4ad29dec9778a21f7/validator/client/beacon-api/sync_committee.go#L99

REST VC fetches the sync subcommittee index of a validator from `/eth/v1/validator/duties/sync/{epoch}`. It requested the duties for the "current epoch", and this PR changes the request to the "epoch for next slot".

Per the [Altair honest validator spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.6.1/specs/altair/validator.md?plain=1#L152-L157), a validator in the sync committee for a slot signs for `slot - 1`. [`compute_subnets_for_sync_committee`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.6.1/specs/altair/validator.md?plain=1#L378-L388) also selects the committee from the epoch of `state.slot + 1`. gRPC path already follows this rule.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Found while gRPC-REST parity checks.

title: Create the validator database on slashing protection import if missing
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

**The issue:**
`validator slashing-protection-history import` fails with

```
validator.db (validator database) was not found
```

when `--datadir` holds no database. 

This is impossible to import the history on a new machine before its validator client first starts, which is the main use case of the import.

**The fix:**
When no database is found, create it in `--datadir`, where the validator client looks for it.

**How to test it?**
1. Export an already existing anti-slashing DB with:
```
validator slashing-protection-history export --datadir=<datadir> --slashing-protection-export-dir=<destination>
```

2. Import the created anti-slashing export file to an **empty** datadir
```
 validator slashing-protection-history import --slashing-protection-json-file=<file> --datadir=<an-empty-directory>
```

On `develop`, step 2 should complain that no datadir is already existing and fail.
On this branch, this should work normally.

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

A peer that has the blocks for a range but not the payloads answers `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRange` with an empty list and a success code. The server walks the payload chain and stops at the first envelope it does not have.

Initial sync took that batch to import without envelopes. The first block got no full node, the second block builds on its payload, and `InsertChain` failed with `invalid parent root`. The scorer does not count that error, and the queue only refetches after the import fails, possibly from the same peer. On focil-devnet-1 two of three genesis syncs stopped at the first batch this way.

#16779 removed `r.err` from this branch because the queue downscores the block peer on every `ErrInvalidFetchedData`, which was unfair when another peer sent the empty list. But `r.err` is also what makes the queue refetch, and the queue only penalizes when the error wraps `ErrInvalidFetchedData`. The branch needed a different error, not no error. The "envelope does not match block" branch below already does it that way.

So: same peer for blocks and envelopes, wrap `ErrInvalidFetchedData` and let the queue count it once (the inline `downscorePeer` call is gone). Different peers, plain error, nobody is penalized, the batch is refetched. Batches whose blocks all build on the same payload still pass without envelopes.

If no peer has the envelopes, the range cannot sync from genesis either way. The node now stops at fetch instead of importing half a batch.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A. Found during a genesis sync of focil-devnet-1 on the Heze branch (#17680).

**Other notes for review**

Genesis sync of focil-devnet-1 with the #17680 branch, which carries this change.

- Before: three runs. Runs 1 and 2 stopped at slots 1-63 with `invalid parent root` and did not recover in 15 and 5 minutes. Run 3 got the envelopes from another peer, hit the same error at batch 256, recovered after 2 minutes, and reached head.
- After: the fixed binary has not done a full genesis sync on the devnet yet.

title: execution: options to serve getPayload and getBlobs in-process
body:
Two functional options on the execution service let an embedder that runs the execution client in the same process serve `engine_getPayloadVX` and `engine_getBlobsV2/V3` as typed in-process calls instead of JSON-RPC:

- `WithGetPayloadOverride` populates the proto `getPayloadMethodAndMessage` already selects, between the deadline setup and the `CallContext` it replaces, so fork dispatch, response wrapping, metrics, spans, and timeouts are unchanged.
- `WithGetBlobsOverride` bypasses the capability cache (it describes a remote endpoint, not an in-process implementation) but keeps `DisableGetBlobsV2`.
- No behavior change when the options are unset.

Follow-up to #17334 (`WithRPCClientDialer`): that removed the socket, this removes the serialization. Measured in a single-binary consumer (geth + prysm in one process, ~4 blobs/block devnet): `engine_getPayload` mean 16.1 ms over in-process JSON-RPC vs 0.39 ms typed. Consumer: https://github.com/satushh/ethereum-node (branch `engine-typed-ab`).

title: Send the `ExitReceived` event from the REST voluntary exit handler
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/voluntary_exits` adds the exit to the pool and broadcasts it, but it does not send the `ExitReceived` operation event. The gRPC `ProposeExit` path and the gossip validation path both send this event.

The fix sends the event after the pool insert and before the broadcast. This is the same order as `SubmitProposerSlashing`. The event data has the same shape as the gRPC path (`ExitReceivedData`).

Note that the aggregate submit path (`SubmitAggregateAndProofsV2`) does not send `AggregatedAttReceived`, will open another PR - #17713.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Found while REST-gRPC parity review

**Other notes for review**

Kurtosis config:
```yaml
participants:
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethereum/client-go:latest
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn:exitevt-before
    cl_extra_params: ["--monitor-indices=5", "--monitor-indices=133"]
    vc_type: prysm
    vc_image: prysm-vc:exitevt
    vc_extra_params: ["--enable-beacon-rest-api"]
    validator_count: 128
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethereum/client-go:latest
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn:exitevt-after
    cl_extra_params: ["--monitor-indices=5", "--monitor-indices=133"]
    vc_type: prysm
    vc_image: prysm-vc:exitevt
    vc_extra_params: ["--enable-beacon-rest-api"]
    validator_count: 128
network_params:
  preset: mainnet
  seconds_per_slot: 6
  shard_committee_period: 0
keymanager_enabled: true
additional_services: []
```

1. Open one SSE stream per BN before any POST: `GET /eth/v1/events?topics=voluntary_exit`.
2. Get a signed exit from the VC keymanager: `POST /eth/v1/validator/{pubkey}/voluntary_exit`. Take `.data`.
3. Run A: POST the exit of validator 5 to cl-1 (BEFORE).
4. Run B: POST the exit of validator 133 to cl-2 (AFTER).
5. Wait 15 s after each POST. Count events per stream and monitor log lines per BN.

And the result:

| POST target | HTTP | SSE event on submitting BN | SSE event on other BN (gossip) | Monitor "exit was processed" on submitting BN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cl-1 BEFORE (validator 5) | 200 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| cl-2 AFTER (validator 133) | 200 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

title: Keep relay links observed while dropping inactive builders
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`DropInactiveBuilders` releases the circuit breaker lock while it calls `isActive`, so that it doesn't nest the forkchoice, breaker and state locks. After retaking the lock it unlinked every *current* endpoint of each inactive index. So if `ObserveRelayBid` added or refreshed a link for that index while the lock was released, that link was erased.

This PR records each candidate's relay links, with the epoch each was last seen, before releasing the lock. After retaking it, only links that are still unchanged are removed. Failure records of inactive builders are still deleted as before.

The impact is low: `ObserveRelayBid` only runs for bids that pass `VerifyBuilderActive(head)`. The two can therefore only disagree when the head state shows the builder as active and the imported block's post-state shows it as inactive.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

`TestBuilderCircuitBreaker_DropInactiveKeepsLinksObservedDuringCheck` reproduces the race deterministically: it calls `ObserveRelayBid` from inside the `isActive` callback. The test fails without the fix. With the fix, `go test -race ./beacon-chain/cache/` passes.

title: REST VC: Query the aggregate attestation by the root of the signed attestation data
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

At the aggregation deadline, the REST VC fetches attestation data again and queries `/eth/v2/validator/aggregate_attestation` by its root. If the head changed after the validator attested (for example, a late block), this is not the data the validator signed. The result is a 404 or a minority-vote aggregate. 

> Collect `attestations` seen via gossip during the `slot` that have an equivalent `attestation_data` to that constructed by the validator. If `len(attestations) > 0`, create an `aggregate_attestation: Attestation` with the following fields.

The [spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.4/specs/phase0/validator.md#construct-aggregate) requires the aggregate over the signed data.

The REST client now records the signed data root for `(slot, committee)` before the attestation POST. The aggregation query uses that root and falls back to the old fetch when there is no entry. After Electra, the key is the `SingleAttestation` committee id, not the data index. The client keeps entries for the two latest slots. The gRPC path and the interface do not change.

Limit: before Electra, keys in one committee can sign different data, and the last recorded root wins. But we might not care about voting pre-Electra.

The sync committee contribution has the same bug but requires more ideas on top of this. A separate PR will fix it.

**Testing (Kurtosis)**

```yaml
participants:
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethereum/client-go:latest
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn:aggroots
    cl_extra_params: ["--disable-quic"]
    vc_type: prysm
    vc_image: prysm-vc:aggroots-after          # late-block node, gRPC VC
    validator_count: 128
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethereum/client-go:latest
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn:aggroots
    cl_extra_params: ["--disable-quic"]
    vc_type: prysm
    vc_image: prysm-vc:aggroots-before         # BEFORE, REST
    vc_log_level: debug
    vc_extra_params: ["--enable-beacon-rest-api"]
    validator_count: 128
  - el_type: geth
    el_image: ethereum/client-go:latest
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: prysm-bn:aggroots
    cl_extra_params: ["--disable-quic"]
    vc_type: prysm
    vc_image: prysm-vc:aggroots-after          # AFTER, REST
    vc_log_level: debug
    vc_extra_params: ["--enable-beacon-rest-api"]
    validator_count: 128
network_params:
  preset: mainnet
  seconds_per_slot: 6
additional_services: []
```

I used [Pumba](https://github.com/alexei-led/pumba) for chaos testing. It delayed one node's egress by 2 s, so its blocks arrived at about 2.1 s:

```console
docker run -d --name aggroots-pumba -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock gaiaadm/pumba:latest \
  netem --duration 17m --tc-image ghcr.io/alexei-led/pumba-alpine-nettools:latest \
  --target <cl-2 IP> --target <cl-3 IP> delay --time 2000 <cl-1 container>
```

So cl-2 and cl-3 will receive block 2 secs later from cl-1.

I believe transport (QUIC vs TCP) is orthogonal here. I disabled QUIC because 2.5 s delay stopped gossip from the delayed node after about 10 slots, and the TCP run (also at a shorter 2.0 s delay) gave stable late blocks. I'm not sure about the root cause here. 

Here's the result:

| 53 late-block slots | aggregates | 404 | aggregate over data the aggregator did not sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| BEFORE | 46 | 7 | 40 |
| AFTER | 53 | 0 | 0 |

FYI in the on-time slots, the two VCs show no difference.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

REST vs gRPC validator client parity audit.

title: Lc backfill builder
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Adds the builder for the light client backfill supplier: `NewLightClientEpochData` turns the canonical blocks around an epoch into the `LightClientEpochData` record that `SaveLightClientEpochData` stores and `LightClientEpochDataByRange` will serve.

Inputs:

| Input | data in the spec |
|---|---|
| `parent`: latest block at or before `start_slot(epoch-1)` | `parent_block_header` |
| `blks`: every block in `(start_slot(epoch-1), start_slot(epoch)]` | `block_data[i]`, `bootstrap_data.execution*` from the last one |
| `FinalizedRootProof`: finalized root and its branch from the post-state of the first block in `epoch-1` | `finalized_root`, `finality_branch` |
| `CurrentSyncCommitteeProof`: `current_sync_committee` root and its branch from the checkpoint block's post-state | `bootstrap_data.current_sync_committee_branch` |

These two functions read the merkle proofs from the state:
- `NewFinalizedRootProofFromBeaconState` 
- `NewCurrentSyncCommitteeProofFromBeaconState`

The builder checks what the caller could get wrong: the blocks link to each other and to the parent, are ascending and inside `(start_slot(epoch-1), start_slot(epoch)]`, and are of the fork their slot says; each proof is from the expected slot and verifies against that block's state root.

Branches of an older fork are padded to the record's fork with `normalize_merkle_branch` (Fulu to Gloas for `sync_aggregate_branch`; Deneb to Electra and Fulu to Gloas for `finality_branch`). The Altair fork epoch keeps its special cases: only a block at the start slot, parent is the block before the start slot, finality is default.

The caller must pass every block in the range. The builder cannot detect a missing last block; both sources (the node's finalized chain and era files) are trusted to be complete.

Test: a block in every slot for all seven forks, with every `block_data` entry and both state proofs checked against the roots they claim, and the execution block hash checked against the checkpoint block; empty slots at both ends; no blocks at a fork epoch (record is the new fork, parent's finality branch is padded); fork boundaries inside one epoch; the Altair fork epoch after genesis and at genesis; the rejected inputs; a round trip through the store.

Part of #17448. Base: `lc-backfill-integrate` (base on `origin/develop`).

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Adds the experimental `GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/leaves` endpoint proposed in [ethereum/beacon-APIs#664](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/664).

Returns the `hash_tree_root` of every active top-level beacon state field, in field order, so consumers can construct proofs over state fields.

title: gloas: attempting to fix restart stall
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

 Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
On glamsterdam-devnet-8, 10 Prysm beacon nodes logged this error every few seconds for hours after their restarts at 15:10–15:21 UTC on 2026-10-19:

```
WARN initial-sync: Block processing failure error=post block process: could not process block: could not insert block 483330 to fork choice store: invalid parent root firstSlot=483329 lastSlot=483330
```
Each failure was followed by:

```
ERROR blockchain: Could not delete block with block root 0x7fb80ce4... error=cannot delete finalized block or state
```
Initial sync now asks forkchoice, not the database, whether a payload envelope still needs to be applied. Before, an envelope already in the database was skipped even if forkchoice had never applied it, which happens after every restart: forkchoice is rebuilt only up to the justified checkpoint, while the database keeps everything from before.

How it stalled 10 Prysm nodes on glamsterdam-devnet-8 (2026-10-19):

1. Slot [[483328](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483328)](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483328) is the justified checkpoint. Its payload arrives late.
2. Slot [[483329](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483329)](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483329) skips that payload and builds on [[483327](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483327)](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483327)'s instead. Dora shows 483328 and 483329 with the same execution block, 412362.
3. Slot [[483330](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483330)](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/slot/483330) builds on 483329's payload (execution block 412363).
4. The nodes restart. Forkchoice is rebuilt up to 483328; the database still has 483329's and 483330's envelopes.
5. Sync re-imports 483329 but drops its envelope because the database has it. Forkchoice never gets 483329 with its payload.
6. 483330 has no parent to attach to and fails with `invalid parent root`. Every retry repeats step 5, and the nodes stay stuck until their databases are wiped.

With the change, step 5 keeps the envelope because forkchoice doesn't have it. Re-applying one is safe: the database write is an overwrite and forkchoice ignores a duplicate payload.
**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

title: fix(sync): stop data column logging on service cancellation
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`Service.Start()` launches `processDataColumnLogs()`, but the logging loop does not observe the service context. After `Service.Stop()` cancels that context, the goroutine continues running and its ticker keeps waking it once per second while the process remains alive.

Return when `s.ctx.Done()` is closed and stop the ticker with `defer ticker.Stop()`. Add a regression test that waits for the routine to receive a log entry, cancels the context, and checks that the routine exits. Include a changelog fragment.

```python
    ACTIVE_FIELDS = active_fields(width=13)

    parent_block_hash: Hash32
    parent_block_root: Root
    block_hash: Hash32
    prev_randao: Bytes32
    fee_recipient: ExecutionAddress
    gas_limit: Uint64
    builder_index: BuilderIndex
    slot: Slot
    value: Gwei
    execution_payment: Gwei
    blob_kzg_commitments: BlobKZGCommitments
    execution_requests_root: Root
    # [New in Heze:EIP7805]
    inclusion_list_bits: InclusionListBits
```

This PR prepares it with the common interface. Now `ReadOnlyBeaconBlockBody.SignedExecutionPayloadBid()` returns the wrapped, read-only version of Gloas bid. Also `ReadOnlyBeaconBlockBody.ExecutionPayloadBid()` is added as most of the callers are interested in unsigned message which is bid itself. `SignedBeaconBlock.SetSignedExecutionPayloadBid` now accepts `ROSignedExecutionPayloadBid` instead of protobuf message.

title: Reject Gloas fork epoch PTC duties before the fork
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently, `POST /eth/v1/validator/duties/ptc/{epoch}` returns `200` with empty data (`[]`) for `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH` before the fork. This PR returns `400 Bad Request` for the same request.

PTC for the Gloas fork boundary is not known. It is dependent on the result from [`initialize_ptc_window`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/fork.md#new-initialize_ptc_window) which also relies on the blocks of `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH - 1` epoch.

Teku VC requests PTC duty prior to the fork, but it's not a root cause. I think Prysm BN should reject the request (in terms of correctness), not returning an invalid `200` response which makes VC confusing. The change allows `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` window so that a VC whose clock is slightly ahead can be covered.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**


<details>


title: Validator client: put the auth token in the wallet directory by default
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Issue:
When running the validator client with `--rpc` and a custom `--wallet-dir`, the Keymanager API auth token is not written to that wallet directory, but to the default one (for example `~/.eth2validators/prysm-wallet-v2/auth-token` on Linux).

Fix:
When running the validator client with `--rpc` and a custom `--wallet-dir`, the Keymanager API auth token is now written to that wallet directory.

**How to test it?**
On develop, run
```
make run validator -- --accept-terms-of-use --rpc --wallet-dir /tmp/prysm-wallet-test
```

The token should **not** be in `/tmp/prysm-wallet-test`, but in the default wallet directory.
(The default wallet directory is visible with `--help` at the `--wallet-dir` line.)


In this branch, run
```
make run validator -- --accept-terms-of-use --rpc --wallet-dir /tmp/prysm-wallet-test
```

The token should be in `/tmp/prysm-wallet-test`.

Updates `google.golang.org/grpc` from 1.81.1 to 1.83.2
Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.83.2

Security

  • server: Reject requests missing both :authority and Host headers with HTTP 400 and status Internal. (grpc/grpc-go#9365)
    • Special Thanks: @​winklemad

Release 1.83.1

Security

  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where nested Principal or Permission rules with :scheme or grpc- prefixed header matchers were not rejected, which could cause DENY rules to fail open. (#9258)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where the host header matcher was not being replaced with :authority in nested Principal or Permission rules. (#9258)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where a header matcher whose name was not lowercase, such as X-Role, matched no header, which could cause DENY rules to fail open. (#9332)
    • Special Thanks: @​alimony
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where a :scheme or grpc- prefixed header matcher was accepted when its name was not lowercase. (#9332)
    • Special Thanks: @​alimony
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where a Host header matcher was not replaced with :authority. (#9332)
    • Special Thanks: @​alimony

Performance

  • transport: Restrict memory overhead of buffering small data frames. (#9331)

Release 1.83.0

Security

  • server: Stop reading from connections when flooded by HTTP/2 frames to mitigate resource exhaustion. The default value for this limit is 100 frames, excluding DATA and HEADERS, and may be changed by setting environment variable GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT.
  • xds/rbac: Support Metadata and RequestedServerName permissions matcher fields. If present in a DENY rule, previously these would be ignored and fail-open.
  • xds/rbac: Fix panic when parsing unsupported fields in NotRule/NotId permissions.
  • xds/rbac: Support the deprecated source_ip principal identifier by treating it as equivalent to direct_remote_ip.
  • xds: Fix panic when parsing route header matchers configured with empty exact_match, prefix_match, or suffix_match strings. (#9223)

New Features

  • xds/googlec2p: Enable DirectPath over Interconnect support for on-premises clients via the force-xds target URI query parameter. (#9133)
  • xds: Enable xDS configuration to control which fields get propagated from ORCA backend metric reports to LRS load reports. (#9145)
  • authz: Add OnPolicyUpdate callback to FileWatcherOptions to notify when an authz policy is loaded or updated. (#9142)
    • Special Thanks: @​hnefatl
  • xds: Add support for the GCP Authentication HTTP Filter, which automatically fetches and attaches GCP Service Account Identity JWT tokens to outgoing RPCs.
    • This feature can be enabled by setting environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_XDS_GCP_AUTHENTICATION_FILTER=true. (#9119)
  • xds: Add support for xDS-based HTTP CONNECT proxies.
    • This feature can be enabled by setting environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_XDS_HTTP_CONNECT=true. (#9151)
  • xds: Add support for contains_match in route header matchers. (#9223)

Bug Fixes

  • credentials/alts: Fix panic when processing malformed frames by validating that the message frame length exceeds the message type field size. (#9197)
  • grpc: Fix compilation on Plan 9 targets (GOOS=plan9), broken since v1.81.0. (#9255)
    • Special Thanks: @​Yusufihsangorgel

title: Validator Exit: Detect the network from the beacon node for the beaconcha.in links.
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bugfix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
**The issue**

When a validator exits, Prysm prints a [beaconcha.in](https://beaconcha.in) link to track the exit.
The network for this link is taken only from the `--<network>` flag (`--sepolia`, `--hoodi`...).
The flag has no effect on the exit itself: the signature domain comes from the beacon node.

As a result, a user can successfully exit a validator on Hoodi without the `--hoodi` flag.
The exit works, but the printed link points to mainnet.
Seeing a mainnet link after exiting a Hoodi validator is confusing and scary. Furthermore, the displayed link is invalid.

Also, the (false) mainnet link is displayed if the network is unknown (devnets, custom configs), which adds to confusion.

Also, if the beacon node genesis could not be retrieved, the command panicks.

**The fix**
- Detect the network from the genesis validators root returned by the beacon node, so the link is always for the network the exit was signed for.
- Print no link for unkown networks (devnets, custom configs) instead of a wrong mainnet link.
- (Holesky is no longer tracked.)
- Return an error when the beacon node genesis cannot be retrieved (instead of panicking).
- Log one line per exited validator, followed by a line with the total count, so the output stays readable when many validators exit at once. Do the same when the signed exits are only written to files.


**Steps to reproduce:**
 Each run really broadcasts an exit, which can't be undone, so the before/after comparison needs two Hoodi validators, A and B. Both must be active, not already exiting, and active for at least 256 epochs.

  You also need a synced Hoodi beacon node with gRPC on <hoodi-bn>:4000, and a wallet holding both validators' keys.

  The `--hoodi` flag is left out on purpose in both runs.

  Before (develop, without the fix)

```
  go run ./cmd/validator accounts voluntary-exit \
    --wallet-dir=/path/to/hoodi/wallet \
    --wallet-password-file=/path/to/password.txt \
    --public-keys=0x<pubkey_A> \
    --beacon-rpc-provider=<hoodi-bn>:4000 \
    --force-exit \
    --accept-terms-of-use
```

Expected output
```
[2026-10-23 10:07:39.22]  INFO accounts: Voluntary exit was successful for the accounts listed. URLs where you can track each validator's exit:
https://beaconcha.in/validator/8d32f024c4520867ed031ae36b1e668bc69c8e77273fca096fc73aaabfffc2f77a859acf3f9f7de17503588402e076cf
```

The displayed link corresponds to a mainnet key, and thus, is invalid.

After (branch with the fix)

```
  go run ./cmd/validator accounts voluntary-exit \
    --wallet-dir=/path/to/hoodi/wallet \
    --wallet-password-file=/path/to/password.txt \
    --public-keys=0x<pubkey_B> \
    --beacon-rpc-provider=<hoodi-bn>:4000 \
    --force-exit \
    --accept-terms-of-use
```

Expected output
```
[2026-10-23 10:11:07.54]  INFO accounts: Voluntary exit was successful pubkey=0xa70c3681e97a url=https://hoodi.beaconcha.in/validator/a70c3681e97a1dc11b6ceee6bc34f90888a0979daafd066cacf26321f22567381d58f07b82530adb16f5d6d976cc5b0f
[2026-10-23 10:11:07.54]  INFO accounts: Voluntary exits were successful count=1
```

The displayed link is the correct one.

title: Speed up beacon node boot time be introducing a data columns sidecars cache dump
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**The issue:**
At startup, the Prysm beacon node walks the whole data column sidecars directory to warm the cache.
It usually takes a few seconds at most, but for an archive node storing multi TB of sidecars, the cache warming can take more than 20 minutes.

During all this time, the node cannot follow the chain.

**The proposal:**
When the node gracefully shutdowns, we dump the content of the cache into the disk.
When the node starts, we load the cache from the corresponding file in the disk. We also delete the file.

If the node is brutally stopped, then, at the next start, the whole cache warmup from file is needed again.

**How to test it**
1. Start the node with an already existing database (preferably containing at least the latest 4096 epochs of data columns sidecars)

The following log should be displayed:
```
[2026-10-23 09:44:46.93]  INFO filesystem: No data column cache snapshot found (first start or previous shutdown was not graceful) path=/root/.eth2/data-columns/cache.snapshot
[2026-10-23 09:44:50.20]  INFO filesystem: Data column filesystem cache warm-up complete elapsed=3.264804762s
```

Indeed, because it is the first start with this feature, no snapshot cache exists.

2. Gracefully stop the beacon node.

The following log should be displayed at the end:
```
[2026-10-23 09:50:34.79]  INFO filesystem: Data column filesystem cache snapshot written elapsed=107.093122ms path=/root/.eth2/data-columns/cache.snapshot
```

3. Check the cache snapshot is effectively in `/root/.eth2/data-columns/cache.snapshot`
4. Restart the beacon node

The following log should be displayed:
```
[2026-10-23 09:52:17.15]  INFO filesystem: Data column filesystem cache warm-up complete (loaded from snapshot) elapsed=114.106631ms
```

Check the file is **not** in `/root/.eth2/data-columns/cache.snapshot`

title: Do not send by range requests (blocks, payload envelopes, blob and data column sidecars) to peers whose advertised earliest available slot is above the requested start slot.
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

**The issue**
Since Fulu, peers advertise an `earliest_available_slot` in their status message. A peer cannot serve blocks, payload envelopes, blobs or data column sidecars before this slot. This is the case for a node that was checkpoint synced or that pruned its history.

Prysm ignores this value when selecting peers.
Initial sync, the skipped slot search and backfill can send a by range request starting below the peer's earliest available slot. 

Such a request fails or returns nothing:
  - the request is lost and has to be retried with another peer,
  - an empty answer can be read as skipped slots.

**The fix**
- Add `FilterByEarliestAvailableSlot` to the peers status. It keeps only the peers whose earliest available slot is lower than or equal to a given slot.
- Initial sync: `filterPeers` now takes the request start slot and drops the peers unable to serve it. This applies to blocks, payload envelopes, blobs and the non skipped slot search. The block provider peer, tried first for payload envelopes and blobs, is checked as well.
- Backfill: for each batch, peers whose earliest available slot is above the batch start are excluded from peer selection.
- Data column sidecars: `computeIndicesByRootByPeer` only assigns a root to a peer if the peer's earliest available slot is lower than or equal to the block slot.
