title: Add a `/kurtosis` PR comment command
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: CI

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Many PRs include a Kurtosis config and commands that reproduce a bug, but reviewers cannot easily run them again. This PR adds a `/kurtosis` comment command. The PR author posts a config and an optional check script. The workflow builds the Prysm images, starts the devnet, and replaces its status comment with the report.

````
/kurtosis [finalize=N] [package=<ethereum-package ref>]

```yaml
participants:
  - cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: {{head}}   # or {{sha:<commit>}}
    vc_image: {{head}}
```

```bash
wait_slot 64
api cl-1-prysm-geth /eth/v1/node/syncing | jq -e '.data.is_syncing == false'
```
````

- Both blocks are optional. Without a yaml block, `.github/kurtosis-pr/default.yaml` runs two nodes on `{{head}}`.
- The run passes when the check script exits 0 and every CL node finalizes epoch N (0 to 50, default 3). Nodes at the same finalized epoch must also agree on the root.
- `package` defaults to ethereum-package `main`. The report shows the resolved commit, so `package=<sha>` repeats a run.
- A newer `/kurtosis` comment cancels the running one. `/kurtosis cancel` only cancels.

**Security**

- Only the PR author can start a run, and only with `MEMBER`, `OWNER`, or `COLLABORATOR` association.
- The job that runs PR code has read-only permissions and unsets `GH_TOKEN` before the check script. The scripts and the Dockerfile come from `develop`.
- Only the `start` and `report` jobs write comments, and they do not run PR code.

**Testing**

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| [Smoke](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6313575101): PR head vs `8c923e6c49` | [✅ pass](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6313580358) in 17 min |
| [#17720 replay](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6319186520): before vs after the fix, SSE capture | [✅ pass](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6319192830). V4 fields in 0 of 26 events before, 26 of 26 after |
| Cancellation by push and by `/kurtosis cancel` | Both runs cancelled, status comments show `⏹️ cancelled` |
| [Default config](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6345733947): `/kurtosis finalize=1` | [✅ pass](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6345739767), `config=default` |
| [Current code](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6364819120): yaml + check script | [✅ pass](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17751#issuecomment-6364854729) in 19 min |

**Other notes for review**

- `issue_comment` runs only the workflow on `develop`, so the tests ran on #17751 with a temporary `pull_request` trigger. This PR does not include that trigger. The real `issue_comment` path runs only after merge.
- #17694 adds the same `.github/kurtosis.Dockerfile`. The PR that merges second drops its copy on rebase.
- A run stops 80 minutes after it starts. A high `finalize` needs a short epoch.
- The minimal preset is not supported. It needs a `-tags minimal` build.

title: Bound hdiff prefix-drop and builder indices before slicing
body:
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR resolves a couple of potential panicking points for hdiff when reading a DB that is either corrupted or from another writer:

- `ApplyDiff` sliced the four prefix-drop queues with `int(uint64 index)`. A diff whose index is `MaxUint64` turned into `-1` and panicked with `slice bounds out of range [-1:]` on every path.
  - => Compares each index (as `uint64`) against the source length and returns an error.
- The Gloas builder diff: a builder index past the registry made the loop append one `nil` builder per missing slot (`for len(builders) <= idx { append(nil) }`), an unbounded allocation driven by a 4-byte wire field, and left `nil` holes that panic later in `HashTreeRoot`.
  - => Enforces a diff the writer produces can only patch an existing entry or append the next one;

title: Harden filesystem slashing-protection decoding and persistence
body:
## What does this PR do? Why is it needed?

Harden the minimal filesystem validator database against invalid protection records and interrupted writes, without changing its serialized YAML format or slashing-protection rules.

Previously, permissive YAML decoding could accept empty or incomplete existing records as zero-valued protection state. Persistence also truncated the live file before writing its replacement. A failed or interrupted write could therefore destroy recorded watermarks, and a subsequent read could mistake damaged state for fresh history, weakening protection against slashable signing.

### Fail closed on invalid existing records

Require exactly one YAML mapping containing an explicit, non-null `lastSignedAttestationSourceEpoch`. Known protection fields must contain valid unsigned 64-bit integers; optional slot and target-epoch fields may remain absent or null.

Reject empty/comment-only/null documents, malformed YAML, non-mapping roots, missing required data, duplicate protection fields, invalid types or ranges, and additional YAML documents. Reject semantic merge keys and alias/non-string field names so YAML decoding cannot bypass field validation.

Validation errors include the record path and propagate through both attestation and proposal checks. Invalid files remain intact rather than being reset or overwritten. This does not reconstruct previously lost history.

Preserve missing-file behavior, nil-save no-ops, legitimate source-zero records, valid existing histories, optional null/zero values, and ordinary unknown string-named fields.

### Replace records without truncating live state

Route initialization and updates through a small, unexported persistence helper:

1. Create a unique hidden temporary file in the destination directory.
2. Apply the configured private file permissions (`0600` by default).
3. Write the complete record and reject short writes.
4. Synchronize and close the temporary file, checking both operations.
5. Atomically rename it over the destination.
6. Synchronize and close the containing directory and each ancestor through the filesystem root before reporting success.

Failures before rename preserve the previous file, or leave a new destination absent. Failures after rename still return an error, although the complete replacement may already be visible; no rollback is attempted.

Initialization preserves existing records and repeats directory barriers even when all requested files already exist or the key list is empty. A retry therefore cannot mistake a previous post-rename synchronization failure for durable success merely because the file exists.

Keep existing-target permission checks. Clean up only the current operation's temporary file, preserve cleanup errors, and ensure interrupted-write debris is not indexed as validator history.

## Other notes for review

### Compatibility and limits

- **Windows writes and initialization for this backend intentionally fail closed.** Unsupported platforms are rejected before filesystem mutation. Opening a store without initialization still permits read-only inspection. There is no best-effort durability fallback; supported platforms also return errors when required filesystem barriers fail.
- The BoltDB backend and unrelated configuration persistence are unchanged. No external dependency, exported API, or on-disk format migration is introduced.
- Atomic replacement does not make the read/check/write sequence transactional. Concurrent-writer locking remains outside this change.
- Corruption that leaves a valid record, including a valid prefix retaining the required source field while losing optional watermarks, may remain undetectable.
- Durability depends on the operating system, filesystem, and storage honoring synchronization primitives. Process-interruption tests are not physical-power-loss tests.

### Testing

The implementation commit was validated with:

```sh
bazel test //validator/db/filesystem:go_default_test \
  --keep_going --test_output=errors --flaky_test_attempts=3 \
  --build_tests_only --nocache_test_results

bazel test //validator/db/filesystem:go_default_test \
  --test_output=errors --flaky_test_attempts=1 --nocache_test_results \
  --test_filter='TestProtection(Persistence|Initialization)' \
  --test_arg=-test.v --test_arg=-test.count=10
```

Coverage includes 35 invalid-record fixtures through the reader and both duty checks; 12 injected failure phases for creation and replacement; permissions, operation ordering, initialization retries, preserved history, and reopened-store behavior. Ten repetitions passed, including 60 killed-writer scenarios at partial-write, pre-rename, and post-rename boundaries.

Formatting, import formatting, Gazelle, and configured analyzers passed. `make build` passed code generation, vet, and builds of `beacon-chain`, `client-stats`, `prysmctl`, and `validator` in an isolated snapshot of the implementation commit, using the pinned compiler and real cryptographic dependencies.

Runtime validation was performed on Linux. The three unsupported-platform refusal tests are skipped on Linux; Windows runtime behavior was not exercised.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR ensures da wait times does not have to block on partial column publish. If we have full DCs already, we should just store them first then republish them as partial to remove partial column broadcast from the critical DA path.

**Which issue does this PR fix?**
Closes https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17774 and https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17761

Note that this problem was mainly because the latest Nethermind release at 2.2.1 enabled sparse bloobpools by default which means it only retains 15% of the blobs which is a problem for supernodes as they should custody 100%. 
The idea solution for supernodes is to set Nethermind's `--TxPool.SparseBlobProviderProbabilityPercent=100` so that supernodes can get most of their blobs from the EL and don't have to fully rely on gossip which is the world partial columns was mainly designed for.

func post(name string, msgs []syncMsg) { body, err := json.Marshal(msgs) must(err) resp, err := http.Post(bn+"/eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees", "application/json", bytes.NewReader(body)) must(err) defer resp.Body.Close() b, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body) must(err) out, err := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"target": bn, "case": name, "slot": msgs[0].Slot, "validators": indices(msgs), "status": resp.StatusCode, "body": strings.TrimSpace(string(b))}) must(err) fmt.Println(string(out)) } func indices(msgs []syncMsg) []string { var r []string for _, m := range msgs { r = append(r, m.ValidatorIndex) } return r } func main() { flag.StringVar(&bn, "bn", "", "beacon node REST URL") mnemonic := flag.String("mnemonic", "", "validator mnemonic") offset := flag.Int("offset", 0, "first sync committee position to use") flag.Parse() // Use the network slot duration, not the mainnet default. var spec struct { Data struct { SlotMS string `json:"SLOT_DURATION_MS"` } `json:"data"` } get("/eth/v1/config/spec", &spec) ms, err := strconv.ParseUint(spec.Data.SlotMS, 10, 64) must(err) cfg := params.BeaconConfig().Copy() cfg.SlotDurationMilliseconds = ms cfg.SecondsPerSlot = ms / 1000 params.OverrideBeaconConfig(cfg) var genesis struct { Data struct { GenesisTime string `json:"genesis_time"` Root string `json:"genesis_validators_root"` } `json:"data"` } get("/eth/v1/beacon/genesis", &genesis) gt, err := strconv.ParseInt(genesis.Data.GenesisTime, 10, 64) must(err) gvr, err := hexutil.Decode(genesis.Data.Root) must(err) var committee struct { Data struct { Validators []string `json:"validators"` } `json:"data"` } get("/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/sync_committees", &committee) var vals struct { Data []struct { Index string `json:"index"` Validator struct { Pubkey string `json:"pubkey"` } `json:"validator"` } `json:"data"` } get("/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators", &vals) count := len(vals.Data) seed := bip39.NewSeed(*mnemonic, "") key := func(i uint64) bls.SecretKey { k, err := util.PrivateKeyFromSeedAndPath(seed, fmt.Sprintf("m/12381/3600/%d/0/0", i)) must(err) sk, err := bls.SecretKeyFromBytes(k.Marshal()) must(err) return sk } // Self-check that the mnemonic matches the network. if got := hexutil.Encode(key(0).PublicKey().Marshal()); got != vals.Data[0].Validator.Pubkey { must(fmt.Errorf("mnemonic mismatch: key 0 %s, state %s", got, vals.Data[0].Validator.Pubkey)) } // Distinct members from the committee, starting at offset, and one non-member. inCommittee := map[string]bool{} for _, v := range committee.Data.Validators { inCommittee[v] = true } var members []uint64 seen := map[string]bool{} for i := *offset; len(members) < 6; i++ { v := committee.Data.Validators[i%len(committee.Data.Validators)] if !seen[v] { seen[v] = true n, err := strconv.ParseUint(v, 10, 64) must(err) members = append(members, n) } } nonMember := uint64(count) for i := (*offset * 7) % count; i < count; i++ { if !inCommittee[strconv.Itoa(i)] { nonMember = uint64(i) break } } if nonMember == uint64(count) { must(fmt.Errorf("no non-member validator")) } // Wait for the start of the next slot plus 300 ms. genesisTime := time.Unix(gt, 0) cur := slots.CurrentSlot(genesisTime) start, err := slots.StartTime(genesisTime, cur+1) must(err) time.Sleep(time.Until(start.Add(300 * time.Millisecond))) slot := cur + 1 var fork struct { Data struct { Previous string `json:"previous_version"` Current string `json:"current_version"` Epoch string `json:"epoch"` } `json:"data"` } get("/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/fork", &fork) prev, err := hexutil.Decode(fork.Data.Previous) must(err) curV, err := hexutil.Decode(fork.Data.Current) must(err) fe, err := strconv.ParseUint(fork.Data.Epoch, 10, 64) must(err) f := ðpb.Fork{PreviousVersion: prev, CurrentVersion: curV, Epoch: primitives.Epoch(fe)} var header struct { Data struct { Root string `json:"root"` } `json:"data"` } get("/eth/v1/beacon/headers/head", &header) root, err := hexutil.Decode(header.Data.Root) must(err) sign := func(s primitives.Slot, sk bls.SecretKey) string { d, err := signing.Domain(f, slots.ToEpoch(s), params.BeaconConfig().DomainSyncCommittee, gvr) must(err) r := primitives.SSZBytes(root) sr, err := signing.ComputeSigningRoot(&r, d) must(err) return hexutil.Encode(sk.Sign(sr[:]).Marshal()) } msg := func(s primitives.Slot, idx uint64, sig string) syncMsg { return syncMsg{Slot: fmt.Sprintf("%d", s), BeaconBlockRoot: hexutil.Encode(root), ValidatorIndex: fmt.Sprintf("%d", idx), Signature: sig} } random, err := bls.RandKey() must(err) infinity := "0xc0" + strings.Repeat("0", 190) post("valid", []syncMsg{msg(slot, members[0], sign(slot, key(members[0])))}) post("wrong_key", []syncMsg{msg(slot, members[1], sign(slot, random))}) post("infinity", []syncMsg{msg(slot, members[2], infinity)}) post("out_of_range", []syncMsg{msg(slot, uint64(count)+1000, sign(slot, key(members[0])))}) post("non_member", []syncMsg{msg(slot, nonMember, sign(slot, key(nonMember)))}) post("past_slot", []syncMsg{msg(slot-1, members[3], sign(slot-1, key(members[3])))}) post("mixed_valid_then_wrong_key", []syncMsg{ msg(slot, members[4], sign(slot, key(members[4]))), msg(slot, members[5], sign(slot, random)), }) } ```

title: Ignore head-state-dependent voluntary exit gossip failures
body:
**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Return IGNORE instead of REJECT when a gossiped voluntary exit fails because the validator already initiated exit, the exit epoch is in the future, or the validator has a pending balance to withdraw. These depend on the head state, so REJECT penalized honest peers on a different head. This matches:
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5596 
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5764

Check exited and future epoch before the active check, as the spec does, so an exit for an already-exited inactive validator is ignored.

**Which issue does this PR fix?**

title: Optimization by pubkey subtraction for aggregated pubkeys
body: **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** `AggregateKeyFromIndices` is called by `createAttestationSignatureBatch` for each attestation. This call loads and adds every attester key, which is a fixed cost per block as the flamegraph above shows. This PR caches one aggregate public key per beacon committee. And later uses the cached pubkey when **subtracting** the aggregated pubkey of the **absent** validators. This optimization is much more powerful where the absent validator set is small, while it also provides a fallback logic when the optimization is in vain (a.k.a. doomed scenario, non-finalization). As the Hoodi measurement shows (the result below), this cuts block state-transition CPU by about **30%** (131 → 92 ms per block). **Which issue does this PR fix?** N/A **Other notes for review** ### Local benchmark - Assumes 99% participation. - Apple M5 Pro, 5 interleaved runs, median: | Validators | Path | ns/op | B/op | allocs/op | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 100k | old | 1,854,212 | 336,226 | 285 | | 100k | new | 96,380 | 81,399 | 359 | | 500k | old | 10,635,861 | 1,546,164 | 605 | | 500k | new | 735,564 | 316,656 | 679 | ```bash go test ./beacon-chain/core/blocks/ -run XXX -bench BenchmarkAttestationSignatureBatch -benchmem -count 5 ``` ### Hoodi measurement - My own Hoodi node. Note that the two windows ran on different blocks, but it's enough to tell where the bottleneck is: | Per block | develop (45 blocks) | this PR (48 blocks) | |---|---:|---:| | `ExecuteStateTransition` CPU | 131.1 ms | 92.3 ms | | `AttestationSignatureBatch` CPU | 63.5 ms | 19.1 ms | | `AggregateKeyFromIndices` CPU | 56.0 ms | 11.5 ms | | `state_transition_processing_milliseconds` median | 182 ms | 112 ms | | Keys loaded for attestations (mean) | 46,693 | 7,159 | **Acknowledgement** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md) and my PR follows its checklist.
